results.claim: The SDK hook roster includes a DirectoryAdded event that fires when a working directory is added mid-session; it is absent from hooks.md's own table, so this page is the only place it is specified.
results.quote: | `DirectoryAdded`                                       | No         | Yes            | A working directory is added during a session                                                                                          | Install dependencies for a repository added mid-session                                                     |
results.ourState: `DirectoryAdded` does not exist anywhere in the repo (`grep -ran DirectoryAdded packages apps docs scripts` → 0). `PluginHookEventName` enumerates 30 names and its own doc comment accounts for exactly two documented events as deliberate deferrals (`MessageDisplay`, `TeammateIdle`) — DirectoryAdded is unaccounted for. The surface it would fire on does exist: we ship session-scoped `addDirectories` grants (`pi-agent.ts:3189`).
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:25 (union), :156 (PLUGIN_HOOK_EVENTS list); grep -ran "DirectoryAdded" packages apps docs scripts → 0 hits

verdict.why:
All three checks positively confirm the finding.

(1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks.md` (883 lines) carries the row at line 181, under `## Available hooks`, in the table headed `| Hook Event | Python SDK | TypeScript SDK | What triggers it | Example |`. Cell-by-cell the actual line is [`DirectoryAdded`][No][Yes][A working directory is added during a session][Install dependencies for a repository added mid-session] — identical to the claimed quote. The two strings differ only in markdown table-cell padding whitespace (`diff` after `tr -s ' '` is identical), which is not a paraphrase.

METHOD CAUTION: my first fetch used the generic filename `hooks.md` in the shared scratchpad and was overwritten mid-analysis by another process — the 883-line SDK page silently became the 3173-line main Hooks reference, briefly making `DirectoryAdded` appear nonexistent. Re-fetched twice to distinct filenames, identical md5 (450577f8dc11d660071fac7c31c3eb14) both times, before trusting the result.

(2) THE CLAIM'S PREMISE HOLDS. `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md` (3173 lines, "# Hooks reference") has ZERO `DirectoryAdded` hits and enumerates exactly 30 events. The SDK page lists those same 30 plus `DirectoryAdded` = 31. So "absent from hooks.md's own table" is literally true, and it explains why our doc comments say 30: that count is correct against the main reference page and simply does not see the SDK page's 31st. `agent-sdk/hooks` is row 30 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a checked Claude contract source under AGENTS.md, not an out-of-scope platform page.

(3) REPO STATE CONFIRMED. `grep -ran DirectoryAdded packages apps` → 0 hits (with `-a`, so NUL-byte files are covered). Cited `hooks-runtime.ts:25` is accurate (the union begins there; 30 names = 28 Claude + `McpServerStart` + `McpToolCall`) and its doc comment does account for exactly two deferrals (`MessageDisplay`, `TeammateIdle`), leaving `DirectoryAdded` unaccounted.

ONE LAYER DOWN — the consequence is real, nothing upstream absorbs it. `mapExternalHookEventName` (`format-adapters.ts:622-646`) resolves in strict order: dialect table → `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` → warning. There is NO generic fallback. `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP` (:123-152) has exactly 28 entries and `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` (:99-102) exactly 2, so a Claude plugin declaring a `DirectoryAdded` hook falls through to `plugin.format.unknown_hook_event` — reported as a typo rather than as a recorded deferral, which is the opposite of the design intent stated at :634-635 ("A documented-but-unemitted event is a deferral, not an unknown name").

ONE LAYER UP — not an owner decision, not a product difference, not a sibling-subsystem mixup. inert-worklist §3 item 5 IS about `hooks-runtime.ts`, but it scopes "do not revive" to the dead executor (`PluginHookRuntime`/`runHooks`/`parseHookOutput`/`createHookRegistryFromProjection`) and explicitly preserves `PluginHookEventName` because three production files import it — verified at `hooks-automation.ts:47` and `format-adapters.ts:11`. None of the other eight decisions touch the hook event roster. Not a de-brand/gateway/subscription difference either. And no name confusion: `CwdChanged` is a distinct SDK-page row (:179) that we DO map (`format-adapters.ts:143`), separate from `DirectoryAdded` (:181).

CORROBORATION: `changelog.md:20` independently announces it — "Added `DirectoryAdded` hook that fires after `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request registers a new working directory mid-session" — so two Claude doc pages carry the event, not one.
verdict.correctedState:
The finding stands; three citation defects should be corrected before it is filed.

CORRECTION 1 — the absence grep is partly self-refuting. `grep -ran DirectoryAdded packages apps docs scripts` no longer returns 0: it hits ~20 lines in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.md` and `docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json` — the sweep's own output. The correct, durable claim is scoped to code: `grep -ran DirectoryAdded packages apps` → 0 hits.

CORRECTION 2 — the load-bearing evidence is uncited, and half the cited evidence is off-limits code. Cited `hooks-runtime.ts:156 (PLUGIN_HOOK_EVENTS)` sits INSIDE the executor that inert-worklist §3 item 5 says not to revive: `PLUGIN_HOOK_EVENTS` is consumed only by `HOOK_EVENT_SET` (:191) → `isPluginHookEventName` (:554) → the dead registry builder. Pointing a reviewer there invites a fix in a file the owner has ruled out. The evidence that actually carries the finding is `packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:123-152` (`CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP`, 28 live entries), `:99-102` (`DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS`, 2 entries), and `:622-646` (`mapExternalHookEventName`, the no-fallback resolution order) — none of which this row cites. Keep `hooks-runtime.ts:25` (the union is live and imported by `hooks-automation.ts:47` and `format-adapters.ts:11`); drop `:156`.

CORRECTION 3 — line drift and an overstatement. The `addDirectories` case is at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3193`, not `:3189` (which is `replaced: dropped` in the preceding `replaceRules` case). Note also that our `addDirectories` arrives as a `PermissionRequest` hook's `updatedPermissions` output and is refused unless `destination === 'session'` (:3194-3199) — so the surface is real but narrower than "we add working directories mid-session"; Claude's `DirectoryAdded` fires on `/add-dir` or the `register_repo_root` control request. Separately, "this page is the only place it is specified" is overstated: `changelog.md:20` also carries it. The accurate phrasing is that the SDK page is the only place it is SPECIFIED IN A TABLE, and the changelog independently corroborates the trigger.

RESTATED FINDING: `DirectoryAdded` is a Claude Code hook event documented on `agent-sdk/hooks.md` (line 181, TypeScript SDK only — Python "No") and announced in `changelog.md:20`, absent from the main `hooks.md` reference. Our fork does not carry it in any of the three gates — `PluginHookEventName` (`hooks-runtime.ts:25-54`), `CLAUDE_HOOK_EVENT_MAP` (`format-adapters.ts:123-152`), or `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` (`:99-102`). Because `mapExternalHookEventName` has no generic fallback, an imported Claude plugin declaring a `DirectoryAdded` hook emits `plugin.format.unknown_hook_event` — a "you typo'd the name" warning — instead of the recorded deferral the code's own comment says a documented-but-unemitted event should get. The `28 of the 30 documented Claude hook events` comment at `format-adapters.ts:118` and the matching comment at `hooks-runtime.ts:12-13` are correct against the main hooks reference (30) but stale against the SDK roster (31). This is the new-event failure mode AGENTS.md flags. Minimum fix is one line in `DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS` plus a refreshed count in both comments; full support additionally needs a union member, a map entry, and an emission point on the session-directory path.

results.claim: Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field whose value is `init` or `maintenance`.
results.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field set to either `"init"` or `"maintenance"`:
results.ourState: Our Setup emission carries `source: 'pi-runtime'` and no `trigger` at all, and it fires on every Pi session start rather than only under `--init-only` / `-p --init` / `-p --maintenance`.

verdict.why:
All three checks confirm the finding, and no upstream/downstream layer rescues it.

(1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim at hooks.md:1082: "In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), Setup hooks receive a `trigger` field set to either `\"init\"` or `\"maintenance\"`:". The firing rule is also verbatim at :1061 — "Fires only when you launch Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in [non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag. It doesn't fire on normal startup." — and the matcher table at :1063-1067 maps `init` -> `claude --init-only`/`claude -p --init`, `maintenance` -> `claude -p --maintenance`.

(2) packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:107 says exactly what was claimed: `await options.emit('Setup', { hook_event_name: 'Setup', source: 'pi-runtime', lifecycle_version: 1 })`, inside `pi.on('session_start', ...)` behind a `sessionStarted` once-guard. A `grep -a` for `'Setup'` across packages/ and apps/ shows this is the ONLY Setup emitter in the repo — no host-side emitter supplies a `trigger`.

(3) Layer up: the frozen contract row at packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:38 declares Setup as `kind: 'observational'`, `terminalDelivery: 'once-per-session'`, `redactedPayload: ['source', 'lifecycle_version']` — the absence of `trigger` is baked into the versioned contract, not an oversight at the emitter. apps/cli/src/index.ts has no `--init-only`, `--init`, or `--maintenance` flag at all. Layer down: the two same-named restriction sets are about hook TYPES, not gating — CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_LIFECYCLE_EVENTS (format-adapters/claude.ts:152) and LIFECYCLE_RESTRICTED_HOOK_EVENTS (automations/types.ts:152) only limit Setup/SessionStart to `command`+`mcp_tool` handlers, and format-adapters.ts:124/183/200 maps an imported Claude plugin's `Setup` hook straight through to the Nessy `Setup` event. packages/shared/src/automations/conditions.test.ts:661-668 asserts the consequence directly: `matcherMatchesSdk(claude('init'), 'Setup', {source: 'pi-runtime'})` is `false` while `claude('*')` is `true` — i.e. an imported Setup hook is catch-all and fires every session.

Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). Not a rebrand, corporate-gateway, or dropped-subscription product difference either.

It IS a gap the fork has already recorded and deliberately deferred — but recorded is not closed. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:24 tables it as "**no counterpart**"; :311 says "`Setup` carries `source` (doc: `trigger`)"; :322 says "Nessy's `Setup` fires every session start (Claude's only under `--init-only` / `-p --init` / `-p --maintenance`)" — both under the heading "Propagation found — reported, not fixed", with register category at :289 "documented, not implemented — Nessy has no --init/--maintenance launch mode". Shipped code carries the same reason at packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:347 (MATCHER_INERT_AGENT_EVENTS) and emits a registration-time `plugin.hooks.matcher_never_matches` warning. Real consequence: a Claude plugin's Setup hook, whose documented purpose is "one-time dependency installation or scheduled cleanup that you trigger explicitly from CI or scripts", runs on every Nessy Pi session start.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with two precisions. (a) packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:107 is the repo's only `Setup` emitter; it sends `{ hook_event_name: 'Setup', source: 'pi-runtime', lifecycle_version: 1 }` — no `trigger` — from `pi.on('session_start')` behind a `sessionStarted` once-guard, so it is once per Pi session, not once per turn. (b) The divergence is in event SEMANTICS, not a missing gate on an existing flag: Nessy's CLI has no `--init-only`/`--init`/`--maintenance` mode at all (apps/cli/src/index.ts), so there is no launch mode the event could be scoped to. The absence is contract-frozen (automations/types.ts:38 redactedPayload = ['source','lifecycle_version']) and knowingly recorded as `documented, not implemented — Nessy has no --init/--maintenance launch mode` (hooks-automation.ts:347; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:24, :289, :311, :322), with a `plugin.hooks.matcher_never_matches` warning shown to hook authors at registration. Imported Claude Setup hooks still register and fire catch-all on every session (conditions.test.ts:661-668).

results.claim: FileChanged input carries `file_path` (absolute path) and `event` (`change` | `add` | `unlink`).
results.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), FileChanged hooks receive `file_path` and `event`.
results.ourState: We emit `path` (only when a path was captured) and `change_kind` set to the mutating TOOL NAME, never `file_path` or `event`. The stdin payload is the event input verbatim (`hookCommandStdinPayload` spreads `...input`), so a hook doing `jq -r .file_path` reads null.

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim at hooks.md:2472 of the live fetch, with the field table at :2474-2477 defining `file_path` as the absolute path and `event` as `change`|`add`|`unlink`, plus a JSON example at :2479-2487. (2) packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:228-232 emits `{ hook_event_name: 'FileChanged', change_kind: toolName, ...(path ? { path } : {}) }`, and the cited hook-command.ts:646 is inside `hookCommandStdinPayload` (:641-651), which spreads `...input` and adds only `hook_event_name` and `cwd` — no key rewriting. The shape is additionally frozen by lifecycle-bridge.test.ts:90. (3) No layer up or down rescues it: `grep -ran change_kind packages apps` returns only lifecycle-bridge, its test, types.ts:805 and the frozen contract row types.ts:73; the emit chain (lifecycleEventSink -> index.ts:1969 `automation_event` -> pi-agent.ts:2325 -> emitAutomationEvent -> dispatchAutomationAgentEvent) renames nothing; and there is no sibling emitter — claude-agent.ts never emits FileChanged, and the other files naming it only register the event name. The only code that knows the documented spelling is the matcher helper `changedFileBasename` (utils.ts:150-154, `input.file_path ?? input.path`), which accepts a key nothing produces. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist.md §3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries), and not a branding/gateway/subscription product difference. It is already written down as an open divergence in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md:307-311 under "Propagation found — reported, not fixed", which corroborates the finding.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with three refinements that strengthen it. (a) The emitter never produces `file_path` or `event`, but the fork is not wholly ignorant of the documented key: the matcher helper `changedFileBasename` (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:150-154) reads `input.file_path ?? input.path`. It is read-side only, so `jq -r .file_path` on stdin still yields null — the claimed consequence holds. (b) The divergence is wider than field names: this fork's FileChanged is not a disk-watcher event at all. It fires on successful completion of a file-mutating TOOL (`FILE_MUTATING_TOOLS = write|edit|replace_in_file|multi_edit`, lifecycle-bridge.ts:52), so there is no `add`/`unlink` distinction available (a deletion never fires it), no watch list built from the matcher, and no `watchPaths` output honoured. (c) `path` is whatever the tool argument carried (`mutatedPath` reads `path ?? file_path ?? filePath`, lifecycle-bridge.ts:85-89), so it is not guaranteed absolute as the doc requires, and it is omitted entirely when the tool_execution_start/end correlation captured nothing.

results.claim: CwdChanged input carries `old_cwd` and `new_cwd`.
results.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), CwdChanged hooks receive `old_cwd` and `new_cwd`.
results.ourState: We emit `cwd` and `previous_cwd`. Neither documented key is produced anywhere (`grep -ran 'old_cwd\|new_cwd' packages apps` → 0 outside docs).

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim at hooks.md:2436, and the event's JSON example at :2440-2447 carries `old_cwd` and `new_cwd` alongside the common `cwd`. (2) The cited lines say what was claimed: lifecycle-bridge.ts:168-172 emits `{hook_event_name:'CwdChanged', cwd, previous_cwd?}`, automations/types.ts:801-802 declares `cwd?`/`previous_cwd?`, and the frozen contract row types.ts:72 lists `redactedPayload: ['cwd','previous_cwd']`. `grep -ran 'old_cwd\|new_cwd' packages apps` is 0 outside docs, including the built dist bundles. (3) No layer up or down rescues it: `hookCommandStdinPayload` (hook-command.ts:641-652) spreads the input verbatim and only back-fills a missing `cwd`, so nothing renames the keys before the hook process reads stdin (or `NESSY_EVENT_DATA`); Claude's `CwdChanged` maps 1:1 onto this event for imported plugins (format-adapters.ts:143, hooks-automation.ts:392), so an imported Claude hook reading `.new_cwd`/`.old_cwd` gets undefined. No sibling producer — `grep -ran 'CwdChanged|old_cwd|new_cwd' packages/shared/src/agent` returns 0, so the Claude backend emits no competing shape, and hooks-runtime.ts:178 is the dead executor already covered by owner decision §3.5. Not among the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3, and not a brand/gateway/subscription product difference — hook payload key names are neither renamed nor dropped by the de-brand. The only plan references (2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md:50, 2026-07-29-hook-context-injection.md:302) reuse the event without ruling on its payload keys.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with a severity correction: the value is present, the key is wrong. The sole producer is packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:168-172, which on a `user_bash` cwd delta emits `{hook_event_name:'CwdChanged', cwd, previous_cwd?}`; automations/types.ts:801-802 and the frozen contract row at types.ts:72 declare the same two keys. Our common `cwd` already carries the NEW directory, which is exactly what the doc's own example puts in `cwd` ("/Users/my-project/src" == `new_cwd`), so `new_cwd` is a missing ALIAS rather than missing data; the old directory is carried, but under the non-contract key `previous_cwd` instead of `old_cwd`. Nothing downstream renames it — hook-command.ts:641-652 passes the payload through verbatim to stdin and NESSY_EVENT_DATA — so an imported Claude plugin hook reading `.old_cwd` or `.new_cwd` gets undefined. Fix is two keys at the emitter (emit `old_cwd`/`new_cwd` in addition to `cwd`) plus the type and the contract row. Separately out of scope for this row: hooks.md:2430/2451 also specify `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` access and a `watchPaths` output for CwdChanged, and plans/2026-07-29-hook-context-injection.md:302 already records that our CwdChanged hooks' env writes are never read.

results.claim: StopFailure input carries `error`, and that field is what the matcher filters on.
results.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), StopFailure hooks receive `error`, optional `error_details`, and optional `last_assistant_message`. The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering.
results.ourState: We emit `error_code` only. The MATCHER path was fixed (`getMatchValueForSdkInput` reads `input.error_code ?? input.error` and maps it through `STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR`), but the payload a hook reads on stdin still has no `error` key, and `error_details` / `last_assistant_message` have no producer.

verdict.why:
All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it.

(1) QUOTE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md` (3173 lines) line 2288 reads exactly: "In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), StopFailure hooks receive `error`, optional `error_details`, and optional `last_assistant_message`. The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering." The field table at :2292-2294 backs it (`error`, `error_details`, `last_assistant_message`), and the JSON example at :2299-2305 shows all three keys. `hooks` is row 115 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP page.

(2) CITED CODE — substance confirmed, one citation line is wrong. `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:214-217` is exact: `case 'StopFailure': { const code = input.error_code ?? input.error ?? ''; return STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR[code] ?? code; }`, with the map at :126-142 — the matcher half is indeed fixed (commit `9a7dbf3e`, "the documented per-event matcher fields, so a matcher can fire at all"). But `pi-agent.ts:7299` is NOT the emitter: that line is a comment inside `emitStopHookOnce`. The real emitter is `emitStopFailureHookOnce` at `pi-agent.ts:7318-7324`, whose payload at :7322 is `{ hook_event_name: 'StopFailure', lifecycle_version: 1, error_code: errorCode.slice(0, 64) }` — no `error`, no `error_details`, no `last_assistant_message`. Line drift only; the claimed behaviour is confirmed 20 lines below the cite.

(3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — no upstream handler rescues it, no sibling-subsystem mix-up.
 - Layer down (what a hook actually reads): `hookCommandStdinPayload` (`packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:641-652`) is `JSON.stringify({ ...input, hook_event_name: ..., cwd: ... })` — a verbatim spread, no field renaming. Both execution authorities use it: the direct spawn (`hook-command.ts:737`) and the host's sandboxed runner (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488`, whose own comment says "One builder for both execution authorities"). So an imported Claude hook doing `input=$(cat); jq -r .error` gets null.
 - Layer up (the emit path): `emitAutomationEvent` → `dispatchAutomationAgentEvent` (`automations/lifecycle-hook-dispatcher.ts:24`) → `AutomationSystem.executeAgentEvent` (`automation-system.ts:629`) pass `input` through untouched; nothing maps `error_code` → `error`.
 - Absence checks run with `grep -a`: `error_details` has ZERO occurrences anywhere in `packages/` or `apps/` outside build `dist/` bundles — no producer, no type field (`automations/types.ts` declares `error?`, `error_code?`, `last_assistant_message?` but no `error_details`). `last_assistant_message` has a producer only for `Stop` (`pi-agent.ts:7304-7306`) and `SubagentStop`; `emitStopFailureHookOnce` takes only a code string, so the API error text available at all three call sites (`pi-agent.ts:6760`, `:6800`, `:6803`) is never forwarded.
 - Sibling-subsystem check: the one place `error` DOES arrive is the Claude-SDK backend, where the SDK itself builds the input and `buildSdkHooksForConfig` (`plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1644-1648`) spreads it verbatim — which is exactly why `getMatchValueForSdkInput` keeps the `?? input.error` fallback. That path is not ours to emit, and `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default. The finding is correctly scoped to Nessy's own emitter.

NOT an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none is this. The opposite is true: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md` § "Propagation found — reported, not fixed" names it twice as an OPEN item — item 2 ("`StopFailure` carries `error_code` (doc: `error`)") and item 4 ("Documented payload fields with no emitter at all: … `StopFailure`'s `error_details` and `last_assistant_message`").

NOT a deliberate product difference either: this is a hook-stdin contract key an imported Claude plugin reads, not a `NESSY_` env rename, a package-scope/binary rename, a dropped subscription flow, or gateway routing.
verdict.correctedState:
Correct as claimed, with one citation fix and one scope qualifier.

Citation fix: the emitter is `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7318-7324` (`emitStopFailureHookOnce`), payload at `:7322` — NOT `:7299`, which is a comment line inside `emitStopHookOnce`.

Corrected state: Nessy's own `StopFailure` emission carries `{ hook_event_name, lifecycle_version, error_code }` and nothing else. The MATCHER path is fixed and matches the doc (`automations/utils.ts:214-217` reads `input.error_code ?? input.error` and projects it through `STOP_FAILURE_DOCUMENTED_ERROR`, `utils.ts:126-142`; landed in `9a7dbf3e`). The PAYLOAD path is not: `hookCommandStdinPayload` (`automations/hook-command.ts:641-652`) spreads the input verbatim for both execution authorities (`hook-command.ts:737` and `server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4488`), so a hook script reading the documented `.error` key gets nothing. `error_details` has zero occurrences repo-wide outside `dist/` bundles (checked with `grep -a`) — no producer and no field on `SdkAutomationInput`. `last_assistant_message` exists on the type and is produced for `Stop`/`SubagentStop` but not for `StopFailure`, even though the API error string is in hand at all three emit sites (`pi-agent.ts:6760`, `:6800`, `:6803`).

Scope qualifier the original row omits: on the Claude-SDK backend the SDK builds the hook input and `plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1644-1648` spreads it verbatim, so `error`/`error_details`/`last_assistant_message` do reach hooks there. The gap is specific to Nessy's own Pi/native emitter — which is the only `StopFailure` producer in the repo (`codex-agent.ts` and `nestor-cloud-agent.ts` emit no `StopFailure` at all, a separate and larger gap).

Status: open and already logged as such in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-b.md` § "Propagation found — reported, not fixed", items 2 and 4.

results.claim: ConfigChange input carries `source` (the configuration type that changed) and optionally `file_path`.
results.quote: In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), ConfigChange hooks receive `source` and optionally `file_path`. The `source` field indicates which configuration type changed, and `file_path` provides the path to the specific file that was modified.
results.ourState: We emit `config_keys` and `config_digest`; neither `source` nor `file_path` is produced, so the documented matcher vocabulary (`user_settings`, `project_settings`, `local_settings`, `policy_settings`, `skills`) can never match — `getMatchValueForSdkInput` deliberately leaves ConfigChange unmatched for that reason.

**1. Quote — exists, but truncated in a way that reverses the claimed behaviour.** `hooks.md:631` carries the sentence verbatim. It is, however, the first of four sentences in that table row. The row continues: "Absent until the first user input. {/* min-version: 2.1.196 */}Requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later". So the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR — "`prompt_id` is a common input field on **every** hook event" — is contradicted by the very row quoted: it is absent on every event before first user input, and gated on a Claude Code version.

**2. Our state — literally true.** `SdkAutomationInput` does start at `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:742` and carries no `prompt_id`. Re-running the grep with the globs quoted (the submitted command dies on zsh with "no matches found") and with `-a`: 0 hits in `packages`/`apps` `.ts`/`.tsx`. The only repo hits are the sweep's own JSON and one plan.

**3a. One layer down — `SdkAutomationInput` does not gate delivery, so "no field" ≠ "hooks can't see it".** Both emitters that actually reach a hook are unfiltered pass-throughs, not allowlists:
- `packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:640-646` — `hookCommandStdinPayload` returns `JSON.stringify({ ...input, hook_event_name: ..., ...(cwd) })`
- `packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:53` — `NESSY_EVENT_DATA: sanitizeForShell(JSON.stringify(input))`
- `packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1643` — `const enrichedInput: SdkAutomationInput = { ...input, ... }`, spreading the Claude SDK's own hook-callback object

A `prompt_id` present on the incoming SDK input lands on the hook's stdin verbatim with zero code change. The TS interface is a documentation surface here, not a filter. (`sdk-bridge.ts` is an allowlist, but only for the `NESSY_*` convenience vars, and upstream has no `$CLAUDE_PROMPT_ID` either.)

**3b. One layer up — the producer is the vendored SDK, and at our pin it does not emit the field.** `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.183` (pinned in root, `packages/core`, `packages/shared`) declares `BaseHookInput` at `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:156-165` as `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode?`, `agent_id?`, `agent_type?`, `effort?` — no `prompt_id`, matching the row's v2.1.196 gate. **3c. The stated purpose is structurally absent, and recorded as a deliberate product difference.** `prompt_id`'s documented value is correlating hook output with the OTel `prompt.id` attribute; `monitoring-usage.md:459,598` puts `prompt.id` exclusively on **events**, "never attached to metrics… intentionally excluded from metrics". Every `OTEL_*` occurrence elsewhere in the repo is managed-settings env passthrough (`config/managed-env.ts:164-168`, `config/managed-approval.ts:78-84`), not an emitter. A synthesized `prompt_id` would correlate with nothing that exists.

Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (checked: seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — but the telemetry deviation it depends on is an equivalent in-code recorded decision.

results.claim: `Bash(*)` is equivalent to a bare `Bash`, and as a deny rule BOTH forms remove the tool from Claude's context.
results.quote: `Bash(*)` is equivalent to `Bash` and matches all Bash commands. As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context.
results.ourState: `Bash(*)` parses to `{ kind: 'bash', pattern: '*' }` — a pattern matcher, not a tool matcher. Context removal is decided by `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl`, which only inspects `rule.matcher.kind === 'tool'`, so a `deny: ["Bash(*)"]` leaves the Bash tool definition in the model's context and denies every call it makes instead of hiding the tool. Same for `PowerShell(*)`.

verdict.why:
The doc sentence is real, but the claimed consequence is false — this is the repo's canonical false positive: "the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handled it."

1. DOC — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` line 82: "`Bash(*)` is equivalent to `Bash` and matches all Bash commands. As a deny rule, both forms remove the tool from Claude's context." Not a paraphrase.

2. CITED FILES — the observations are individually true, and both are irrelevant to the claim.
   - `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-permission-rules.ts:310` really does return `{ rule: { action, match: { kind: 'bash', pattern: specifier } } }`. But that raw matcher is compiled at `permission-dsl.ts:347` into `{ kind: 'bashPattern', pattern, action }` — the claim stops at the parser and never follows the compile step.
   - `permission-dsl.ts:900-905` really is `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl`, and it really only inspects `rule.matcher.kind === 'tool'`. **But that function has ZERO production callers.** Repo-wide `rg -a 'isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl' . --glob '!node_modules'` returns only its own declaration, one comment reference at :977, and two assertions in `permission-dsl.test.ts:547-548`. It does not decide context removal. The claim named the wrong function.

3. ONE LAYER UP/DOWN — the behaviour is implemented, doc-cited in-code, and wired to the signed manifest.
   - The real decider is `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` (`permission-dsl.ts:930`), whose `case 'bashPattern'` at :951-958 carries the exact quoted sentence as its comment and returns `matcher.pattern.trim() === '*' && identity.permissionName === 'Bash'`.
   - It is applied by `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (`permission-dsl.ts:972`), called in production at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1759`, whose result becomes `allowedBindingNames` on the manifest passed to `finalizePiExecutionManifest` — i.e. the tool is removed from the SIGNED manifest the subprocess advertises, not merely gated.
   - Positive control, both green (`bun test`, 22 pass / 0 fail / 116 expects): `permission-dsl.test.ts:484` asserts `kept('Bash')` and `kept('Bash(*)')` produce the identical surviving list while `kept('Bash(git *)')` keeps bash; and `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/whole-tool-deny-manifest.test.ts:155` is an `it.each` row literally labelled `'the equivalent Bash(*) form'` that asserts the advertised manifest's `tools[].binding.piName` does NOT contain `bash` and that the gate still denies. Both halves of the doc sentence are enforced, and enforcement plus removal are asserted together so neither substitutes for the other.

4. THE PowerShell TAIL IS DOUBLY UNFOUNDED. The quoted context-removal sentence at :82 is Bash-specific; the PowerShell section at :235-237 says only "a bare `PowerShell` or `PowerShell(*)` matches every command" — it never claims context removal. And there is no PowerShell tool in this harness to remove: `rg -a "permissionName: 'PowerShell'" packages apps` returns nothing, and `harness-tool-descriptor.ts` has no `powershell` hit at all. PowerShell exists here only as a rule dialect (`claude-powershell-rule.ts`), not as an advertised tool.

Not an inert-worklist row and not a fork product difference — `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` has no `Bash(*)`/whole-tool entry. The only places this claim's text appears in the repo are the sweep documents that generated it: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.md:38` and `docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json`.
verdict.correctedState: Implemented and conformant. `Bash(*)` parses to `{ kind: 'bash', pattern: '*' }` (`claude-permission-rules.ts:310`) and compiles to `{ kind: 'bashPattern', pattern: '*' }` (`permission-dsl.ts:347`). Context removal is NOT decided by `isWholeCapabilityDeniedByPermissionDsl` — that function has no production caller. It is decided by `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` (`permission-dsl.ts:930`), whose `case 'bashPattern'` at :951-958 quotes permissions.md:82 and treats a bare `*` pattern as a whole-tool deny (`matcher.pattern.trim() === '*' && identity.permissionName === 'Bash'`), while any narrower pattern stays a specifier that gates without removing. `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (:972) applies it in production at `pi-agent.ts:1759`, producing `allowedBindingNames` on the SIGNED execution manifest, so `deny: ["Bash(*)"]` and `deny: ["Bash"]` both drop the bash binding from what the model ever sees — and the gate independently denies, so removal never stands in for enforcement. Covered by `permission-dsl.test.ts:484` and `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/whole-tool-deny-manifest.test.ts:155`; 22 pass / 0 fail. `PowerShell(*)` has no advertised PowerShell tool in this harness to remove, and permissions.md never claims PowerShell context removal.

results.claim: `Skill(<name pattern>)` is a supported rule format that matches by skill name.
results.quote: | `Skill(deploy *)`              | Skill                     | [Skill name matching](/docs/en/skills#restrict-claude’s-skill-access) |
results.ourState: `parseClaudeRuleString` has no `Skill` case; `Skill(deploy *)` contains no `param:` colon, so it falls through to the `default:` branch and returns an inert warning ("uses a specifier form no permission check matches; the rule is ignored"). verdict.why: Fabricated quote on the wrong page, plus a false consequence. (1) The claimed sentence does not exist on https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md in any form. Fetched copy: 567 lines, 60,850 bytes, md5 ad63081821d6d5c0ad82519f183a3c0f. `grep -in skill` yields exactly two hits — line 445 (".claude/skills/" in the live-reload table) and line 507 (strictPluginOnlyCustomization) — neither a rule row, and the page contains no table of the claimed three-column shape. Its "## Tool-specific permission rules" section (line 160) has exactly seven subsections: Bash, PowerShell, Read and Edit, WebFetch, MCP, Agent (subagents), Cd. No Skill subsection, no `Skill(` anywhere. The genuine contract lives on a DIFFERENT page, skills.md § "Restrict Claude's skill access" (lines 603-627), as a fenced code block containing `Skill(commit)` / `Skill(review-pr *)` / `Skill(deploy *)` followed at line 627 by "Permission syntax: `Skill(name)` for exact match, `Skill(name *)` for prefix match with any arguments." The finding presents an invented markdown table row as a verbatim quote from a page that never carried it. (2) The consequence is false and names the wrong subsystem. `parseClaudeRuleString` lives in `pi-harness/` and serves the Pi harness, which has NO `Skill` tool binding at all: `pi-harness/harness-tool-descriptor.ts` binds only `skill_validate` (:136, :271) and `read_skill_resource` (:184, :317); Pi materializes skill content into the turn via `materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation` rather than dispatching a `Skill` tool call. On the other backend, `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1118` places `Skill` in `disallowedTools` unconditionally: `const disallowedTools: string[] = ['EnterPlanMode', 'ExitPlanMode', 'AskUserQuestion', 'Skill'];`. So no `Skill` tool call exists in either runtime for a deny rule to gate — nothing is "silently granted" that a supported rule form would have denied. (3) It is also not silent: the `default:` branch returns `inert('claude_rule.unmatched_form', 'Permission <action> rule "…" uses a specifier form no permission check matches; the rule is ignored.')`, and that diagnostic is consumed at `managed-policy.ts:1017-1026` and `permissions-config.ts:529`. (4) Not one of the nine owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (checked; the nearest skill row, `SkillMetadata.disallowedTools`, sits in §2 and is a different symbol — itself an instance of the §4 shape-4 trap this finding also falls into).
verdict.correctedState: The mechanical half of the code claim is accurate; the citation and the consequence are not. Accurate: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-permission-rules.ts` has no `Skill` case (`grep -an Skill` on the file returns zero hits); its switch covers Bash, PowerShell, Read/Edit, Write/NotebookEdit/Glob, WebFetch, Agent, Cd, then `default:`. `Skill(deploy *)` carries no `param:` colon, so `PARAM_SPECIFIER` misses and it reaches the `inert('claude_rule.unmatched_form', …)` at lines 378-381. There is no `skill` matcher kind in `CompiledMatcher` — the kinds are tool, bash, bashPattern, powershell, path, pathGlob, cdPath, host, mcp, agent, parameter, at permission-dsl.ts lines 77-88 (the finding cites 76-87, off by one). Wrong: the doc page. `Skill(name)` / `Skill(name *)` is specified on skills.md lines 616-627, not permissions.md, and not as a table row — the finding's "quote" is fabricated. Wrong: the consequence. Neither backend exposes a `Skill` tool that such a rule would gate. Pi binds only `skill_validate` and `read_skill_resource` (harness-tool-descriptor.ts:136/184/271/317) and injects skill content directly; the Claude Agent SDK backend hard-blocks the SDK `Skill` tool at claude-agent.ts:1118. Skill invocation in this fork is gated by source enablement, `disable-model-invocation`, and path gating — a different subsystem from the tool-permission DSL. A correctly-scoped version of this observation would read: "Nessy does not model skill invocation as a permission-gated `Skill` tool, so Claude's `Skill(name)` name-matching rules have no surface to bind to; an imported rule is diagnosed as `claude_rule.unmatched_form` rather than applied." That is a design difference in how skills are dispatched, not a silent grant, and its doc contract is skills.md, not permissions.md.

(2) IT IS A RECORDED, DATED, REASONED DEVIATION — not a discovery. Three places already carry it:

results.claim: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is a managed-only setting that blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources; it accepts `true` or an array naming a subset.
results.quote: | `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`                | Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings. `true` locks all four surfaces; an array such as `["skills", "hooks"]` locks only the named ones.
results.ourState: No reader (`grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` → 0). We implement the per-surface locks `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` and `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, but nothing locks user/project SKILLS or AGENTS to plugin-or-managed origin.

verdict.why:
The divergence survives the challenge, but two of its evidence claims are wrong and must be corrected before it is used.

LEG 1 — QUOTE: CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions.md` -> line 507 contains the claimed text as an exact substring (Python `in` test = True). The claim truncates before the line's trailing `See [`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`](/docs/en/settings#strictpluginonlycustomization)`, which is a truncation, not a paraphrase. Not a refutation.

LEG 2 — CITED FILE:LINE: ONE OF THREE IS WRONG. In `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts`, `:177` really is `allowManagedHooksOnly` and `:203` really is `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, but `:129` is `readonly allowedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]` — an MCP allowlist, not a managed-only lock. And the OUR STATE sentence "We implement the per-surface locks allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly" is false for the middle one: `grep -ran allowManagedMcpServersOnly --include=*.ts` returns 6 hits, ALL of them prose inside comments (`sandbox-settings.ts:357,459`, `permissions-config.ts:1007`, `managed-only-locks.test.ts:236`, `managed-policy.ts:737,1321`) — it is not a field of `ManagedPiPolicyV1` and not in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS`. Its absence is a recorded decision with a reason: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93` files it under "What we do not implement" with category `inapplicable — one tier carries these keys` — "Nessy has no user, project or local settings surface that carries allowedMcpServers or deniedMcpServers at all... Adding the key would declare a lock that enforces nothing."

LEG 3 — GREP -> 0 IS FALSE, BUT THE CONSEQUENCE SURVIVES. `grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` returns 5 hits, not 0: `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:333323` and the four copies at `apps/electron/{,dist/}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`. All are gitignored build output (`git check-ignore` confirms `.gitignore:7:dist`) carrying a vendored zod schema: `strictPluginOnlyCustomization: preprocess(t => Array.isArray(t) ? t.filter(r => hU.includes(r)) : t, union([boolean, array(enum(hU))])).optional().catch(undefined)` with `hU = ["skills","agents","hooks","mcp"]`. The string occurs EXACTLY ONCE per bundle, so the parsed field is never read by name — declared, not enforced. No first-party `.ts`/`.tsx` file references it (only docs do). So the identifier claim is sloppy but the behavioural claim stands.

LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — NO UPSTREAM HANDLER, NO SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CONFUSION. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (managed-policy.ts:501-534) is 34 keys and none of them locks skill or agent ORIGIN; `refuseUnknownKeys` (:727-733) drops any unknown key with disposition `stripped`, so an admin document carrying `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is silently degraded rather than honoured. There is no second settings surface that could absorb it: the only `managed-settings.json` references are `managed-env.ts:27` (a comment), `self-config-deny.ts:74-87` (deny-path computation) and `managed-policy-loader.ts:57` (our `managed-policy.json` sits in the same directory). The surfaces the doc names really do load from user/project scope here: project skills at `packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:485-486,523-524` (`PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`) and project subagents at `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:215` (`.claude/agents`) — gated only by the per-user trust/consent flow, which is a user decision, not an admin lock. Plugin-scope keys (`allowedPluginKeys`/`deniedPluginKeys`/`enabledPlugins`) narrow plugins, never user or project skills/agents.

OWNER-DECISION CHECK — NOT ONE OF THE NINE. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 lists SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is not among them.

PRODUCT-DIFFERENCE CHECK — DOES NOT APPLY. This is not a dropped subscription flow, a gateway retarget or a rename. The fork invests heavily in exactly this surface (a 34-key managed Pi policy with `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `disableAllHooks`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, `sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`), so a missing admin lock is a gap in a surface we are deliberately building, not a scoped-out one.

PRIOR-REGISTRATION — PARTIAL, AND WORTH KNOWING. The gap is already noted in three places but never as a closed decision: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:95` records only the `mcp` surface as `documented, not implemented — a settings key we do not carry`; `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:46` lists it among admin locks and `:559` (R30) among skill/agent visibility controls; `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-rules-tier.md:34` notes it has no `rules` surface. It appears in neither `2026-07-29-deviation-register.md` nor `2026-07-30-parity-report.md`, so the skills/agents half has no owner ruling.

results.claim: A tool result's `content` array may carry `resource` and `resource_link` blocks in addition to text/image/audio, and the runtime converts a resource link into a text block naming the link.
results.quote: The `content` array in a tool result accepts `text`, `image`, `audio`, `resource`, and `resource_link` blocks. You can mix them in the same response.
results.ourState: The MCP proxy's result reducer handles exactly `text`, `image` and `audio`. A `resource` block's payload (`resource.text` / `resource.blob`, the actual content) and a `resource_link` block are both skipped by the loop, so in any result that also contains a text block the resource content is silently lost — the `JSON.stringify(result)` fallback only fires when zero parts were extracted.

verdict.why:
Refuted on subsystem mismatch — the exact recurring false positive AGENTS.md names ("identically-named symbols in a sibling subsystem"). The quote and the code are both accurate; the mapping between them is not.

(1) QUOTE: verbatim at custom-tools.md:455. But the finding stopped two sentences early. The full line reads: "…You can mix them in the same response. In TypeScript, THE SDK saves audio blocks to disk and Claude receives a text block with the saved file path; in Python, THE SDK drops audio blocks from the tool result and logs a warning. THE SDK converts resource link blocks to a text block containing the link's name, URI, and description." Every conversion the sentence promises is attributed to the Agent SDK acting on a handler's return value.

(2) CODE: confirmed. packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2138-2166 handles only `text` and `image`/`audio`; `resource`/`resource_link` fall through, and `parts.join('\n') || JSON.stringify(result)` fires the raw-JSON fallback only when zero parts were extracted. `grep -ran resource_link` over packages/ and apps/ (NUL-safe, node_modules excluded) returns nothing repo-wide. One layer down, NessyMcpClient.callTool (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:478-503) forwards the MCP SDK result untouched, so nothing upstream converts the block first.

(3) SUBSYSTEM — the refutation. custom-tools.md governs IN-PROCESS SDK custom tools (`tool()` + `createSdkMcpServer`) and explicitly routes the other case elsewhere at line 859: "To connect to external MCP servers (filesystem, GitHub, Slack) instead of building your own, see Connect MCP servers." mcp-pool.ts IS that external-MCP client pool — the sibling subsystem the page hands off. The surface this page actually governs in our fork is packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:600-633, where every pool tool is wrapped by the SDK's own `tool()` helper; its handler returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: result.content }] }`. A text-only content array is a permitted use of the documented API — the five block types are options a handler MAY return, not an obligation it must satisfy. And because we ship the Claude Agent SDK unmodified, the resource-link→text conversion the sentence describes is present in our runtime for any handler that does return such a block.

There is also no Claude contract on the other side to diverge from: agent-sdk/mcp.md, the page custom-tools.md defers to for external servers, is 900 lines containing zero occurrences of `resource_link`, "resource block", "content block", "content array" or "audio". Claude publishes no documented rule for how a host reduces an external MCP server's result content blocks, so no Claude doc page is violated by mcp-pool.ts's reducer.

Not one of the nine owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3, and not a fork product difference (subscription flows, gateway, rename) — it fails on the doc-mapping, not on either of those.

Residual, offered as an observation rather than a finding: the underlying behaviour is real. An external MCP server returning a text block alongside an embedded `resource` block loses the `resource.text`/`resource.blob` payload, because the non-empty `parts` array suppresses the JSON.stringify fallback. If anyone wants to file that, the contract source is the MCP specification's EmbeddedResource/ResourceLink content types, not agent-sdk/custom-tools.md — and it must be scoped to the MCP client pool, naming both backends (Pi and Claude share the pool), not to the SDK custom-tool surface.
verdict.correctedState:
The Claude Agent SDK's own handling of `resource` and `resource_link` blocks — the behaviour custom-tools.md:455 actually specifies — is present in this fork, because the SDK ships unmodified and packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:600-633 registers MCP source tools through the SDK's `tool()` + `createSdkMcpServer` helpers. Those handlers return a single `text` block, which the page permits; the five block types are options for a handler, not requirements on it.

Separately, and outside what that page governs: packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2138-2166 — the external-MCP client pool's result reducer, shared by the Pi and Claude backends — extracts only `text`, `image` and `audio` blocks from an upstream server's result. A `resource` block's `resource.text`/`resource.blob` payload and a `resource_link` block are skipped, so when the same result also carries a text block the resource payload is dropped (the `JSON.stringify(result)` fallback at :2166 fires only when `parts` is empty, i.e. a resource-only result does survive as raw JSON). `resource_link` appears nowhere in the repo. Nothing upstream converts these blocks first: NessyMcpClient.callTool (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:478-503) forwards the MCP SDK result untouched. No Claude Code doc page specifies this reduction — agent-sdk/mcp.md, the page custom-tools.md defers to for external servers, does not mention content-block types at all — so this is a gap against the MCP specification, not a Claude-docs divergence.

verdict.why:
The quote and the code citation are both accurate; the CONSEQUENCE is false, and I measured it false.

1. QUOTE — verbatim. `settings.md:1008` reads exactly "* `npm`, `file`, `directory`: not supported for host pattern matching". The 8-type enumeration under "All supported source types" (`:934`-`:1013`) is real too. Doc half of the claim stands.

2. CODE — exact. `managed-marketplace-entries.ts:167-207` is `parseManagedMarketplaceEntry`; only `github`/`url`/`hostPattern`/`pathPattern` have cases, and `default:` (`:205-206`) returns ``managed marketplace allowlist entry declares an unsupported source "…"``. Measured against the claim's own example: `{"source":"git","url":"https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git"}` → `[]`, drop `{at:"strictKnownMarketplaces[0]", reason:'…unsupported source "git"', effect:"stripped"}`.

3. CONSEQUENCE — refuted by measurement (probe at scratchpad `mkt-probe-91fc.test.ts`, 5 pass; repo suite `managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts` 11 pass):
   - `{"source":"url","url":"https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git"}` → **allows that exact marketplace**. `matchesManagedMarketplaceEntry` case `url` (`:584-588`) compares `entry.url === identity.raw`, and `identity.raw` is the byte-identical string the admin/user types at add.
   - `{"source":"hostPattern","hostPattern":"^gitlab\\.example\\.com$"}` → allows both `https://gitlab.example.com/tools/plugins.git` and `git@gitlab.example.com:tools/plugins.git`, rejects `gitlab.com`. This is the form BOTH pages prescribe for exactly this case: the bullet one line ABOVE the quoted sentence says "`git`: extracts hostname from the URL (supports both HTTPS and SSH formats)", and `plugins/org.md#allowlist-with-strictknownmarketplaces (was line 771 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)` says "prefer a `hostPattern` entry over a literal URL so all forms match". The quoted sentence is not evidence that `git` needs its own entry type — it is part of the passage explaining that `hostPattern` IS how `git` sources are admitted.
   - `file`/`directory` → `pathPattern`, which `settings.md` itself defines as "regex pattern matched against the `path` field of `file` and `directory` sources". Measured: an anchored pathPattern admits the doc's own `/usr/local/share/claude/acme-marketplace.json` and `/opt/acme-corp/approved-marketplaces`, and rejects a sibling path.
   So "that marketplace can never be allowlisted" is false — only the JSON spelling is rejected.

4. DIRECTION — fail-closed, not silent. Measured: the stripped `git` entry leaves an empty allowlist, so the marketplace is BLOCKED, never admitted. A dropped allowlist entry can only narrow. The drop is recorded through `ManagedDropSink` with a reason naming the source, which matches Claude's own documented managed-settings behaviour (`settings.md:186`: "strips that entry, records a warning, and enforces every remaining valid policy").

5. `npm` names a marketplace source Claude itself cannot produce. `plugins/cli-reference.md#plugin-marketplace-add (was line 953 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page)` — the reference for `claude plugin marketplace add <source>` — lists four forms only: "GitHub `owner/repo` shorthand, git URL, remote URL to a `marketplace.json` file, or local directory path". `npm` appears in that page only as a PLUGIN source inside a catalog (§ npm packages, `:392-437`). results.claim: Running the sandbox inside an unprivileged container requires the nested-sandbox setting (`enableWeakerNestedSandbox`).
results.quote: Unprivileged containers need the nested-sandbox setting described in [Sandboxing troubleshooting](/docs/en/sandboxing#troubleshooting).
results.ourState: No such key exists in `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`; `resolveLinuxIsolation` builds an `unshare`/`firejail` profile and fails closed with `process-isolation-unavailable` when the namespace cannot be created, so a supervised session cannot run inside an unprivileged container at all.

verdict.why:
Refuted on two independent grounds: it is an already-recorded deviation, and its stated mechanism is wrong.

**1. The doc sentence is real.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandbox-environments.md` line 106 carries the quote verbatim: "You can layer the built-in Bash sandbox inside the container for per-command restrictions. Unprivileged containers need the nested-sandbox setting described in [Sandboxing troubleshooting](/docs/en/sandboxing#troubleshooting)." The setting name is also correct — `sandboxing.md:458` names `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` and explains it makes "the inner sandbox bind-mount the container's existing `/proc` instead" of a fresh one.

**2. The cited code is accurate, as far as it goes.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180` — `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` holds exactly seven entries (`excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots`, `deniedWriteRoots`, `additionalWritableRoots`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `network`, `filesystem`); `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` is absent (verified `grep -ran`, zero hits anywhere in `packages/`). The precondition is present too: our bwrap invocation passes `'--proc', '/proc'` at `packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:304` — precisely the fresh-`/proc` mount the doc says fails in an unprivileged container.

**3. THE REFUTATION — this is an already-recorded deviation, and the "OUR STATE" text is copied from our own register.** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:288` already reads: "**not implemented** — sandbox-environments.md:106 -- \"Unprivileged containers need the nested-sandbox setting\", i.e. enableWeakerNestedSandbox, which makes bubblewrap bind-mount the container's existing /proc instead of a fresh one. We have no such key: resolveLinuxIsolation fails closed with process-isolation-unavailable, so Nessy cannot run inside an unprivileged container at all." That row was harvested from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md:191` — item 5 of a nine-row list Task 3 of that plan wrote deliberately, categorising every remaining line of this exact doc page as `not implemented` or `inapplicable`. Per AGENTS.md, a plan's category string is where a deviation's reason lives. It is NOT one of the nine inert-worklist §3 owner decisions (I checked; none of the nine concerns sandboxing keys), but it is a dated, landed, generated-register entry covering this page line-for-line. Our own sweep data already says so: `docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:1030` notes that "`autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` and `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` … carry dated \"documented, not implemented\" decisions in the deviation register."

**4. One layer down, the mechanism is also wrong** — the "consequence is false" shape AGENTS.md warns about. `resolveLinuxIsolation` does *not* reliably "fail closed with `process-isolation-unavailable`" inside an unprivileged container. `resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher` (`packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23-37`) is a `realpathSync` + `isFile()` + `accessSync(X_OK)` check with **no runtime probe**. So with bwrap installed — the normal case in any container image meant to sandbox — `applyFilesystemIsolation` returns `status: 'enforced'`, and the `if (filesystem.status !== 'enforced') throw` at `linux.ts:49` never fires. The plan is built and the failure lands *later, at spawn*, as bwrap's own "Can't mount proc" error, not as `process-isolation-unavailable`. Only the network leg probes at all (`usableUnsharePath` spawnSync's `unshare -n true`, `network-isolation.ts:27-31`), and even it throws only when firejail is *also* missing.

**5. Sibling-subsystem naming error.** The claim says `resolveLinuxIsolation` "builds an `unshare`/`firejail` profile". Those are the two *network* backends (`network-isolation.ts:39`). The filesystem layer — the one the doc's setting is actually about — is **bwrap-preferred**, firejail-fallback (`filesystem-isolation.ts:263, 313`). Naming unshare/firejail hides the fact that the affected component is exactly bubblewrap.
verdict.correctedState:
Accurate but already recorded, and the mechanism needs rewriting.

The key genuinely does not exist: `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180`) has seven entries and `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` is not one of them (zero occurrences repo-wide under `grep -ran`). The condition the setting exists to fix is genuinely present: `packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:304` passes `'--proc', '/proc'` to bwrap, the fresh-`/proc` mount that an unprivileged container refuses.

But this is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:288`, a `documented, not implemented` row generated from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md:191`, where Task 3 deliberately categorised all nine remaining lines of `sandbox-environments.md`. A recorded decision, not a new defect.

The failure mode, corrected: `resolveLinuxIsolation` does not fail closed here. `resolveTrustedIsolationLauncher` (`trusted-isolation-launchers.ts:23-37`) only checks that the binary exists and is executable — there is no runtime probe — so with bwrap installed, `applyFilesystemIsolation` reports `status: 'enforced'`, `linux.ts:49` does not throw, and the isolated command instead dies at spawn with bwrap's own `/proc` mount error. `process-isolation-unavailable:linux:<profile>:filesystem` is raised only when neither bwrap nor firejail is installed at a trusted path. The one leg that does probe is network (`usableUnsharePath`, `network-isolation.ts:27-31`), and it throws only if firejail is missing too. So the honest statement is "a supervised session fails inside an unprivileged container with an opaque bwrap spawn error rather than a diagnosable isolation refusal" — which, if anything, is a *better* row than the one on file, and the remediation text in `isolation-remediation.ts` ("install bwrap (bubblewrap) or firejail so writes can be scoped to the workspace") would be actively misleading there, since bwrap is already installed.

results.claim: The built-in Bash sandbox is the only approach the product enforces itself, delivered through the `sandbox` settings keys in managed settings.
results.quote: **Built-in Bash sandbox**: the only approach Claude Code enforces itself. Deliver the `sandbox` settings keys through [managed settings](/docs/en/settings#settings-files), either as a file managed by your MDM or through [server-managed settings](/docs/en/server-managed-settings) on Claude.ai.
results.ourState: Managed delivery of a `sandbox` block exists and is parsed tolerantly, but the deliverable key set is a strict subset (no `enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`, `credentials`, `bwrapPath`, `socatPath`), so the documented enforcement configuration cannot be deployed verbatim.

verdict.why:
The quote exists verbatim at sandbox-environments.md:124, and the cited evidence is accurate at the identifier level: sandbox-settings.ts:394 strict-keys the managed `sandbox` block against SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS (:172-180 — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem), and none of the six named keys is in it. The CONSEQUENCE is false — the inert worklist's own recurring false-positive #3 ("the identifier really is unwired while the consequence is false, because something upstream already handled it").

The claim truncates line 124, dropping the third sentence — "See Enforce sandboxing with managed settings for the keys to deploy and how to keep developers from widening the policy" — and then measures us against settings.md's full 30-row key table instead of the enforcement config that section actually specifies. That config is sandboxing.md:400-406: {"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"failIfUnavailable":true,"allowUnsandboxedCommands":false}}, plus "Add excludedCommands", "Add sandbox.credentials entries for credential directories such as ~/.aws and ~/.ssh", and the two lock keys.

Measured against that, key by key:
- allowUnsandboxedCommands:false — SHIPS, deliverable via managed policy, is a floor the user layer cannot unlock (host-sandbox-settings.ts:46-49), wired at SessionManager.ts:3580 and enforced at the spawn: process-supervisor.ts:467-470 throws `process-isolation-unsandboxed-commands-disallowed`.
- excludedCommands — SHIPS, same path (SessionManager.ts:3579, process-supervisor.ts:476-481).
- allowManagedReadPathsOnly / allowManagedDomainsOnly (the "keep developers from widening" half) — both SHIP (SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS/SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS at :182-183).
- enabled — no key because isolation is not opt-in here. ProcessSupervisor.start calls resolveProcessIsolation unconditionally for every supervised process (process-supervisor.ts:185); the only two bypasses are the two documented keys above (resolveIsolationDowngrade, :463-482). There is no state in which an admin would need to write `enabled: true`.
- failIfUnavailable — no key because there is no warn-and-run-unsandboxed path to suppress. When no backend can express the policy, resolveProcessIsolation THROWS `process-isolation-unavailable:<platform>:<profile>[:<reason>]` with remediation text (isolation-remediation.ts) and the spawn fails. Claude's default is the opposite; the key exists to buy what we do unconditionally.
- credentials — no key, but the protection the doc's advice buys is a built-in unconditional floor: credentialDenyRoots(homedir(), CONFIG_DIR) is seeded into the deny layer at host-sandbox-settings.ts:61-66 and names ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.nessy, ~/.netrc, ~/.gnupg, ~/.kube, browser cookie stores (credential-deny-roots.ts:102-136) — i.e. the exact two dirs the doc tells the admin to add. It is deliberately retained even when filesystem.disabled is set (isolation.ts:56-63, sandbox-settings.ts:798-806), and the code cites Claude's own sandboxing.md:271 "There is no built-in credential deny list" as why it composes its own. On this key we are STRICTER than the documented configuration.
- bwrapPath / socatPath — a written decision already on disk: managed-composition.ts:56-60, "sandbox.bwrapPath and sandbox.socatPath have no counterpart in our schema; there is nothing to compose for them." socatPath configures Claude's sandbox network proxy, which this fork does not have (our network dimension is a boolean egress denial across three backends — isolation.ts denyNetworkEgress).
- autoAllowBashIfSandboxed — a DATED RECORDED DEVIATION, not a defect: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-5.md:115, category "documented, not implemented", reason "the documented default `true` is conditioned on `sandbox.enabled`, an opt-in Nessy has no analogue of: supervised-process isolation here is unconditional, so porting the default verbatim would auto-approve EVERY Bash command."

Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — but two of the six keys carry equivalent dated decisions in the plans, and three more are absent because their enforcing state is the fork's unconditional floor.

Residual truth worth keeping, and it is narrower than the row: sandbox.credentials.envVars (deny/mask, injectHosts, allowPlaintextInject) has no analogue — our floor denies credential FILES, not secret environment variables — and that half needs network.tlsTerminate we also lack. That is a specific missing capability, not "the documented enforcement configuration cannot be deployed".
verdict.correctedState: The documented enforcement OUTCOME is our unconditional floor, not an undeployable config. Managed delivery of a `sandbox` block exists and is parsed tolerantly (sandbox-settings.ts:378-397). Of the enforcement config sandboxing.md:400-406 actually specifies, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` and `excludedCommands` are deliverable and enforced at the spawn (SessionManager.ts:3579-3580 → process-supervisor.ts:467-481), and both managed-lock keys (`filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`) ship. `enabled` and `failIfUnavailable` have no keys because supervised-process isolation is unconditional and fails closed here: resolveProcessIsolation is called for every process (process-supervisor.ts:185) and throws `process-isolation-unavailable:<platform>:<profile>` with remediation rather than falling back to unsandboxed execution — i.e. the state those two keys exist to buy is our default. `credentials` is superseded by a stricter built-in floor (credentialDenyRoots seeded at host-sandbox-settings.ts:61-66; ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.nessy and 15 more, retained even under filesystem.disabled), which Claude explicitly does not ship. `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` carries a dated "documented, not implemented" decision (deviation-unit-5.md:115), and `bwrapPath`/`socatPath` a written no-counterpart decision (managed-composition.ts:56-60) — socat backs a sandbox network proxy this fork does not have. The one real remaining gap is narrower: `sandbox.credentials.envVars` (deny/mask, injectHosts) and its `network.tlsTerminate` prerequisite are absent, so secret ENV VARS are not stripped or masked for sandboxed commands the way credential files are denied.

verdict.why:
The doc quote is genuine and the two code observations are literally true, but the finding is refuted on two independent grounds: it is a dated owner decision already on the tracker, and its stated consequence is already delivered one layer up.

1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 243 carries the sentence exactly as quoted, in § "Protect credentials". `deny`/`mask`, `injectHosts` and `allowPlaintextInject` are all real (`:267`, `:275`-`:279`, `:293`, `:301`). No refutation here.

2) CODE — LITERALLY TRUE, BUT `:321` IS MISCHARACTERIZED. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180) is `excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem` — no `credentials`. `grep -ran credentials` on that file returns only `:321` and `:324`; `injectHosts`/`allowPlaintextInject`/sandbox-`envVars` return zero repo-wide. But `:318-327` does not misapply anything: it says "`settings.md:200`'s `sandbox.credentials` row applied to the sub-block we actually have", i.e. a deliberate, argued borrow of the doc's ONLY published nested-block tolerance rule, quoted in full with the reason ("Returning `undefined` for a wholly invalid `network` is what makes the rest of `sandbox` still apply"). The sibling site says so outright — `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1164`: "Shaped like `settings.md:200`'s `sandbox.credentials` row, which is the doc's only nested-document case". Reading that as a misapplied citation is the reverse of what the comment does.

3) OWNER DECISION — this is R19, parked. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690` is row R19, status ⏸, scope "Egress proxy and domain policy: HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS5 per session, wildcard allow/deny, first-use approval …, **`mask` mode for named env vars**", marked "**PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — 'нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом'**", with the plan deliberately retained (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md`). That plan scopes the whole block: `:15` "there is **no mask/deny path for `credentials.envVars` today** — Task 4 adds `deny` there"; `:31` lands the documented `mask`-without-`tlsTerminate` failure. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218` carries "R19 — `credentials.envVars` `mask` … Half-shipped, then parked by owner decision — so nothing is live". It is NOT one of inert-worklist §3's nine (those are a different set), but it is an equivalent dated owner decision recorded in three places. More: this exact sweep's sibling row was already dispositioned once — audit `:478` records "the three newer `sandbox` keys and the egress-disclosure item (R19, parked by owner decision)" among findings that "belonged to an existing row or a parked owner decision", and notes the disclosure premise was refuted outright.

4) CONSEQUENCE REFUTED UPSTREAM (trap shape #3). `credentials.files` protection ships, unconditionally, by a different name: `credentialDenyRoots` (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) seeds `deniedReadRoots` at the same isolation boundary via `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:61`, `managed-policy-resolution.ts:225` and `packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/script-sandbox.ts:83`. Its list includes `~/.ssh` and `~/.aws` — the doc's own two example entries — plus `~/.nessy`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, `~/.docker`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.config/gh|gcloud`, `~/.azure`, browser cookie/login stores, and `~/Library/Keychains`. Claude's page states the opposite default at `:271`: "There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted." So on the `files` half a default Nessy install is STRICTER than a default Claude install; what is missing is the configurability, not the protection. Only the env-var half (`envVars` deny, and `mask`, which needs the TLS-terminating proxy that R19 parked) has no analogue — and that is exactly what R19's plan holds.

Net: the shipped state is deliberate and recorded, one half of the claimed exposure does not exist, and the `:321` half of the evidence describes a documented design choice as an error.

results.ourState: `SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS` is `['deniedDomains','allowedDomains','allowManagedDomainsOnly']`. `strictAllowlist` has no reader; the only fail-closed egress lever is `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, which is managed-only.

verdict.why:
The quote is real and the cited line is real — but the row is a line item inside a dated owner decision, and its stated our-state is factually wrong.

1) QUOTE — VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 324 carries the sentence character-for-character, including the `{/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}` comment. No paraphrase. Confirmed.

2) CITED LINE — ACCURATE. `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182` is exactly `const SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS = ['deniedDomains', 'allowedDomains', 'allowManagedDomainsOnly'] as const;`. `grep -rani strictallowlist` (with `-a`, so NUL-byte files are covered) over the whole repo returns ZERO production/source hits — only `docs/superpowers/plans/` and the sweep's own JSON. The identifier really is unread. Confirmed.

3) LAYER UP — IT IS A PARKED OWNER DECISION. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690`, row 8: **R19 ⏸ "PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — «нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»"**, with the plan deliberately retained "for when restrictions are wanted". That plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md`, and `strictAllowlist` is an unchecked task in it at `:26` — verbatim the same contract ("DENY instead of prompt. Honored only from user / managed / CLI `--settings`") the finding restates. Instead of restricting, commit `d214cb63` deliberately OPENED egress (shell moved from the `workspace` profile to `networked`). This is not one of the nine §3 decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md`, but it is a dated owner decision of the same class, recorded in the audit rather than the worklist. Audit `:478` already records an earlier finder hitting this same row and being told it belonged to R19.

4) LAYER DOWN — THE PREMISE "INSTEAD OF PROMPTING" HAS NO LOCUS HERE. Claude enforces the host allowlist with a proxy OUTSIDE the sandbox (same page, `:321`). This fork ships no such proxy, so its sandbox egress decision is binary by construction: `sandbox-settings.ts:830` — `export type SandboxEgressDecisionV1 = 'open' | 'denied';` with `:827` "There is no third value, and that is a platform fact rather than a design preference," backed by measured evidence at `:845-873` (Seatbelt rejects `(remote ip "github.com:443")` and even an IP literal with `host must be * or localhost`; `unshare -n`/`firejail --net=none` are whole-namespace; the Windows profile has one `network.enabled` boolean). There is no per-host prompt for a sandboxed command to convert into a deny, so a `strictAllowlist` reader added alone would be inert. The fork's honest substitute already ships and is emitted, not silent: `resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement` (`:900`) returns every configured `allowedDomains`/`deniedDomains` entry as an `unenforceable` diagnostic naming the reason, consumed in production at `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:200` and `SessionManager.ts:290`; `/doctor` prints `sandboxed-command egress: open` on a default install (audit `:478`).

5) SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM NEAR MISS. The only domain-prompt path that exists is in the PERMISSION layer, not the sandbox layer: `pre-tool-use.ts:1986-1996` prompts only when the Bash base command is literally `curl` or `wget`, checked against a session whitelist (`permission-manager.ts:475/483`). It reads neither `allowedDomains` nor `deniedDomains` and any other binary bypasses it. Wiring `strictAllowlist` there would be trap #4 — right name, wrong subsystem.

6) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE IS WRONG ON ITS SECOND HALF. "`allowManagedDomainsOnly`, which is managed-only" is false in this fork: `sandbox-settings.ts:599` composes it as `all.some(layer => layer.network?.allowManagedDomainsOnly === true)` — an OR across EVERY layer, deliberately (`:85-87`: "restricts, so it is boolean-OR … the tighter side wins"). Any layer can set it, so the fail-closed lever is strictly more reachable than the row asserts. A row whose our-state is wrong cannot be dispatched as written.
