Quote verified verbatim.** `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 456 carries it exactly: "Set [`allowAppleEvents`](/docs/en/settings#sandbox-settings) to `true` in your user, managed, or CLI settings to allow them." Cited code is accurate.** `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180` is the closed seven-entry `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` list (`excludedCommands`, `deniedReadRoots`, `deniedWriteRoots`, `additionalWritableRoots`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `network`, `filesystem`); `:182` and `:183` are the `SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS` / `SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS` sub-lists. `assertKnownKeys` (`:216-221`) throws on anything else. `grep -ran` over first-party source confirms zero hits for all seven. So the identifier half stands.)

**3. REFUTATION A — the second half of the very line quoted gives a workaround we DO have.** Line 456 does not end where the finding stops reading. Its last sentence: "Alternatively, add the command to `excludedCommands` to run it outside the sandbox." `excludedCommands` is `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS[0]` — the first entry of the exact block cited as evidence — and it is enforced end to end: `SessionManager.ts:3579` -> `process-supervisor.ts:77,476` -> a recorded `downgrade.reason === 'excludedCommands'` receipt (`:211`) and a risky-band prompt (`pre-tool-use.ts:2100-2124`). (ii) What `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation` buys — access to `com.apple.trustd.agent` — Nessy grants UNCONDITIONALLY: `NETWORK_SANDBOX_MACH_SERVICES` (`packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/mach-services.ts:93-98`) lists `com.apple.SystemConfiguration.configd`, `com.apple.TrustEvaluationAgent`, `com.apple.trustd` and `com.apple.trustd.agent`, emitted into every network-capable profile at `filesystem-isolation.ts:210` alongside `(allow network*)` (`networked` and `plugin-mcp`, per `isolation/darwin.ts:41-42`). **5. REFUTATION C — the third limb is an already-recorded deviation, ruled on earlier in this same sweep.** `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` / unprivileged containers is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:288`, a dated `documented, not implemented` row generated from `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-sandbox-network-enforcement.md:191`, and it is finding f030 of this sweep (already refuted as a recorded decision). Both are recorded reasons, not new defects.

**6. Sibling-subsystem / consequence-vs-identifier errors in the remaining keys.** `network.allowMachLookup` is not absent as a capability — mach-lookup policy is implemented and deliberately narrowed to a probe-derived allowlist (`mach-services.ts:65-71, 93-98`, rationale at `:1-45`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-sandbox-mach-and-protected-paths.md`); it is a built-in constant rather than a user key. `network.allowLocalBinding`, `allowUnixSockets` and `allowAllUnixSockets` have nothing to un-block: the darwin networked/plugin-mcp profile emits a blanket `(allow network*)` (`filesystem-isolation.ts:210`), which already permits localhost bind and AF_UNIX connect, and on Linux we install no seccomp filter at all (`grep -ran seccomp` over `packages/session-tools-core/src` -> 0), so the syscall filter those keys switch off does not exist. results.claim: The sandbox settings-file write denies resolve symlinks, so a symlink appearing at a protected settings path has its target added to the deny list for the next command.
results.quote: The deny rules resolve symlinks: when a symlink appears at a protected settings file path after startup, the sandbox adds its target to the deny list for the next command, so a linked settings file can't be edited through the link.
results.ourState: `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` builds the deny set lexically; the file contains no `realpath`, `lstat` or symlink handling, so a settings file symlinked out of the protected directory stays writable from inside the sandbox.

verdict.why:
REFUTED — textbook "the identifier really is unwired, but the consequence is false because something upstream already handled it".

1. DOC SENTENCE: verbatim, confirmed. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md` line 478 contains the quoted sentence exactly. Reading the WHOLE line matters: it is gated `{/* min-version: 2.1.210 */}` and ends "Before v2.1.210, the deny rules didn't resolve symlinks." So this is a recent Claude addition — and we already match it.

2. CITED FILE: the literal claim about the file is TRUE but irrelevant. `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:47` `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` does build its list with a plain `join`, and `grep -a` confirms the file has no `realpath`/`lstat`/`readlink`/`symlink`. It is a pure, platform-parameterised NAME LIST — canonicalisation is deliberately not its job.

3. ONE LAYER UP — the behaviour is implemented, in the single funnel every backend passes through. In `/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts`:
- `:313-338` `resolveProcessIsolation` composes the write-deny set and terminates it with `.flatMap(root => denyRootPair(root, 'write'))` — so EVERY root `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` returns is piped through it, alongside the credential floor, the shared-git roots and the settings-file `deniedWriteRoots`.
- `:211-219` `denyRootPair` returns `[lexical, canonical]`, where `canonical = nearestExistingRealpath(resolve(root))`.
- `:113-130` `nearestExistingRealpath` is `realpathSync` with an ENOENT walk-up to the nearest existing ancestor (needed precisely because `<workspace>/.claude` and `/etc/nessy` usually do not exist), and an EACCES/EPERM fallback to the path as written.
- `:132-152` quotes the claimed sentence VERBATIM in the code comment as the reason both halves exist. We in fact go BEYOND the doc: Claude adds only the target; we keep the path AS WRITTEN too, because `unlink` acts on the link and not its target, so the link cannot be removed and replaced with an ordinary file at the protected name.

4. "for the next command" = per-spawn re-resolution, satisfied. `resolveProcessIsolation` is invoked inside `ProcessSupervisor.start` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:185`), so a link created after startup is re-paired before the next command is spawned.

5. POSITIVE CONTROL, run live on this darwin host — not a profile-text assertion but a real kernel test. `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.test.ts:327` ("refuses the protected path, refuses it through a symlink, and leaves a sibling alone") spawns real `/bin/bash` under the composed Seatbelt profile, symlinks `<workspace>/.claude -> <workspace>/linked-claude`, and asserts the write through the link fails with `Operation not permitted`, that `linked-claude/settings.json` was never created, that BOTH `(deny file-write* (subpath …))` entries appear in the profile, and that `rm` of the link itself is refused. A sibling `settings.json` in the same writable root still writes, so this is a deny of one tree and not a retreat to a read-only workspace. Result: `1 pass, 0 fail, 10 expect() calls`. `process-supervisor.test.ts:383,413` assert the same pair contract for the read and write deny paths.

The exact bypass the finding predicts ("a settings file symlinked out of the protected directory stays writable from inside the sandbox") is the scenario this test executes and measures as BLOCKED. Not an inert-worklist §3 owner decision and not a fork product difference — it is simply implemented, one call frame above the cited line.

Minor real nit, not a gap: the JSDoc block at `isolation.ts:132-152` documents `denyRootPair` but physically sits above `readAllowRootPair` (which has its own block at `:154-163`), leaving the actual `denyRootPair` at `:211` uncommented. Cosmetic doc drift only; behaviour is as tested.
verdict.correctedState: We DO resolve symlinks for the settings-file write denies, and we do it per spawn. `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:47`) is intentionally a pure name list; canonicalisation is centralised one layer up in `resolveProcessIsolation` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.ts:313-338`), which pipes every deny root — self-config, credential floor, shared-git, settings-file `deniedWriteRoots` — through `denyRootPair` (`isolation.ts:211-219`). That returns the pair `[path-as-written, nearestExistingRealpath(path)]` (`isolation.ts:113-130`, `realpathSync` with an ENOENT walk-up for not-yet-created roots and an EACCES/EPERM fallback). `resolveProcessIsolation` runs inside `ProcessSupervisor.start` (`process-supervisor.ts:185`), i.e. once per command, which is the doc's "for the next command". We exceed the documented behaviour by also denying the link's own name so it cannot be unlinked and replaced. Proven end-to-end by a real sandboxed-`bash` darwin test at `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation.test.ts:327`, which passes on this host.

results.claim: `"streamable-http"` is accepted as an alias for `"http"` in `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files.
results.quote: In `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files, `"streamable-http"` is accepted as an alias for `"http"`.
results.ourState: `parseProjectMcpServer` branches on `type === 'http' || type === 'sse'`, then `'ws'`, then `undefined|'stdio'`, and returns `null` for anything else — the caller logs `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config` and drops it. The Claude plugin adapter has the same closed set. The alias exists only inside the vendored Pi/session-MCP bundles under `apps/electron/dist`, never in our own parser.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp.md, line 375 reads in full: "For the streamable HTTP transport, use `\"type\": \"http\"` instead. In `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files, `\"streamable-http\"` is accepted as an alias for `\"http\"`. The programmatic `mcpServers` option accepts only `\"http\"`." The claimed sentence is the middle sentence, character-for-character. The third sentence is the second-half trap and it does NOT reverse the conclusion: it restricts the alias to JSON config files, which is exactly the surface our parser owns. agent-sdk/mcp is row 32 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP-registry page. (2) CITED FILES CONFIRMED. packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:119 `if (type === 'http' || type === 'sse')`, :144 `if (type === 'ws')`, :163 `if (type === undefined || type === 'stdio')`, :177 `return null` — a closed set with no alias arm; :211 emits `Ignoring ${label} server "${slug}": unsupported MCP server config`. The adapter's closed set is real but the line drifted: it is packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1040 (`rawTransport === 'stdio' || 'http' || 'sse' || 'ws'`), not :1034, which is inside the preceding comment. (3) CONSEQUENCE TESTED SEPARATELY, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Ran parseMcpServersDocument over two entries in one document: {type:'http',url:...} and {type:'streamable-http',url:...}. Output: only `control_http` survives; warnings = ["Ignoring .mcp.json server \"alias_streamable\": unsupported MCP server config"]. The control proves the rig works, so the absence is a real absence. LAYER UP: no normalizer exists between file and parser. `grep -a` for streamable-http across packages/ and apps/*/src returns zero hits in our own source; the same closed set is repeated independently at codex.ts:905, native-sources.ts:454, plugins/schema.ts:624, mcp-pool.ts:183 and plugins/types.ts:170, so nothing upstream rewrites the value. LAYER DOWN: the vendored alias is real and does NOT rescue the entry. apps/electron/dist/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js and session-mcp-server/index.js carry the SDK's own zod schema `z.enum(["http","streamable-http"]).transform(() => "http")`, and main.cjs carries the bare enum constant — matching the claim that it lives only in vendored bundles. But Pi is handed an explicit `Record<string, SdkMcpServerConfig>` (pi-agent.ts:7014, base-agent.ts:1698) already filtered by our parser; the `.mcp.json` strings inside the Pi bundle are the SDK's settings-schema descriptions (enabledMcpjsonServers/disabledMcpjsonServers), not an independent workspace read on our path. So the entry is dropped before any vendored schema could coerce it. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns the MCP transport alias, and grep -a for streamable-http across docs/superpowers/plans and the parity audit returns nothing. NOT A PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: this is generic MCP transport-name parsing, unrelated to the dropped subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rename.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with two citation corrections and one path correction. The `.mcp.json` reader `parseProjectMcpServer` (packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:119-177) branches on `'http'|'sse'`, then `'ws'`, then `undefined|'stdio'`, and returns null otherwise; `parseMcpServersDocument:211` then logs `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config` and drops the entry. The Claude plugin adapter's identical closed set is at format-adapters/claude.ts:1040 (the claim cited :1034, which is comment text); the Codex adapter (codex.ts:905) and native-sources.ts:454 use the same closed set minus `ws`. Also correct the live path: the exported `loadProjectMcpServers` helper has NO production caller (test-only, base-agent.test.ts:803); the shipped `.mcp.json` read is runtime-pool-servers.ts:461 via the capability materializer, plus capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:129 for contribution detection — both funnel through the same `parseMcpServersDocument`, so the drop and the warning are identical on the live path. results.quote: When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions.
results.ourState: `TOKEN_LIMIT = 12000` is the persist threshold and there is no `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (or Nessy-prefixed) env reader anywhere. The per-tool `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` half IS implemented, clamped to the documented 500,000 ceiling.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding. MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS', ':1040 up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters'. results.claim: A `managed-mcp.json` file at a system path takes exclusive control: only its servers load, and `claude mcp add` is refused.
results.quote: If you deploy a `managed-mcp.json` file, Claude Code loads only the servers that file defines. Users cannot add, modify, or use any other MCP servers, including plugin-provided servers.
results.ourState: No reader for the file at any of the three documented system paths (grep -a for `managed-mcp.json` hits docs and comments only). There is no exclusive-control mode and therefore no way to express the documented "disable MCP entirely" pattern — `deniedMcpServers` blocks only what it names. Recorded in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91.

verdict.why:
Legs 1 and 2 hold, but leg 3 fails: the finding's load-bearing consequence is false, and it fails in exactly the sibling-list shape AGENTS.md warns about.

(1) QUOTE - VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-mcp.md` (361 lines) line 43, under `## Exclusive control with managed-mcp.json`, carries the claimed text as an exact substring. Reading the WHOLE line: it is three sentences, and the third is "The file also suppresses claude.ai connectors unless you [allow them alongside the managed set](#allow-claude-ai-connectors-alongside-the-managed-set)." That is a truncation, not a paraphrase, and it does not reverse the conclusion. Not a refutation.

(2) ABSENCE - CONFIRMED. `grep -rlacF 'managed-mcp.json' packages apps` returns five files, ALL of them built bundles (`packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js`, `apps/electron/{dist/,}resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js`), and both distinct hit sites are zod `.describe()` prose inside a vendored Claude Code settings schema, not a reader. `grep -rnaF` over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` is empty. No path constant matches `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`, `/etc/claude-code/` or `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\`, and `grep -rna 'exclusive control|exclusive-control'` over `packages apps` (minus dist) is empty, so the `claude mcp add` refusal string does not exist either. The cited evidence range is real: `managed-policy.ts:1573` is `export function isManagedMcpServerAllowed(...)`, whose docblock at `:1558-1571` cites `managed-mcp.md` § *How a server is evaluated*. So the FIRST half of OUR STATE - no `managed-mcp.json` reader, no exclusive-control mode, no add-time refusal - is true, and it is recorded at `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91` under "What we do not implement" with the category `documented, not implemented - a separate deployment channel`.

(3) CONSEQUENCE - FALSE. OUR STATE says "There is no exclusive-control mode and therefore no way to express the documented 'disable MCP entirely' pattern - `deniedMcpServers` blocks only what it names." It examined only the denylist. The instrument for deny-all is the SIBLING list, and the same page documents it: managed-mcp.md:145 - "| `allowedMcpServers` | All servers allowed | No servers allowed | Only matching servers allowed |" for unset / empty array / populated. The vendored Claude schema in our own bundle repeats it: "If empty array, no servers are allowed."

We implement that, and it is tested. `parseManagedMcpEntryList` preserves `[]` (`root[field] === undefined ? undefined : parse(...)`, `managed-policy.ts:1307-1312`, emitted at `:1447`), and `evaluateManagedMcpServer` (`managed-mcp-entries.ts:489-509`) returns `true` only when `allowed === undefined` or something matches - an empty array falls through every branch to `allowed.some(...)` === false. Pinned by `managed-mcp-entries.test.ts:324` (`isManagedMcpServerAllowed(lists({allowedMcpServers: []}), SERVER)` -> `false`) and `:346` (`strict({allowedMcpServers: []}).allowedMcpServers` -> `[]`).

It reaches both populations the doc's Disable-MCP row names. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:704` and `:709` drop every native MCP inventory record that fails the gate, and `:730-733` drops every PLUGIN-provided MCP candidate (`isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, pluginMcpServerIdentity(candidate))`) - so "including plugin-provided servers" is covered by the same seam.

And it is deliverable at a system path. `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48-50` reads the rebranded managed file at `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json` (darwin), `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json` (linux) and `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` (win32). What is missing is the DEPLOYMENT half of `managed-mcp.json` (pushing a fixed server set out to users, which no Nessy key does) and the add-time refusal feedback (`sources.CREATE` does not consult the policy - recorded at `managed-mcp-access.md:97`; a denied server is filtered at load, so it never runs, but the user sees silent disappearance rather than an error).

Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 - I checked all nine; none concerns MCP deployment. verdict.correctedState: Nessy has no reader for `managed-mcp.json` at any of the three documented system paths (`grep -rnaF` over `packages/*/src`, `apps/*/src` is empty; the only bundle hits are zod `.describe()` prose in a vendored Claude settings schema), no exclusive-control mode, and no `claude mcp add`-style refusal - `sources.CREATE` does not consult the policy, so a user can create an MCP Source the policy denies and sees silent disappearance rather than an error. BUT the claim that there is "no way to express the documented 'disable MCP entirely' pattern" is false: it looked only at `deniedMcpServers`. The page's own table at managed-mcp.md:145 gives `allowedMcpServers: []` = "No servers allowed", and we implement exactly that - `parseManagedMcpEntryList` preserves the empty array (`managed-policy.ts:1307-1312`, `:1447`), `evaluateManagedMcpServer` (`managed-mcp-entries.ts:489-509`) then admits nothing, pinned by `managed-mcp-entries.test.ts:324,346`. results.claim: Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the launch directory plus every additional working directory, and sends `notifications/roots/list_changed` when that set changes.
results.quote: Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or the `additionalDirectories` setting.
results.ourState: The MCP client is constructed with `capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}` — the `roots` capability is never advertised, so `roots/list` is never requested and no `list_changed` roots notification is emitted. A server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots gets nothing. Confirmed absent repo-wide with `grep -a`.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding; nothing refutes it. (1) QUOTE IS VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md returns the sentence character-for-character on line 108 (Python substring test: True). Note: a first curl produced a truncated 33 KB body; the full 80 866-byte fetch is the one verified. Reading the WHOLE line does not reverse the conclusion, it strengthens it — the line is five sentences: 'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the stable project root and doesn't change when you add or remove working directories mid-session. A server that limits its own filesystem access to a set of allowed directories should implement the MCP roots/list request instead. Claude Code answers roots/list with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with --add-dir, /add-dir, or the additionalDirectories setting. Claude Code sends notifications/roots/list_changed when that set changes. Before v2.1.203, roots/list returned only the launch directory and Claude Code didn't send notifications/roots/list_changed.' The second sentence explicitly routes allowed-directory scoping to roots/list rather than to the project-dir env var, and the fourth sentence independently confirms the list_changed half of the claimed behaviour. (2) CITED CODE MATCHES. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 constructs `new Client({name:'nessy-agent',version:'1.0.0'}, {capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? {elicitation:{form:{},url:{}}} : {}})`. The only capability ever declared is elicitation, and only when a handler is supplied; the R24 comment above it states the policy 'advertise only what we honour'. packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:78-90 pins that surface exactly (`sdkClient._capabilities.elicitation` toEqual `{form:{},url:{}}`, undefined without a handler) — so the capability set is deliberately narrow and roots is not in it. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, and it holds. Absence: `grep -ra` (NUL-safe) for roots/list, ListRoots, listRoots, sendRootsListChanged, RootsListChangedNotification over packages/ and apps/ returns ZERO hits in Nessy source. The only hits are inside built bundles and third-party binaries, and each was opened and confirmed to be the vendored MCP SDK's own protocol table, not an implementation: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js and apps/electron/dist/resources/bridge-mcp-server/index.js each contain `ListRootsRequestSchema = RequestSchema.extend({method: literal("roots/list")})` plus its entry in `ServerRequestSchema`, with `setRequestHandler(ListRoots` count = 0 in both; the remaining hits are the prebuilt codex-app-server binaries. No `registerCapabilities` call exists anywhere in the repo, so nothing adds roots after construction either. LAYER UP — is something upstream already handling it? No, and this is the check that could have refuted it. Nessy's pool is the ONLY MCP client that connects third-party servers, so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path: claude-agent.ts:1136-1150 builds `Options['mcpServers']` from in-process `sourceProxies` ('Per-source proxy servers from centralized MCP pool… the pool owns all source connections centrally', claude-agent.ts:474-477) rather than handing raw MCP configs to the Claude SDK, and mcp/pool-server.ts:211-213 re-exposes the same pool to Codex/Pi as `nessy-pool-proxy` with `capabilities: {tools:{listChanged:true}}`. LAYER DOWN — sibling MCP clients omit roots too, so there is no other client that answers: api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument at all and validation.ts:411-413 passes `capabilities: {}`. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM TRAP checked and cleared: the ~60 other `roots` hits in the repo are unrelated same-name symbols in different subsystems — sandbox/filesystem containment (session-tools-core credential-deny-roots.ts, pi-harness/isolation.ts), `--add-dir` memory-file scoping (capabilities/native-sources.ts), test temp-dir arrays, Codex FuzzyFileSearchParams.roots, and client.ts:886's own 'plugin-mcp-working-directory-outside-authorized-roots' (which contains where a plugin MCP PROCESS is launched, and never reaches the wire as a roots/list answer). NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, and listSessionSummaries — none is MCP roots. The parity audit corroborates rather than excuses: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1787 lists roots/list among grep-absence claims 're-confirmed absent repo-wide at the time', and grep over docs/ finds no plan and no parity row for it. NOT A DELIBERATE FORK DIFFERENCE: this touches no dropped subscription flow, no gateway routing and no rename — and the fork already owns the exact inputs a roots/list answer needs, so this is a missing surface rather than a missing concept: `additionalDirectories` is a first-class persisted setting (config/storage.ts:132, config/validators.ts:191/227) resolved by packages/shared/src/agent/additional-directories.ts into a `roots: string[]`, and `--add-dir` roots are already modelled in capabilities/types.ts:197-201. One imprecision in the original wording, too small to refute: it is the SERVER that sends `roots/list` to the client, not the client that requests it; the accurate mechanism is that without the declared capability a spec-compliant server never asks, and a server that asked anyway would get a 'Method not found' because no ListRootsRequestSchema handler is registered.
verdict.correctedState: Nessy never exposes MCP roots to any server. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 declares `capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}` — `roots` is never declared, no `ListRootsRequestSchema` handler is registered, `sendRootsListChanged` is never called, and no `registerCapabilities` call adds it later; client-transport.test.ts:78-90 pins the elicitation-only capability set. The two sibling MCP clients omit it as well (api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument; validation.ts:411-413 passes `capabilities: {}`). Repo-wide `grep -ra` finds `roots/list`/`ListRoots` only in the vendored MCP SDK protocol tables inside built bundles (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/bridge-mcp-server/index.js — `setRequestHandler(ListRoots` count 0 in both) and in the prebuilt codex-app-server binaries, never in Nessy source. The consequence holds for every backend because Nessy's own pool is the sole MCP client that connects third-party servers — claude-agent.ts:1136-1150 hands the Claude SDK in-process pool proxies instead of raw MCP configs, and mcp/pool-server.ts:211-213 re-exposes the same pool to Pi/Codex — so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path. Precise mechanism: because the client advertises no `roots` capability, a spec-compliant server never sends `roots/list`, and one that sent it anyway would receive 'Method not found'; `notifications/roots/list_changed` is likewise never emitted. A server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots therefore gets nothing. The inputs already exist — `additionalDirectories` is persisted (config/storage.ts:132, validators.ts:191/227) and resolved into a `roots: string[]` by agent/additional-directories.ts, and `--add-dir` roots are modelled in capabilities/types.ts:197-201 — so this is an unimplemented surface, not a deliberate deviation: it is absent from inert-worklist §3's nine owner decisions and has no parity row or plan, while 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1787 independently re-confirms it absent.

results.claim: `"streamable-http"` is a valid value of the `type` field wherever MCP servers are configured in JSON.
results.quote: When configuring MCP servers via JSON in `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`.
results.ourState: Our `.mcp.json` parser and the Claude plugin adapter both accept only `stdio|http|sse|ws`; an entry copied verbatim from an MCP server's own documentation is dropped with `unsupported MCP server config`.

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) DOC: the sentence exists VERBATIM at line 78 of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md (HTTP 200, 1282 lines): "When configuring MCP servers via JSON in `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`." The line is two sentences and the second one REINFORCES rather than reverses: "The MCP specification uses the name `streamable-http` for this transport, so configurations copied from server documentation work without modification." (One early curl of the same URL returned the agent-sdk/mcp page instead - CDN variance - but two independent re-fetches were byte-identical and both carry the sentence at line 78.) (2) CITED CODE: packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:119 is exactly `if (type === 'http' || type === 'sse') {`; the function then handles 'ws' (:144) and `undefined|'stdio'` (:163) and returns null (:177) for anything else. The Claude plugin adapter's closed set is packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1040 (`rawTransport === 'stdio' || ... 'http' || 'sse' || 'ws' ? rawTransport : undefined`); the claim cited :1034, a comment line six lines up inside the same block - trivial line drift, same location. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, with a positive control: running parseMcpServersDocument on `{mcpServers:{alias:{type:'streamable-http',url:...}, plain:{type:'http',url:...}}}` returns only `["plain"]` and emits the warning verbatim as claimed - `Ignoring .mcp.json server "alias": unsupported MCP server config` (project-config.ts:211). ONE LAYER UP: nothing normalizes the alias before the parser. The live materialization path (packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:456-466) JSON.parses the raw file text and passes it straight to parseMcpServersDocument, and loadProjectMcpServers (:218-236) does the same; `grep -rn -a -i streamable` over the repo finds the token ONLY in vendored apps/electron/dist bundles, docs-site prose, and unrelated MCP-SDK transport class names - there is no alias table anywhere in our own source. ONE LAYER DOWN: native-sources.ts:mcpServerRecords creates an inventory record per server name regardless of `type`, so the entry is inventoried and then silently dropped at materialization - it never reaches the pool. SIBLING SUBSYSTEMS CHECKED: the Codex adapter has the same closed set (codex.ts:905, stdio|http|sse), and MCP *Sources* (a Source config.json spelling it `transport`, not `type`) are a different subsystem that always connects over Streamable HTTP anyway (validation.ts:158-164) - the finding names the right subsystem (.mcp.json reader + Claude plugin adapter), so the 'wrong sibling' refutation does not apply. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 covers this (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: `.mcp.json` is a repository-owned shared contract file, and this very parser is written against this very page - it cites `mcp.md:707`, `:735`, `:138` and `:147` inline - so the page is a contract we opted into, not a Claude-subscription/rename surface we dropped.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED, with two scope narrowings that do not rescue it. Our `.mcp.json` reader (packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:89-177) and the Claude plugin adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1040) each accept a closed transport set and neither maps `streamable-http` to `http`. A project or plugin `.mcp.json` entry copied verbatim from an MCP server's own documentation is parsed to null, logged as `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config` (project-config.ts:211) or as the adapter diagnostic `Claude MCP server requires a command (stdio) or url (http/sse/ws).`, and never reaches the pool - verified by running the parser, not only by reading it. Narrowing 1: of the three JSON surfaces the doc sentence names, only `.mcp.json` exists in this fork; `~/.claude.json` and `claude mcp add-json` are Claude Code CLI surfaces this rebranded fork does not ship, so the affected surfaces are project `.mcp.json`, plugin-bundled `.mcp.json`, and inline plugin manifest MCP maps. Narrowing 2: on the Claude backend only - off by default via NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE - claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`, so the Claude Agent SDK additionally reads project `.mcp.json` through its own loader, which does honour the alias; our pool still drops it, and the default Pi backend has no such fallback. Fix is a one-line alias normalization applied at both readers (and, for consistency, the Codex adapter at codex.ts:905), mapping `streamable-http` to `http` before the transport switch.

results.claim: `headersHelper` runs a command at connection time whose stdout JSON is merged into the connection headers, with `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`/`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL`/`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in its environment and a 10-second timeout.
results.quote: If your MCP server uses an authentication scheme other than OAuth, such as Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO, use `headersHelper` to generate request headers at connection time.
results.ourState: Not implemented for any transport. Both readers detect the field and emit a warning (`"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored`) and a deferred-capability record; the server still connects with static headers only.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass in the finding's favour; the divergence is real. (1) VERBATIM. The quoted sentence exists word-for-word at mcp.md:761, under the heading '### Use dynamic headers for custom authentication'. I read the WHOLE line: it is a two-sentence line and the second sentence REINFORCES rather than reverses — 'Claude Code runs the command and merges its output into the connection headers.' Every element of the claimed behaviour is verbatim-supported in the same section: 'The command must write a JSON object of string key-value pairs to stdout'; 'The command runs in a shell with a 10-second timeout, from the session's current working directory'; 'Dynamic headers override any static `headers` with the same name'; and the env table lists exactly CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME (server name), CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL (server URL) and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT ('Set only when a plugin provides the server'). The field is also documented for ws at mcp.md:147 and listed among plugin server fields at mcp.md:320. So the doc side is not a paraphrase and not cherry-picked.
(2) CITED LINES. Both citations say what was claimed. packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:147-148 is `if (raw.headersHelper !== undefined) { problems.push('"headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored'); }`, preceded by the docblock at :139-143 'headersHelper is READ AND REPORTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — there is no dynamic header generator anywhere in this codebase for any transport'. packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1058 pushes the warning 'Claude MCP server "<name>" declares headersHelper, which is not implemented for any transport; static headers still apply.' AND `deferred.push({ externalKind: 'mcp', reasonCode: 'plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported' })` — so the deferred-capability record is real, on the plugin path.
(3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both layers. Nothing upstream or downstream implements it. Binary-safe `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'headersHelper'` over packages/*/src and apps/*/src returns 25 hits in 6 files and every one is a reader, a docblock, or a test — there is no executor, no spawn, no shell call. `grep -rna --binary-files=text 'CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME|CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL'` over packages, apps and scripts returns ZERO hits, so the documented helper environment is not constructed anywhere. One layer down at the vendored runtime: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js contains headersHelper exactly 3 times (lines 350316, 350319, 350320) and all three are `headersHelper: l3.string().optional()` inside the sse/http/ws zod schemas — the Pi SDK ACCEPTS the field and never consumes it, so no downstream layer silently rescues the behaviour. Our readers strip it before the pool anyway. No sibling-subsystem misnaming is possible: headersHelper is a single MCP-config field name and the only two parsers of it are the two cited.
(4) NOT AN OWNER DECISION. I read all nine dated entries in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). headersHelper is not among them and appears nowhere in that file. It is instead an OPEN, recorded deviation: 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:369 and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-mcp-surfaces.md:117/:142/:154 name it 'documented, not implemented', and the parity audit's N8 row (:726) closes ws transport while leaving this explicitly open.
(5) NOT A FORK PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. headersHelper is transport-level MCP auth, not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not a rebrand, not gateway-specific. If anything the fork is the doc's own stated audience — 'Kerberos, short-lived tokens, or an internal SSO' is precisely a corporate-gateway deployment.
One correction to the finding's OUR STATE, which makes our position WORSE than claimed, not better, and therefore does not refute it: 'Both readers detect the field and emit a warning' is FALSE for the .mcp.json reader on http and sse. In project-config.ts the headersHelper check sits ONLY inside the `if (type === 'ws')` arm (:144-153); the http/sse arm (:119-134) never touches raw.headersHelper, and parseMcpServersDocument (:190-213) has no generic unknown-key sweep. I proved this with a positive control rather than by reading alone — a temporary bun test through parseMcpServersDocument, since deleted, with the ws case as the control that shows the rig can observe the warning: WS -> ['.mcp.json server "events": "headersHelper" is not implemented for any transport; it was ignored.']; HTTP -> config {"type":"http","url":"https://x.test/mcp"}, warnings []; SSE -> config {"type":"sse","url":"https://x.test/mcp"}, warnings []. So on the transport the doc's own two examples use ('type': 'http'), a project .mcp.json headersHelper is dropped in total silence — the exact failure mode the code comment at :141-143 says it exists to prevent ('an operator ends up debugging a 401 that has nothing to do with their token'). The only test covering that warning, mcp/__tests__/ws-transport.test.ts:46-57, uses type 'ws', which is why the hole survived.
verdict.correctedState: Not implemented for any transport, and confirmed unimplemented one layer down as well: the vendored Pi SDK bundle carries `headersHelper` only as an optional zod field on its sse/http/ws schemas (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:350316/350319/350320) and never executes it, and `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME`/`CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL` appear nowhere in the repository. The two readers do NOT behave alike, contrary to the original claim. The plugin adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1058) warns for every transport and also files a deferred-capability record (`plugin.deferred.claude_mcp_headers_helper_unsupported`). The project `.mcp.json` reader (packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:147-148) emits its warning ONLY from the `ws` arm; the http/sse arm at :119-134 drops `headersHelper` with no warning at all and no deferred record, and there is no generic unknown-key sweep in parseMcpServersDocument (:190-213) to catch it. Verified empirically against the parser with the ws case as a positive control: ws yields one warning, http and sse yield zero. Since mcp.md documents `headersHelper` primarily for http/sse and both of its examples use `"type": "http"`, the common case is the silent one. Net effect: an http/sse server connects with static headers only and the operator is told nothing; a ws server connects with no headers sent at all (the SDK's WebSocket transport takes only a URL, per parity-audit row N8) but at least names the drop.

results.claim: Project-scoped `.mcp.json` servers require per-server approval before use, resettable with `claude mcp reset-project-choices`.
results.quote: For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` files.
results.ourState: The only gate is whole-workspace trust; inside a trusted project every `.mcp.json` server is materialized without an individual approve/reject step, and none of `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` or a reset command exists.

verdict.why:
Quote and cited lines are accurate, but the load-bearing sentence of the claimed our-state — "The only gate is whole-workspace trust; inside a trusted project every `.mcp.json` server is materialized without an individual approve/reject step" — is false in three separate ways. This is the mcp.md twin of f029 (settings.md) and fails for the same reason, verified independently here.

1. QUOTE — VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md` line 418, read whole: "For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` files. If you need to reset these approval choices, use the `claude mcp reset-project-choices` command." The second sentence reinforces rather than reverses. Related context at :169 (`⏸ Pending approval`), :173 (v2.1.196 — approvals are read only after workspace trust), :206 (`enabledMcpjsonServers`/`disabledMcpjsonServers` control `.mcp.json` approval). `mcp` is row 128 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a valid Claude contract page.

2. CITED LINES — ACCURATE. `native-sources.ts:995` is exactly `if (context.projectTrustState === 'trusted') {`; `:1067` is where `.mcp.json` becomes records via `mcpServerRecords(...)`. `project-config.ts:190-215` is the body of `parseMcpServersDocument`, which validates shape and warns, and gates nothing. A NUL-safe `grep -rna` over `packages/` and `apps/` finds `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` and `reset-project-choices` in NO source file (only in `docs/architecture/unified-plugin-adapter-runtime.md:198` prose and the sweep's own JSON). That identifier-absence half holds.

3. ONE LAYER UP — REFUTES THE CONSEQUENCE. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:699-708` filters the native inventory per record before the resolver sees it:

    if (!isPiCapabilityTurn) return true
    if (record.kind === 'mcp' && !isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, {
      name: record.logicalName,

with the comment at `:700-703` citing `managed-mcp.md:150` so "a denied server cannot escape by being renamed." Do not re-file this row as written; its quote is invented. If any part is re-filed, it is the narrow user-tier gap already captured by f029, and it must be stated against what actually exists:

The cited line packages/shared/src/marketplace/external-catalog-adapters.ts:160 is the array member 'defaultEnabled', not the drop itself; the governing mechanism is MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS at :153-166 (an explicit allowlist) applied by the copy loop at :235-255, which never sees `relevance`. results.claim: Installing a plugin that declares dependencies resolves and installs them automatically, fetching each at the highest `{plugin-name}--v{version}` git tag that satisfies the range.
results.quote: When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically and lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output.
results.ourState: No auto-install and no tag enumeration. The module header records the reason: no marketplace source in this repo enumerates git tags, so resolving a range against "whatever the catalog currently holds" would make `~2.1.0` silently mean latest. A declared dependency that is not already installed surfaces as `dependency-unsatisfied` and disables the dependent plugin.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-dependencies.md returns 224 lines; line 11 opens with the claimed sentence character-for-character: 'When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically and lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output.' The rest of that four-sentence line does NOT reverse it - it reinforces auto-install ('/reload-plugins and the background plugin auto-update reinstall it', 'Re-running claude plugin install ... also resolves any outstanding missing dependencies', 'Dependencies from a marketplace you have not added are left unresolved'). The tag-enumeration half of the claimed behaviour is also verbatim, at :127 ('Claude Code lists the marketplace's tags, filters to those starting with secrets-vault--v, and fetches the highest version satisfying ~2.1.0') and :110 ('Tag each release as {plugin-name}--v{version}') and :45 ('The dependency is fetched at the highest tagged version that satisfies this range'). The page is row 141 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a legitimate Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP page. (2) CITED FILE. packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts:15-23 says exactly what was claimed, near-verbatim: 'What is NOT here, and why ... - **Auto-install and tag-based version resolution** (`:11`, `:108`-`:127`). No marketplace source in this repo enumerates `{plugin-name}--v{version}` git tags; every source is a catalog-pinned ref, an npm package or a URL. Resolving `~2.1.0` against "whatever the catalog currently holds" would make a constraint silently mean latest, which is worse than refusing'. The same reason is restated at plugins/types.ts:690-693 and format-adapters/claude.ts:1575-1581. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, one layer up and one down. Down: `grep -a` for `--v` / `git tag` / `ls-remote` / `listTags` across packages/shared/src/plugins/ finds NO tag enumeration anywhere - the only tag-ish hits are npm `dist-tags.latest` handling in install-service.ts:1489-1520 and a GitHub archive-route comment at :1738. Up: format-adapters/claude.ts:1608-1612 pushes a `dependency-auto-install` deferred record whenever a manifest declares dependencies, i.e. the absence is deliberate and surfaced, not an oversight. The disabling consequence is real and live: resolvePluginDependencyErrors (dependencies.ts:68) has two production callers - capabilities/resolver.ts:2150 (via resolveActiveDependencyErrors) and apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:424 - and resolver.ts:1703-1707 sets `enabled = false` with `unavailableReason = 'dependency-unsatisfied'` for EVERY capability of the dependent plugin. So both halves of the claimed our-state hold. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM TRAP CHECKED AND AVOIDED: install-service.ts has ~40 hits for 'dependenc*', but those are npm RUNTIME dependencies of executable plugins (lockfiles, quotas, `plugin.install.runtime_dependency_*`) - a different subsystem from plugin-to-plugin manifest `dependencies`. The finding names the right one. NOT AN INERT-WORKLIST §3 DECISION: all nine dated owner decisions there were read (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) - none is plugin dependency auto-install. NOT A FORK PRODUCT DIFFERENCE either: it is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rename. CONTEXT THAT DOES NOT REFUTE BUT SHOULD TRAVEL WITH THE ROW: this is a known, tracked, reasoned deferral rather than an unnoticed defect. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:138 already marks the page 🟨. The parity audit's B1 row (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:701) explicitly spins it out: 'dependency auto-install becomes its own row (it needs a git-network capability, which is not what "finish B1" means)'. And docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md §7 calls it 'the one place where the *shape* of what the docs describe is genuinely unbuilt rather than deliberately narrowed', with a hard prerequisite absent from the repo. So the gap is real and open - it just already has an owner-visible record and a home.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with two additions. Additions: (a) the absence is actively surfaced, not silent - format-adapters/claude.ts:1608-1612 emits a `dependency-auto-install` deferred record for any manifest that declares dependencies; (b) the disabling consequence is enforced at capabilities/resolver.ts:1703-1707, which sets enabled=false with unavailableReason='dependency-unsatisfied' on EVERY capability of the dependent plugin (not merely a badge), and the same rule is shared with the CLI at apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:424 so `plugin list` and the app cannot disagree. Beyond auto-install, four adjacent doc behaviours are also absent for the same root cause and are recorded in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md §7: range intersection across dependents and its `range-conflict` install failure (:142), the cross-marketplace refusal and `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` (:81, :104), `--prune` of orphaned auto-installed dependencies and the provenance bit it needs (:196), and the `no-matching-tag` error (:215). What IS implemented from the page: load-time semver checking via `satisfies` with includePrerelease:false (:48), `dependency-version-unsatisfied` (:214), `range-conflict` for unparseable ranges (:213), fixpoint evaluation so a disabled dependency counts as unsatisfied (:212), transitive enable via resolveTransitiveDependencies and the enabled-dependents disable guard (management-service-v2.ts:694, :741). Status: real, open, already tracked as its own parity row with a git-tag-enumeration prerequisite that does not exist in this repo.

results.claim: A cross-marketplace dependency is refused unless the root marketplace lists the target in `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn`.
results.quote: To allow it, the maintainer of the root marketplace adds the target marketplace name to `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` in `marketplace.json`.
results.ourState: The field is not carried past catalog parse and no `cross-marketplace` error exists; the adapter comment records that with nothing auto-installed there is no install to refuse, and the `marketplace` field on each dependency is carried so the check has its input the day auto-install lands.

verdict.why: Quote is verbatim (plugins/host-marketplace.md#depend-on-and-recommend-other-plugins (was line 83 of the retired plugin-dependencies page)) and the cited docblock exists (claude.ts:1582-1589; the claim's 1576-1584 span is off by ~6 lines but lands in the same comment). The identifier facts are all accurate: `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` has zero readers anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep -a: the only hits are the claude.ts:1583 comment, two plan docs and the deviation register), no `cross-marketplace` error code exists (grep -a for 'cross-marketplace|crossMarketplace' over all .ts returns one comment at plugins/types.ts:703), and `PluginDependencyDescriptor.marketplace` really is carried and consumed (dependencies.ts:91,99; management-service-v2.ts:711,714,748). The CONSEQUENCE is what fails, in the exact 'enforcement one layer up' shape AGENTS.md and inert-worklist section 4 item 3 warn about. The doc scopes the refusal to auto-install: ':81' reads 'Claude Code refuses to AUTO-INSTALL a dependency that lives in a different marketplace', and ':104' blesses the escape hatch 'Users can still install the dependency manually first, which satisfies the constraint without changing the allowlist.' Nessy auto-installs no plugin dependency at all -- verified one layer down: `resolvePluginDependencyErrors` (dependencies.ts:68-140) only resolves declared dependencies against ALREADY-INSTALLED subjects and emits dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-version-unsatisfied / range-conflict, and `resolveTransitiveDependencies` (management-service-v2.ts:696-728) throws `plugin.manage.dependency-not-installed` rather than fetching; nothing in the plugin install path resolves a dependency from a marketplace. So every cross-marketplace dependency Nessy can ever satisfy is one the user installed manually, which is precisely the path ':104' says satisfies the constraint WITHOUT the allowlist. The trust property the field protects -- 'This prevents one marketplace from silently pulling in plugins from a source you have not reviewed' -- is therefore satisfied strictly more conservatively than Claude, not violated. What differs is only the diagnostic string (dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-not-installed instead of a `cross-marketplace` error naming the field), not the security outcome. It is also an already-recorded deviation with a written reason, harvested by scripts/regenerate-deviation-register.py from docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md:243 into docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:392 (and an earlier one at 2026-07-29-marketplace-entry-authority.md:226). It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 -- I checked all nine and none concerns marketplaces or dependencies -- so it is refuted as a false consequence plus a recorded deviation, not as a section-3 owner decision.
verdict.correctedState: Accurate as far as the identifiers go, but the divergence does not exist as a behaviour gap. `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` has no reader in packages/ or apps/ and no `cross-marketplace` error code exists, yet plugins/host-marketplace.md#depend-on-and-recommend-other-plugins (was line 81 of the retired plugin-dependencies page) scopes the refusal to AUTO-INSTALL and :104 states that manually pre-installing the dependency satisfies the constraint without the allowlist. Nessy auto-installs no dependency on any path (dependencies.ts:68-140 resolves only against installed subjects; management-service-v2.ts:696-728 throws plugin.manage.dependency-not-installed rather than fetching), so manual pre-install is the only path that exists and every satisfied cross-marketplace dependency is doc-conformant by :104. The `marketplace` field is not merely parked for a future check -- it is live input today at dependencies.ts:99 and management-service-v2.ts:711/748, where it selects which marketplace a dependency resolves in. The only real delta is the diagnostic code (dependency-unsatisfied / dependency-not-installed rather than a `cross-marketplace` error naming the field to set). Recorded deviation: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md:243.

results.claim: Every subprocess the Bash/PowerShell tool and hook commands spawn carries an environment marker announcing that it is running inside the coding agent; third-party CLIs gate behaviour on it.
results.quote: Claude Code sets the [`CLAUDECODE`](/docs/en/env-vars) environment variable to `1` for every command it runs through the Bash and PowerShell tools, and for [hook](/docs/en/hooks) commands.
results.ourState: Nessy sets no equivalent marker in tool subprocesses. The only `CLAUDECODE` references in the repo REMOVE it from a child env (`apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62` strips it to dodge the Claude SDK nesting guard) and there is no `NESSYCODE`/`NESSY_CODE` replacement anywhere. This is not the ordinary brand-prefix rename: the variable is read by third-party tools, not by us, so no NESSY_-prefixed name substitutes for it, and CLIs that adapt their output for agent use (non-interactive mode, no colour, machine-readable output) do not adapt for Nessy.

verdict.why: Quote is verbatim (first sentence of plugin-hints.md line 17) and the cited file:line is exactly as claimed (apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:60-62 destructures CLAUDECODE out of the child env with the stated Claude-SDK-nesting reason; packages/server/src/__tests__/smoke.test.ts:44,173 do the same). The finding fails on the other two checks. (1) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. Read whole, this page defines one mechanism: CLAUDECODE (and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION from v2.1.172) gates a CLI's <claude-code-hint /> stderr marker, and line 149 states 'The hint protocol only takes effect for plugins listed in the official Anthropic marketplace, claude-plugins-official. Anthropic curates that marketplace at its discretion' — a rebranded T-Bank fork cannot list there, so the protocol has no terminus for us. Asserting CLAUDECODE=1 from a non-Claude product is a brand claim, and it contradicts a boundary this repo records in shipped source: packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:94-96 — the generic plugin runtime env 'Emits Nessy names plus the unbranded PLUGIN_* compatibility aliases — never Claude aliases' — with CLAUDE_* names emitted ONLY under an explicit per-plugin claude-plugin-env-v1 / codex-plugin-env-v1 compat profile (data-paths.ts:111-155). A blanket CLAUDECODE=1 on every Bash and hook subprocess has no such profile. (2) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE IS FALSE AS AN ABSOLUTE. Bash-tool subprocesses do not get the raw host env: local-tools/runtime.ts:232-259 routes through runCommand into ProcessSupervisor, which defaults to the 'restricted' environment profile (process-supervisor.ts:717-733) whose hostEnvironment() filters process.env through the RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT allowlist at process-supervisor.ts:703-711. That allowlist contains NESSY_AGENT_VERSION, which apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:145 sets to app.getVersion() in the same process that constructs SessionManager (index.ts:711) and therefore the supervisor (SessionManager.ts:3574). So in the packaged desktop app every Bash-tool subprocess DOES carry a Nessy-presence env marker; what is missing is only that it wears a name third-party CLIs do not know. Separately, on the Claude backend (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1) the vendored node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude binary — 19 CLAUDECODE occurrences — is what runs Bash, so those subprocesses get the real marker from Claude Code itself; that is precisely why server-spawner.ts:62 must strip it. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS INVERTED. There is no <claude-code-hint /> reader anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep -ra, zero hits outside docs). Setting CLAUDECODE=1 would make gating CLIs emit raw hint tags that Nessy cannot strip, injecting them into model context — a regression, not a fix. The two absences are coupled and coherent, and the restricted allowlist already strips an inherited CLAUDECODE from Bash subprocesses, so the phase1 companion worry ('any CLI that gates on a variable we do inherit would leak the raw tag') is handled one layer down as well. Not listed in inert-worklist section 3 or 4, but it is the product-difference carve-out the task names.
verdict.correctedState: Nessy does not set CLAUDECODE, and deliberately so: the variable's only documented role on this page is gating a <claude-code-hint /> marker whose install prompt fires only for Anthropic's curated claude-plugins-official marketplace, which this fork cannot use, and the repo records the rule that Claude-branded env names are emitted only under an explicit per-plugin compat profile (packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:94-96, :141-155), which a blanket Bash/hook variable has none. It is also not true that no marker reaches tool subprocesses: those run under the 'restricted' environment profile whose allowlist (process-supervisor.ts:703-711) admits NESSY_AGENT_VERSION, set by apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:145 in the same process as the supervisor, so packaged-app Bash subprocesses carry a Nessy-presence marker under a Nessy name; that same allowlist strips any inherited CLAUDECODE. On the opt-in Claude backend the bundled claude-agent-sdk binary sets CLAUDECODE itself, which is why apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62 removes it to clear the SDK's nesting guard. The only real residue is that third-party CLIs cannot recognise the Nessy-named marker — and since Nessy has no reader for the hint tag, adopting the Claude name would leak raw <claude-code-hint /> lines into model context rather than gain anything.

results.claim: A marketplace plugin entry may carry `category`, `tags`, `relevance` (marketplace-specific) plus any manifest field including `license`, `keywords`, `repository`.
results.quote: You can include any field from the [plugin manifest schema](/docs/en/plugins-reference#plugin-manifest-schema), such as `description`, `version`, `author`, `commands`, and `hooks`, plus these marketplace-specific fields: `source`, `category`, `tags`, `strict`, and `relevance`.
results.ourState: `MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS` carries only the path fields plus `displayName`, `description`, `version`, `author`, `homepage`, `defaultEnabled`, `dependencies`. `category`, `tags`, `relevance`, `license`, `keywords` and `repository` are dropped at catalog parse and never reach the adapter — grep for `'category'`/`'tags'`/`'license'`/`'keywords'` in that file returns zero. `category` and `tags` are the documented organisation/search axes, so a marketplace that categorises its plugins loses that in our Discover list.

verdict.why: Doc sentence CONFIRMED verbatim at plugins/marketplace-reference.md#entry-and-plugin-json (was line 195 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) (whole line read; single sentence after a one-clause preamble, no reversal). The IDENTIFIER claim is also accurate: MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS (external-catalog-adapters.ts:153) carries the 7 path fields plus displayName/description/version/author/homepage/defaultEnabled/dependencies, and `grep -a` returns zero for category/tags/relevance/license/keywords in that file. The finding is refuted on its CONSEQUENCE, on four independent grounds. (1) It is a deliberate, reasoned, TESTED decision, not an oversight. The allowlist's own docblock at :141-152 states it: 'Deliberately an ALLOWLIST, not a copy of the entry: a catalog row is untrusted input from a repository the user may not control, and a key no adapter reads has no business travelling through the install record onto disk. The metadata half is the subset the Claude adapter actually consumes (normalizeClaudePluginBundle).' A committed regression test pins it: marketplace/__tests__/external-catalog-adapters.test.ts:406-431 places `relevance: { keywords: ['review'] }` on an entry under the comment 'Not a field any adapter reads - must not travel with the definition' and asserts fields keys equal ['description','mcpServers','skills','version']. The finding's own example field is the one the test names. (2) WRONG LAYER - the stated consequence is unreachable from the cited line. `fields` is a MANIFEST OVERLAY consumed by the format adapter, not the browse-row source. The Discover row is MarketplaceCatalogItem (marketplace/types.ts:340-400), built by proposalToCatalogItem (registry-catalog-items.ts) from entryDescription/entryVersion/capabilities/source - and that interface has no category/tags/keywords member at all. Carrying `category` into `fields` would put it in a manifest overlay whose target type, NessyPluginManifest (plugins/types.ts:715-758), also has no category/tags/license/keywords/repository. (3) NOT MARKETPLACE-ENTRY-SPECIFIC - our plugin.json reader drops exactly the same fields: schema.ts:501-525 rebuilds the manifest copying only description/publisher/homepageUrl/defaultEnabled/dependencies, and `grep -c -a license` returns 0 in format-adapters/claude.ts, plugins/schema.ts and plugins/types.ts. So this is a uniform 'we do not model informational metadata' property applied identically to plugin.json and to a marketplace entry, not a divergence at the catalog parse. (4) NO DOCUMENTED BEHAVIOUR IS MISSED, and the drop is not a rejection. The quoted sentence establishes only that an entry MAY carry these fields; the doc tables gloss them as 'Plugin category for organization' / 'Tags for searchability' / 'Discovery tags' and no page in the Claude Code corpus (plugin-marketplaces.md, discover-plugins.md, plugins.md, plugins-reference.md) documents Claude Code reading, rendering or filtering by category, tags or keywords. plugins/manifest-reference.md#unrecognized-fields (was lines 470-471 of the retired plugins-reference page) states the opposite posture verbatim: 'Claude Code ignores top-level fields it does not recognize. You can keep metadata from another ecosystem in plugin.json and the plugin still loads.' Our parser does the same - ExternalPluginCatalogPluginDto has an index signature, unknown keys emit no diagnostic and the entry still resolves and installs. Finally the 'Discover list' phrasing names a SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: Nessy's Discover shelves group per-registry (MarketplaceBrowsePage sections keyed by marketplaceRegistryId), and the tag/tenant/profession facet vocabulary that does exist belongs to the corporate Skills Market API (marketplace/client.ts:123-133,185-188), a different data source from a Claude marketplace.json - so there is no category axis for an external catalog to lose. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; those are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) - but it is the same class: a decision with a written reason and a guarding test. Separately: `relevance` is already tracked on its own as coverage-map row 60 (plugin-relevance, red), so folding it into this row double-counts a registered gap; and that row's note ('relevance passes inside the marketplace entry fields') is contradicted by the test above and should be corrected to 'dropped at parse'.
verdict.correctedState: MARKETPLACE_ENTRY_CARRIED_FIELDS (packages/shared/src/marketplace/external-catalog-adapters.ts:153) is a deliberate security allowlist, documented at :141-152 and pinned by a regression test at marketplace/__tests__/external-catalog-adapters.test.ts:406-431. It carries exactly the keys the format adapter can act on. category, tags, relevance, license, keywords and repository are IGNORED, never rejected: the entry still parses, resolves its source and installs, which matches plugins/manifest-reference.md#unrecognized-fields (was line 470 of the retired plugins-reference page) ('Claude Code ignores top-level fields it does not recognize'). The omission is not marketplace-entry-specific - NessyPluginManifest (plugins/types.ts:715-758) and our plugin.json reader (plugins/schema.ts:501-525) model none of these fields either. The claimed Discover-list consequence is unreachable from this line: the browse row MarketplaceCatalogItem (marketplace/types.ts:340-400) has no category/tags member and Discover shelves group by registry, not by entry category; the tag facets that exist belong to the separate corporate Skills Market API (marketplace/client.ts:123-133). If a category/tag browse axis for external catalogs is wanted, that is a new product feature spanning MarketplaceCatalogItem and the browse UI, not a parser fix - and it is undocumented in Claude's corpus. The one genuinely open sub-item, relevance, is already tracked as coverage-map row 60 (plugin-relevance).

results.claim: A pre-populated, read-only plugins directory can be pointed at with an environment variable so container/CI images start with marketplaces and plugin caches already present, with a second variable to install directly into that path at build time.
results.quote: Set the `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR` environment variable to point at this directory.
results.ourState: No seed-directory concept exists. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` and `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS` all return zero hits under `--include='*.ts'` repo-wide, and there is no NESSY_-prefixed equivalent for any of them. The offline/airgap escape hatch the page recommends (`KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE`) therefore has no counterpart, which matters for a corporate-network fork.

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at plugins/org.md#seed-containers-and-ci (was line 635 of the retired plugin-marketplaces page) (two-sentence line, second half does not reverse it). The narrow identifier half is true: no CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR / layered read-only seed directory exists. But the finding is refuted on both its evidence and its consequence. (1) EVIDENCE FALSE AS STATED: the claim says all five names 'return zero hits under --include=*.ts repo-wide'. PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR returns 5 hits -- packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:11 and :99, workspaces/index.ts:46, plus two in __tests__/paths.test.ts. Bare-name grep collision with a real managed-cache-root constant; the sweep never re-ran its own command. (2) CONSEQUENCE FALSE for the variable the finding singles out as mattering: KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE is an OPT-IN in Claude Code to stop it deleting and re-cloning a marketplace whose background pull failed. Our fork does the non-destructive thing UNCONDITIONALLY, by design. packages/shared/src/marketplace/registry-source.ts mergeFailedFetch keeps the previous catalog under the failed fetch's signature and explicitly refuses to delete the on-disk copy ('after a failed refresh it is the only surviving copy, and removing it turns a recoverable state into an unrecoverable one'), citing the same bug one subsystem over from mcp.md. upgrade() (:857-870) on a non-persistable fetch leaves the row and its signature untouched and returns typed fetch-failed / fetch-timeout, 'so the catalog the user can still browse stays the catalog an install resolves against'. There is no destructive default here to need an escape hatch from -- the airgap resilience the page sells via the flag is our floor, not our gap. (3) PREFER_HTTPS likewise: packages/shared/src/plugins/source-resolver.ts:115-116 -- 'Claude clones shorthand over SSH by default (:553); we resolve to the HTTPS repository URL because codeload is the acquisition route this app has.' The flag's effect is our unconditional default. (4) GIT_TIMEOUT_MS is not absent as a concept: REGISTRY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000 (registry-source.ts:54) with an options.fetchTimeoutMs override (:323) and a distinct 'fetch-timeout' upgrade reason -- configurable, just not env-driven. (5) The seed directory's container/CI intent is served by a deliberate product difference, not left open: admin pre-provisioning arrives through server-delivered managed settings (packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts, gateway /api/v1/cli/managed-settings) as extraKnownMarketplaces, registered idempotently by PluginRegistrySource.ensureDeliveredMarketplaces() (:341-378) under the same strictKnownMarketplaces allowlist an interactive add passes, with catalogs cached to disk. This fork delivers policy through its corporate gateway rather than through container env vars. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none touches marketplaces or seeding).
verdict.correctedState: No CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_* environment variable is honoured, and there is no layered read-only seed directory: a container image cannot point Nessy at a pre-populated plugins tree via env var. That is the whole of the true gap, and it is narrower than the finding claims. The finding's grep is wrong -- PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR has 5 hits under --include='*.ts' (packages/shared/src/workspaces/paths.ts:11,:99; workspaces/index.ts:46; two tests) as the managed cache-root constant. More importantly the three behaviours the flags buy are already our unconditional defaults, so their absence is not a gap: keep-marketplace-on-failure is default and non-optional (registry-source.ts mergeFailedFetch keeps the last resolved catalog and never deletes the on-disk copy; upgrade() leaves the row unstamped on fetch-failed/fetch-timeout so browse and install keep resolving against it), HTTPS-for-owner/repo-shorthand is default (source-resolver.ts:115-116, deliberately diverging from Claude's SSH default), and the git fetch timeout is configurable in-code (REGISTRY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS 45s, options.fetchTimeoutMs). results.claim: A plugin may ship a `settings.json` at its root whose `agent` key activates one of the plugin's own subagents as the main thread, and whose values outrank a `settings` block in `plugin.json`.
results.quote: Plugins can include a `settings.json` file at the plugin root to apply default configuration when the plugin is enabled. Currently, only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys are supported.
results.ourState: The file is detected and recorded as a deferral only — `CLAUDE_RETAINED_SURFACE_FIELDS` carries `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }`, which pushes a `plugin.deferred.claude_settings` row and nothing else. Neither key is read anywhere: `grep -ran "subagentStatusLine" --include='*.ts' .` returns zero hits repo-wide. A plugin whose whole purpose is to change the main thread's agent installs and silently does nothing.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quote is VERBATIM at plugins.md:298, and reading the whole section rather than the one line strengthens it: :300 says "Setting `agent` activates one of the plugin's custom agents as the main thread, applying its system prompt, tool restrictions, and model", and :308 says "Settings from `settings.json` take priority over `settings` declared in `plugin.json`. Unknown keys are silently ignored." Nothing in the second half reverses the claim. (2) The cited state is accurate, with a 5-line citation drift: the row is at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275, not :2270 (:2270 is a comment about `dependencies`). It reads exactly `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }`, and addClaudeRetainedSurfaceDeferrals (:2278-2317, called at :270 with the bundle rootDirectory) fires on existsSync(<root>/settings.json), pushes `plugin.deferred.claude_settings` (reasonCode template at :2302) and, unlike the `themes` row, carries no `refusal` diagnostic, so the author is told nothing at install. `grep -ran subagentStatusLine` over the repo returns hits only inside docs/superpowers/specs/data/*.json (the sweep's own files) — zero source hits, confirmed with -a. (3) One layer up and one layer down both hold. Sibling-subsystem check: packages/shared/src/plugins/plugin-settings.ts also owns a file literally named settings.json, but it is the per-plugin data-path option store for MCPB user_config descriptors (the only producer of PluginSettingDescriptor is format-adapters/mcpb.ts:130) and has nothing to do with a Claude plugin-root file; claude.ts:2084's `'settings'` is a member of CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS, an LSP server knob, a third unrelated `settings`. Consequence check, separate from the identifier: the fork has NO main-thread-agent override at all — no mechanism anywhere reads an agent name and installs it as the main thread — so nothing upstream honours the key by another route. The nearest live analogue, plugin-shipped output styles, IS honoured (capabilities/runtime-output-styles.ts, resolver.ts:612), which is the positive control proving plugin-shipped default-behaviour surfaces are otherwise wired; the settings.json path is the one that is not. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) and not in the deviation register. Not a deliberate product difference either: importing Claude plugin bundles is a supported first-class surface of this fork, unrelated to the dropped subscription flows or the rebrand.
verdict.correctedState: Substantively confirmed, with two corrections. Citation: the row is at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275 (not :2270 — that line is a comment about `dependencies`). Consequence: 'silently does nothing' is right for a FIRST install but needs the nuance that the deferral is machine-readable. Shipping a plugin-root settings.json pushes `{ externalKind: 'settings', reasonCode: 'plugin.deferred.claude_settings' }` and flips compatibility.state to 'partial', but the install path (management-service-v2.ts:191-199) returns no requiresConfirmation, so describeInstallOutcome (useMarketplaceInstall.ts:54-72) reports neither blocked nor needsConfirmEnable, PluginsPage.tsx:291 never records the deferred list, and the user gets a plain success toast — no diagnostic, since only the `themes` row carries a `refusal`.
