results.claim: A folder under a skills directory containing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` with no marketplace and no install step, discovered in place rather than copied into the cache.
results.quote: Any folder under a skills directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest is loaded as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` on the next session, with no marketplace and no install step.
results.ourState: Not implemented. `grep -ran "skills-dir"` over the repo hits only plan/spec prose — including `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:197` which itself records "skills-dir plugins undetected (B1, still not started)". Skill discovery walks `.claude/skills` at project and ancestor depth (`native-sources.ts` line ~1065, tagged `d${depth}`) but never checks a skill folder for a plugin manifest, so a bundle laid out this way contributes its SKILL.md and silently drops its agents, hooks and MCP servers.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the divergence survives. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md` -> line 375, exact match. The whole line continues 'Scaffold one with `plugin init`. Unlike a marketplace install, the plugin is discovered in place rather than copied into the plugin cache.' -- it reinforces the claim, it does not reverse it. The surrounding section (lines 372-411, '## Skills-directory plugins') adds a three-row table (`:381`-`:382`: `<skills-dir>/foo/SKILL.md` with no manifest = a plain skill; `<skills-dir>/foo/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` = 'A plugin `foo@skills-dir`, which can bundle its own skills, agents, hooks, and more'), a scope table (`~/.claude/skills/` personal, `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` project-behind-trust), `:401`'s no-ancestor-walk warning, and `:408`/`:411` 'There is no `uninstall` step because nothing was installed from a marketplace' / `claude plugin disable my-tool@skills-dir`. `:874` and `:911` repeat it for `plugin init`. (2) CITED EVIDENCE. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:197` reads verbatim: '| P7 | Skill listing capped at 4 000 chars / 180 per entry vs Claude's 1 536 per entry; output styles unscanned; skills-dir plugins undetected (B1, **still not started**) | Give B1 a start date or re-home the three rows | ~ medium |'. Corroborated by `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md:557` ('**Skills-directory plugins** (`<name>@skills-dir`) -- that is the B1 batch.') and by the B1 row in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:701`, which lists 'skills-dir plugins' among B1's items, declares 'B1 fully closed 2026-07-30 (`6cdbd80e`)', and never mentions the item again -- neither in the closed list nor in the 'Genuinely remaining' list nor in the two items recorded as leaving B1 (`bin/`-on-PATH, dependency auto-install). It was dropped silently, not implemented and not decided. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-b1-audit.md` contains no skills-directory-plugin measurement either (its only `skillsDir` hit, `:109`, is about the Claude adapter's `CLAUDE_DEFAULT_SKILLS_DIR` in manifest path resolution -- B1a, a different subsystem). (3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN, consequence verified separately from the identifier. Every skills-directory scanner in the fork is the single function `skillRecords` in `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:266-310`, called from exactly five sites (`:903` `~/.agents/skills`, `:904` `<configDir>/skills`, `:949` `<workspaceRoot>/skills`, `:1016` `.nessy-agent/skills`, `:1065` `.agents/skills` per ancestor depth). It admits an entry only when `join(slugPath, 'SKILL.md')` exists (`:282`-`:283`) and emits `kind: 'skill'`; it never stats `.claude-plugin/`, never reads a manifest, and there is no other kind it can emit. Nothing upstream handles the case: `grep -rn "\.claude-plugin" --include=*.ts` over `packages/`+`apps/` returns manifest readers only in the install/marketplace path -- `format-adapters/claude.ts:145` (bundle adapter, runs on a staged bundle), `plugin-manifest-probe.ts:51` (a `raw.githubusercontent.com` GET for a marketplace DETAIL page), `registry-catalog-fetcher.ts:167`, `marketplace/repository-install.ts:22`, `workspaces/storage.ts:284`. Every one of those requires an install that stages into the plugin cache; even the `local-path` source kind (`plugins/types.ts:933`, `install-service.ts:513`, `source-resolver.ts:378`) runs `createPluginStagingArea`, so it is a copy-with-install-step, the opposite of the doc's 'discovered in place'. `management-service-v2.ts` / `store-v2.ts` have no disk-discovery entry point at all (`grep -i discover` yields one unrelated OAuth comment). NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, `availableModels`, `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, `ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops`, `hooks-runtime.ts`, `SdkMcpServerConfig.required`, `SessionMirrorStore.delete`, `MirrorSessionKey.subpath`, `listSessionSummaries`) touches skills-directory plugins. NOT A REBRAND DIFFERENCE: the absent thing is the mechanism (in-place plugin discovery from a skills tree, no marketplace, no install), which is missing whatever the directory is named. POSITIVE CONTROL for the absence: the same `grep -a` sweep does find live non-prose `skills-dir` hits -- `packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:511` (a debounce key string), `format-adapters/manifest-paths.ts:30` and two test files (a `custom-skills-dir` fixture name), and `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:56`, which asserts that a managed-policy entry `{ source: 'skills-dir' }` is DROPPED as invalid -- so the grep is not silently skipping the tree, and the one place the token does reach shipped policy code rejects it, which is consistent with the feature being absent rather than hidden.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed absent, with three corrections to the finding's prose. (a) The claim 'grep -ran "skills-dir" over the repo hits only plan/spec prose' is false: there are live non-prose hits -- `packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:511` (debounce key), `packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/manifest-paths.ts:30` plus `__tests__/manifest-paths.test.ts:85` and `__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:3497-3509` (a `custom-skills-dir` fixture), and `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:56`, which asserts a managed-policy `{ source: 'skills-dir' }` entry is dropped as invalid. None implement the feature, so the conclusion holds, but the absence must be stated against the code path, not against the grep. (b) The claim that 'skill discovery walks `.claude/skills` at project and ancestor depth (native-sources.ts line ~1065)' names the wrong directory. `native-sources.ts:1065` walks `PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` = `.agents/skills` (`packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:37`); the other four `skillRecords` call sites are `~/.agents/skills` (`:903`), `<configDir>/skills` (`:904`), `<workspaceRoot>/skills` (`:949`) and `.nessy-agent/skills` (`:1016`). `.claude/skills` is not scanned anywhere in the fork -- `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.claude/rules` are read beside ours (`:1049`-`:1058`, `:1108`), but `.claude/skills` is not among them. (c) The stated consequence is conditionally wrong and understates the gap. Because `skillRecords` admits a folder only when `<folder>/SKILL.md` exists (`native-sources.ts:282`), a doc-conformant skills-directory plugin -- which per `plugins/org.md#keep-skills-directory-plugins-loading (was line 382 of the retired plugins-reference page)` bundles its skills at `<folder>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and need have no root `SKILL.md` at all -- contributes NOTHING, not 'its SKILL.md minus the agents/hooks/MCP'. Only the subset of such bundles that happen to also carry a root `SKILL.md` degrade to a bare skill. Corrected statement: the fork has no in-place plugin discovery of any kind; every plugin must be resolved through `install-service.ts` and staged into the plugin cache (including the `local-path` source kind), so `<skills-dir>/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` is never read, `<name>@skills-dir` is never a plugin key, `plugin init` is deliberately not implemented (`apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:39` routes it to `/create-plugin` and the bundled `plugin-creator` skill), there is no `/reload-plugins`, and the doc's admin control for the source -- `{"source": "skills-dir"}` in `blockedMarketplaces`/`strictKnownMarketplaces` (`plugins/marketplace-reference.md#source-values-valid-only-in-policy-lists (was line 911 of the retired plugins-reference page)`) -- is parsed as an invalid entry and dropped (`managed-marketplace-entries.test.ts:56`). The item was listed under parity row B1, never measured in `2026-07-29-b1-audit.md`, and silently dropped when B1 was declared closed at `6cdbd80e`; it has no plan and no owner decision.

results.claim: Eight optional LSP fields govern server lifecycle and diagnostics injection, two of them with defaults (`restartOnCrash` defaults to `true`, `diagnostics` defaults to `true`).
results.quote: `restartOnCrash`        | Whether to restart the server after it crashes. Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to leave a crashed server stopped instead of restarting it
results.ourState: All eight are parsed as declared-but-unread: `CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS` lists `transport`, `initializationOptions`, `settings`, `startupTimeout`, `shutdownTimeout`, `restartOnCrash`, `maxRestarts`, `diagnostics`, and the reader emits a `plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread` warning naming them. The capability that reaches the runtime carries only `command`, `args`, `languages`, `env`, `workspaceFolder`. An author who sets `diagnostics: false` to suppress automatic diagnostic injection, or `restartOnCrash: false` on a server that crash-loops, gets neither.

verdict.why: Quote and identifier both check out; the CONSEQUENCE attached to the quoted field is false by measurement. (1) Quote verbatim at plugins/manifest-reference.md#lspservers (was line 262 of the retired plugins-reference page), whole line read, no reversing second half; the only adjacent qualifier is :266 ('restartOnCrash and shutdownTimeout require Claude Code v2.1.205 or later'), which does not reverse it. (2) Cited claude.ts:2075 sits inside the doc-comment (2053-2090) for CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS at :2081; the eight names match exactly, the warning plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread is emitted at :2158-2164, and the capability built at :2166-2177 carries only command/args/languages/env/workspaceFolder. So the declared-but-unread half is CONFIRMED. (3) The claim's harm for restartOnCrash is inverted. Nessy has no LSP restart mechanism at all: LspService.fail() (pi-harness/lsp-service.ts:382-387) is terminal, the read loop throws 'lsp-process-closed' on process exit (:282), and nothing respawns; SessionManager provisions LspService once per agent construction (getOrCreateAgentUnchecked, :11597-11660) and shouldRetainPiLspService only disposes a non-ready service at the NEXT agent construction. The repo's own deviation audit already states it: 'a crashed server stays failed forever' (2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:153). So an author who sets restartOnCrash:false gets exactly the documented outcome (crashed server left stopped), and there is no crash-loop for the flag to stop. 'gets neither' is refuted for the very field the quoted sentence is about; the divergence on that field runs the other way (the documented default true is what we do not implement). Secondary: the whole plugin-LSP surface is Pi-only (provider === 'pi' at :11597 and :12313), a harness this fork built itself, so Claude's supervisor semantics were never being mirrored. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions, but it is a recorded scope decision - docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-instruction-memory-and-diagnostics.md 'Deliberately out of scope': 'restartOnCrash / maxRestarts. Absent repo-wide; LSP crash handling is terminal by design today ... Restart policy is its own decision' and 'A per-server diagnostics flag. Nothing parses one' - and it is tracked open as parity-audit row P8. The channel choice (warning diagnostic, not a deferred row) is itself a measured decision recorded at claude.ts:2053-2080 and plan 2026-07-31-plugins-and-marketplace.md C5.
verdict.correctedState: All eight fields (transport, initializationOptions, settings, startupTimeout, shutdownTimeout, restartOnCrash, maxRestarts, diagnostics) are indeed parsed-but-unread at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2081, with a named plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread warning at :2158 and a capability carrying only command/args/languages/env/workspaceFolder at :2166. But the user-visible harm is not what was claimed. restartOnCrash: Nessy never restarts a crashed language server (LspService.fail() at pi-harness/lsp-service.ts:382-387 is terminal; no respawn anywhere), so restartOnCrash:false is satisfied by accident and no crash-loop is possible; the unimplemented behaviour is the documented DEFAULT true. diagnostics: this half stands - automatic post-edit diagnostic injection is real and on by default (AGENT_FLAGS.editFeedbackEnabled true at SessionManager.ts:454, recordPiLspDiagnostics at :2351 folded into the edit-feedback payload via buildEditFeedbackRunner at :5286), so diagnostics:false is genuinely not honoured. The concrete harm the claim missed is startupTimeout: LspService defaults to 12s (lsp-service.ts:142) while the only two official catalogue plugins that declare the field (jdtls-lsp, kotlin-lsp) ask for 120s, so they abort at initialize today - recorded as OWED in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-plugins-and-marketplace.md row C5. The whole plugin-LSP path is Pi-only (provider === 'pi'), which is a separate already-recorded audit row (P8).

results.claim: `userConfig` values are substituted as `${user_config.KEY}` into MCP and LSP server configs and (for non-sensitive values) into skill and agent content.
results.quote: Each value is available for substitution as `${user_config.KEY}` in MCP and LSP server configs and hook commands.
results.ourState: The option schema, the sensitivity split, the storage-source restriction and the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` export are all built; the `${user_config.*}` substitution into MCP/LSP configs and skill/agent content is not, and the surface carries its own deferral row `plugin.deferred.claude_user_config_substitution`. verdict.why: The quoted sentence exists verbatim at plugins/manifest-reference.md#environment-variables (was line 577 of the retired plugins-reference page) (whole line reads: 'Each value is available for substitution as ${user_config.KEY} in MCP and LSP server configs and hook commands. Non-sensitive values can also be substituted in skill and agent content. All values are exported to hook processes as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> environment variables, where <KEY> is the option key uppercased.' — note :579 then carves the shell back out: shell-form hook commands, monitor commands and MCP headersHelper REJECT ${user_config.*}). The claimed OUR STATE is stale and its consequence is false. Commit 2a1f6cb7 (2026-07-30, 'fix(plugins): a plugin's user config reaches its MCP, LSP and skill surfaces') added packages/shared/src/plugins/user-config-substitution.ts — a 355-line module that substitutes ${user_config.KEY} into MCP command/args/cwd/env/url/headers (substituteMcp, :251) and LSP command/args/env/workingDirectory/workspaceFolder (substituteLsp, :280), plus pluginUserConfigContentValues (:341) for the non-sensitive skill-content subset. It is WIRED, not dead: packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1837-1865 calls PluginUserConfigValues + substitutePluginCapabilityUserConfig on every mcp/lsp candidate and builds skillUserConfig for skill candidates; packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:685-687 performs the skill-body expansion. 23 tests pass across packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/user-config-substitution.test.ts and packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/plugin-user-config-substitution.test.ts. This is the repo's documented recurring false positive in its exact shape: the cited identifier is real but the consequence was already handled a layer up. Not an inert-worklist §3 owner decision (no user_config row there) and not a deliberate product difference. What genuinely survives is smaller and differently shaped: (1) the deferral row at format-adapters/claude.ts:2263-2267 is STALE — 2a1f6cb7 never touched claude.ts, so the compatibility report still emits plugin.deferred.claude_user_config_substitution and format-adapters.test.ts:2718 still asserts it, over a comment claiming the substitution is unbuilt; (2) AGENT content is genuinely not substituted — resolver.ts:1863 gates skillUserConfig on candidate.kind === 'skill', and the separate 'agent' binding (resolver.ts:1237-1249) carries no pluginUserConfig, so :577's 'skill and agent content' is half-covered.
verdict.correctedState: ${user_config.KEY} substitution IS built and wired for MCP server configs, LSP server configs and skill content. packages/shared/src/plugins/user-config-substitution.ts (commit 2a1f6cb7, 2026-07-30) substitutes into MCP command/args/cwd/env/url/headers and LSP command/args/env/workingDirectory/workspaceFolder with sensitive values allowed, and exposes only the non-sensitive subset to skill bodies (a sensitive key referenced in a skill body stays a literal placeholder by construction). capabilities/resolver.ts:1837-1865 is the call site; runtime-skill-content.ts:685-687 expands the body. results.claim: Omitting the `skills` option enables every discovered user and project skill from the filesystem locations `settingSources` names; passing a list or `[]` is the only way to narrow it.
results.quote: When omitted, discovered Skills are enabled and the Skill tool is available, matching CLI behavior.
results.ourState: `buildClaudeSessionOptions` returns only `systemPrompt`, `settingSources` and (for a child) `maxTurns`; `skills` is never set, and `settingSources` is spelled `['user', 'project', 'local']`. So every `SKILL.md` under `~/.claude/skills/` and `<cwd>/.claude/skills/` is enabled inside a Claude-backend session, chosen by the SDK rather than by Nessy's capability resolver — the resolver's own visibility state, `enabled:false` policy and skill listing do not reach that set. Conformant with this page; the divergence is that Nessy has a second, authoritative skill-gating system that the Claude backend does not project onto the SDK.

verdict.why: Leg 1 passes: the sentence exists verbatim at line 33 of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills.md, and the rest of that line ('Pass "all" ... or [] to disable all. When you set `skills`, the SDK adds the Skill tool to `allowedTools` automatically.') does not reverse it. Leg 2 half-fails: the named function does not exist. `grep -rn buildClaudeSessionOptions` over packages/ and apps/ returns nothing; the real helper is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308), and the cited :301 is the closing brace of its systemPrompt literal. Its own doc comment says it is a three-option SLICE ('The turn-shape SDK options Nessy passes explicitly ... Extracted from chatImpl's inline options object so the three shapes are testable'), NOT the session options object. `settingSources: ['user','project','local']` at :305 and the absence of `skills` are both real. Leg 3 refutes the finding: the actual Options object is assembled at claude-agent.ts:1213-1630 and one layer down it disables the SDK skill mechanism outright. :1118 `const disallowedTools: string[] = ['EnterPlanMode','ExitPlanMode','AskUserQuestion','Skill'];`, wired in at :1626, and :1629 `plugins: []` carrying the comment at :1627-1628 'No plugins — skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute (the model reads SKILL.md files directly, enforced by PrerequisiteManager)'. The installed SDK typings define the effect precisely (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1303-1307): disallowedTools tools 'will be removed from the model's context and cannot be used, even if they would otherwise be allowed.' So the SDK Skill tool is absent from every Claude-backend turn and no SDK-discovered SKILL.md is invocable. The claimed consequence — 'every SKILL.md under ~/.claude/skills/ and <cwd>/.claude/skills/ is enabled ... chosen by the SDK rather than by Nessy's capability resolver' — is therefore false: Nessy's resolver (BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext / capabilityTurnRuntime.view, materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation, PrerequisiteManager) is the only skill path that reaches the model, exactly as intended. results.claim: Dynamic context uses an inline `` !`<command>` `` placeholder that may appear anywhere in the body, whose output replaces the placeholder in place, with a ` ```! ` fenced block for multi-line commands.
results.quote: The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude.
results.ourState: `runtimeSkillContextCommand` recognises a different syntax: a bare `!command` that must be the FIRST non-empty top-level body line, backticks not part of the form, fenced blocks skipped as prose, and a second `!` line throwing `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous`. Output is appended (`outputs.join('\n\n')`) rather than substituted at the placeholder. The docs' own example skill (`- PR diff: !`gh pr diff``, three placeholders inside list items) yields zero substitutions here; a skill whose first line IS `` !`git diff HEAD` `` passes the backticks through to the Bash permission evaluator as part of the command string.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass and the consequence was reproduced by execution, not inferred.

(1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md line 494 reads exactly: "The `` !`<command>` `` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude. The command output replaces the placeholder, so Claude receives actual data, not the command itself." The second sentence of the two-sentence line reinforces rather than reverses: it states substitution-at-the-placeholder explicitly. Corroborated on the same page: :518 "Each `` !`<command>` `` executes immediately", :519 "The output replaces the placeholder in the skill content", :524 substitution "runs once over the original file", :526 "only recognized when `!` appears at the start of a line or immediately after whitespace" (so mid-line placeholders after whitespace ARE legal), and :528-536 the ` ```! ` fenced form for multi-line commands. The docs' own quickstart at :82 puts `` !`git diff HEAD` `` under a `## Current changes` heading and :89 says Claude Code "replaces the line with its output".

(2) CITED LINE. packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts:32 is `if (!first || !first.startsWith('!')) return undefined` — exactly as claimed. :20-31 walks lines, toggling a `fenced` flag on any /^\s*```/ line and skipping fenced content and blanks, and takes the FIRST surviving line as `first`. :33 `const command = first.slice(1).trim()` — everything after the bare `!` becomes the command, backticks are not part of the recognised form and are not stripped. :48 throws `runtime-skill-context-command-ambiguous` on a second top-level `!` line. There is no other implementation: `grep -ran` over packages/apps finds exactly one caller (base-agent.ts:2412) and one other `` !` `` site (format-adapters/claude.ts:655), which merely CLASSIFIES the pattern as `bash-execution` capability metadata and performs no substitution.

(3) CONSEQUENCE, TESTED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER. Ran the real exported function against the docs' own bodies (bun, importing the shipped module):
  - docs' `pr-summary` skill body (three `` !`gh …` `` placeholders inside list items) => undefined. Zero substitutions.
  - docs' quickstart `summarize-changes` body (`## Current changes` then a standalone `` !`git diff HEAD` `` line) => undefined. Zero substitutions — the doc's own worked example is inert here.
  - body whose first line IS `` !`git diff HEAD` `` => command string "`git diff HEAD`", backticks included.
  - documented multi-line ` ```! ` fenced block => undefined; the fence toggle at :24 classifies it as prose.
Downstream: base-agent.ts:2446 returns `outputs.join('\n\n')` and :2805 folds that string into `messageParts` as its own block joined with '\n\n' — appended, never substituted at a placeholder. Permission side: SessionManager.ts:4595 builds `const permissionInput = { command: request.command, cwd: pinnedCwd }` and :4597 feeds it straight to `shouldAllowToolInMode('Bash', input, …)` plus `evaluatePermissionDslV1` — so the backtick-wrapped string is what the Bash allowlist matches against and what would be executed, where in bash `` `git diff HEAD` `` is command substitution, not the command.

NOT AN OWNER DECISION. 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 lists nine dated decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — none covers skill dynamic-context syntax. The only §3-adjacent skills row is `SkillMetadata.disallowedTools`, a different field. The introducing commit b83ccd05 ("feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals", Step 5 "Govern skill shell context") records the 32 KiB/5 s budget and "inject the result as volatile context" but records no decision to diverge from the placeholder syntax. Not a branding/rename difference and not a dropped-subscription-flow difference.

SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK. The composer `!` shell gate (SessionManager.ts:2708, :16263) is user-typed composer shell, a different subsystem; the finding correctly names the skill dynamic-context path. session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:241 independently confirms the repo's own understanding is a one-shell "inline expansion" for a skill's `` !`command` `` blocks.

One narrowing the claim omits, which does not rescue it: materializeRuntimeSkillContext returns '' unless `capabilityTurnRuntime.provider === 'pi'` and the skill has `pluginRuntime` set (base-agent.ts:2407, :2411), so user/project skills and the whole Claude backend never run a command at all. That widens the gap rather than closing it.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED, with two additions. results.ourState: Two divergences on one line. (1) Our executor runs only for skills with `skill.pluginRuntime` set and only when `runtime?.provider === 'pi'` — a user or project skill, and any skill on the Claude backend, never executes its command. verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at skills.md:539, but that line has four sentences and the finding read only the first. Both halves of the claimed divergence fail. CITATION: base-agent.ts:2391 is a bare closing brace inside latestSkillSelections; the real gates are :2405 (runtime?.provider !== 'pi') and :2411 (!skill?.pluginRuntime), inside materializeRuntimeSkillContext (:2401). HALF 1 (scope): that our host executor runs only for plugin skills is the recorded deliberate posture, not drift. The parity audit's Deliberate-differences table (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547) states 'No shell execution from skill/command bundle text (!`cmd`, @file detected and deferred) | Keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed. The defect is the silence, not the refusal', and the closure is visible in code: format-adapters/claude.ts:655 classifies !`...` as bash-execution and emits a plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution diagnostic (:741-749), so custom commands are detected-and-deferred, not silently dropped. The narrow re-opening for plugin skills is its own recorded unit — commit b83ccd05 'feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals', plan step 5 'Govern skill shell context' (docs/current-plans/pi-claude-post-parity.md at that commit), which specifies exactly the executor contract, the 32 KiB cap and the 5 s timeout now in capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts. (a) On the Claude backend the setting IS live: it is declared in the shipped SDK's own settings type, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:4922 'Disable inline shell execution in skills and custom slash commands from user, project, or plugin sources', and is present in the claude binary and in the bundled apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js — with settingSources user/project/local the SDK reads it from the same settings.json the page names. results.claim: A settings key overrides per-skill visibility from settings rather than frontmatter, with four states, absent meaning `on`, and `off` also hiding the skill from SDK and Remote-Control command lists.
results.quote: The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter.
results.ourState: No reader. `grep -ran "skillOverrides"` over the repo hits only two planning documents (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193` and the r-queue verification spec). None of the four states exists, so the only way to hide a skill checked into a shared repo is to edit its SKILL.md.

verdict.why: All three checks pass and no refutation was found. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at skills.md:637 under the heading '### Override skill visibility from settings'. The whole line is three sentences and none of them reverses the conclusion: 'The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter. Use it for skills whose SKILL.md you don't want to edit, such as ones checked into a shared project repo. The `/skills` menu writes it for you: highlight a skill and press `Space` to cycle states, then `Enter` to save to `.claude/settings.local.json`.' The four-state table (on / name-only / user-invocable-only / off), 'A skill that is absent from `skillOverrides` is treated as "on"' (:652) and the v2.1.199 SDK/Remote-Control clause (:650) are all present as claimed. (2) The cited repo evidence is accurate: `grep -ran skillOverrides` (with -a, so NUL-bearing files are not skipped) hits docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193 and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:264,:559 plus this sweep's own output files. A case-insensitive sweep for every plausible Nessy renaming of the key (skilloverride, skill_override, skillVisibility, name-only/nameOnly, user-invocable-only/userInvocableOnly) finds no settings key of any spelling; packages/shared/src/config/{storage.ts,validators.ts,config-defaults.json} and pi-harness/managed-policy.ts carry no skill-visibility key at all. (3) One layer up and down, the CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier and it holds for the subsystem named. Candidate refutations checked and each ruled out: (a) Plugin capabilities DO have a persisted settings-side toggle (`setCapabilityEnabled` -> capabilities.json via packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts, tri-state per scope global<workspace<project with a managed tier on top) - but that store's own docblock scopes it to plugin capabilities, its PolicyTarget is {pluginKey, pluginInstanceId}, and Claude's page explicitly exempts plugin skills ('Plugin skills are not affected by `skillOverrides`. (b) Native capabilities in resolver.ts:1595 derive `enabled` from `record.sourceEnabled`, which native-sources.ts sets only from a Source's `sources/<slug>/config.json` `enabled` field - skills have no such config file. (c) The only other native disable path is `sessionSelection.transientlyDisabledKeys` (resolver.ts:739,:1574,:1618,:1774), which is transient by design AND has no producer anywhere outside resolver.ts - so even the session-scoped half is unwired. (d) `Skill(name)` permission rules are not an escape either: `Skill` appears in BUILT_IN_TOOLS (pre-tool-use.ts:134) but there is no `Skill` entry in PI_TOOL_BINDINGS, from which PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES is derived, and skills are invoked via `[skill:name]` markers through extractModelSkillInvocations, not through a permission-gated `Skill` tool. (f) The model-facing listing, prompt-builder.ts buildSkillListingPart, filters solely on `disableModelInvocation` - a frontmatter field - confirming the listing side reads no settings override. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns skill visibility (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). Not a deliberate fork difference either: skill visibility is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ renaming. On the contrary, the parity audit itself names this gap - 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1651 lists 'settings-level "restrict skill access" and "override skill visibility"' among what P7/P9 closed their frontmatter rows without, routed to R30a; R30's closure notes cover argument substitution, `effort`, `paths` and the /doctor surface, and never mention shipping skillOverrides. So the row is marked done on a scope that never included this half.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with two refinements to the wording. (1) The absence is exact for NATIVE skills: no reader of `skillOverrides` or of any renamed equivalent exists in packages/ or apps/; the string occurs only in planning documents (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:264,:559) and in this sweep's own generated artifacts. results.claim: The skill listing has a character budget that scales with the model's context window, is raisable by a settings key or an environment variable, and caps each entry's combined `description` + `when_to_use` at 1,536 characters.
results.quote: To raise the budget, set the [`skillListingBudgetFraction`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) setting (e.g. `0.02` = 2%) or the `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` environment variable to a fixed character count.
results.ourState: None of `skillListingBudgetFraction`, `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` or `skillListingMaxDescChars` has a reader. The 1,536 constant exists (`MAX_DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`) but is applied only as a ceiling on a description DERIVED from the body, not to the listing entry; the listing path instead clamps each catalog entry's description at a hard 512 chars (`capability-catalog.ts:107`, `clampedText(input.description, 'description', 512, …)`) with no context-window scaling and no per-entry cap of 1,536.

verdict.why: Doc quote is VERBATIM (skills.md line 920, first sentence of a four-sentence line; the rest adds skillOverrides "name-only" and skillListingMaxDescChars, and does not reverse the claim). The cited evidence line is also correct: packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:81 is `const MAX_DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 1_536;`, applied only to a description DERIVED from the body. And `grep -ran` (NUL-safe) over all .ts/.tsx/.js/.json outside node_modules/dist returns ZERO hits for skillListingBudgetFraction, SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET and skillListingMaxDescChars, so the identifier half of the claim is true. The finding is refuted on step 3: the stated OUR STATE names the WRONG SUBSYSTEM and therefore reports a false consequence. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/capability-catalog.ts:108` (not :107 -- line 107 is `kind: input.kind,`) is NOT the skill listing path. It is the Pi-harness capability/tool catalog whose kinds are `'builtin' | 'session' | 'plugin' | 'mcp' | 'app'` (capability-catalog.ts:9) -- there is no skill kind -- and whose own comment at :84-88 says the clamped text is "Free text shown to the model in `mcp__tool_search` results." That is the sibling-subsystem trap named in AGENTS.md and in inert-worklist section 4 shape 4. The REAL skill listing is `PromptBuilder.buildSkillListingPart()` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:403-447), and it does have a listing character budget and a per-entry description cap: `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (:105) enforced at :433 with a truthful "(N more skills not listed)" overflow at :441-444, and `SKILL_LISTING_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS = 180` (:113) applied per entry by `boundedListingText` (:126-131). So "no listing budget" and "512 chars per entry" are both wrong; the true numbers are 4,000 total and 180 per entry. The deviation is also RECORDED WITH A REASON, not undiscovered: prompt-builder.ts:107-113 cites Claude's figure explicitly -- "Claude truncates a skill's `description` (plus `when_to_use`) at 1,536 characters in its own listing, but that is a per-entry cap against a much larger listing budget; here one verbose skill must not be able to consume the whole block, so an entry gets one line" -- and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md states it as a Global Constraint (:64-67: the listing "must be bounded by a stated budget, and the budget must be a constant with a comment saying what it costs, not a magic number"), with a measured cost table at :580-590. The driver is architectural and fork-specific: the listing rides Pi's CACHED system prefix and is paid on every request of every session (prompt-builder.ts:99-104), which is also why a fixed constant was chosen over a context-window fraction. It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) -- it is a plan-recorded design decision instead.
verdict.correctedState: Nessy DOES implement a bounded skill listing, in `PromptBuilder.buildSkillListingPart()` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:403-447): a whole-listing budget of `SKILL_LISTING_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` characters (:105, enforced :433, with a truthful "(N more skills not listed)" overflow line :441-444) and a per-entry description cap of `SKILL_LISTING_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS = 180` (:113, applied by `boundedListingText` :126-131). `capability-catalog.ts:108`'s 512-char `clampedText(input.description, ...)` belongs to a DIFFERENT subsystem -- the Pi capability/tool catalog behind `mcp__tool_search`, whose kinds are builtin/session/plugin/mcp/app and include no skills -- and is not the skill listing path. The genuine residual difference is narrower than claimed and is a recorded design decision, not an oversight: (a) the budget is a fixed 4,000-character constant rather than 1% of the model's context window, chosen deliberately because the listing sits inside Pi's cached system prefix and is paid on every request (prompt-builder.ts:99-104; plan 2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md:64-67 requires "a constant with a comment saying what it costs"); (b) it is not user-tunable -- `skillListingBudgetFraction`, `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET` and `skillListingMaxDescChars` have no reader anywhere in the repo (verified with NUL-safe `grep -ran`); (c) our per-entry cap is 180 characters, tighter than Claude's 1,536, and prompt-builder.ts:107-113 states the reason (one verbose skill must not consume the whole block); (d) overflow drops WHOLE ENTRIES in key order and reports the count, where Claude drops DESCRIPTIONS by least-invoked priority and keeps every name. `MAX_DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 1_536` (skills/storage.ts:81) correctly mirrors Claude's number for its own separate purpose: bounding a description derived from the SKILL.md body.

results.claim: Four frontmatter fields govern where and how a skill runs: `context: fork`, `background` (default `true` for a fork as of v2.1.218), `hooks` scoped to the skill's lifecycle, and `shell: bash|powershell` for inline command blocks.
results.quote: Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation.
results.ourState: All four are explicitly parsed-and-dropped: `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` maps `context` → 'skills do not run in a forked subagent context here', `background` → "it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented", `hooks` → 'per-skill hook scopes are not implemented', `shell` → 'inline shell blocks always run under bash'. The list is deliberate and documented in-file; a skill that sets `context: fork` runs inline in the main conversation instead of in an isolated subagent, which is a behaviour inversion rather than a no-op.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; nothing refutes the finding. (1) VERBATIM: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md` (933 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 547 reads in full: "Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. It won't have access to your conversation history." The quoted sentence is the first of three on that line and the two that follow reinforce rather than reverse it. The other three fields are in the frontmatter reference table: `:271` `background` — "Only applies with `context: fork`. Set to `false` to wait ... Default: `true`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later."; `:272` `hooks` — "Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle."; `:274` `shell` — "Shell to use for !`command` and ```! blocks in this skill. Accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`." The claimed behaviour is accurate on every field, including the v2.1.218 default. (2) CITED LINE: packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:246 declares `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` and :247-:250 carry the four mappings word for word as claimed ('skills do not run in a forked subagent context here'; "it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented"; 'per-skill hook scopes are not implemented'; 'inline shell blocks always run under bash'). The in-file comment block at :223-:245 states the reasoning, so the finding does not misrepresent our state. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — the consequence was verified separately from the identifier. Down: the map's only consumer is validation.ts:352, which emits an author-facing WARNING from `skill_validate`; nothing else reads it. `rg -na` across packages/ and apps/ finds no read of a skill-frontmatter `context` key anywhere — not in packages/shared/src/skills/{types,storage}.ts, not in packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts, not in the Claude plugin format adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts maps no skill `context`). Up: the sibling-subsystem trap is present and does NOT rescue the row. This repo does have a fork mechanism (`FORK_AGENT_NAME = 'fork'`, packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:208; R29a/R29b, docs/architecture/fork-subagents.md, /subtask), but it is the Agent-tool/`/subtask` conversation fork that INHERITS the parent conversation — the opposite of skills.md:547's fresh, history-less subagent — and no skill frontmatter routes into it. The neighbouring `agent` field IS implemented, which is exactly why the group looks supported, but base-agent.ts:2540 `applySkillInvocationGrant` uses it as an agent CEILING on the invoking turn (`setSkillInvocationAgentCeiling`, throws 'Invoked skill agent unavailable'), not as skills.md:270's fork target. So the consequence holds: a SKILL.md carrying `context: fork` is expanded inline into the main conversation with full history, where Claude would run it as an isolated subagent. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 — none of the nine concerns skill frontmatter. It is, however, a recorded deliberate decision one level down: worklist §5 U-E asked for 'warn instead of allowlist' and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-e.md:9 and :125-:138 record the ruling **warn** (commit 55b711ce), with `hooks` and `background` already costed and deliberately not half-built in R30c. That makes the gap deliberate and documented — which the finding already says — but not closed, and not a §3 do-not-fix entry. Not a Nessy product difference either: no subscription flow, gateway or rebranding is involved. Only wording quibbles: the fields are not 'parsed' into anything (SkillMetadataSchema is .passthrough(); they are warned about and dropped), and 'behaviour inversion' overstates it slightly — dropping the field yields the same inline behaviour a fieldless skill would get, so the divergence is a missing isolation guarantee rather than an inverted one.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with two wording corrections. `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:246-251) lists `context`, `background`, `hooks` and `shell` with exactly the four reasons quoted; its only consumer is validation.ts:352, which turns each into an author-facing WARNING from `skill_validate` ("'<key>' is a documented field this runtime does not implement — it will be ignored"). The fields are not parsed into any runtime value — SkillMetadataSchema is `.passthrough()` — and no code anywhere reads a skill-frontmatter `context`. The repo's `fork` (FORK_AGENT_NAME, definitions.ts:208; /subtask, R29a/R29b) is a conversation-INHERITING Agent-tool fork, the opposite of skills.md:547's history-less subagent, and no skill frontmatter routes into it; the neighbouring `agent` field is implemented as an agent ceiling on the invoking turn (base-agent.ts:2540), not as skills.md:270's fork target. Consequence: a skill setting `context: fork` is expanded inline into the main conversation with full history instead of running isolated — a missing isolation guarantee (same as a fieldless skill), which is more precise than calling it a behaviour inversion. Deliberate and recorded at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-e.md:9,:125-138 (ruling **warn**, commit 55b711ce; `hooks`/`background` costed in R30c) — but not one of the nine §3 owner decisions, so the gap is open, not closed.

results.claim: A skill in a nested `.claude/skills/` below the working directory loads lazily under a directory-qualified name when Claude touches a file in that subtree, and both variants stay available when names clash.
results.quote: The nested one appears under a directory-qualified name, `apps/web:deploy`.
results.ourState: Not implemented. Skill discovery walks `.claude/skills` at the working directory and its ANCESTORS (`skillRecords(join(dir, PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR), projectScope, \`d${depth}\`, …)`), which satisfies the parent-directory half, but there is no descendant scan, no lazy load on file touch, and no directory-qualified naming — `grep -ran "directory-qualified\|qualified name"` under `packages/` returns nothing relevant. A monorepo package's own skills are unreachable unless the session starts in that package.

verdict.why: All three checks pass, so the gap survives. (1) The quote is VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md` line 128 reads exactly `* The nested one appears under a directory-qualified name, `apps/web:deploy`.` The whole surrounding block reinforces rather than reverses it: line 122 (`Skills also load from nested `.claude/skills/` directories below your working directory. When Claude reads or edits a file in a subdirectory, skills from that subdirectory's `.claude/skills/` become available.`), line 124 (`If a nested skill shares a name with another skill, both stay available.`), line 132 (`Typing `/deploy` runs the project-root skill. Type the qualified name `/apps/web:deploy` to run the nested variant explicitly.`), line 134 (unqualified invocation appends the directory-qualified variant list), and the §`Discovery from parent and nested directories` restatement at line 152 (`Skills in nested `.claude/skills/` directories below your starting directory aren't loaded at startup. They load the first time Claude reads or edits a file inside that subdirectory`). (2) The cited line is accurate. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:1063-1066` is `const layers = ancestorsUpTo(workingDirectory, context.projectRoot); layers.forEach((dir, depth) => { records.push(...withTier(skillRecords(join(dir, PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR), projectScope, `d${depth}`, projectRealRoot), 'portable')); });`, and `ancestorsUpTo` (`:730`) walks strictly UPWARD (`current = dirname(current)`) — parents only, never children. The five `skillRecords(` call sites in the file (`:903` `~/.agents/skills`, `:904` `<configDir>/skills`, `:949` workspace `skills`, `:1016` `.nessy-agent/skills`, `:1065` the ancestor walk) are the complete set; none takes a descendant directory. (3) One layer up and one layer down both check out, including the two named traps. UP: the fork DOES have a lazy, file-touch-triggered delivery channel — `base-agent.ts:1152 getPathScopedRulePreToolUseContext` composes `cache.pathScopedRules + cache.pathGatedSkills + nestedInstructionProbe()` and dispatches activations on every file-touching tool call — but its three consumers are path-scoped rules, `paths:`-gated skills ALREADY in the inventory, and nested INSTRUCTION files (`activateNestedInstructionFiles` -> `discoverNestedInstructionFiles`, whose loop iterates `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES` only, `native-sources.ts:846`). So the exact mechanism the doc describes exists in this repo for AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and was deliberately not extended to skill directories. Nothing upstream already handles it: the consequence is real, verified separately from the identifier. DOWN / sibling-subsystem trap: `grep -rain 'directory-qualified|qualified name|apps/web:deploy'` over `packages/` returns only unrelated hits — `native-sources.ts:250 qualifiedKey()` is an internal dedupe key (`kind::scope::workspaceId::projectKey::discriminator::logicalName`), never a model- or user-facing skill name; `TurnCard.tsx:709` 'qualified name (workspaceId:slug)' is the WORKSPACE-scoped naming subsystem, not directory-scoped; `automations/types.ts:427` is MCP tool naming. Distinct subsystems, so no false refutation there. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated entries in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) touches skill discovery, and no plan or audit row records a decision to skip nested skills — the only other repo mention is `2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:567`, which records the doc behaviour as unimplemented, not as declined. Not a rebrand or product-scope difference either: this is discovery topology, unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows or the corporate-gateway targeting.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed gap, with one wording fix to the original 'our state' and one mitigation it omitted. FIX: the ancestor walk is over the FORK's own skill directories, not `.claude/skills`. `PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR = '.agents/skills'` (`packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts:37`), plus `.nessy-agent/skills` at the working directory (`native-sources.ts:1016`); `.claude/skills` is never read as a project skill source anywhere in the repo (the fork reads `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.claude/rules` beside its own, but not `.claude/skills`) — a separate, rebrand-adjacent divergence that does not affect this row's verdict. The substantive claim is otherwise exact: `skillRecords` is called on ancestors only (`ancestorsUpTo`, `native-sources.ts:730`, walks via `dirname`), there is no descendant scan, no first-touch lazy skill load, and no directory-qualified skill name — `qualifiedKey` (`:250`) is an internal record key and `TurnCard.tsx:709`'s `workspaceId:slug` is a different subsystem. Consequence verified independently and holds: a monorepo package's own `.agents/skills` or `.nessy-agent/skills` is invisible unless the session's working directory is at or below that package. MITIGATION the original omitted: a root-level skill can still be scoped to a subtree via the `paths:` frontmatter field, which IS implemented end to end (`native-sources.ts:301 skillPaths` -> `resolver.ts:1017/1664` -> `base-agent.ts:1161 cache.pathGatedSkills` -> lazy activation on file touch). That covers 'this skill applies when working in apps/web' but not 'apps/web owns its own skill directory', so the gap stands. The nearest existing machinery to extend is `discoverNestedInstructionFiles` + `nestedInstructionProbe`, which already implements the identical parent/nested split for instruction files.

results.claim: Auto memory under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` and claude.ai MCP connectors load regardless of `settingSources`, and each has a named opt-out that the host must set.
results.quote: Because the inputs above are read regardless of `settingSources`, an SDK process can pick up host-level configuration and per-directory memory.
results.ourState: `buildClaudeSessionOptions` sets `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` and nothing else. None of `autoMemoryEnabled`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` or `strictMcpConfig` appears anywhere in the repo (repo-wide `grep -ran` excluding node_modules returns zero). Consequences for this fork specifically: a Claude-backend session writes memories into `~/.claude/projects/`, outside Nessy's config dir and outside its capability inventory; and when the opt-in Claude Pro/Max login is used, the user's claude.ai MCP connectors attach to the session without passing Nessy's MCP source approval, which `mcpServers: {}` explicitly does not suppress.

verdict.why: Doc sentence CONFIRMED verbatim at line 100 of claude-code-features.md, inside a <Warning> whose subject is multi-tenant isolation. The rest of the finding does not survive. (1) WRONG FUNCTION NAME: there is no `buildClaudeSessionOptions` in this repo; the function at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308 is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions`, a deliberate three-option TURN-shape slice (systemPrompt / settingSources / optional child maxTurns), not the session options object. Same misnomer already recorded in the f057 verdict. Cited line :301 is the `}` closing `systemPrompt`; `settingSources` is :305. (2) THE ABSENCE GREP IS FALSE AS STATED. `grep -ranE 'autoMemoryEnabled|CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY|disableClaudeAiConnectors|ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS|strictMcpConfig' . | grep -v node_modules` returns 5 hits, not zero. Two of them are RECORDED OWNER DECISIONS in docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93 'What we do not implement': claude.ai connectors + `disableClaudeAiConnectors` are categorised `inapplicable` ('We have no claude.ai account-side MCP connectors. Nessy's connector Sources are materialized from PLUGIN manifests ... and have no claude.ai origin to suppress'), and `--mcp-config`/`--strict-mcp-config` filtering is likewise `inapplicable` ('We have no such CLI flags'). Auto memory is a tracked queue row, not an unknown gap: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1670-1676 item 12 already names `autoMemoryEnabled`, `autoMemoryDirectory` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` as a subsystem to cover. Only `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` is genuinely absent everywhere. (3) THE LOAD-BEARING CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, ONE LAYER UP -- the repo's textbook 'identifier unwired, consequence already handled upstream' shape. The claim is that 'a Claude-backend session writes memories into ~/.claude/projects/, outside Nessy's config dir'. It does not. packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:221-226 (`workspaceClaudeConfigDir`) + :254-255 (`buildClaudeSubprocessEnv`) set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to `<CONFIG_DIR>/workspaces/<workspaceId>/claude-config` for every Claude SDK subprocess, assigned AFTER envOverrides so an ambient host value cannot win. It is live, not dead code: `getDefaultOptions` (options.ts:276) is the only SDK options builder and it calls it, and SessionManager.ts:11840 and :18699 both put `NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID: managed.workspace.id` into envOverrides on the real session path (guarded by packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/workspace-claude-config-dir.test.ts). Per env-vars.md:356 `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` overrides '(default: `~/.claude`). All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path', and memory.md:356 puts auto memory at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` -- i.e. under that same directory. So auto memory lands at `~/.nessy-agent/workspaces/<id>/claude-config/projects/<project>/memory/`: inside Nessy's config dir, and additionally isolated PER WORKSPACE, which is stricter than the CLI default the doc describes. The doc's own multi-tenant advice is 'run each tenant in its own filesystem' -- which is materially what the per-Workspace config dir already does; the CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY half of that advice addresses cross-tenant leakage that per-Workspace redirection has already removed. (4) Product-shape context: `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` defaults OFF, so the Claude Pro/Max card is absent from default builds -- the claim concedes the opt-in but the residual is smaller than framed.
verdict.correctedState: The cited symbol is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308), not `buildClaudeSessionOptions`; it is a turn-shape slice and settingSources is at :305, not :301. It does spell settingSources as ['user','project','local'] (documented as equivalent to omitting it), and none of the five named opt-outs is set in code. But the finding's absence grep is wrong (5 non-node_modules hits, including two recorded owner decisions), and its primary consequence is wrong. AUTO MEMORY: refuted. options.ts:221-226/254-255 point CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at <CONFIG_DIR>/workspaces/<id>/claude-config for every Claude SDK subprocess, wired live via getDefaultOptions:276 and SessionManager:11840/:18699 (NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID). Since auto memory lives under the config dir (memory.md:356 + env-vars.md:356), memories are written to ~/.nessy-agent/workspaces/<id>/claude-config/projects/<project>/memory/ -- inside Nessy's config dir and isolated per Workspace, stricter than the CLI default. STRICTMCPCONFIG and DISABLECLAUDEAICONNECTORS: recorded owner decisions, docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:93 categorises both `inapplicable`. AUTOMEMORYENABLED / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY: already a tracked parity-audit row (2026-07-25 audit item 12), not an unknown gap. The only residual worth carrying forward, materially narrower than claimed: when the opt-in Claude Pro/Max OAuth flow supplies CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (llm-connections.ts:1057) -- a claude.ai login token, not a `claude setup-token` token -- the doc says claude.ai account connectors would attach and that mcpServers: {} does not suppress them. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does NOT mitigate this, because connectors are fetched account-side rather than from the config dir, and ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS is the one identifier genuinely absent repo-wide. This is unverified by live evidence and applies only to a build with NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE enabled (default OFF); it is a small hardening item (set ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false in buildClaudeSubprocessEnv), not the isolation defect described.

results.claim: With `settingSources` including `"project"`, hooks from the workspace's own `.claude/settings.json` execute inside the SDK session with no extra configuration.
results.quote: If you already have hooks in your project's `.claude/settings.json` and you set `settingSources: ["project"]`, those hooks run automatically in the SDK with no extra configuration.
results.ourState: We opt into `'project'` and `'local'` unconditionally, so a cloned repository's `.claude/settings.json` hooks run in a Claude-backend session. Nessy has its own project-trust gate for exactly this class of content — `native-sources.ts:995` reads project resources only when `context.projectTrustState === 'trusted'` — but that gate governs the Nessy capability runtime, not the Claude SDK subprocess, which reads the same files independently. The two trust boundaries disagree for the same directory.

verdict.why: REFUTED AS A DOC DIVERGENCE, though the underlying security observation is real and was already on record. (1) QUOTE: verbatim, line 190 of the fetched .md. The line is two sentences; the first ('Both types execute during the same hook lifecycle.') does not reverse it. (2) EVIDENCE LINE: drifted. claude-agent.ts:301 is the closing brace of the systemPrompt object; the actual `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']` is line 305, inside buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions. Content confirmed, anchor stale (older plans anchored :301 too). (3) THE REFUTATION: this page is not violated - it is satisfied. Line 84 of the same page says 'Omitting `settingSources` is equivalent to ["user", "project", "local"]', and the code comment at claude-agent.ts:302-304 says exactly that: 'Omitting this loads all three sources (CLI defaults). Spelling out the same three keeps today's behavior - including CLAUDE.md discovery, which needs project - while making the choice visible instead of implicit.' We implement the documented default verbatim, and the finding's own 'our state' text concedes that project hooks run. There is no gap against this page; the row is classified 'gap' but names no behaviour the page specifies and we lack. What it actually describes is a Nessy-internal inconsistency between two trust subsystems, which this page neither specifies nor governs. (4) ALREADY RECORDED: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-phase4-findings.md:347-350 states the identical seam under 'Two doors this unit does not close, both recorded rather than faked' - 'we pass settingSources: [user,project,local] to that SDK, so an opened repository's own .claude/settings.local.json can set outputStyle and the SDK honours it inside the preset, whatever our resolver decides. The trust gate this unit added covers our resolver and not the SDK's.' It is carried into the generated deviation register (2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:237) via the output-style-contract plan. Same door, sibling symptom (outputStyle instead of hooks). It is NOT one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 - I read all nine and none is this. (5) CONSEQUENCE, VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, AND IT HOLDS - so I do not refute on that ground: resolveSpawnCwd (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) prefers session.sdkCwd, and sessions/storage.ts:200 sets `sdkCwd = options?.workingDirectory ?? getSessionDirPath(...)`, so for a project session the SDK subprocess cwd IS the opened repository. Nessy's own gate is real and does cover the same file: native-sources.ts:995 opens the trusted-only branch, and :1051-1059 reads `.claude/settings.json` / `.claude/settings.local.json` as project-scope 'permission' records inside it. And the upstream gate that could have made the consequence false does not: I disassembled the installed native binary (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude). `$D()` builds the allowed-source list from the settingSources allowlist plus flagSettings/policySettings with no trust check; `kvl()` collects `hooks` from [userSettings, projectSettings, localSettings] filtered only by `allowManagedHooksOnly`; and Claude Code's own workspace-trust predicate short-circuits in SDK mode - `function fve(){if(kr())return!0;return Ip()}` with `function kr(){return!Nt.isInteractive}`, so hasTrustDialogAccepted never gates a non-interactive subprocess. The trust-boundary disagreement is therefore genuine. (6) TWO SCOPING CORRECTIONS the finding overstates: it is project sessions only - a workspace-only session gets sdkCwd = Nessy's per-session directory, and the page (line 86) says project settings.json and hooks load only from <cwd>/.claude/ with no parent-directory fallback, so no repository hooks load there; and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE defaults OFF, which since SDK 0.2.113 means the native claude binary is not bundled, so the Claude backend cannot spawn at all in a default packaged build.
verdict.correctedState: Not a divergence from agent-sdk/claude-code-features.md. buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305, not :301) passes settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local'] - byte-identical to the default the same page documents at line 84 - with a comment recording the choice. Filesystem hooks from a project's .claude/settings.json consequently run in the SDK subprocess exactly as the page says they will; that is conformance, not a gap. The real content is a Nessy-internal inconsistency, and it was already recorded before this sweep: our project-trust gate (native-sources.ts:995, reading .claude/settings.json at :1051-1059 only when projectTrustState === 'trusted') governs the Nessy capability resolver, while the Claude SDK subprocess reads the same files itself with no trust check - verified in the installed native binary, where the source allowlist carries no trust predicate and Claude's own hasTrustDialogAccepted gate short-circuits to trusted whenever the session is non-interactive. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-phase4-findings.md:347-350 states this same door for the sibling outputStyle symptom, and the deviation register carries it. Scope is narrower than claimed: project sessions only (a workspace-only session's sdkCwd is a Nessy-owned directory, and project hooks have no parent-directory fallback), and the Claude backend is off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE), which omits the native binary the subprocess needs.

results.claim: File checkpointing must be turned on per-session through the SDK option; when it is not, the session performing a rewind has no checkpoint data and the rewind cannot restore anything.
results.quote: The SDK sets the `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING` environment variable internally only when `enable_file_checkpointing` (Python) or `enableFileCheckpointing` (TypeScript) is enabled on the session performing the rewind; the bare CLI never sets it.
results.ourState: `enableFileCheckpointing` occurs 0 times in `claude-agent.ts` (verified with `grep -ac`, so a NUL byte cannot be hiding it). The SDK query options object built around `claude-agent.ts:1245` passes `cwd`, `includePartialMessages`, `tools`, `permissionMode`, `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`, `hooks` and the turn-shape options — never `enableFileCheckpointing`. Nessy's own `createFileCheckpoint` has only two non-test callers (Pi's local tool runtime and the Nestor Cloud executor); Claude's Write/Edit/NotebookEdit calls all execute inside the SDK subprocess, so nothing on the Claude path writes a checkpoint.

verdict.why: Doc sentence verified verbatim at line 767 of the curl'd page (whole line read; the surrounding troubleshooting block does not reverse it). The cited repo facts are all accurate: grep -ac enableFileCheckpointing packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts -> 0 (the file really does carry NUL bytes, so -a mattered), grep -ac rewindFiles -> 0, the SDK Options literal opens at claude-agent.ts:1213 and never names either symbol, file-checkpoints.ts:571 is createFileCheckpoint, and its only two non-test callers are packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1644 and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:155. The finding is still refuted on two independent grounds. (1) WRONG CONTRACT / WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The quoted sentence governs the SDK's own rewind API - Query.rewindFiles() and claude -p --rewind-files - and the 'File rewinding is not enabled' error they raise. Nessy never calls that API (rewindFiles occurs 0 times repo-wide outside docs). Nessy's rewind is an independent engine: revertFileCheckpoint / rewindToMessage (SessionManager.ts:13687, :13776) read OUR manifest at <sessionPath>/file_checkpoints/, never the SDK store. So the missing option is not the cause of an empty Claude rewind, and setting it would not change one observable byte - it would populate a store no Nessy code reads. This is trap #3 from inert-worklist section 4 in its causal form: the identifier really is unwired, but the stated causal chain is false. (2) DATED RECORDED DECISION WITH A WRITTEN REASON - not one of the nine in inert-worklist section 3, but a plan-level one, which AGENTS.md treats as exactly the same kind of artifact ('A plan is where a deviation's reason lives'). docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-claude-backend-turn-contract.md Task 6 ran this precise investigation and concluded 'Scope chosen: none. Stopping and reporting, per the plan's stop condition,' naming two blockers that make Query.rewindFiles() unreachable: claude-agent.ts:2345 nulls this.currentQuery in chatImpl's finally while rewind is a between-turns action after strictDrainSessionForMutation, so no subprocess exists to receive the SDKControlRewindFilesRequest; and rewindFiles takes an SDK user-message UUID that nothing on the Claude path captures. The plan then lists 'Setting enableFileCheckpointing: true on its own' as deliberately NOT done, because with no reachable caller it is a speculative unused option. docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md:124 and :130 carry the same verdict as shipped architecture record. The underlying product gap is real but is already an open, tracked row, not a new divergence: 2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md P4 (Tier 2), which also corrects the harm this finding inherits - the SDK store lands in ~/.claude/file-history/, not the working dir.
verdict.correctedState: Nessy does not use the Claude Agent SDK's file-checkpointing or its rewindFiles() control request at all; both identifiers are absent from claude-agent.ts and from the whole repo outside docs. The genuine consequence, already recorded and open, is narrower than the finding states and is not caused by the missing option: because a Claude-backend session's Write/Edit/NotebookEdit run inside the SDK subprocess, our beforeDispatch never fires, so no entries exist in <sessionPath>/file_checkpoints/. rewindToMessage({restoreFiles:true}) then truncates the transcript and returns success with restoredCheckpoints: 0, and the ungated 'Revert last file edit' menu item (SessionMenu.tsx:237) returns 'No file checkpoint found'. results.claim: A background subagent that stops producing output is caught by a stall watchdog, which aborts it, marks the task failed and surfaces the error to the parent with any partial result.
results.quote: For background subagents only, `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` sets a stall watchdog that fires when a `run_in_background` subagent stops producing output; it is not a total-runtime deadline.
results.ourState: No stall or idle watchdog exists for background subagents. `runBackground`/`runAllAndSeal` is bounded only by the abort signal; there is no output-idle timer. Repo-wide `grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog'` over `packages/shared/src`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src` and `packages/server-core/src` returns no match, while the same sweep for `NESSY_*TIMEOUT*` returns `NESSY_ASK_USER_TIMEOUT_MS`, `NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` and `NESSY_BROWSER_OPEN_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS` — so the grep is a working positive control, not a false absence.

verdict.why: The quoted sentence EXISTS VERBATIM (hosting.md line 341, 'Known limitations' table, row 'No per-subagent wall-clock deadline'; whole line read, the second half does not reverse it). The cited file:line is also real: subagent-tool.ts:605-616 is the background-dispatch return and the Pi orchestrator has no output-idle timer there. The finding still fails on four counts. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the exact trap named in inert-worklist section 4 item 4. agent-sdk/hosting.md governs the Claude Agent SDK, and CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS is a knob of the Claude Code binary itself. This fork vendors that binary and the implementation is live inside it: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude contains 'g=je.CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS||600000' inside the async-agent loop (adjacent to turnStartTime, setMode("responding"), shouldNotifyOwner). Nessy does not scrub it: claude-agent.ts:915 deletes only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. So on the backend this page is about, the stall watchdog is present and honoured with its 600000 ms default. The consequence ('no stall or idle watchdog exists for background subagents') is therefore false for the subsystem the doc names, and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts is Nessy's own Pi orchestration, not an Agent SDK run_in_background subagent. (2) THE CLAIMED POSITIVE CONTROL IS FALSE. The finding asserts grep -ran 'STALL|stallTimeout|watchdog' over packages/shared/src, packages/pi-agent-server/src and packages/server-core/src 'returns no match'. It does match, in a named directory: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6076 ('truly hung subprocesses are caught by the stdio death watchdog') and, substantively, packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:230-419, which implements a real two-timer connect watchdog with an explicit IDLE arm (createConnectWatchdog(connectIdleMs, connectCeilingMs), watchdog.kick(), Promise.race([client.connect(transport), watchdog.promise])). An absence claim whose own grep is demonstrably wrong does not stand. (3) THE DOC'S PRIMARY PRESCRIPTION IS IMPLEMENTED. The row is a documented LIMITATION of the SDK, not a required feature, and its first sentence is 'Cap each subagent with maxTurns in its AgentDefinition.' Nessy carries maxTurns end to end: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:401/418-419/451 validates it (positive integer, string-or-number), packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:163 carries it onto the descriptor, and spawner.ts:571-574 forwards it with the comment 'The host enforces maxTurns and clamps permissionMode against the parent'. So the named mitigation is built on the Pi path too, and the claim that the run is 'bounded only by the abort signal' is wrong on top of maxTurns, stop_task and the capability-generation teardown reachable through registerBackgroundChildTask's BackgroundTaskRegistry entry. (4) THE CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR EMBELLISHES THE DOC. The page says only that the watchdog 'fires'; 'aborts it, marks the task failed and surfaces the error to the parent with any partial result' appears nowhere on the page. Finally, this is not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3, and it is not a deliberate product difference (subscription-flow drop, gateway targeting, NESSY_ rename) - it is refuted on subsystem misattribution plus a false absence, not on scope. The coverage map already verdicts agent-sdk/hosting as green, 'all built' via R6.
verdict.correctedState: The Claude Agent SDK's own stall watchdog is present in this fork, because the fork vendors the Claude Code binary that implements it: node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude reads CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS with a 600000 ms default in its async-agent loop, and Nessy passes the environment through untouched (claude-agent.ts:915 deletes only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN). The doc row's primary prescription, maxTurns in AgentDefinition, is implemented on the Pi path as well: validated at packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:401/418-419/451, carried at packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:163, forwarded and host-enforced per spawner.ts:571-574. What is genuinely absent is narrower and belongs to a different subsystem: Nessy's own Pi orchestrator (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:585-617 plus background-child-task.ts) has no output-idle timer of its own and no NESSY_-prefixed analogue of the env var, so a Pi background subagent that goes silent without exhausting maxTurns is bounded only by maxTurns, stop_task and the abort signal.
