results.claim: With the `project` setting source enabled, project instructions are discovered at either `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` in the working directory.
results.quote: The SDK reads CLAUDE.md when the matching setting source is enabled: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory, and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
results.ourState: The project instruction-file set is `PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md']`, joined against each ancestor/nested directory only. `.claude/` is read for `rules/` (`CLAUDE_RULES_DIR`) and for permission files, but never for `CLAUDE.md`: `grep -ran "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, 'CLAUDE|'\.claude', 'CLAUDE"` over `packages` returns nothing, and the only two hits for the literal `.claude/CLAUDE.md` in `.ts` files are prose comments (capabilities/types.ts:199, base-agent.ts:972). A repo whose instructions live at `.claude/CLAUDE.md` contributes no project context.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the gap survives, with two corrections to the original 'our state'. (1) QUOTE IS VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts.md` line 54 begins exactly: "The SDK reads CLAUDE.md when the matching setting source is enabled: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory, and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`." The rest of that multi-sentence line reinforces rather than reverses it: "Default `query()` options enable both sources, so CLAUDE.md loads automatically... CLAUDE.md loading is controlled by setting sources, not by the `claude_code` preset." Line 360 restates it. And this is NOT an SDK-only quirk: `memory.md:60` (the load-order table) gives Project instructions as "`./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`" and `memory.md:69` says "A project CLAUDE.md can be stored in either `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`", so the CLI contract is the same. (2) CITED LINES ARE ACCURATE. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:82` is `export const PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md', 'CLAUDE.local.md'];` and `:845` is `for (const fileName of PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES) { ... const absolutePath = join(dir, fileName);`. Every one of the five production consumers joins a bare name onto a DIRECTORY, never onto `.claude`: `:845` (nested), `:987` (workspace root), `:1077` (ancestor walk, `join(dir, name)`), `:1088` (working directory, `join(workingDirectory, name)`). `grep -ran "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` shows the only path-building use is `:1056`, `join(workingDirectory, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, name)` for `settings.json`/`settings.local.json`; `CLAUDE_RULES_DIR` (`:727`) is `.claude/rules`. No NUL-byte blind spot: every absence grep used `-a`. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. A probe calling the production entry point `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` on a trusted temp project holding BOTH `<root>/CLAUDE.md` and `<root>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` returned exactly one instruction record (`logicalName: 'CLAUDE.md'`, `sourcePath: <root>/CLAUDE.md`) and zero records of any kind whose JSON mentions `.claude`. The control fires, the subject does not. The legacy route is the same: `readProjectContextFile(root)` from `packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts` returned `null` for the `.claude/CLAUDE.md`-only fixture (`CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS` at `:31` is directory-level, and its user tier is `~/.nessy-agent`, `:136`). ONE LAYER UP / DOWN, both traps checked. UP: the lazy channel IS wired in production — `base-agent.ts:1162 nestedInstructionProbe()` -> `:1175 activateNestedInstructionFiles` -> `:1252 discoverNestedInstructionFiles` — so it is not an unwired identifier; but it is triggered by a file READ and delivers to message history, so it does not satisfy the launch-time `'project'`-source contract the quote describes. DOWN / sibling subsystem: `.claude/` IS read by this fork for three other things (`settings.json` and `settings.local.json` as permission records at `native-sources.ts:1050-1058`, and `.claude/rules/` as a memory tier at `:1110`), so naming the wrong subsystem is ruled out — the divergence is specifically the instruction-file location, inside a `.claude/` interop surface the fork otherwise implements. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated entries in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) touches instruction-file discovery, and `grep -ran '\.claude/CLAUDE\.md' docs/` finds no decision to decline the location — only `2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:536/545`, which scoped R28 to `.claude/rules/` and recorded `.claude/CLAUDE.md` as a documented `--add-dir` target, i.e. unimplemented rather than declined. NOT A REBRAND OR PRODUCT-SCOPE DIFFERENCE: the user tier's move to `~/.nessy`/`~/.nessy-agent` is the rebrand and is a separate matter; the project-scope `.claude/` directory is read verbatim elsewhere in the same function, and this has nothing to do with the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows or the corporate gateway.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed gap. Two corrections to the original wording. FIX 1 (grep detail): the literal `.claude/CLAUDE.md` has FIVE `.ts` hits, not two, and the base-agent one is at :980, not :972 — `capabilities/types.ts:199`, `agent/base-agent.ts:980`, `agent/memory/memory-store.ts:205`, plus tests `capabilities/__tests__/rules-scope-gating.test.ts:10` and `agent/__tests__/rules-unscoped-launch.test.ts:5`. All five are prose comments, so the substance is unchanged: no code path joins `.claude` to `CLAUDE.md`. FIX 2 (consequence overstated): 'contributes no project context' is true for the launch-time contract but not absolutely. There is one narrow, incidental path — the nested on-demand discovery treats `.claude` as an ordinary subdirectory, so `discoverNestedInstructionFiles(<root>/.claude/settings.json, <root>)` DOES return `<root>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (measured). That path fires only after the agent touches some file under `<cwd>/.claude/` in the same capability generation, delivers into the message history rather than the pinned block, is capped at `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILES = 8` files and `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 KiB` per file, and is not re-injected after compaction. Precise statement of the divergence: with the `project` setting source enabled, `<cwd>/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is never loaded at launch and never enters the pinned instruction block; it reaches context only incidentally, if and when a file under `<cwd>/.claude/` is read. Two adjacent facts the original omitted: an ANCESTOR directory's `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is never loaded at all (the `:1077` ancestor walk joins bare names onto each directory, and the nested walk covers only paths strictly below the cwd); and the `--add-dir` opt-in behind `NESSY_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_MEMORY` (`native-sources.ts:928-938`) loads only `<root>/.claude/rules` and `<root>/.agents/rules`, not `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — which contradicts the comment at `capabilities/types.ts:199` that says `--add-dir` loads `.claude/CLAUDE.md`. The smallest fix is to add `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (and, per memory.md, keep `CLAUDE.local.md` at the directory root) to the eager project-instruction join at `native-sources.ts:1077` and `:1088`.

results.claim: Setting the telemetry enable switch plus at least one exporter makes the agent export spans, metrics and structured log events over OTLP to a collector.
results.quote: Telemetry is off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and choose at least one exporter.
results.ourState: There is no telemetry emitter. `grep -ran 'startSpan|tracer|trace_id|traceparent|TRACEPARENT'` over `packages` and `apps` returns zero non-test hits, and no `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` or `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` reader exists. The only OTEL surface is a five-entry allowlist/classification of exporter-transport variables used by the managed-settings approval dialog, which passes them through without anything consuming them. `packages/shared/src/agent/runtime-telemetry.ts` is an in-process per-turn record, not an OTLP export. (The Claude backend inherits the process env, so an operator who exports the variables would get telemetry from the SDK's own `claude` subprocess; the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing.)

verdict.why: Doc sentence confirmed verbatim (observability.md:41, whole line; the trailing second sentence 'The most common configuration sends all three signals over OTLP HTTP to a collector.' does not reverse it). The cited evidence is real but the finding's central factual claims are false. (1) 'There is no telemetry emitter' is wrong: packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts is a full OTLP/HTTP metrics exporter (interval flush, shutdown drain, delta/cumulative temporality, nessy.token.usage + nessy.cost.usage sums) and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts is a full OTLP/HTTP logs exporter (batched resourceLogs, six-event closed set, HMAC-salted workspace/session hashes, one retry). (2) 'no CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY ... reader exists' is wrong: usage-metrics.ts:301-306 telemetryOptedIn() reads env.NESSY_ENABLE_TELEMETRY as primary and env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY as the compat alias, and it is the gate for BOTH signals (otlp-telemetry.ts:43,200). 'no OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER / OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER reader' is wrong: otelExporterDisabled() (usage-metrics.ts:318-325) reads both selectors and honours 'none' as a hard disable, called at usage-metrics.ts:336 and otlp-telemetry.ts:202. (3) The claim that the managed-settings allowlist passes OTEL vars through 'without anything consuming them' is the inference that fails: parseConfig in both exporters consumes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _HEADERS, _TIMEOUT and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL — four of the five allowlisted entries — plus the per-signal _METRICS_ENDPOINT/_LOGS_ENDPOINT overrides and _METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE. (4) Consequence check one layer up and one layer down: both are wired end to end, not inert. storage-runtime.ts:272-273 constructs them; SessionManager.recordUsageMetrics (:3004) is called from the single usage-event site at :18382 whose own comment says 'The one emission site every backend passes through ... Pi, the Claude SDK, Codex and Nestor Cloud all land here'; emitPiTelemetry (:2984) feeds the log exporter; shutdown drains at :19246; and both hosts pass them through (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:723, packages/server/src/index.ts:241). (5) The parenthetical 'the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing' is exactly backwards — Pi is the only runtime carrying BOTH signals, since the harness log exporter is deliberately Pi-gated (:2988) while metrics are deliberately not provider-gated. The coverage map already records this page as built (2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:184, row B2, green). Not an inert-worklist section 3 decision; the residual gaps are recorded deliberate fork decisions (bank-fork privacy posture in the usage-metrics header, NESSY_ prefix rename with Claude compat alias).
verdict.correctedState: Two of the three documented signals are implemented as real OTLP/HTTP exporters, gated on exactly the documented switch plus exporter selectors. Metrics: packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts — createUsageMetrics() built at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:273, fed for EVERY backend (Pi, Claude SDK, Codex, Nestor Cloud) at SessionManager.ts:18382 via recordUsageMetrics (:3004), interval flush plus shutdown drain. results.claim: A result message with `subtype: "success"` can still be a failure: `is_error` is true and `api_error_status` carries the HTTP status when the agent loop finished but the final API call errored.
results.quote: On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.
results.ourState: `adaptResult` resolves the terminal reason from `stop_reason` and `subtype` only: `msg.subtype === 'success' ? undefined : ...`. Neither `is_error` nor `api_error_status` is read anywhere on the Claude path (`grep -an 'is_error|api_error'` over `backend/claude/event-adapter.ts` matches only the assistant-message `error` field at :295 and the auth `msg.error` at :660; `claude-agent.ts` has no hit at all). A turn that ends `subtype: "success", is_error: true, api_error_status: 529` is emitted as `{ type: 'complete', usage }` with no `terminalReason` and no error event, i.e. indistinguishable from a clean success.

verdict.why: Quote is verbatim (python.md:1665, whole line reads '* `is_error`: `True` when the conversation ended in an error state. Always `True` on the `error_*` subtypes. On `subtype="success"` it is `True` when the final model request failed, meaning the agent loop completed but the last API call returned an error.'), and the IDENTIFIER half of the finding is true: adaptResult (event-adapter.ts:578-585) derives terminalReason from stop_reason + subtype only, and grep -a shows no read of is_error, api_error_status or terminal_reason anywhere on the Claude result path. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, which is exactly this repo's recurring false-positive shape: something one layer up already handled it. Disassembling the shipped CLI (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude) shows the success-result emitter derives BOTH flags from the last assistant message and nothing else: `if(vs.type==="assistant"){ ... Eo=Boolean(vs.isApiErrorMessage), wr=vs.apiErrorStatus??null }` then `yield{type:"result",subtype:"success",is_error:Eo,api_error_status:wr,...}`. That assistant message is built exclusively by the factory `tc({content,apiError,error,errorDetails})`, which sets `isApiErrorMessage:!0` AND `error:<SDKAssistantMessageError>`; `nRn` then stamps `r.apiErrorStatus=e.status`. Every one of the 44 `return tc({...})` branches supplies an error code (a 529 lands in `if(e instanceof es && e.status>=500)` -> `error:"server_error"`; the terminal fallbacks use `error:"unknown"`). The wire serializer `function*Fct` forwards it unconditionally: `yield{type:"assistant",message:r.message,parent_tool_use_id:null,session_id:kt(),uuid:r.uuid,error:r.error,...}`. So the very message that makes is_error true and carries api_error_status arrives at our adapter one message BEFORE the result, with `error` set, and adaptAssistant (event-adapter.ts:294-300) intercepts it first -- `if ('error' in message && message.error) { events.push(await this.callbacks.mapSDKError(...)); return; }` -- yielding a typed_error built by mapClaudeSdkAssistantError (claude-agent.ts:2660-2675, claude-sdk-error-mapper.ts:210). Covered by an existing test: claude-event-adapter.test.ts:231 'should handle SDK errors via callback' asserts assistant {error:'rate_limit'} -> typed_error. A 529 turn is therefore NOT 'indistinguishable from a clean success' and NOT emitted with 'no error event'. Not an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision (none of the nine touch this) and not a deliberate fork difference.
verdict.correctedState: Partially true but the stated consequence is wrong. TRUE: adaptResult (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:578-585) reads only stop_reason and subtype, so an api-error success result gets terminalReason undefined, and neither is_error, api_error_status nor terminal_reason is read anywhere on the Claude path. FALSE: that the turn is indistinguishable from a clean success. The shipped CLI sets is_error/api_error_status on a success result solely from the last assistant message's isApiErrorMessage/apiErrorStatus, and that same message is emitted on the wire with error:<SDKAssistantMessageError> ('server_error' for a 529 via the status>=500 branch); adaptAssistant intercepts it at event-adapter.ts:294-300 and pushes a typed_error via mapClaudeSdkAssistantError before the result ever arrives. The real residual gap is narrower and cosmetic-to-diagnostic: we lose the numeric HTTP status (api_error_status) and the complete event carries no terminalReason ('api_error') for that turn, so an api-error completion is labelled 'complete' alongside a user-visible typed_error rather than being marked terminal. Worth an enrichment (read api_error_status into the typed_error details and map terminal_reason==='api_error' onto terminalReason), not an error-surfacing fix.

results.claim: The store's `load()` and `list_subkeys()` calls during resume materialisation are bounded by a per-call timeout, defaulting to 60 seconds.
results.quote: Per-call timeout for `session_store.load()` and `list_subkeys()` during resume materialization, in milliseconds
results.ourState: Only `append` is timed out — `appendWithEnvelope` races the call against `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000`. The load path has no timeout at all: `restoreSessionFromMirror` does a bare `await store.load(...)`, and `restoreMissingMirroredSessions` calls it in a serial loop over every session directory during the pre-listing boot sweep. A mirror root on a stalled network mount therefore hangs session listing at startup indefinitely instead of failing after a bounded wait. (The quoted sentence is the `load_timeout_ms` row on agent-sdk/python.md; session-storage.md documents the same `load` call but does not restate the bound.)

verdict.why: Fails all three checks. (1) CITATION. The quoted sentence does not exist on the cited page: the word 'timeout' occurs ZERO times in all 306 lines of agent-sdk/session-storage.md (grep -aic 'timeout' = 0; 'per-call' = 0). It is verbatim on agent-sdk/python.md:868, a ClaudeAgentOptions field row, with a differently-worded TypeScript twin at agent-sdk/typescript.md:431 marked '*Alpha.*'. The finding self-discloses this, but a finding filed under slug agent-sdk/session-storage whose contract sentence lives on another page is the citation failure the protocol treats as refuting outright. session-storage.md imposes no timeout requirement of any kind. (2) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. typescript.md:431 reads: 'Timeout in milliseconds for each `sessionStore.load()` and `sessionStore.listSubkeys()` call during resume materialization. If the adapter doesn't settle within this window, the query fails instead of hanging. Ignored when `sessionStore` is not set.' That bounds the SDK calling ARBITRARY USER-SUPPLIED adapter code (S3/Redis/Postgres over the network) and its documented outcome is to FAIL THE QUERY. packages/shared/src/sessions/mirror/ is not that surface. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md:7 records the owner decision in the plan header: 'No shipped runtime consumes Claude's SDK option - the page is a design template, so the interface shape is portability guidance, not a compatibility surface', and the names were deliberately changed to SessionMirrorStore/MirrorSessionKey to avoid colliding with the local store-v2 SessionStore. There is exactly ONE adapter: config/session-mirror-settings.ts:37-38 throws 'unknown session mirror adapter' for any name but 'directory' (host.ts:76-78 carries the same note), so the pluggable-network-backend hazard class the bound exists for cannot be configured in this fork. (3) CONTRACT INVERSION. The documented behaviour on timeout is that the query FAILS. Our restore is deliberately the opposite and says so at restore.ts:76 and :90 - 'Never throws - a broken mirror must not break session open' - returning false. Adopting the documented bound verbatim would make a mirror stall fail session open, reversing a shipped intentional deviation. (4) THE list_subkeys HALF IS A DATED OWNER DECISION. 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 item 8: 'MirrorSessionKey.subpath + SessionMirrorStore.listSubkeys - 2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md, Task 4: subagent-transcript restore via listSubkeys is contract-ready in the adapters but has no host producer yet - the queue mirrors only the main session JSONL today ... (exactly the documented consequence of the missing half).' restore.ts never calls listSubkeys, so half the claimed behaviour has no call to bound, by recorded decision. (5) CONSEQUENCE OVERSTATED ON ITS OWN FACTS. The identifier claim is literally true - restore.ts:129 is a bare `await store.load(...)` and SessionManager.ts:7573 awaits restoreMissingMirroredSessions inside initialize() before initGate.markReady(), so a stall there would block IPC. But the claimed remedy does not deliver the claimed benefit for the claimed scenario: the only adapter reads via fs/promises.readFile (directory.ts:74) on a filesystem path, and on a hung NFS/SMB mount that pins a libuv threadpool thread in an uninterruptible kernel wait - a Promise.race would resolve the JS promise while the thread stays pinned, and with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4 every other fs op in the process stalls regardless. Blast radius is also narrower than stated: restore.ts:98 returns immediately when no sessionMirror is configured (the default, 'absent config = no mirror, zero overhead'), and restore.ts:111 skips every session whose local jsonl is present and readable, so the normal boot performs zero mirror reads.
verdict.correctedState: Accurate as an identifier observation, wrong as a doc divergence. agent-sdk/session-storage.md contains no timeout requirement (0 occurrences of 'timeout'); the quoted sentence is the Python SDK's ClaudeAgentOptions.load_timeout_ms row (python.md:868), whose TypeScript twin loadTimeoutMs is marked '*Alpha.*' (typescript.md:431) and bounds the SDK's calls into a USER-SUPPLIED SessionStore adapter, failing the query on expiry. Nessy has no such pluggable surface: session-mirror-settings.ts:37-38 fails closed on any adapter but 'directory', and the plan header (2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md:7) records that the SDK interface is 'portability guidance, not a compatibility surface'. Our restore contract is deliberately the inverse of the documented one - 'Never throws - a broken mirror must not break session open' (restore.ts:76). The list_subkeys half is inapplicable by dated owner decision (inert-worklist section 3 item 8: listSubkeys is contract-ready in the adapters with no host producer). What remains is a narrow, opt-in-only robustness note, not a parity gap: with sessionMirror configured on a stalling mount, the pre-listing sweep awaited in SessionManager.initialize():7573 could block startup - though a JS-level Promise.race would not actually unblock it, since the hang is an uninterruptible fs read pinning a libuv threadpool thread, not a slow in-JS network call.

results.claim: The SDK's resumable transcripts live under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so relocating that variable relocates the resume corpus.
results.quote: Sessions are stored under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl`, or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` if you set the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable, where `<encoded-cwd>` is the absolute working directory with every non-alphanumeric character replaced by `-` (so `/Users/me/proj` becomes `-Users-me-proj`).
results.ourState: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv sets env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to <workspaceRoot>/claude-config whenever NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID is present, with no migration of any pre-existing projects/ transcripts and no per-workspace fallback lookup. The function's own doc-comment enumerates the hazards as 'TWO HAZARDS :356 NAMES, BOTH CHECKED AND CLEAR' — credentials and settings — even though the env-vars sentence it quotes says 'All settings, session history, and plugins are stored under this path'. Session history is the third hazard and is not addressed.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:255 (`if (workspaceConfigDir) env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = workspaceConfigDir;`), hazard list at packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:196; no migration — `grep -ran "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" --include="*.ts" packages apps` returns only options.ts and plugins/data-paths.ts

verdict.why: DOC SENTENCE CONFIRMED VERBATIM, sessions.md line 272, inside a <Tip>. Reading the WHOLE line changes what it demands: the Tip opens 'If a `resume` call returns a fresh session instead of the expected history, the most common cause is a mismatched `cwd`.' and closes 'If your resume call runs from a different directory, the SDK looks in the wrong place. The session file also needs to exist on the current machine.' Its subject is the <encoded-cwd> half, not the config-dir half, and it prescribes no migration and no fallback lookup. Line 274, the next non-blank line, prescribes the mitigation this fork actually built: 'To resume sessions across machines or in serverless environments, mirror transcripts to shared storage with a SessionStore adapter.' CITED CODE CONFIRMED AS FACT: options.ts:255 is `if (workspaceConfigDir) env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = workspaceConfigDir;`, the hazard heading is at :196, and `grep -ran CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR --include=*.ts packages apps` returns only options.ts, plugins/data-paths.ts and tests. Every code fact in the finding is true. THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, ONE LAYER UP AND ONE LAYER DOWN -- four ways. (1) NO LOOKUP IS POSSIBLE TO OMIT. `workspaceClaudeConfigDir` (options.ts:221-226) is `join(getWorkspaceRootPath(workspaceId), 'claude-config')` -- a pure deterministic function of the Workspace id, mkdir'd on demand, assigned AFTER envOverrides so an ambient host value cannot win (guarded by agent/__tests__/workspace-claude-config-dir.test.ts:43-52). Within a Workspace the transcript is written and read at the identical path on every spawn. There is no per-Workspace state to fall back to; a 'fallback lookup' would have nothing to look up. Steady-state resume is unaffected. (2) THE FRAGILE HALF -- THE ONE THE DOC ACTUALLY WARNS ABOUT -- IS HANDLED WITH MORE MACHINERY THAN THE DOC DESCRIBES, NOT LESS. `sdkCwd` is pinned at session creation and never moves: claude-agent.ts:1260-1266 'Use sdkCwd for SDK session storage - this is set once at session creation and never changes. This ensures SDK can always find session transcripts regardless of workingDirectory changes'; SessionManager.ts:14319-14325 `preserveSdkCwd` -- 'Never move `sdkCwd`, whatever the session's message count ... that same launch directory is the ONLY thing a resume can fall back to when the worktree is gone ... would silently delete the anchor'; a fork carries the PARENT's sdkCwd (SessionManager.ts:9088-9091, claude-agent.ts:3053) precisely so 'cross-CWD branches (e.g., worktree <-> main repo) fail with No conversation found' does not happen; and `resolveSpawnCwd` (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) is a four-candidate, existence-checked fallback chain. That IS the per-session fallback lookup the finding says is missing, on the axis the doc names. (3) THE SDK JSONL IS NOT THIS FORK'S RESUME CORPUS OF RECORD, SO RELOCATING IT DOES NOT RELOCATE THE RESUME CORPUS. sessions/mirror/types.ts:5-7: 'Local disk is written FIRST and stays authoritative.' The user-visible transcript is `StoredSession.messages` in the workspace-partitioned v2 session store; that is what the UI renders and what a `SessionBundle` carries across machines. SessionManager.ts:18950-18953 proves the ownership on the move path: it regenerates `sdkCwd` for the target workspace because 'The source sdkCwd points to a path on the originating server which doesn't exist here', and ships `messages` in the bundle regardless -- i.e. the design already assumes the SDK jsonl does not travel. (4) A MISSED SDK TRANSCRIPT IS DETECTED AND RECOVERED, NOT SILENT. claude-agent.ts:1937-1966 detects the SDK's silent empty resume (`wasResuming && !receivedAssistantContent && !_isRetry`), clears sdkSessionId, calls `buildRecoveryContext()` (base-agent.ts:1944-1971) fed by SessionManager.ts:11913 `getRecoveryMessages` -- Nessy's OWN stored messages -- yields 'Restoring conversation context...' and retries. So the entire worst case of 'no migration' is a bounded, user-visible context truncation (last 6 messages, 1000 chars each) on the FIRST turn after upgrade for sessions that predate the redirect. Not loss of the resume corpus. THE 'THIRD HAZARD NOT ADDRESSED' CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE REPO'S OWN RECORDED VERIFICATION. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:166 already states '`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves storage off `~/.claude` (so the sweep must be config-dir-relative, and this is also B3's per-workspace `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` item)' -- the session-history consequence was written down at the moment the B3 item was specified, not overlooked. Same file :402 fact 12 repeats it from sessions.md. AND IT IS A RECORDED DECISION, NOT A DEFECT: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-isolation-hardening.md:82-95 Task 3 specifies the per-workspace redirect deliberately, in the shape plugins/data-paths.ts already used, with gate 'two workspaces do not see each other's config'. Per-Workspace session history IS the intent of that change -- a Workspace's sessions belonging to that Workspace is the product shape, so 'session history moves' is the feature, not an unhandled hazard. It is not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none matches), but it is a decision recorded in a plan, which the repo rule treats identically. RESIDUAL, AND IT IS A COMMENT NIT ONLY: env-vars.md:356 names four things (settings, session history, plugins, credentials); the doc-comment's 'TWO HAZARDS `:356` NAMES, BOTH CHECKED AND CLEAR' undercounts what the quoted sentence enumerates even though the two it omits are non-hazards here (session history moving per-Workspace is the intent; plugins were already redirected per-plugin by plugins/data-paths.ts:115/131). Also worth noting in passing: that plan has no `## Tracker` section, which the Editing Rules require. Neither is a behavioural divergence from the cited page.
verdict.correctedState: Not a divergence. The doc sentence is confirmed verbatim (sessions.md:272) and the fork does exactly what it describes: it sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so SDK transcripts live under it. The cited code facts are all true -- options.ts:255 sets it to <workspaceRoot>/claude-config from NESSY_WORKSPACE_ID, there is no migration of pre-existing ~/.claude/projects transcripts, and no config-dir fallback lookup -- but none of the three is a defect. (a) No fallback lookup is possible to omit: workspaceClaudeConfigDir (options.ts:221-226) is a pure deterministic function of the Workspace id, so within a Workspace the write path and the read path are the same path on every spawn; steady-state resume is unaffected. (b) The axis the Tip actually warns about, <encoded-cwd>, is handled deliberately and with more machinery than the page describes: sdkCwd is pinned at session creation and never moved (claude-agent.ts:1260-1266; SessionManager.ts:14319-14325 preserveSdkCwd), a fork spawns at the parent's sdkCwd (SessionManager.ts:9088-9091), and resolveSpawnCwd (claude-agent.ts:3045-3067) is a four-candidate existence-checked chain. (c) The SDK jsonl is not the resume corpus of record: sessions/mirror/types.ts:5 states local disk 'is written FIRST and stays authoritative', StoredSession.messages is the user-visible transcript, and SessionManager.ts:18950-18953 regenerates sdkCwd on a cross-server move precisely because the SDK file does not travel. (d) A missed SDK transcript is detected, not silent: claude-agent.ts:1937-1966 catches the SDK's empty resume, clears sdkSessionId, and replays Nessy's own messages via buildRecoveryContext (base-agent.ts:1944-1971 / SessionManager.ts:11913) with a visible 'Restoring conversation context...' status. So the whole exposure of 'no migration' is one bounded context truncation on the first post-upgrade turn of a pre-existing session. The per-Workspace redirect is a recorded decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-isolation-hardening.md:82-95 Task 3, whose gate is 'two workspaces do not see each other's config', and its session-history consequence was already written down at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:166. The only accurate residual is cosmetic: the options.ts:184-196 doc-comment says 'TWO HAZARDS :356 NAMES' while env-vars.md:356 enumerates four items; a one-line amendment noting that per-Workspace session history is the intent, that plugins were already redirected by plugins/data-paths.ts:115/131, and that pre-Task-3 sessions land in buildRecoveryContext on first resume would make the comment match the sentence it quotes. Separately, that plan carries no ## Tracker section, which the repo's Editing Rules require.

results.claim: The set of dispatchable slash commands is discovered from the system/init message's slash_commands array.
results.quote: Only commands that work without an interactive terminal are dispatchable through the SDK; the `system/init` message lists the ones available in your session.
results.ourState: The init branch of the Claude event adapter captures only `msg.tools`; `slash_commands` has no reader anywhere in the repo (`grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` → 0 hits). The session therefore cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625 (init branch reads `msg.tools` only); absence confirmed with `grep -ra "slash_commands" packages apps` (0 hits)

verdict.why: Doc sentence verified verbatim (slash-commands.md line 9, last of a three-sentence paragraph; nothing later in the line reverses it) and the cited code is accurate: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:622-630 adaptSystem's init branch captures only msg.tools, and `grep -ran "slash_commands" packages apps` returns 0 hits while node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:3994 does declare `slash_commands: string[]`. The IDENTIFIER claim therefore holds. The CONSEQUENCE — 'the session cannot tell the user, or itself, which commands the running CLI actually offers' — is false, and it names the wrong subsystem. Slash-command discovery in this fork does not live in the Claude event adapter; it is a first-party, backend-independent subsystem that does not consult the CLI at all: (1) packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts scans .nessy-agent/commands and .agents/commands (workspace root + trust-gated project root) for markdown commands; (2) SessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16016-16048) merges those native commands with plugin prompt/workflow commands, skill commands and MCP prompt commands and serves them over RPC_CHANNELS.workspace.LIST_CUSTOM_SLASH_COMMANDS ('workspace:listCustomSlashCommands', channels.ts:305, handler workspace.ts:72); (3) apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/AppShell.tsx:1408 loads that list and apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx renders it alongside Nessy's own built-ins (agents, automations, compact, context, create-skill, create-plugin, export, init, memory, model, clear, help, subtask, usage, every permission mode, recent folders). So the session DOES tell the user which commands it offers. It also tells itself: the agent-callable SlashCommand tool carries its own whitelist and /help listing (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10,29-35; pi-agent.ts:5403-5424). Reading msg.slash_commands would in fact be WRONG here, because Nessy is the executor, not a pass-through. A custom command is resolved and body-expanded server-side (SessionManager.resolveCustomSlashCommand at :16080, invoked from rpc/sessions.ts:317-325) and sent as an ordinary prompt — the CLI never sees the '/name' token, so the CLI's dispatchable set does not bound ours. Only ONE command is ever handed to the SDK verbatim, guarded by the fork's own constant SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] (claude-agent.ts:1665-1674). Everything else in the SDK's list (/clear, /context, /usage, bundled code-review/verify skills) is either a Nessy-owned UI command with different semantics or not a Nessy command at all; merging the CLI's array into the composer menu would advertise commands Nessy does not dispatch and would make the menu differ per backend, which is unacceptable when Pi is the default backend and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE is off by default. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns slash commands), but it matches false-positive shapes 3 and 4 recorded in section 4 of that same file: enforcement one layer up, and an identically-named concern in a sibling subsystem.
verdict.correctedState: The Claude event adapter's init branch (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:625) captures only `msg.tools`; `slash_commands` is read nowhere (0 hits under packages/ and apps/), even though the installed SDK declares it (sdk.d.ts:3994). This is by design, not a gap: the fork does not derive its command surface from the CLI. packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts discovers commands from disk, SessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries (SessionManager.ts:16016) merges native + plugin + skill + MCP-prompt commands, and the composer serves them over workspace:listCustomSlashCommands, so the session does report its available commands to the user. Custom commands are body-expanded server-side (resolveCustomSlashCommand, SessionManager.ts:16080) and sent as ordinary prompts, so their dispatchability never depends on the CLI's list; only `/compact` is forwarded verbatim, gated by the fork's own SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS constant (claude-agent.ts:1665). The one honest residual is cosmetic and backend-local: because SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS is a hardcoded one-element list rather than an intersection with the init array, a future built-in the CLI adds would not be forwarded — but no user-visible command surface depends on that.

results.claim: /clear is an SDK-dispatchable command that resets conversation context, alongside /compact.
results.quote: The `/clear` command resets the conversation to an empty context, so subsequent prompts start with no prior conversation history.
results.ourState: ClaudeAgent's dispatch allowlist is `const SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] as const;`. Every other slash command — /clear, /context, /usage — falls through to buildTextPrompt and is sent as an ordinary context-wrapped prompt rather than dispatched as a command.

verdict.why: All three checks pass, so the finding stands. (1) QUOTE — verbatim at slash-commands.md:212, under the heading '### `/clear` - Reset conversation context'. The rest of that two-sentence line does not reverse it ('The previous conversation remains on disk and can be returned to by passing its session ID to the resume option'), and the page's other qualifiers do not rescue us: :214's 'no practical effect' caveat is scoped to one-shot query() calls that start with EMPTY context, whereas every ClaudeAgent turn passes `resume: this.sessionId` (claude-agent.ts:1607) so context is non-empty; and :217's version gate ('/clear in the SDK requires Claude Code v2.1.117 or later') is satisfied — the bundled binary reports '2.1.183 (Claude Code)' (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude --version, SDK 0.3.183). (2) STATE — the constant is exact, at claude-agent.ts:1665, not the cited :1643 (line drift only; :1643 is now `attemptedBranchCutoff`). It is the only definition of that identifier in the repo (grep -a; the only other hit is the built apps/electron/dist/main.cjs:404259), so no sibling-subsystem confusion. (3) CONSEQUENCE — verified separately and independently of the identifier, and nothing upstream or downstream handles /clear. Upstream: the composer menu ships a `clear` entry (slash-command-menu.tsx:162, asserted by slash-command-menu.test.tsx:29), composer capabilities expose it to every backend (`slash: { commandIds: 'all' }`, composer-capabilities.ts:103), and dispatchSlashCommandAction falls through all the UI-handler branches to MESSAGE_COMMANDS.clear = '/clear' (slash-command-actions.ts:57) and calls submitCommand, i.e. it is sent as an ORDINARY MESSAGE (FreeFormInput.tsx:1034 -> onSubmit). Mid-path: SessionManager.sendMessage's only command classifier is parseSessionCommand (SessionManager.ts:15095) and BaseAgent.chat's only one is the same function (base-agent.ts:2758); session-command.ts claims ONLY /compact and /subtask, so /clear takes the composed-context branch — which means by the time chatImpl sees it the pinned capability block is already prefixed and the `^\/([a-z]+)` match at :1670 cannot even fire. Downstream: buildTextPrompt (claude-agent.ts:2429-2468) pushes contextParts first and the user text last, so the model receives '/clear' as trailing prose. The one function that would implement it, clearSessionMessages (sessions/storage.ts:457, doc-comment 'Used for /clear command'), has NO production caller (only the index.ts re-export), and agent.clearHistory() likewise has no non-test caller. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 touches slash commands (they are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, and three SessionMirrorStore rows). Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference either — the /clear menu entry is shipped and user-reachable. The parity report even marks `agent-sdk/slash-commands` as 'all built' (2026-07-30-parity-report.md:161). The nearest prior art is the parity audit's S15 note (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md, ~:527): '/clear and /help are dead the same way and deliberately NOT classifier-claimed until implemented' — an explicitly OPEN follow-up ('until implemented'), i.e. corroboration of this finding, not a decision to leave it.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with three corrections. (a) The cited line has drifted: the constant is `const SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'] as const;` at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1665 (:1643 is now `attemptedBranchCutoff`). (b) /context and /usage do NOT fall through to buildTextPrompt — dispatchSlashCommandAction returns early for them and opens native UI (openContext / refreshUsage+openUsage, slash-command-actions.ts:104-129), so they never reach the agent at all; that is a legitimate local implementation, not a gap. The commands that really are submitted as message text are /clear and /help (MESSAGE_COMMANDS, :55-74). (c) The allowlist is not the only gate and not the whole story: the product-wide classifier `parseSessionCommand` (packages/shared/src/slash-commands/session-command.ts:45) claims only /compact and /subtask, and BaseAgent.chat (base-agent.ts:2758) prefixes the pinned capability block to everything else — so /clear is dead on the Pi backend too (pi-agent.ts:6477 uses the same classifier), not only under ClaudeAgent. Net user-visible state: the composer ships a 'Clear' command that, on every backend, reaches the model as trailing prose inside a context-wrapped prompt and clears nothing; clearSessionMessages (sessions/storage.ts:457) and agent.clearHistory() both exist with no production caller. Note for whoever fixes it: adding 'clear' to SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS alone would not work — it must first be claimed by parseSessionCommand so the bare command survives context composition — and because each turn is a one-shot query() with `resume`, the fix likely also needs the local sdkSessionId reset that clearSessionMessages already implements, per slash-commands.md:214.

results.claim: A schema-bearing run that ends success but produces no structured_output must be surfaced as a failure, not as a clean completion.
results.quote: A result can also end with subtype `success` but no `structured_output` value, for example when the run completes without the agent producing a structured output. Treat that case as a failure as well.
results.ourState: The Claude result adapter spreads `{}` when the subtype is success and `structured_output` is undefined, which is byte-identical to the schema-less turn's complete event. Downstream consumers of `structuredOutputSubtype` cannot distinguish 'no schema rode this turn' from 'a schema rode it and the agent produced nothing'.

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim (structured-outputs.md line 397, whole line read; the third sentence reinforces rather than reverses: 'The example below treats a result as successful only when the subtype is success and structured_output is present, and handles every other result as a failure'). The cited code line is real: event-adapter.ts:613-615 does spread {} when subtype==='success' and structured_output is undefined. But the CONSEQUENCE is false — this is the repo's recurring 'enforcement one layer up' false positive. The doc's rule is a rule for the CALLER that supplied the schema, and in this fork that caller is the CLI, which knows: apps/cli/src/index.ts:463 `const structuredMode = outputSchema !== undefined && !streamJson`, and the complete handler at :517-532 implements the doc's three branches exactly — success+present prints the value, error_max_structured_output_retries prints the errors and exits 1, and the final else emits the doc example's literal string 'Run ended without a structured output' and sets exitCode=1. So a schema-bearing Claude turn that ends success with no structured_output is surfaced as a failure, not a clean completion. Positive control run (temp copy of apps/cli/src/run.test.ts with the exhaustion fixture replaced by a bare `{ type: 'complete' }` — byte-identical to what the Claude adapter emits in the disputed case): `bun test -t 'sendAndStream exits non-zero'` printed `Error: Run ended without a structured output` and passed with exitCode 1; temp file deleted. The decision is also recorded, not accidental: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-structured-output.md:102 — 'success-without-output exits 1 (the docs' example branches)'. Sibling-subsystem note: the Pi backend implements structured output itself (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3481-3482 synthesizes structuredOutputErrors=['run completed without a structured output'] and always stamps structuredOutputSubtype), so its event is self-describing; the Claude backend delegates to the SDK and lets the schema-supplying caller decide. Both reach the same doc-mandated outcome. No non-schema-supplying consumer exists — grep -a across apps/electron, packages/ui, apps/webui, apps/viewer finds zero readers of structuredOutput*; SessionManager.ts:16982-16990 only forwards. Not in inert-worklist section 3, and not a branding/subscription product difference — refuted on the consequence.
verdict.correctedState: event-adapter.ts:613-615 does emit a bare complete event for a schema-bearing Claude turn that ends subtype 'success' with no structured_output, but the doc's requirement is met one layer up: the only consumer is the CLI, which set the schema itself (apps/cli/src/index.ts:463 structuredMode) and whose complete handler (:517-532) routes that exact event to the doc example's own failure branch — stderr 'Run ended without a structured output', exit 1 (verified by positive control). The residual, non-doc difference is cosmetic and internal: the Pi backend always stamps structuredOutputSubtype so its agent_end is self-describing, while the Claude path relies on caller knowledge. Adding an explicit subtype on the Claude side would be a consistency nicety, not a documented-contract fix.

results.claim: Subagents may nest three layers below the main conversation by default, and the limit is settable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH.
results.quote: By default, subagents can spawn subagents of their own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
results.ourState: DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH is 1 in the spawner and DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth is 1 in the host manifest, deliberately kept in lockstep. A depth-2 spawn is refused with `Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`. No CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (or NESSY_ equivalent) reader exists — the only repo occurrences of that identifier are in audit prose under docs/. This was correct when the page documented a default of 1 (v2.1.217–218); v2.1.219 raised it to 3 and made it configurable.

results.ourState: The Claude result adapter never reads msg.terminal_reason. verdict.why: Doc sentence is verbatim (curl of agent-sdk/typescript.md, the bullet list under 'Several fields on the result carry diagnostic detail beyond subtype'; neighbouring bullets do not reverse it). The identifier half of the finding is also true: event-adapter.ts:581-585 derives terminalReason from stop_reason==='refusal' then the 4-entry CLAUDE_RESULT_SUBTYPE_REASON table at :50-57 with an unrecognized-subtype fallback to 'provider_error', and `grep -ra terminal_reason` over packages/ and apps/ finds zero reads in source (only comments, tests and plans). The CONSEQUENCE, which is what was filed, is false in both halves of its own enumerated list. (1) Five of the eight named values -- prompt_too_long, image_error, model_error, blocking_limit, rapid_refill_breaker -- are, in the very binary we bundle, ALWAYS preceded by an assistant API-error message the loop yields before it returns the reason: `tc({content: ..., error: 'invalid_request'})` for prompt_too_long/image_error/blocking_limit/rapid_refill_breaker (blocking_limit's content is literally the constant OF="Prompt is too long") and `error:'rate_limit'` for the model_error arm, and the SDK forwards that code to the consumer (`yield {type:'assistant', ..., error: r.error}`). Our adapter consumes exactly that one layer up: event-adapter.ts:293-301 -> claude-agent.ts:2660 mapSDKErrorToTypedError -> claude-sdk-error-mapper.ts, which has a dedicated 'Context Window Exceeded' branch keyed on 'prompt is too long'/'context window' plus 'Rate Limit Exceeded' and an 'Invalid Request' fallback that already advises /compact. So the user gets a specific, actionable typed error card, not an undifferentiated provider error, and the premise 'the SDK put the specific cause on the same message' is wrong -- the cause arrives earlier, on a different message, and we do read it. This is the repo's documented recurring false positive: the identifier is unwired, the consequence is handled upstream. (2) The other three named values -- hook_stopped, stop_hook_prevented, aborted_tools -- sit in the binary's CLEAN-turn bucket (the reason switch routes completed/stop_hook_prevented/hook_stopped/tool_deferred/max_turns/aborted_streaming/aborted_tools to Ie('turn'), and only blocking_limit/rapid_refill_breaker/prompt_too_long/image_error/model_error to Oe('turn', reason)), and the result subtype is chosen by `Gmo(lastMessage, stop_reason)` -- the shape of the last message -- not by the reason at all. There is no second channel: SessionManager.reportHookErrors (:5421-5450, the role:'info' warning path) is wired only into the `executeAgentEvent` arm of trackAgentAutomationSystem (:5384-5391), NOT into the buildSdkHooks arm (:5392-5405), and hookErrors covers non-blocking hook failures anyway, not decisions. The positive control is the same event on three sibling backends, all of which run it host-side and surface the reason: pi-agent.ts:6430-6433 (`blocked: reason || 'A <event> hook blocked this prompt.'`), codex-agent.ts:462-467 (`yield { type: 'error', message: reason }`), nestor-cloud-agent.ts:275-278. `grep -an 'UserPromptSubmit|emitAutomationEvent'` over claude-agent.ts returns 0 hits, so ClaudeAgent is the one backend with no host-side prompt gate. (4) CONSEQUENCE, local_command_output half — REFUTED, sibling-subsystem shape. Slash commands in this fork are first-party and resolved server-side (see verdict f073); claude-agent.ts:1662-1674 hands the SDK exactly one command, SDK_SLASH_COMMANDS = ['compact'], whose output is a compact_boundary, already handled. The CLI will therefore never emit local_command_output for a Nessy session, so 'local slash-command output for display' describes an unreachable message, not a gap. (5) Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (none touches the Claude event adapter or hook feedback), and not a rebrand or dropped-subscription product difference — the Claude backend ships and is user-enableable, `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` being off by default only narrows the blast radius.

results.claim: A PreToolUse hook may return permissionDecision 'defer', and the run then ends carrying deferred_tool_use so the host can resume the pending call.
results.quote: When a `PreToolUse` hook returns `permissionDecision: "defer"`, the result has `stop_reason: "tool_deferred"` and `deferred_tool_use` carries the pending tool's `id`, `name`, and `input`.
results.ourState: Implemented on the Pi backend only (pi-agent.ts:3868 handles decision==='defer' and emits deferredToolUse). On the CLAUDE backend the PreToolUse translation switch handles allow/modify/block/ask and never emits permissionDecision:'defer', and the result adapter never reads msg.deferred_tool_use — `grep -ran "deferred_tool_use|deferredToolUse" packages apps` returns no hit under agent/backend/claude/ or claude-agent.ts. The SDK 0.3.183 supports both halves (`HookPermissionDecision = 'allow' | 'deny' | 'ask' | 'defer'`, `deferred_tool_use?: SDKDeferredToolUse`).
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 (allow/modify/block/ask only); packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:581-619 (no deferred_tool_use read); Pi counterpart at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3866-3893

verdict.why: Doc sentence is VERBATIM (typescript.md:1319); the rest of that line ('Read this field to surface the request in your own UI, then resume with the same session_id to continue') supports rather than reverses it, and the SDK halves exist in 0.3.183 (sdk.d.ts:779 HookPermissionDecision includes 'defer'; :3880 deferred_tool_use). Sibling Claude-only gaps are already parked with the same reason (R13 file checkpoints :706; 'Bash isolation on the Claude backend' :753; the managed-filter bound :227-232). (2) WRONG SEAM CITED. claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 does NOT contain the allow/modify/block/ask switch - those lines are the additionalContext assembly and the continueWith() helper; the switch is at :1450-1468. More importantly that switch is on checkResult.type, the internal runPreToolUseChecks permission result, whose union has no 'defer' arm on EITHER backend: Pi handles defer at the hook-decision layer (pi-agent.ts:3872, 'hookDecision?.decision === defer'), never at runPreToolUseChecks. verdict.correctedState: Defer is implemented on the shipped Pi runtime only: pi-agent.ts:3872 honours a PreToolUse hook decision of 'defer' on headless single-tool-call turns, emitting complete{terminalReason:'tool_deferred', deferredToolUse}, with tool_deferred_unavailable on resume (pi-agent.ts:4695-4700) and forwarding through SessionManager.ts:18328 and dto.ts:357. The adapter half has no reachable consequence today because mergeClaudeSdkHooks:133 strips all trusted SDK PreToolUse matchers, leaving our own callback as the only PreToolUse hook the SDK sees, so no tool_deferred result can ever be produced. results.claim: An approval that may outlive the process should return the defer hook decision so the run can end and resume later from the persisted session.
results.quote: If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the [`defer` hook decision](/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later), which lets the process exit and resume later from the persisted session.
results.ourState: The defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only. Under the Claude backend the PreToolUse translation emits allow/modify/block/ask and never permissionDecision:'defer', so an approval that outlives the host process has no documented exit — the tool call stays blocked until the query is cancelled.

verdict.why: Sentence verified verbatim (user-input.md line 15), but the WHOLE line reverses the finding: 'The callback can stay pending indefinitely. Execution remains paused until your callback returns, and the SDK only cancels the wait when the query itself is cancelled. If a user might take longer to respond than your process can reasonably stay running, return the defer hook decision...'. Pending-forever is the documented NORM; defer is the conditional alternative for a process that cannot stay running. The identifier half of the claim is true (ClaudePreToolUseHookPipelineResult.hookDecision at claude-agent.ts:145 is typed 'allow' | 'ask' only, runClaudePreToolUseHookPipeline at :177 drops any other decision, the checkResult switch at :1450-1571 emits only allow/modify/block/ask/prompt, and grep -a finds no tool_deferred or deferred_tool_use anywhere under packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/). The CONSEQUENCE is false on two independent grounds. (1) One layer up, R7 Task 4 already provides exactly the capability defer exists to provide, and it is backend-agnostic: SessionManager.ts:12694 assigns managed.agent.onPermissionRequest = request => this.handleAgentPermissionRequest(managed, request) on the generic agent, and ClaudeAgent's case 'prompt' (claude-agent.ts:1518-1571) publishes through it; that handler persists PiPendingApprovalV1 into managed.pendingApproval (SessionManager.ts:6410-6430; 'pendingApproval' is in SESSION_PERSISTENT_FIELDS, sessions/types.ts:48), reprojectPendingApproval (:6622) re-fires the prompt through the production PermissionRequest band on open after restart, and settleDurableApproval (:6674) settles it with no live agent, an ALLOW re-driving the interrupted turn. The parity audit R7 row records this live-proven under CDP pass 11: a pending consent survives a SIGKILL, re-fires on open, and completes. So a Claude-backend approval that outlives the host process does have an exit, and it does not require cancelling the query. (2) The mechanism itself is scoped away from this surface by Claude's own contract: hooks.md:1587 states defer 'is for integrations that run claude -p as a subprocess and read its JSON output... Claude Code honors this value only in non-interactive mode with the -p flag. In interactive sessions it logs a warning and ignores the hook result.' Nessy's Pi implementation mirrors that gate exactly (pi-agent.ts:3872-3878, gated on this.config.isHeadless and on a single-tool-call turn), so 'the defer round trip exists on the Pi backend only' actually means 'on the headless surface only' — Pi does not defer in the desktop app either. On the interactive Claude surface the documented behavior IS to ignore a defer, which is what the pipeline does (a defer decision is neither block nor allow/ask at :167/:177, so the call falls through the normal permission flow). The claimed evidence line range is also off: claude-agent.ts:1428-1434 is the steer-message/continueWith block, not the decision translation. The only genuine residue is cosmetic/edge — no warning is logged when an ignored defer arrives, and a headless run on the Claude backend would not produce tool_deferred termination — neither of which is the claimed consequence.
verdict.correctedState: Nessy's Claude backend implements the documented default: the PreToolUse callback stays pending indefinitely while the approval is surfaced to the user (claude-agent.ts:1518-1571). It never emits permissionDecision:'defer' and never consumes deferred_tool_use — which matches Claude's own rule that defer is honored only in non-interactive `claude -p` runs and is warned-and-ignored in interactive sessions (hooks.md:1587); Nessy's Pi defer is gated on isHeadless for the same reason, so the mechanism is headless-only on both backends, not Pi-only. An approval that outlives the host process is handled one layer up and backend-agnostically by R7 durable approvals: the prompt is persisted as pendingApproval, the process may exit, and on restart + session open reprojectPendingApproval re-fires it through the production PermissionRequest band with settleDurableApproval re-driving the interrupted turn on ALLOW (live-proven against SIGKILL, CDP pass 11). Residual, both minor and outside the claim: an ignored defer from a trusted PreToolUse hook is dropped silently instead of logging a warning, and a headless Claude-backend run would not terminate with tool_deferred.

results.claim: A subagent may nest up to three layers below the main conversation by default (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` default 3, raised from 1 in v2.1.219).
results.quote: By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation.
results.ourState: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1` in the spawner and `depth: 1` in `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG`, kept in lockstep on purpose. Depth 1 is exactly Claude's "nesting off" value. The repo's own note (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`, R30 row: "default 1 — already matched by P9's depth-1 fix, so this one is closed") is now stale against the page.
results.evidence: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107; refusal path at spawner.ts:518-519 (`Subagent depth limit exceeded (1)`)

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding stands. (1) DOC — the sentence exists VERBATIM at line 862 of the curl'd https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md, under the heading '### Let subagents spawn their own subagents' (:860). Read whole: the line continues 'At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork, so a subagent at the limit does its delegated work itself and returns one summary. A fork at the limit keeps `Agent` in its inherited tool list, but the tool returns an error instead of spawning.' — that second half describes behaviour AT the limit and does not reverse the default. Corroborated on the same page: :866 '{/* min-version: 2.1.217 */}To change the limit, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH…', :876 'Set `1` to turn nesting off', and the version Note at :885-886 — 'v2.1.172 through v2.1.216: … up to five layers deep, and the limit couldn't be changed' / 'v2.1.217 through v2.1.218: the limit defaulted to one … v2.1.219 raised the default to three.' So the claimed history (default 3, raised from 1 in v2.1.219) is exactly what the page says, and `sub-agents` is row 164 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, i.e. a real Claude Code contract page. (2) CODE — packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 is `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, with the docblock at :105-108 'Default child-session nesting depth: ONE level of delegation. Must stay in lockstep with DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth'. packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107 is `depth: 1` inside DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG, with the mirror comment at :104-106. The refusal is spawner.ts:513-520: `const depth = (args.depth ?? 0) + 1` then `if (depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)) return failure(args.agentDef.name, `Subagent depth limit exceeded (${cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH})`)`. packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:47 documents the same: 'depth | 1 | … Default is ONE level of delegation'. No env override exists: a NUL-safe repo-wide `grep -ral SPAWN_DEPTH .` returns five paths, ALL under docs/ (this sweep's own data plus 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md) — zero in packages/, apps/ or scripts/ — and `grep -ran 'NESSY_[A-Z_]*DEPTH' packages apps scripts` returns nothing. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, both directions. Layer up: maxDepth reaches the spawner only via `maxDepth: config.orchestrator?.depth` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1279), and the single production seed builder — SessionManager.ts:4152-4164 — populates contextSeed, sessionDepth, sessionIsFork, forkSubagent and tierModelMap and NEVER `depth`, so normalizePiOrchestratorConfig falls back to DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth = 1 on every real session. Nothing upstream already raises it. Layer down: the behaviour is positively tested with a control on the same rig — spawner.test.ts:542-548 'refuses a grandchild at the default depth but still admits a child' asserts child.status === 'done', grandchild.status === 'error' containing 'depth limit', and started === 1; :550-555 'still allows a grandchild when the config raises the depth' passes maxDepth 2 and the identical grandchild spawn succeeds. :537-540 pins both constants to 1. So the absence is proved, not assumed. Sibling-subsystem check: this is the Pi orchestrator's own spawner (the default runtime; NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE is off by default), the depth gate is the only one on that path, and the fork-cannot-fork rule is a separate unconditional flag (spawner.ts:96-98, :502-504) rather than a depth derivative — so the subsystem is named correctly. NOT an owner decision: the nine dated entries in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. Depth is not among them. NOT a deliberate product difference either — it is not a subscription-flow drop, a gateway concern, or a rename. The originating plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-subagent-trust.md, Task 4, tracker row 4 'done') lowered DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH 5→1 to reconcile four disagreeing defaults, and the audit then closed the parity row precisely BECAUSE Claude documented 1 at the time: 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:559 reads 'CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (default 1 — already matched by P9's depth-1 fix, so this one is closed)', echoed at :555 'which is exactly what P9 shipped, so the depth limit needs no work'. That closure is now stale: the page moved to 3 in v2.1.219 and our value did not move. The claimed our-state is accurate in every particular, including that depth 1 is exactly Claude's documented 'nesting off' value (:876).
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as written, with two additions worth carrying. (a) The effective production value really is 1, not merely the constant: the only host seed of the orchestrator config (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4152-4164) never sets `depth`, so `maxDepth: config.orchestrator?.depth` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1279) resolves to undefined and DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH wins on every session; spawner.test.ts:542-555 proves the grandchild refusal and, as a positive control, that maxDepth 2 admits it. (b) The gap is two-part — the default is 1 against Claude's 3, AND there is no configurable override at all (no CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH reader and no NESSY_ equivalent anywhere in packages/, apps/ or scripts/), so a host can only raise nesting by supplying `orchestrator.depth` in the execution manifest, which no production path does. Note the shape of the deviation: at the limit we return `Subagent depth limit exceeded (N)` from the call, which matches the page's FORK behaviour (:862 'the tool returns an error instead of spawning') but not the named-subagent behaviour (:862/:326 'withholds the Agent tool'); spawner.ts:514-517 records that deviation knowingly. The stale closure at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:555 and :559 should be reopened. Same underlying gap as f076 (agent-sdk/subagents), f130 (changelog) and f164 (env-vars) — one fix closes all four.

results.claim: A session-wide cap of 200 spawned subagents exists, raisable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`, and the Agent tool fails with `Subagent spawn limit reached` when it is hit.
results.quote: By default, Claude can spawn at most 200 subagents per session.
results.ourState: No per-session subagent counter or cap exists anywhere. `orchestrator.maxAgents` (default 1000) is scoped to ONE workflow run only — `packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49` calls it "maximum `agent()` calls per workflow run" and it is wired solely into the workflow tool (`packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497` `getMaxAgents`). A session can spawn subagents without bound.
results.evidence: `grep -ran "MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION|Subagent spawn limit|sessionSpawn" packages apps/electron/src` → no output; packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497

verdict.why: The doc sentence is verbatim (sub-agents.md:893, section 'Session subagent limit'; whole line adds the env var, 'no upper bound, but the limit can't be turned off', and 'Requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later'). The cited repo lines are also accurate as far as they go: packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49 does describe maxAgents (default 1000) as 'maximum agent() calls per workflow run', and packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1497 does pass getMaxAgents into createWorkflowTool. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and the word 'solely' is the error. maxAgents has a SECOND consumer the name-based grep never reached: packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280 passes it into the shared spawner as maxFanout (configureSpawnerForGeneration), and packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:603 stamps it onto EVERY spawn's budgets as 'fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100'. configureSpawner is the single spawner used by the subagent tool, forks, the review tool and workflow agents alike (index.ts:131,1274,1803,1883). The host then enforces it cumulatively per session at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 - 'if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error("child-session-fanout-limit")' - where 'children' is the persisted, UNFILTERED record list for this parentSessionKey; the status filter on the adjacent line is the separate concurrency check. So a finished subagent still counts, exactly like Claude's session limit. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.test.ts:178-183 proves it: after child-1 is stopped, a start with fanout:1 rejects with child-session-fanout-limit. Default is 1000 (DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.maxAgents, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109), plumbed through the init contract (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:314). The claimed evidence grep is true but proves only that Claude's NAMES are absent, not that the mechanism is: this repo spells it fanout/maxAgents, which is the exact 'identifier looks unwired, consequence is false because another layer already handles it' trap AGENTS.md warns about. 'No per-session subagent counter or cap exists anywhere' and 'A session can spawn subagents without bound' are both false. Not an inert-worklist owner decision and not a de-brand difference - just a wrong reading.
verdict.correctedState: A cumulative per-session subagent cap DOES exist, under different names. orchestrator.maxAgents (default 1000, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109) reaches the shared spawner as maxFanout (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280) and rides on every spawn as budgets.fanout (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:603), for subagents, forks, review and workflow agents alike. The host enforces it at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 by counting ALL child records for the parent session, terminal ones included, and throws 'child-session-fanout-limit' when the count reaches the budget. Two real but much narrower divergences remain: (1) naming and defaults - 1000 rather than 200, no CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION env var (it is set through orchestrator config), and the error is 'child-session-fanout-limit' rather than 'Subagent spawn limit reached' with the doc's 'do the rest yourself' guidance; (2) accounting shape - each session node keeps its own counter, clamped downward on inheritance via Math.min at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:11142, whereas Claude charges nested subagents, forks and background subagents to one session-wide budget. Also note the sibling limits already match in kind: orchestrator.concurrency (16) is checked on the adjacent line 149 as the concurrent-subagent analogue, and orchestrator.depth is the depth limit.

results.claim: 20 concurrently running subagents is the default ceiling, configurable via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, with the error `Concurrent subagent limit reached`.
results.quote: By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`, and the error tells Claude not to retry.
results.ourState: One shared semaphore, `DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16`, further narrowed at runtime to `min(concurrency, cpuCores - 2)`. It is also the workflow ceiling, where 16 IS the documented number (`workflows.md`: "Up to 16 concurrent agents"), so the two documented limits are collapsed into one and the subagent side sits 4 below spec. There is no `Concurrent subagent limit reached` error — over-limit spawns queue on the semaphore instead of failing.

verdict.why: All three legs survive the challenge. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL of sub-agents.md line 903, under the heading '### Concurrent subagent limit' (line 901), begins with the quoted sentence character-for-character. The rest of that line does not reverse it: 'Spawning succeeds again when the running count drops below the limit. To change the limit, set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS to any positive whole number. Sessions with ultracode active are exempt: the limit isn't enforced there. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later.' Line 905 makes the separation the finding depends on explicit: 'Agents that other features run, such as workflow agents and agent team teammates, follow their own limits instead.' (2) CITED LINES ARE ACCURATE: spawner.ts:103 'const DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 16'; :136-142 computeEffectiveConcurrency returns Math.max(1, Math.min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2)); :204 'let semaphore = new Semaphore(computeEffectiveConcurrency(DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY))' with :208 rebuilding it from nextRuntime.concurrency. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN. Down: Semaphore.acquire (:165-186) pushes an over-limit caller onto a queue and rejects only on an aborted signal, and every spawn runs inside semaphore.run at :587 -- so an over-limit spawn blocks, it never fails. Up: all five spawn paths share that one module singleton -- subagent-tool.ts:282, workflow-tool.ts:466, review-tool.ts:304, subtask.ts:84, guardian-runner.ts:57 -- and our own packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46 documents the scope of 'concurrency' as 'subagent, workflow', i.e. the collapse is already written down on our side. The error string does not exist in source: grep -ra 'Concurrent subagent limit' over packages/ apps/ returns only this sweep's own doc/JSON rows; grep -ra MAX_CONCURRENT over packages/ apps/ returns only marketplace DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES = 2, so no env var (Claude- or NESSY-named) feeds the cap. WRONG-SUBSYSTEM CHECK: two nearby limits that DO fail are not this one -- subagent-tool.ts:150 throws 'parallel tasks cannot exceed N' (DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS = 100) for the size of ONE call's task array, a per-invocation batch cap; and server-core/src/sessions/live-agent-ceiling.ts refuses with 'live-agent-ceiling-reached' against a memory-derived host-wide runtime bound max(2, RAM/2GiB), evicting idle sessions first. Neither is a per-session count of running subagents, and neither carries the documented threshold or message. WORKFLOW HALF CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: workflows.md:320 reads 'Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer on machines with limited CPU cores', so both our number and our cpuCores narrowing are exactly the workflow contract -- which is what makes the subagent side (a flat 20, a hard failure, an env var, an ultracode exemption) the part that diverges. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated items in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 are the seatbelt wildcard, the availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed filter placement, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys and listSessionSummaries -- none touches concurrency. verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with three refinements. (a) The number and the CPU narrowing are not wrong per se -- workflows.md:320 verbatim is 'Up to 16 concurrent agents, fewer on machines with limited CPU cores', so packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:103 + :136-142 match the WORKFLOW contract exactly. What diverges is that the single module-level semaphore at :204/:208, entered by every spawn at :587, is the only gate for the subagent path too (subagent-tool.ts:282, workflow-tool.ts:466, review-tool.ts:304, subtask.ts:84, guardian-runner.ts:57; scope documented as 'subagent, workflow' in packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46), where sub-agents.md:903 specifies an independent per-session ceiling of 20 running subagents, a hard `Concurrent subagent limit reached` failure that tells Claude not to retry, a CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS override, and an ultracode exemption -- and sub-agents.md:905 says workflow agents 'follow their own limits instead'. (b) There is a further consequence the finding did not state: sub-agents.md:905 says an in-session /subtask fork 'takes a slot while it runs and is never blocked by the limit', but ours enters the same semaphore via subtask.ts:84, so a user-started /subtask CAN be queued behind a fan-out.
