results.claim: A subagent definition may carry a `hooks` frontmatter block whose hooks run only while that subagent is active, with frontmatter `Stop` converted to `SubagentStop` at runtime; the field is ignored for plugin subagents.
results.quote: Define hooks directly in the subagent's markdown file. These hooks only run while that specific subagent is active and are cleaned up when it finishes.
results.ourState: `hooks` is not in `UserAgentDefinition` (the frontmatter/JSON shape), not in `AgentDefinition`, and not in the runtime descriptor. A `hooks:` block in an imported Claude agent file is parsed as frontmatter and then silently dropped — no diagnostic, unlike the `TeammateIdle` deferral. `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` from `settings.json` ARE supported (`packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:171-172`); only the per-agent frontmatter channel is missing.

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at sub-agents.md:617 (whole line, nothing reverses it), and the identifier half of the claim is true: `hooks` is absent from `UserAgentDefinition` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:253-271) and from `AgentDefinition` (:58-122). The CONSEQUENCE is false, which is the refutation. (1) NOT SILENT. `reportFrontmatterHookDeclarations` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:437-500, invoked for every adapter at :375-382) reads each imported skill/agent file, and on presence of a `hooks` frontmatter key pushes a `warning` diagnostic `plugin.format.frontmatter_hooks_unregistered` ('Subagent "<path>" declares frontmatter hooks. Nessy does not register component-scoped hooks, so they will not run...') PLUS a deferral `{externalKind:'hook', reasonCode:'plugin.deferred.frontmatter_hooks_unregistered', sourcePath}` that forces `compatibility.state` to `partial`. That is the SAME `compatibility.deferred` channel the claim says this is 'unlike' (TeammateIdle) — so the stated contrast is exactly backwards. The covering test (packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:88-142) builds a Claude bundle whose `agents/reviewer.md` carries precisely a `hooks: Stop:` block and asserts the warning + deferral + `partial`; run at HEAD: 4 pass / 0 fail. (2) RECORDED OWNER DECISION, twice. Parity-audit row D9 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:737) is this exact finding, closed 2026-07-30 by commit e1d322a1 ('fix(plugins): skill and subagent frontmatter hooks register or are refused') deliberately as the LOUD-REFUSAL half: 'Registration was not attempted: it needs the component-lifetime scoping the page describes, and the adapter half was locked.' Row R30c (:698) separately costed `hooks` and deliberately did not half-build it — 'no per-subagent hook scope and the value is a nested event map the flat parser cannot represent'. (3) FOR THE CASE THE CLAIM NAMES, THE DROP IS DOC-CONFORMANT. The claim's subject is 'an imported Claude agent file', i.e. a plugin bundle; sub-agents.md:229 says plugin subagents do not support `hooks`/`mcpServers`/`permissionMode` and 'These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin.' Nessy enforces that structurally, deleting the three keys before any read (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:388-431, PLUGIN_IGNORED_AGENT_FRONTMATTER), and that code comment quotes the same doc line — so for plugin agents our behaviour MATCHES Claude, it does not diverge. (4) Wrong-subsystem citation. The claimed proof that SubagentStart/SubagentStop are supported, `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:171-172`, points at the dead second hook executor that inert-worklist section 3 item 5 lists as an owner decision ('Do not revive hooks-runtime.ts... a second, unreachable hook executor'); the live contract is AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1 in packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:66-67. The conclusion is right, the evidence names the wrong subsystem.
verdict.correctedState: Per-agent frontmatter `hooks` are genuinely not REGISTERED in Nessy — there is no component-lifetime hook scope, and no `Stop`->`SubagentStop` conversion — but they are not silently dropped, and the gap is a dated recorded decision, not an unnoticed defect. Since commit e1d322a1 (2026-07-30, parity row D9) any imported skill or subagent whose frontmatter carries a `hooks:` key produces a warning diagnostic (`plugin.format.frontmatter_hooks_unregistered`) and a deferral (`plugin.deferred.frontmatter_hooks_unregistered`) in the same channel as the TeammateIdle deferral, downgrading the bundle to `partial` and failing `validate --strict`. For plugin-bundled subagents specifically — the case the finding cites — not honouring `hooks` is what sub-agents.md:229 requires, and Nessy enforces it structurally by deleting the key before any field is read (runtime-agent-definition.ts:399-431). Session-wide `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` are live via automations/types.ts:66-67, not via the dead plugins/hooks-runtime.ts. The only open residue is registration of frontmatter-scoped hooks for NATIVE (non-plugin) agent definitions, costed and deferred under R30c.

results.claim: A subagent `name` containing `:` is refused at load, because `:` is reserved for plugin-scoped identifiers.
results.quote: Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`.
results.ourState: `normalizeName` only trims and lowercases; no character validation. Our plugin capability keys DO contain colons (`qualifiedKey` joins with `::`, `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:263`) and become an agent's `name`/`aliases` (`runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154`). `resolveAgentDefinition` matches on exact `name` BEFORE searching `aliases`, so a workspace or project markdown agent file may declare a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key and be selected ahead of the alias lookup. Only the built-in and `fork` names are reserved.

verdict.why:
The quote is real and the cited lines say what was claimed, but the CONSEQUENCE is false and was measured false — the repo's recurring 'the identifier is unwired, but something upstream already handled it' shape, compounded by the finding naming the wrong field (frontmatter `name`) in the wrong subsystem.

1. DOC — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md` -> 1250 lines, 94956 bytes, md5 cf7b0c7d5ff8adff60f6a174cd6938f4. The claimed string is an exact substring of line 277 (checked in Python, not by eye). Reading the WHOLE line changes nothing against the finding — it reinforces it: `| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier using lowercase letters and hyphens. [Hooks](/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart) receive this value as `agent_type`. The filename doesn't have to match. {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}Names can't contain `:`, which is reserved for [plugin-scoped identifiers](/docs/en/plugins) such as `my-plugin:reviewer`. Claude Code doesn't load a file whose name contains one and logs an error to the debug log. Before v2.1.218, such names were accepted |`. So the doc half stands, and the rule is version-gated at v2.1.218.

2. FILE — CONFIRMED AS WRITTEN, all four citations. `packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283` is exactly `normalizeName(name) { return name.trim().toLowerCase(); }` with no character validation. `:725-726` is exactly `defs.find(def => def.name === normalized) ?? defs.find(def => def.aliases?.includes(normalized))`. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:250-264` `qualifiedKey` does `.join('::')`. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:153-154` is `name: hasUnqualifiedAlias ? descriptor.name : descriptor.key` / `aliases: [...new Set([descriptor.key, ...])]`. There is no colon check anywhere in the agents subsystem (`grep -ran` over `packages/shared/src/agents/` and `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/` for `includes(':')`, `indexOf(':')`, `/:/`, `[a-z0-9-]`, `colon`: zero non-test hits).

3. CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED ON THREE INDEPENDENT GROUNDS.

(a) The stated exploit path is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: markdown definitions and runtime (plugin-key-bearing) definitions are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. `loadAgentDefinitions` guards the entire markdown block with `if (options.runtimeDefinitions === undefined)` (definitions.ts:670-684) and only then appends `options.runtimeDefinitions ?? []` (:686). Plugin capability keys reach this function ONLY as runtime definitions, so in any load where a plugin key exists, no workspace/project markdown file has been read at all. Every production caller supplies the field and never leaves it `undefined`: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:513` and `workflow-tool.ts:591` both pass `options.getRuntimeAgentDefinitions?.() ?? []`, and `review-tool.ts:300` passes `[]`.

MEASURED, with a positive control (an ABSENCE needs one):
  CONTROL (runtimeDefinitions omitted): a workspace `reviewer.md` DOES override the built-in -> systemPrompt "I AM THE OVERRIDE."   <- the rig can see shadowing
  PROD SHAPE (runtimeDefinitions: []): same file on disk -> systemPrompt "You are a reviewer agent. Focu…"  <- markdown never loaded
  IMPOSTOR TEST: workspace `impostor.md` with frontmatter `name: "agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer"` alongside a runtime definition whose definitionKey is that same string -> `resolveAgentDefinition('agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer')` returns "I am the REAL plugin agent." The impostor is absent from the map entirely.

(b) The finding names the WRONG FIELD for the path that carries plugin keys. In the capability/runtime pipeline an agent is named by its FILENAME, not by frontmatter `name`: `native-sources.ts:332` `const logicalName = entry.name.replace(/\.md$/i, '')`, and the runtime binding is `resolver.ts:965` `agent: { key, name: record.logicalName, … }` for native agents and `resolver.ts:1245` `name: candidate.logicalName` for plugin agents; the descriptor then carries `name: agent.name` (`pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:643`). The frontmatter `name` key is read only by `definitions.ts`'s own parser (`parseMarkdownAgentDefinition:534-536`) — i.e. exactly and only in the fallback path where, per (a), no plugin key can be present. So "a workspace or project markdown agent file may DECLARE a colon-bearing name equal to a plugin's capability key" cannot happen: in the path that has plugin keys, the declaration is ignored.

(c) The reservation's RATIONALE does not transfer. Claude reserves `:` because its plugin-scoped reference syntax is literally `my-plugin:reviewer`. This fork implements no such syntax — a plugin-scoped agent is referenced by its opaque `::`-joined qualified key or by its short logical name, and nothing else: `base-agent.ts:2557` (`candidate.key === agent || (candidate.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias && candidate.name === agent)`) and `runtime-agent-definition.ts:224-225` (`value.key === reference` ?? `value.logicalName === reference`). A single `:` is therefore not a namespace separator here and cannot collide with one.

Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` (read all nine: SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries — none touches agent name validation). Not a rebrand or a subscription-drop difference either. It is refuted on measurement, not on category.
verdict.correctedState: What survives is a narrow hygiene divergence with no security or shadowing consequence: `normalizeName` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283) only trims and lowercases, so a markdown subagent file that declares a colon-bearing frontmatter `name` LOADS instead of being refused — measured: both `has:colon` and `agent::plugin::-::-::::reviewer` load with zero entries in `onInvalidDefinition`, whereas Claude Code v2.1.218+ skips such a file and logs to the debug log. The finding's impersonation consequence is false. A markdown-declared name can never shadow a plugin capability key, because `loadAgentDefinitions` reads markdown ONLY when `options.runtimeDefinitions === undefined` (:670-684) and plugin keys arrive exclusively as runtime definitions, while every production caller passes the field (subagent-tool.ts:513, workflow-tool.ts:591, review-tool.ts:300). Independently, the capability path names native and plugin agents by `logicalName` — filename or plugin component name (native-sources.ts:332, resolver.ts:965 and :1245) — and ignores frontmatter `name` entirely, so the declaration the finding relies on is not read on that path. And `:` is not a namespace separator in this fork at all: there is no `plugin:agent` reference form, only the opaque `::`-joined qualified key or the short logical name (base-agent.ts:2557, runtime-agent-definition.ts:224-225). The `name`-before-`aliases` order at :725-726 is real but not exploitable through the claimed route. Residual work, if any, is cosmetic parity: reject `:` in `normalizeName` and report it through the existing per-file `onInvalidDefinition` skip.

results.claim: When `memory` is set, the subagent gets a real memory directory: prompt instructions to read/write it, up to the first 200 lines or 25KB of its `MEMORY.md` injected, and Read/Write/Edit force-enabled.
results.quote: The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory.
results.ourState: `memory` is parsed, validated against `user|project|local`, and carried on the definition and the runtime descriptor — and consumed by nothing. No `agent-memory/<name>/` directory is created, no memory prompt block is composed for a child, and no tool is force-enabled. Our own code comment admits it: "Parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned". A read-only agent definition with `memory: project` therefore cannot write the memory it is told it has.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md (1250 lines) has the quoted sentence at :520 as a whole single-sentence bullet — '* The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory.' No second clause reverses it. Its two sibling bullets at :521 and :522 carry the rest of the claimed behaviour verbatim ('the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` ... whichever comes first'; 'Read, Write, and Edit tools are automatically enabled'), and :512-514 give the three directories. The one gating clause, :516 ('if you turn auto memory off ... the `memory` field has no effect'), does NOT excuse us: this fork HAS a live auto-memory subsystem (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts, memory-cleanup.ts 'dream' pass, the `remember` tool, MEMORY.md records at global/workspace/project/session scope in capabilities/native-sources.ts), and there is no autoMemoryEnabled-equivalent master switch to be off — `grep -rna 'autoMemory'` finds only the marker/cleanup constants, no gate. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:90-95 reads exactly as claimed — the comment is 'Persistent memory scope for this agent (`user` / `project` / `local`). / Parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet / provisioned — see the R30c report.' The scope type and its Claude-doc directory mapping are at :37-44, the strict normalizer at :366-370, and the throw-on-typo at :414/:427-428 ('Invalid <label>.memory: expected user, project or local'). The second cited site is exact: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173 is '...(descriptor.memory ? { memory: descriptor.memory } : {}),' — a pure spread pass-through. A third carrier the finding did not name: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:141 (descriptor field), :336-339 (runtime parse) and :616-620 (frontmatter parse), all validate-and-carry only. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both directions. Down: `grep -c -a memory packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts` returns 0 — the module that actually spawns a subagent never sees the field, so nothing composes a memory prompt block from it and nothing force-enables Read/Write/Edit. Up: `grep -rna 'agent-memory' --include=*.ts --include=*.js --include=*.cjs --include=*.mjs packages apps` (with -a, per the NUL-byte trap) returns exactly two hits, both the doc comment at definitions.ts:40-41 — no directory is ever built or created. Sibling-subsystem check (the `disallowed-tools` shape): the fork's memory code IS a different subsystem — session/user/project MEMORY.md via native-sources.ts:910/1028/1093 and the capability `memory` view — and it is keyed on scope discovery, never on AgentDefinition.memory; naming it would be naming the wrong subsystem. Upstream-already-handled check: the Claude SDK backend cannot be quietly doing it either — claude-agent.ts has no `agents:` SDK option and no memory handling (its four `memory` hits are 'in-memory'/'memory growth' comments), and subagents run the Pi harness path. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) — it appears only as row 23 of the RAW sweep 2026-07-29-inert-contracts.md:95, the file that worklist's own header says is 'not the list to work from'. Not a deliberate product difference either: no subscription flow, no gateway scoping, no rename. What it IS is an already-recorded deviation that confirms rather than refutes: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-subagent-frontmatter.md:143 categorises `memory` as 'documented, not implemented — ... the per-agent memory DIRECTORY (agent-memory/<name>/, MEMORY.md injection, auto Read/Write/Edit) is a subsystem we do not have' (commit b31d6421), harvested into the deviation register at :306, and the parity audit's R30c row (2026-07-25 audit:698) says the same: 'costed with categories and NOT half-built'. Costed-and-deferred is an open gap, not a decision to keep it.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as a real divergence, with one clause of the submitted wording tightened. Accurate: `memory` is parsed and strictly validated against user|project|local in three places (definitions.ts:366-370 with a throw at :427-428; pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:336-339 and :616-620), carried on AgentDefinition (definitions.ts:95) and on the runtime descriptor (runtime-agent-definition.ts:141), and passed through to the orchestrator at pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173 — where consumption ends. spawner.ts contains zero occurrences of `memory`; no agent-memory/<name>/ directory is created anywhere (the string exists only in definitions.ts:40-41's doc comment); no MEMORY.md is injected on account of the field; no Read/Write/Edit force-enable exists. Overstated in the submission and corrected here: 'no memory prompt block is composed for a child' should read 'no PER-AGENT memory block is composed'. A child session does receive inherited MEMORY.md content as pinned `memory` context — the capability view's memory records survive child intersection (pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:188) and are added as pinned context at pi-harness/context-resource.ts:66 — but those come from the session/user/project MEMORY.md discovery in capabilities/native-sources.ts, are identical for every subagent, and are not keyed on the `memory:` field. Likewise 'cannot write the memory it is told it has' is only true when the AGENT AUTHOR writes memory instructions into the definition body (the doc's own tip at sub-agents.md:529-532); the host itself never tells the agent it has memory, which makes the field silently inert rather than actively misleading. Net: an author who writes `memory: project` gets strict validation, a definition that round-trips the value, and no cross-session learning of any kind.

results.claim: The output scan prepends a marker line when a subagent report imitates a harness tag OR mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` / `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, leaving the text itself unchanged.
results.quote: **Marker line**: the scan prepends a line starting with `[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):` when the report imitates a tag like `<system-reminder>` or mentions permission settings such as `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
results.ourState: `scanSubagentOutput` defangs `<untrusted|system-reminder|nessy_agent_environment` tags and line-leading `Human:`/`Assistant:` by inserting a zero-width space, and strips C0/C1 control characters. It never prepends a marker line, and it has no permission-setting pattern at all — a child report containing `bypassPermissions` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` reaches the parent with nothing flagged. Two secondary differences on the same sentence pair: we insert U+200B where the page specifies a backslash (invisible vs visible), and we DO remove control characters where the page says "The scan never removes or rewords anything".

verdict.why: All three checks pass, so the gap survives the challenge. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md finds the sentence at line 799, inside the '### Subagent output scanning' section, character-for-character as quoted. The line is a two-sentence line and the SECOND sentence reinforces rather than reverses: 'Permission-setting mentions get the marker line, but the text itself stays as written.' The section preamble also states 'The scan never removes or rewords anything; it makes two kinds of change you may notice in a report:' followed by two bullets, 'Backslash insertion' and 'Marker line'. Feature is gated at v2.1.210+ per the page's own Note. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/prompts/untrusted-text.ts is 75 lines and is exactly as described. HARNESS_TAG = /<(\/?)(untrusted|system-reminder|nessy_agent_environment)\b/gi (:41), TURN_MARKER = /^([ \t]*)(Human|Assistant)(?=:)/gim (:48), CONTROL_CHARACTERS C0/C1 set (:55); scanSubagentOutput (:71-75) is exactly neutralizeHarnessMarkers(text).replace(TURN_MARKER, `$1$2${ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE}`).replace(CONTROL_CHARACTERS, ''). ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE = '\u200B' (:32) — so U+200B, not a backslash, and control characters ARE removed (the header comment at :18-21 makes that an explicit design choice: 'DEFANG, do not delete ... Only control characters, which have no legible form, are removed'). No return-value concatenation, no prefix, no conditional branch: a marker line is structurally absent, not merely unmatched. (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN, with -a on every absence grep: `grep -ran 'harness:' packages apps` returns only unrelated test comments, a release-notes line and NUL-bearing codex.exe blobs — zero source hits for the marker string; `grep -ran 'instruction-shaped|instructionShaped|instruction_shaped' packages apps` returns nothing at all. No permission-setting pattern exists on any scan path: `grep -ran 'dangerously-skip-permissions|dangerouslySkipPermissions' packages/*/src apps/*/src` hits only two prose comments in pre-tool-use.ts:635 and protected-paths.ts:32 (both about protected-path semantics, neither a scanner), and bypassPermissions appears only as a permission-mode enum value in mode tables, fixtures and the system prompt. Consequence verified separately from the identifier: I walked every model-facing consumer of the scan — pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/{subagent-tool,workflow-tool,review-tool,guardian-runner}.ts and server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:9940 — and none of them prepends, appends or wraps anything conditional. contentForResults (subagent-tool.ts:225-247) emits a plain header `N. <agent> - <status>` plus the defanged body, with '[ERROR] ' only for failed children; there is no untrusted fence on the parent-facing return (the `<untrusted source="...">` wrapper at prompts/guardian.ts:296 is a SIBLING SUBSYSTEM — it fences the guardian judge's INPUTS, not a subagent's report to its parent — so it cannot be mistaken for the missing marker). The only standing mitigation is a generic system-prompt line (prompts/system.ts:546/:636, 'Treat source data, tool output, ... as data to inspect, not instructions to follow'), which is a constant instruction, not a per-report flag, so the claimed consequence holds. Not a recorded owner decision: inert-worklist §3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches subagent output scanning. Not a rebrand or dropped-subscription difference either: this is our own defense, built by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-subagent-trust.md Task 2, whose stated goal was defanging on eight model-facing child paths; that plan never considered a marker line or a permission-mention pattern, so the omission is unrecorded rather than decided. One scoping caveat worth carrying into any fix: the gap is in OUR Pi orchestrator path; a Claude-provider session's subagents run inside the SDK's native claude binary (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.183, feature-flagged off by default via NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE), where upstream's own scan would apply if that binary is >= 2.1.210.

results.claim: A resumed session restores its permission mode, EXCEPT `plan` and `bypassPermissions`, which are never restored.
results.quote: Permission mode: the mode the session was in. `plan` and `bypassPermissions` are never restored; [bypassing permissions](/docs/en/permission-modes#skip-all-checks-with-bypasspermissions-mode) must be enabled again at launch, with one of its launch flags or `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in [settings](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings).
results.ourState: The persisted `permissionMode` is restored verbatim. `normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode` runs only a provider-shape normalization (`normalizePiPermissionMode`) and has no exclusion list; `setPermissionMode(restoreModeKey, managed.permissionMode ?? 'default', { changedBy: 'restore' })` then installs it as-is. There is no bypass re-acceptance gate anywhere (`grep -rani "bypassAccepted|acceptedBypass|bypassDisclaimer"` → no hits), so a session last left in `bypassPermissions` comes back in `bypassPermissions` after an app restart, and a session left in `plan` comes back in `plan`.

verdict.why:
STEP 1 PASSES — the quote is real. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md` = 195 lines / 23345 bytes (md5 e9c5f0abe3ea3562407d8ac63a1162f8). The sentence is at :34 verbatim, in the bullet list under `### What a resumed session restores`. Read WHOLE, the line carries two more sentences and neither reverses it: '`auto` is restored only when your account still meets the auto mode requirements. Pass `--permission-mode` to override the restored mode.' The page is in the corpus snapshot (`scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv` -> `sessions	Manage sessions`). This is the one part of the finding that holds.

STEP 2 PASSES — the cited lines exist and say what was claimed. `SessionManager.ts:7617` is `const normalizedPersistedMode = this.normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode(managed)`, `:7622` is `setPermissionMode(restoreModeKey, managed.permissionMode ?? 'default', { changedBy: 'restore' })`, `:7639` is `if (normalizedPersistedMode) this.persistSession(managed)`; `:17351` is the normalizer. Correct file, correct content.

STEP 3 KILLS IT — the OUR STATE sentence is FALSE on BOTH of its supporting assertions, and each is a documented false-positive shape from this repo's own list.

(a) 'has no exclusion list' — FALSE, and it is the reason 'restored verbatim' is wrong. `normalizePersistedSessionPermissionMode` (:17351) calls `normalizeSessionPermissionMode` (:17345), which for a Pi session calls `normalizePiPermissionMode` (:17341) = `normalizeManagedPermissionMode(mode, this.managedPiPolicy.disabledPermissionModes)`. `disabledPermissionModes` IS a permission-mode exclusion list, applied to the persisted mode at exactly the restore point, and it demotes rather than merely rejects (`mode-types.ts:134-151`, fallback chain). The repo PINS the demotion for this exact mode: `SessionManager.orchestration.test.ts:952-957` builds `restored = { permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions', previousPermissionMode: 'auto' }` under a policy with `disabledPermissionModes: ['allow-all']`, asserts the normalizer returns `true`, and asserts `restored` comes back `{ permissionMode: 'acceptEdits', previousPermissionMode: 'acceptEdits' }` — and the `true` drives `:7639`, which rewrites the demoted mode to disk. The list is EMPTY BY DEFAULT (`pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1136` `disabledPermissionModes: Object.freeze([])`), which is a default, not an absence. Per audit row R30b, Claude's own `disableBypassPermissionsMode` settings key IS this list spelled `['allow-all']`, and `settings.md:386` says that key 'works from any scope' — so the org-level control Claude documents for exactly this is the control we ship.

(b) 'There is no bypass re-acceptance gate anywhere' — FALSE, and it is the wrong-identifier-names shape (inert-worklist §4 shape 4: name the subsystem, not a guessed identifier). The gate is `apps/electron/src/renderer/lib/bypass-permissions-gate.ts`: `needsBypassPermissionsAcknowledgment` / `recordBypassPermissionsAcknowledgment`, storage key `nessy:bypass-permissions-acknowledged`. It is wired at `App.tsx:1362` inside `handleSessionOptionsChange` — `if (updates.permissionMode === 'bypassPermissions' && needsBypassPermissionsAcknowledgment()) { setPendingBypassSwitch(...); return }` — held in state at `App.tsx:326`, rendered by `components/BypassPermissionsDialog.tsx` (mounted `App.tsx:2007`, accept records the ack `:2011`), and tested at `lib/__tests__/bypass-permissions-gate.test.ts:16-30`. Its docblock cites the very rule the finding invokes: 'Claude makes bypass launch-only and shows a one-time responsibility acknowledgment. The desktop analog: the FIRST activation of `bypassPermissions` on this install raises a confirmation dialog.' None of the three greps the finding ran (`bypassAccepted|acceptedBypass|bypassDisclaimer`) can hit any of those names.

RECORDED OWNER DECISIONS COVER BOTH HALVES.
• PLAN half: a harvested category string at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:465` — 'Claude's plan mode exits on plan approval; ours stays persistent — accepting a plan transitions the session through one deliberate clamped force-set and re-entry is explicit, so a session never silently leaves plan merely because a plan was approved' — written in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-claude-mode-vocabulary.md:220-224` (§'Category strings — what stays stricter than Claude'), landed as commit `c4f71c17` under audit row V1. Plan is deliberately a PERSISTENT mode in this fork, the opposite framing from Claude's transient plan; restoring it is the stricter direction, not a weakening.
• BYPASS half: audit row V1 (`2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md`, 'Owner decision 2026-07-31') adopts Claude's vocabulary plus 'gates (bypass reachable only behind an explicit enable with a responsibility dialog …)'. Carried in shipped source at `mode-types.ts:71-79`: 'permission-modes.md makes bypass launch-only ("can only be set at startup"), and the desktop analog is an explicit enable — a workspace `cyclablePermissionModes` that names it, or the mode menu behind the first-activation responsibility dialog.' The doc's remedy is CLI-launch-shaped ('one of its launch flags or `permissions.defaultMode`'); an Electron app has no launch flag, and the substitute was chosen deliberately, not missed.

WHAT SURVIVES, MUCH NARROWER (see correctedState). The ack is once-per-install in localStorage and is consulted only on the ACT of switching, never on restore; a NUL-safe `grep -ran bypassPermissions` over `apps/electron/src/main`, `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap` and `packages/server/src` returns zero non-test hits, so no startup path re-gates it. With the default empty `disabledPermissionModes`, a session last left in bypass does return in bypass after a restart without a second dialog. That residue is 'the one-time ack is not re-checked at restore' — not 'no gate and no exclusion list exist', which is what was filed and is false.
verdict.correctedState: Not restored verbatim and not ungated. The restore path at SessionManager.ts:7617 runs disabledPermissionModes through normalizeManagedPermissionMode, which DEMOTES a persisted mode and re-persists it (pinned by SessionManager.orchestration.test.ts:952-957: persisted bypassPermissions restores as acceptEdits under disabledPermissionModes:['allow-all'], the same list Claude's disableBypassPermissionsMode maps to). A bypass responsibility gate does exist — apps/electron/src/renderer/lib/bypass-permissions-gate.ts, wired at App.tsx:1362 and rendered by BypassPermissionsDialog.tsx — the finding's three grep spellings simply do not name it. Restoring `plan` is a recorded owner decision (deviation-register:465, plan 2026-07-31-claude-mode-vocabulary.md:220-224, commit c4f71c17): plan is deliberately a persistent mode here, which is the stricter direction. Bypass's launch-only rule was deliberately translated to a desktop analog by owner decision 2026-07-31 (audit row V1; mode-types.ts:71-79), since the desktop has no launch flag. Residual gap, narrower than filed: the acknowledgment is once-per-install and is checked only when the user switches modes, not at restore, so with the default empty disabledPermissionModes a session left in bypassPermissions returns in bypassPermissions after an app restart with no second dialog.

results.claim: Auto memory loads the first 200 lines OR 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever limit is reached first.
results.quote: The first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, load at the start of each session.
results.ourState: `readMemoryFile` caps at `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines and nothing else — there is no byte cap anywhere (`grep -ran "25 \* 1024|25600|25000" packages/shared/src` finds only unrelated token budgets). A MEMORY.md of 200 long lines loads unbounded bytes into every session's system prompt. sub-agents.md repeats the same rule for per-agent memory ("the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` in the memory directory, whichever comes first"), so the gap applies on both paths.

verdict.why: Tried to refute on all three axes and could not. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works.md gives the sentence word-for-word on line 74, inside the '## What Claude can access' bullet list: '* **[Auto memory](/docs/en/memory#auto-memory).** Learnings Claude saves automatically as you work, like project patterns and your preferences. The first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md, whichever comes first, load at the start of each session.' Read the WHOLE line — the preceding sentence is scene-setting and nothing in it reverses or qualifies the limit. memory.md:384 and sub-agents.md:521 restate the same rule, so the sub-agents.md half of the claim is also verbatim-accurate. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-32 is `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` = `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — a line slice with no byte check. Exactly as claimed. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and in both directions: no byte cap exists anywhere on the memory path. `grep -ran` over packages/ apps/ for 25*1024 / 25600 / 25000 / maxBytes / byteLimit (with -a, so NUL-carrying files are not skipped) returns only unrelated things: a 25_000-token skill-reattach budget, plugin-artifact and execution-receipt truncators, and RULE_PATTERN_EXPANSION_BYTE_LIMIT = 4MB in agent/memory/rule-matching.ts, which is a glob-expansion budget, not a load cap. One layer UP makes the gap larger, not smaller: prompts/system.ts:453-455 skips loadMemoryPromptBlock entirely when `capabilityContextPinned` — which is the live route on every normal send — and the pinned route reads each memory layer through capabilities/materializer.ts:168-184 `readText`, a whole-file `readFileSync` with no cap, whose content base-agent.ts:976-1014 `composePinnedCapabilityContext` pushes verbatim into the block. So on the live path there is not even a 200-line cap; the 200-line `readMemoryFile` survives only in the legacy fallback composer and in the import-scan pass at capabilities/native-sources.ts:427. One layer DOWN rules out the sibling-subsystem trap: capabilities/native-sources.ts:772 does define MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10*1024 with real truncation at :875-877, but that applies to lazily-read nested CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction files, a different subsystem, and never to MEMORY.md memory layers. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touch memory sizing). Not a rebrand, gateway or dropped-subscription product difference either. Only imprecision worth noting, and it does not refute: the claim says the overflow lands in 'every session's system prompt', whereas on the Claude backend the pinned block rides the user-message tail and only the legacy composer puts it in the system prompt; and the sub-agents.md path is a different defect (per-agent memory is unimplemented end to end — f089/f148 — so nothing is truncated there because nothing is loaded).
verdict.correctedState: There is no 25KB byte cap on auto-memory loading anywhere in the repo, and the live path applies no cap at all. `readMemoryFile` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:29-32) slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines with no byte check, but it is only reached by the LEGACY composer: prompts/system.ts:455 calls `loadMemoryPromptBlock` solely when the capability runtime is NOT pinned. On the live route the MEMORY.md layer is read whole by capabilities/materializer.ts:168-184 `readText` and pushed verbatim into the pinned block by base-agent.ts:976-1014, so neither the 200-line limit nor the 25KB limit is enforced. The only byte cap on any instruction content is MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 (capabilities/native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), which covers lazily-read nested CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md files, not MEMORY.md.

results.claim: `NO_PROXY` accepts a space-separated list as well as a comma-separated one.
results.quote: # Bypass proxy for specific requests - space-separated format
results.ourState: Both NO_PROXY parsers split on commas only. `parseNoProxyRules` calls `splitCommaSeparated` (`str.split(',')`), and the Pi interceptor does `NO_PROXY.split(',')`. `NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"` therefore yields one rule whose host is the whole string, which matches no hostname — every request goes through the proxy with no error or warning, the opposite of what the operator configured.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass and the consequence reproduces under a positive control.

(1) DOC — the quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at network-config.md:30, and the whole line is just that comment; the following lines are its payload: line 31 `export NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"`, line 32 `# Bypass proxy for specific requests - comma-separated format`, line 33 the comma twin, line 34-35 `# Bypass proxy for all requests` / `export NO_PROXY="*"`. Both formats are presented as accepted spellings of the same variable, so the claimed behaviour is a fair reading, not a paraphrase. The page also states `All environment variables shown on this page can also be configured in settings.json`, so the settings-side field inherits the same contract. Our own earlier verification file already recorded this reading (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:720).

(2) CODE — confirmed, with one line of drift in the citation. `splitCommaSeparated` is `network-proxy-utils.ts:11-13` and is literally `str.split(',')`. `parseNoProxyRules` calls it at :222, not :221 (the page-relative anchor drifted by one; the identifier and behaviour are exactly as claimed), and its own docblock at :210 says `Parse a comma-separated NO_PROXY string`. The Pi interceptor is verbatim as cited: `unified-network-interceptor.ts:84-86` does `NO_PROXY.split(',')`, fed by :69 `process.env.NO_PROXY || process.env.no_proxy`. No whitespace handling exists on any path; `normalizeProxyString` (storage.ts:2556-2559) only trims the outer edges of the whole string, and the Settings > Network field (AppSettingsPage.tsx:88) likewise only `.trim()`s.

(3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN — the consequence is real, not absorbed by anything upstream, and the claim if anything UNDERSTATES the surface. Layer up: `pi-agent.ts:1466` spawns the Pi subprocess with `env: { ...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ... }`, so an operator who exports the documented space-separated `NO_PROXY` in their shell has it inherited straight into the interceptor when no in-app proxy setting overrides it (`proxy-env.ts:70-73` emits NO_PROXY only when `settings.enabled` AND `settings.noProxy` are set). `network-runtime.ts:197-215` restores the launch environment's NO_PROXY on disable precisely so an operator-provided proxy survives — i.e. the env spelling is a supported input, not an internal-only channel. Layer down: `getProxyForUrl` (interceptor :106-109) returns PROXY_URL whenever bypass fails and the wrapper sets it explicitly as Bun's `proxy:` fetch option (:2386, :2432-2434), which overrides whatever Bun would have decided from the env itself — so the mis-parse actively forces the request through the proxy. There is also a THIRD surface the finding does not name: `apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:216-218` builds Chromium's `proxyBypassRules` as `splitCommaSeparated(settings.noProxy).join(',')`, so every Electron session partition (browser pane, update feed, default) gets the same single bogus rule. No warning anywhere: the only proxy logging is booleans (`hasNoProxy: true`, network-proxy.ts:245-251) and a debug-only line (interceptor :112).

POSITIVE CONTROL (required for a silent-failure claim) — ran both parsers against the doc's own two example strings. Space form: one rule `{host: "localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com"}`, and bypass=false for localhost:3000, example.com, api.example.com and 192.168.1.1. Comma form (the control on the same rig): four rules, bypass=true for all four URLs. The interceptor's replicated parser gives the same split (space -> false, comma -> true). So the failure is measured, not inferred.

NOT an owner decision: absent from all nine dated rows in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries). NOT a deliberate fork difference either: this is not a subscription flow, a gateway target or a rename — the surrounding code treats this very page as its contract and cites it by line (network-config.md:58, :83, :101 in network-proxy-utils.ts; :78, :92-98 in proxy-env.ts), and mTLS/certStore on the same page were implemented from it.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED, with the scope widened and one anchor corrected. Three surfaces split NO_PROXY on commas only, not two: (a) packages/shared/src/config/network-proxy-utils.ts:11-13 splitCommaSeparated, reached from parseNoProxyRules at :222 (the finding said :221) — this drives the Electron undici dispatcher and the headless server's fetch trust chain; (b) packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:84-86, the Pi subprocess, which reads the ENV spelling at :69; (c) apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts:216-218, which pre-splits on commas before handing Chromium proxyBypassRules, so the Electron sessions (browser pane, update feed, default partition) lose the bypass too. Measured with a positive control: NO_PROXY="localhost 192.168.1.1 example.com .example.com" produces exactly one rule whose host is the entire string and bypasses nothing, while the comma twin bypasses all four hosts. The mis-parse is not merely inert — the interceptor sets Bun's explicit `proxy:` fetch option once bypass returns false (:2386, :2432-2434), so the request is actively routed through the proxy. Nothing warns: proxy logging is booleans only. The env spelling is genuinely reachable by an operator, since pi-agent.ts:1466 spreads process.env into the subprocess and proxy-env.ts only overwrites NO_PROXY when the in-app proxy is enabled with a noProxy value. Fix is one line — split on /[\s,]+/ in splitCommaSeparated's NO_PROXY caller and in the interceptor — but note splitCommaSeparated is SHARED with parseCertStoreSources (certStore, network-proxy-utils.ts:37), where the documented separator is comma only, so widen a NO_PROXY-specific splitter rather than the shared helper.

results.claim: Subagents spawned by a workflow run in `acceptEdits` regardless of the session's permission mode; file edits are auto-approved and only the launch prompt follows the session mode.
results.quote: The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode.
results.ourState: No workflow-specific permission floor exists. Workflow `agent()` calls go through the same `spawnChildSession` as ordinary subagents, which forwards only `args.agentDef.permissionMode` and otherwise omits it so the host inherits the parent's mode. `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts packages/shared/src/workflows/` returns nothing. A workflow launched from a `default`-mode session therefore prompts on every file edit its agents make — for a fan-out of dozens of agents, in a run the page describes as unattended.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass, and the challenge made the finding STRONGER rather than weaker.

(1) DOC SENTENCE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows.md` line 181, read whole: "Your permission mode controls only the launch prompt above. The subagents the workflow spawns always run in `acceptEdits` mode and inherit your [tool allowlist](/docs/en/settings#permission-settings), regardless of your session's mode. File edits are auto-approved." The quoted sentence is the middle of three; neither neighbour reverses it — the third sentence reinforces it. Line 183 scopes the floor ("Shell commands, web fetches, and MCP tools that aren't in your allowlist can still prompt you mid-run"), so the floor is edits-only, not blanket. The one apparent tension, line 125 ("a workflow started this way runs inside the session's existing permission mode, and its agents' tool calls receive the same permission checks and sandboxing as any other tool call"), is about the keyword route not changing the SESSION's mode and is consistent with 181+183: acceptEdits still runs every other check, it only auto-approves edits. Page is row 193 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a Claude Code contract page.

(2) CITED CODE — accurate. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:570-575` builds the child restrictions and forwards permissionMode only when the agent def carries one: `...(args.agentDef.permissionMode === undefined ? {} : { permissionMode: args.agentDef.permissionMode })`; the comment at :328-330 states the omission semantics outright — "`permissionMode` is OMITTED, which the host reads as 'inherit the parent's mode verbatim'". Absence re-verified with `-a` (NUL-byte trap): `grep -ran acceptEdits packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/ packages/shared/src/workflows/ packages/shared/src/config/workflow-settings.ts` → no output. `workflow-tool.ts:560-623` (`runAgent`) builds SpawnChildSessionArgs with agentDef/model/effort/cwd/signal/depth/ownerTaskId/background and NO permission field, so workflow agents take the identical path as ordinary subagents — confirmed by `options.spawn ?? spawnChildSession` at :466.

(3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN — consequence verified separately from the identifier, and the identifier check UNDERSTATED it. Up: the host does not merely inherit, it CLAMPS narrow-only. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10406-10417` (`startPiChildRuntime`, depth 1): `childPermissionMode = record.restrictions.permissionMode ? clampPermissionModeToParent(requested, parentPermissionMode) : parentPermissionMode`, and `:10910-10934` applies the same narrow-only rule to nested child ceilings. Because `PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER` (mode-types.ts:63) ranks acceptEdits(4) above default(3), `clampPermissionModeToParent('acceptEdits','default')` returns `'default'` — so from a default-mode session the documented floor is unreachable EVEN IF an agent def explicitly requests acceptEdits. Down: the auto-approve is gated on the mode. `pre-tool-use.ts:1660` sets `autoAllowFileWrites` only when `effectivePermissionMode === 'acceptEdits'`, and `:1930-1948` returns a `file_write` PromptInfo for every FILE_WRITE_TOOLS call when that flag is false. And the prompt is not swallowed by the child being hidden: `SessionManager.ts:6452-6484` (`permissionSurfaceRouting`) deliberately walks to the nearest visible ancestor so a hidden child's prompt renders in the human's main session. So the claimed consequence — a default-mode workflow prompts per file edit, per agent, across the fan-out — is real end-to-end, not an unwired-identifier artefact.

NOT a recorded owner decision: absent from `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (all nine read; none touches workflows or permission floors) and from §4's false positives. NOT a deliberate product difference: no NESSY_ rename, no dropped subscription flow, no gateway concern. It was in fact SPECIFIED and then not built — `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:288` flags it explicitly ("Launch consent and the subagent permission floor are absent… That is a permission-floor statement, not a UX note") and :294 item (e) asks for both halves, but the executing plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-workflow-recipes-and-governance.md` Task 5 implemented only the launch consent (`workflow_launch` prompt type, per-project remember). The floor half was dropped silently with no deviation recorded, so the audit row R4's ✅ overstates coverage on this point.
verdict.correctedState: Half of the doc's paragraph is implemented, half is missing. IMPLEMENTED: the per-run launch consent gated by session permission mode (`workflow_launch` prompt type, per-workflow-per-project remember; plan 2026-07-27-workflow-recipes-and-governance.md Task 5), and tool-allowlist inheritance by the child. MISSING: the `acceptEdits` floor for workflow-spawned subagents. Workflow `agent()` calls (`workflow-tool.ts:560-623`) use the same `spawnChildSession` as ordinary subagents, which forwards `permissionMode` only when the agent def sets one (`spawner.ts:575`; omission means "inherit the parent" per `spawner.ts:328-330`). Stronger than the original claim: the host clamps NARROW-ONLY (`SessionManager.ts:10411-10417` at depth 1, `:10926-10934` for nested ceilings), and since `PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER` ranks acceptEdits above default, `clampPermissionModeToParent('acceptEdits','default')` yields `'default'` — an agent def cannot opt in to the floor from a default-mode session either. Consequence confirmed through the whole chain: `pre-tool-use.ts:1660` enables `autoAllowFileWrites` only for `acceptEdits`, `:1930-1948` mints a `file_write` prompt otherwise, and `SessionManager.ts:6452-6484` routes a hidden child's prompt to the nearest visible ancestor, so a default-mode workflow fan-out really does put one modal in front of the user per file edit per agent. `grep -ran acceptEdits` over the orchestrator, `packages/shared/src/workflows/` and `workflow-settings.ts` returns nothing, and no workflow setting exposes a mode (`ResolvedWorkflowSettings` carries only disableWorkflows/sizeGuideline/keywordTriggerEnabled).

results.claim: A saved workflow invoked without input sees `args` as `undefined`.
results.quote: If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script.
results.ourState: The runtime substitutes an empty object: `compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}))`. A script that branches on `args === undefined` (or on `!args`) to supply defaults never takes that branch, because `{}` is truthy and defined.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows.md line 227 reads in full: "Claude passes the list as structured data, so the script can call array and object methods on `args` directly without parsing it first. If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script." The quoted sentence is exact, and the first half of the two-sentence line does not reverse it. (2) CITED SITE: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:750 is exactly `returnValue = await compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}));`. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and with a positive control: compiling `return JSON.stringify({typeofArgs: typeof args, isUndefined: args === undefined, falsy: !args, nullishDefault: (args ?? 'DEFAULT-BRANCH-TAKEN')})` through the real compileWorkflowScript gives, with our call-site expression (input.args undefined ?? {}): {"typeofArgs":"object","isUndefined":false,"falsy":false,"nullishDefault":{}}; the SAME script with args passed through unmodified (the documented Claude behaviour) gives {"typeofArgs":"undefined","isUndefined":true,"falsy":true,"nullishDefault":"DEFAULT-BRANCH-TAKEN"}. The control proves the sandbox itself does not default -- sandbox.ts:277-300 passes api.args straight in as the `args` Function parameter -- so the `?? {}` at the call site is the sole cause and the branch really is unreachable. LAYER UP: normalizeInput (workflow-tool.ts:186) carries `args: params.args` through unchanged and the tool schema (:436) marks args optional ('Optional JSON value exposed inside the script as args'), so nothing upstream supplies a value; no slash-command layer injects one either (packages/shared/src/workflows/ has no args producer). LAYER DOWN: the nested `workflow(nameOrRef, recipeArgs)` helper repeats the identical coalescing at :660 -- so there are TWO chokepoints, not the one the finding cites. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns the workflow runtime (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries). Nuance worth recording, not a refutation: the substitution is more lenient than the spec in one direction (`args.foo` yields undefined instead of throwing a TypeError), but it silently defeats the documented `args ?? default` / `if (!args)` idiom a model writing a script from Claude's page would use.
verdict.correctedState: The runtime substitutes an empty object at BOTH invocation chokepoints, not one: the tool's own run (`compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}))`, workflow-tool.ts:750) and the in-script nested-workflow helper (`compileWorkflowScript(source)(makeApi(recipeArgs ?? {}))`, workflow-tool.ts:660). normalizeInput (:186) leaves an omitted `args` as undefined and the sandbox does not default it (sandbox.ts:277-300 injects api.args verbatim as the `args` Function parameter), so the coalescing is the sole cause. A script that branches on `args === undefined`/`!args`/`args ?? d` to supply defaults therefore never takes that branch. results.claim: A `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root, in .gitignore syntax, causes matching gitignored files to be copied into every worktree Claude creates with git.
results.quote: To copy them automatically when Claude creates a worktree, add a `.worktreeinclude` file to your project root.
results.ourState: The string `worktreeinclude` does not occur anywhere in our source (only in a planning spec, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`, as an unbuilt item). `worktreeCreateCommands` emits only `worktree add`, optional `sparse-checkout set`, and `checkout`; `worktreeSymlinkPlan` handles only `symlinkDirectories`. results.claim: Under the default `"fresh"` base, Claude Code refreshes `origin/HEAD` before branching — fetching the default branch when the repo has not been fetched in 24 hours, capped at five seconds, falling back to the cached ref.
results.quote: For a `"fresh"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails.
results.ourState: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` for `baseRef: 'fresh'` emits exactly `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/HEAD` (allowFailure) then local `HEAD`. There is no fetch, no staleness check and no timeout anywhere on the worktree path (`grep -ran "'fetch'" packages/server-core/src` → no hit). A repository whose `origin/HEAD` was last updated weeks ago silently branches every "fresh" worktree off that stale commit — which is the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding; nothing refutes it. (1) VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md line 112 opens with the quoted sentence character-for-character: "For a `\"fresh\"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails." I read the WHOLE line: its two remaining sentences REINFORCE rather than reverse the claim - "If no remote is configured, or `origin/HEAD` isn't cached locally and can't be fetched, the worktree falls back to your current local `HEAD`" (the half we DO implement) and "Before v2.1.208, a fresh worktree used whatever `origin/HEAD` was already cached locally" (which names our current behaviour exactly). The page is row 194 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude Code contract page, not Codex/MCP. (2) CITED CODE: worktree-git-plan.ts:39-53 is verbatim as claimed - for baseRef 'fresh' it returns exactly [{operation:'base-fresh', args:['-C',repoRoot,'rev-parse','origin/HEAD'], allowFailure:true}, {operation:'base', args:['-C',repoRoot,'rev-parse','HEAD']}]. No fetch, no last-fetch timestamp, no default-branch resolution. SessionManager.ts:10150 is the sole production call site (the only other hits are the import at :136 and worktree-git-plan.test.ts, which pins the exact argv - so the missing fetch is frozen by a test). (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN. Down: runWorktreeGit (SessionManager.ts:10020-10048) is the only git runner on this path; it spawns `git` with host-built argv under a read-only sandbox profile - it does not prepend or inject anything. Up: the WorktreeLeaseService policy.select at :10144-10161 just loops the candidates and takes the first non-empty sha; git.create (:10164) consumes that sha with `worktree add -b`. No fetch upstream. Repo-wide absence check with -a and a positive control: `grep -ranE "'fetch'|\"fetch\"" --include='*.ts' packages apps` returns only WebFetch permission-DSL tests and a schema fixture - zero git-fetch call sites; the same grep style DOES find `command: 'git'` at SessionManager.ts:10033 and eight git invocations in workspace/git-branches.ts (which also never fetches), so grep is reading these files. packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts contains neither 'fetch' nor 'origin/'. Sibling-subsystem check: there is no second worktree-creation path - session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts (EnterWorktree) routes through the same lease service, and no other module runs `git worktree add`. NOT an owner decision: inert-worklist section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions - none touches worktrees. NOT a deliberate product difference either: worktree-settings.ts:68-76 records the ONE intentional worktree deviation (bgIsolation default 'none' instead of 'worktree') and explicitly says of the other key "Documented default for `baseRef` is `\"fresh\"` and we match it" - so freshness is claimed, not disclaimed. definitions.ts:51-54 goes further and asserts the isolation contract is "already satisfied here: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` resolves `origin/HEAD` first", a claim that is now stale against the page. The origin of the gap is visible: our contract distillation (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:126) captured baseRef as '"fresh" default = origin/<default-branch>' with no fetch clause, and the implementing plan 2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md contains the word 'fetch' only in an instruction to fetch raw markdown - i.e. we built against the pre-v2.1.208 page and the upstream refresh behaviour landed afterwards. CONSEQUENCE verified separately from the identifier: `git rev-parse origin/HEAD` resolves refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, a purely local remote-tracking ref that only moves on fetch, so on a repo last fetched weeks ago every 'fresh' worktree branches off the stale cached commit with no error and no signal - exactly what the page says changed in v2.1.208.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with two precision fixes to the claim's wording. (a) 'no timeout anywhere on the worktree path' is too strong: every worktree git command DOES carry a 60s process timeout (SessionManager.ts:10043, `timeoutMs: 60_000`). What is absent is the doc's five-second cap specific to the freshness fetch - moot, because no fetch is issued at all. (b) 'sole call site' is right for production only; worktree-git-plan.test.ts:14-28 also calls it and pins the exact two-candidate argv, so the missing fetch is asserted by a test and any fix must update that test. Everything else stands: for baseRef 'fresh' the candidates are exactly `git -C <root> rev-parse origin/HEAD` (allowFailure) then `git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD`; there is no `git fetch`, no last-fetch staleness check and no default-branch resolution anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (verified with grep -a plus a positive control), and neither runWorktreeGit below nor WorktreeLeaseService/EnterWorktree above supplies one. Nessy therefore implements the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed, and it is not a recorded owner decision or a rebranding/product difference - worktree-settings.ts explicitly claims parity on baseRef while disclaiming only bgIsolation, and definitions.ts:51-54 carries a now-stale comment asserting the base-branch contract is satisfied.

results.claim: MEMORY.md is loaded truncated to whichever comes first of 200 lines or 25 KB.
results.quote: The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation.
results.ourState: Only a 200-line constant exists (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`); there is no byte cap anywhere in the repo. Worse, the LIVE path does not apply even the line cap: pinned memory layers are read through `materializer.readText`, which returns the whole file, and `composePinnedCapabilityContext` pushes that content verbatim. The 200-line `readMemoryFile` is only used by the legacy fallback composer and by the import-scan pass.

verdict.why: Tried to refute on all three axes and could not. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md, line 384, word for word: 'The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation.' Read the WHOLE line — it is a three-sentence line and the other two REINFORCE the claim ('Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start.' / 'Claude keeps `MEMORY.md` concise by moving detailed notes into separate topic files.'). :30 restates it in the comparison table ('Every session (first 200 lines or 25KB)'), :386 adds the post-write measurement against 'the 200-line and 25KB read limits', and :390 scopes it ('This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length'), which is the one qualifier that could have refuted this and does not — see (3). (2) CITED FILES: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-32 is `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` = `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — a line slice, no byte check. capabilities/materializer.ts:181 is `const content = readFileSync(contentPath);` inside `readText` (169-186), a whole-file read returned at :186 with no cap. base-agent.ts `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (~976-1014) does `for (const layer of runtime.view.memory) { const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource); ... }` and pushes `content` verbatim into `<capability-layer>` bodies; the cited 989-1006 window is the rule-parse/import-strip tail of that same loop (the `readText` call itself sits a few lines above at ~977), so the line range is loose by ~12 lines but points at the right function and the right loop. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, both directions. Live-path claim CONFIRMED end to end: prompts/system.ts:453-455 `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, and `capabilityContextPinned` is positional arg 12 of `getSystemPrompt`, passed as `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` by BOTH live backends (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256). So whenever the capability runtime is active — the normal turn — the 200-line `readMemoryFile` composer is skipped entirely and MEMORY.md rides the uncapped pinned path. `rg -na 'MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT|readMemoryFile'` over packages/ apps/ (with -a; native-sources.ts does carry NUL bytes) returns exactly three non-test consumers: memory-store.ts itself, the legacy `loadMemoryPromptBlock` chain, and capabilities/native-sources.ts:427, the `@import` scan — which matches the claim's last sentence precisely. The only test asserting the cap (memory-store.test.ts:47 'caps prompt reads to 200 lines') tests `readMemoryFile` directly, i.e. the dead branch. Byte-cap claim CONFIRMED: no 25KB constant exists on the memory path; the only instruction byte cap in the repo is MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 (capabilities/native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), and that is the SIBLING subsystem — lazily discovered nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction files, never a MEMORY.md memory layer. (I nearly missed that constant by piping a grep through `head -30`, the exact trap AGENTS.md warns about.) The doc's :390 carve-out does not rescue us either: this fork's MEMORY.md is the auto-memory index, not a CLAUDE.md analogue — the `remember` session tool appends agent-written entries stamped `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` to session/project/user MEMORY.md (session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:21-49) and a scheduled auto-memory cleanup pass ages them out, while human project instructions live in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md on the separate nested-instruction path. The fork also already carries the 200-line constant lifted from this very page, so matching this limit was the intent, not an out-of-scope Claude-ism. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 — the only memory-adjacent row there is PiPendingApprovalV1.requestedAt, unrelated. Not a rebrand, gateway, or dropped-subscription product difference. Two imprecisions that do not refute: the pinned block is not literally 'the system prompt' on the Claude backend (it rides the pinned context block, not `presetAppend`), and the same uncapped read applies to `.agents/rules` layers, which the claim does not mention.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with the live path worse than the doc gap alone implies. No 25KB byte cap exists anywhere on the memory path. `readMemoryFile` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:29-32) slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines with no byte check, but it is reachable only from the LEGACY composer: prompts/system.ts:453-455 calls `loadMemoryPromptBlock` solely when `capabilityContextPinned` is false, and both live backends pass `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` for that argument (pi-agent.ts:6607, claude-agent.ts:1256). On the live route every `runtime.view.memory` layer — project/user/session MEMORY.md and the `.agents/rules` files — is read whole by capabilities/materializer.ts:169-186 `readText` and pushed verbatim into the pinned capability block by `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (base-agent.ts ~976-1014), so neither the 200-line nor the 25KB limit is enforced on any turn that runs the capability runtime. The 200-line cap survives only in the legacy fallback composer, in the `@import` scan at capabilities/native-sources.ts:427, and in the one test that calls `readMemoryFile` directly. The repo's only instruction byte cap, MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 (capabilities/native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), governs lazily discovered nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files and never MEMORY.md.

results.claim: `@path` imports are recognised anywhere in a CLAUDE.md line, not only when the line begins with `@`.
results.quote: To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md:
results.ourState: `parseMemoryImportPath` returns null unless the TRIMMED LINE ITSELF starts with `@`. Both of the page's own examples — `See @README for project overview and @package.json ...` and `- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md` — are silently not imported. Only a whole-line `@path` (the shape our own CLAUDE.md uses) works.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass, and the consequence was reproduced by executing the shipped code rather than inferred.

(1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md` line 101 reads exactly: "To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md:" — single-sentence line, nothing after the colon reverses it. The whole surrounding section supports the mid-line reading rather than a merely 'anywhere in the file' reading: :95 "CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using `@path/to/import` syntax"; :99 "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks. To mention a path in your CLAUDE.md without importing it, wrap it in backticks: writing `` `@README` `` keeps the text literal, while `@README` outside backticks imports the file." — i.e. ANY unfenced `@README` imports; and the fenced example at :104-107 is decisive, carrying TWO imports mid-sentence on one line ("See @README for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands for this project.") and one after a list bullet ("- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md"). A third example at :116 is "- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md", also not line-initial.

(2) CITED LINE. packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:49-64 is exactly as claimed: after the `@import ` prefix branch, `if (!trimmed.startsWith('@') || trimmed.startsWith('@@')) return null;` at :55-57, where `trimmed = line.trim()`. There is no regex scan of the line interior. `grep -ran parseMemoryImportPath` over the repo finds one definition and exactly three call sites: memory-store.ts:83 (readMemoryFileWithImports), capabilities/native-sources.ts:428 (memoryFileRecords import walker), agent/base-agent.ts:1005 (strips import lines from a memory layer's pinned body). All three inherit the line-start gate; there is no second, laxer parser.

(3) CONSEQUENCE, TESTED SEPARATELY. Ran the shipped exports under `bun test`. parseMemoryImportPath returns null for all three of the page's own examples — "See @README ... and @package.json ..." => null, "- git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md" => null, "- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md" => null — while "@AGENTS.md" => "AGENTS.md" and "  @docs/git-instructions.md" => "docs/git-instructions.md". End-to-end through the real loader: a project MEMORY.md whose body is the docs' verbatim example block, with README / package.json / docs/git-instructions.md present on disk, yields a `<memory>` prompt block containing the literal `@`-lines and NONE of the three files' content markers. Zero imports resolved.

NOT AN OWNER DECISION AND NOT A PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 lists nine dated decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD; availableModels/enforceAvailableModels; autoMode.classifyAllShell; ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops; plugins/hooks-runtime.ts; SdkMcpServerConfig.required; SessionMirrorStore.delete; MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys; listSessionSummaries/listSessions) — none touches memory import parsing, and §4's false-positive shapes do not apply (this is not a getter/setter pair, not a default-parameter read, not enforcement one layer up, and the sibling-subsystem check is answered below). No branding/rename or dropped-subscription-flow framing applies. The only recorded Nessy-specific behaviour here is the EXTRA `@import <path>` form at :51-53, which adds a shape rather than removing one.

SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK (this is where the claim needs correcting, in the direction of a LARGER gap, not a smaller one). `@`-import expansion in this fork exists only for the MEMORY.md family and rules files: native-sources.ts routes MEMORY.md (:909 global, :978 session, :1027 project `.nessy-agent`, :1092 project) and rules (:691) through `memoryFileRecords`, whose walker at :427-429 is the only importer. The three files the doc sentence is actually ABOUT — PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md','CLAUDE.md','CLAUDE.local.md'] (native-sources.ts:82) — are emitted by `fileRecord('instruction', …)` at :988, :1082 and :1089 and never enter that walker. They become `promptLayers` (resolver.ts:966-967, views.ts:215-216), and base-agent.ts:966-974 pushes each layer's content VERBATIM; the import-stripping filter at :1005 sits in the separate `runtime.view.memory` loop, not the promptLayers loop. So in an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md, no `@path` import is expanded at all — mid-line or whole-line — and the raw `@…` line reaches the model as literal text. This fork's own CLAUDE.md `@AGENTS.md` only appears to work because AGENTS.md is independently loaded as its own instruction record.

ONE NARROWING THAT DOES NOT RESCUE THE CLAIM. On the Claude backend, claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']`, so the Agent SDK loads CLAUDE.md itself with Claude's own import semantics — the divergence does not exist there. But `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` is off by default and the default Pi backend goes through our parser, where the gap is real and reproduced.

'' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`. Only loadMemoryPromptBlock reaches readMemoryFileWithImports -> readMemoryFile(maxLines = 200), so the 200-line cap lives exclusively on the legacy branch.
