results.quote: To persist a chain across sessions, set `fallbackModel` in [settings](/docs/en/settings) as an array:
results.ourState: The stored-config schema types `fallbackModel` as a bare string (`z.string()`, default `''`, trimmed on load), and `PiAgent.getFallbackModel()` normalizes that single value. A settings file written from Claude's page (an array) fails validation rather than configuring a chain; there is no de-duplication, no three-entry cap and no `"default"` expansion.

verdict.why: Step 1 passes: the sentence is verbatim at model-config.md:373, and the whole line plus its section confirm the chain semantics (':361' block: 'Chains are capped at three models after duplicate removal, and extra entries are ignored'; ':381' 'Each entry accepts a model name or alias, and "default" expands to the default model'). Step 2 mostly passes with line drift: validators.ts:135 is exactly `fallbackModel: z.string()`; storage.ts:189 is really :194 (`fallbackModel: ''` in FALLBACK_CONFIG_DEFAULTS) with the trim at :273-276; pi-agent.ts:6233-6235 is really :6256-6258 (`getFallbackModel()` -> `normalizePiFallbackModelId(loadConfigDefaults().workspaceDefaults.fallbackModel)`). Step 3 FAILS, and it fails on exactly the shape the repo's audit history names. (a) The stated consequence -- 'A settings file written from Claude's page (an array) fails validation' -- is false. `ConfigDefaultsSchema` is never run in production: `loadConfigDefaults()` (storage.ts:233) does `readJsonFileSync` and hand-normalizes; the only `safeParse` in storage.ts is `StoredConfigTopLevelSchema` at :856, against a different file (config.json). `ConfigDefaultsSchema` is referenced only by `config/__tests__/validators-stored-config.test.ts`. This repo already recorded that trap: parity-audit.md:1040 and plans/2026-07-27-retention-and-checkpoint-gc.md:37 call it 'instance SIX of the recurring defect ... Production never validates config through zod ... Changing only the validator changes nothing.' f106 is instance seven. An array does not error -- storage.ts:273-276 (`typeof ... === 'string' ? trim() : ''`) and models-pi.ts:20-22 (`normalizePiFallbackModelId`) each coerce a non-string to `''`, so the array is silently discarded into 'no fallback', with no validation failure and no user-visible message. (b) The interop framing describes a path that does not exist. This `fallbackModel` is a Nessy key under `workspaceDefaults` in `~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json` -- a file `syncConfigDefaults()` (storage.ts:200-227) unconditionally OVERWRITES from the bundled asset on every launch -- not Claude's top-level `settings.json` key. pi-agent.ts:2994 states outright 'we have no reader for `~/.claude/settings.json`', and grepping (`-a`) apps/electron/src, packages/ui, apps/cli, packages/server, packages/server-core finds no `fallbackModel` surface at all. Pasting Claude's JSON snippet into a Claude settings file changes nothing here; it is the sibling-subsystem/identical-name trap from inert-worklist section 4 item 4. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (none mention fallback), and not a de-brand/subscription-drop difference. The arity gap itself is real but is already a recorded deviation: deviation-register.md:110, '**not implemented** -- model-config.md:361 configures an ordered chain ... Neither exists' (that entry's tail 'read by nothing' is now stale -- pi-agent.ts:6257 reads it).
verdict.correctedState: Real gap, wrong mechanism and wrong subsystem. Nessy has no fallback CHAIN: `workspaceDefaults.fallbackModel` is a single string (validators.ts:135 `z.string()`; default `''` at storage.ts:194; trimmed at storage.ts:273-276), and the runtime does exactly one hop -- `getRetryFallbackModel` (pi-agent.ts:6313-6324) returns that one id for the six codes in FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES (pi-agent.ts:337-343), `retryWithFallbackModel` `setModel`s to it and re-runs the turn with `fallbackModelRetry: true`, so a second failure has nowhere to go. There is no `fallbackModels` array anywhere in the repo, hence no dedup, no three-entry cap, no `"default"` expansion, no allowlist filtering and no compaction context-window rule. But an array does NOT fail validation: `ConfigDefaultsSchema` is test-only, `loadConfigDefaults()` never zod-parses, and both storage.ts:273-276 and `normalizePiFallbackModelId` coerce any non-string to `''` -- the chain is silently dropped to 'no fallback'. And the file involved is Nessy's own `~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json` (rewritten from the bundled asset every launch, with no UI to set the key), not Claude's `settings.json`, for which this fork has no reader (pi-agent.ts:2994).

results.claim: Default effort is `high` on every effort-capable model (except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`).
results.quote: The default effort is `high` on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`.
results.ourState: One global constant, `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL = 'medium'`, applies to every model, and there is no per-model default nor the documented cross-session hold on a model's first run. (Already carried in the deviation register at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:100`, but it is a changed default and is reported here as such.)

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md line 454 is exactly "The default effort is `high` on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`." It is a one-sentence line, so there is no second half reversing it; the neighbouring line 456 strengthens rather than weakens the claim ("When you first run Fable 5, Opus 4.8, or Opus 4.7, Claude Code applies that model's default effort even if you previously set a different level for another model, and holds it across sessions until you make an explicit effort choice ... Opus 5 has no such hold"). (2) CITED LINE: packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts:63 is `export const DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL: ThinkingLevel = 'medium';` as claimed. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and in both directions. One layer down: resolveEffortLevel (thinking-levels.ts:200-206) ends `?? input.fallback ?? DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL` with no model argument at all; the only model-aware rule in the file, clampThinkingLevelToModel + NARROWED_EFFORT_MODELS (:220-247), implements model-config.md:452 and only ever LOWERS an already-chosen level - it is not a default source. One layer up: SessionManager.ts:8900-8903 resolves caller -> trusted project default -> workspace default -> getDefaultThinkingLevel(), and getDefaultThinkingLevel (config/storage.ts:2481-2489) reads config.defaultThinkingLevel then bundled config-defaults, never the model id. apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:23 ships "thinkingLevel": "think", which normalizeThinkingLevel maps to 'medium', so the shipped effective default really is medium. base-agent.ts:473 uses the same constant. `grep -a` for defaultEffort/defaultThinking across the repo finds no per-model default field anywhere, and no hold/explicit-choice flag exists in thinking-levels.ts or SessionManager. Sibling-subsystem check: the Claude backend does not carry its own default either - claude-agent.ts only maps an already-resolved level through THINKING_TO_EFFORT (:234), so naming the wrong subsystem is not in play. Not a deliberate product difference: the fork does ship claude-opus-4-7 (config/models.ts:142, plus the Bedrock alias rows at :19-73), so the Opus 4.7 exception is live here, and the Claude provider is opt-in-but-present rather than dropped. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) - none touch effort. CAVEAT ON VALUE, NOT ON TRUTH: this is a known, already-recorded deviation, not a new discovery. deviation-register line 100 and plans/2026-07-29-effort-precedence.md:180 both carry the identical 'documented, not implemented' string for model-config.md:454/:456, and the finding itself discloses that. Its novelty is zero; its accuracy is intact.
verdict.correctedState: Accurate as filed, with one refinement. The default is not a bare constant in practice: it resolves through caller -> trusted project default -> workspace default -> app config `defaultThinkingLevel` -> bundled `config-defaults.json` (`"think"`, normalized to `medium`) -> `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL` (thinking-levels.ts:63). It is therefore user- and workspace-configurable, but at no point in that chain is the model id an input, and the shipped value is `medium`. There is no per-model default (no `defaultEffort` in `MODEL_REGISTRY`; `clampThinkingLevelToModel`/`NARROWED_EFFORT_MODELS` only narrow a level already chosen, per model-config.md:452) and no persisted explicit-choice flag, so the model-default hold of model-config.md:456 cannot exist either. Already carried at deviation-register:100 and plans/2026-07-29-effort-precedence.md:180 - report it as a duplicate of a recorded deviation, not as a new finding.

results.claim: Managed policy reaches devices through four sources in priority order (server-managed, plist/registry, file-based, HKCU registry), and the first non-empty one wins.
results.quote: Claude Code checks the four sources below in priority order and applies the first one that returns a non-empty configuration.
results.ourState: Only two sources exist: the server-delivered payload and the on-disk policy file. There is no macOS plist reader and no Windows registry reader (`grep -a` for `HKLM`, `SOFTWARE\\Policies`, `com.anthropic.claudecode` and plist reading finds nothing in our source; the only hits are vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources). The composition module states the two-source assumption as fact, and the winner label type has only `delivered | file | none`, so /status-style channel reporting can never say `(plist)`/`(HKLM)`/`(HKCU)`.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:4 ("We have exactly two, and they are the two the documentation names"), :130 (ManagedPolicyWinnerV1); packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48

verdict.why: All three checks pass, so the gap survives. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup.md line 45 carries the sentence exactly as quoted. Reading the WHOLE line does not reverse it — the remaining two sentences only add the cross-source lock-key carve-out and note that a configured policyHelper makes its output the only source those checks read; line 54 adds that policyHelper 'preempts all four sources'. The table at lines 47-52 names the four: Server-managed (Highest), plist/registry (High, macOS com.anthropic.claudecode / Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode), File-based managed (Medium), Windows user registry HKCU (Lowest). (2) CITED LINES: managed-composition.ts:4 does read 'We have exactly two, and they are the two the documentation names'; :130 is `export type ManagedPolicyWinnerV1 = 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'`; managed-policy-loader.ts:48 is the darwin file path '/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json'. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier: resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-138) has exactly two seams — `file` (loadManagedPiPolicyWithDiagnostics) and `delivered` (getDeliveredManagedPolicy) — and feeds only those into composeManagedPolicySources. Nothing upstream supplies a third. `grep -a` for HKLM/HKCU/HKEY_LOCAL/SOFTWARE\Policies/plist/CFPreferences/systemPreferences/getUserDefault/'reg query' across packages/*/src, apps/electron/src and apps/cli returns only (a) prose comments in managed-composition.ts:29,:44 and config-doctor.ts:12, (b) docs/, (c) an unrelated MachineGuid `reg query` in credentials/backends/secure-storage.ts:105, and (d) vendored bundles under packages/pi-agent-server/dist. No plist reader, no registry reader. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels filter placement, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) — none touches a managed delivery channel. NOT a rebrand artefact either: the file channel was ported under Nessy paths (/Library/Application Support/Nessy, /etc/nessy, %ProgramData%\Nessy), so a Nessy-domain plist and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Nessy would be the analogue and neither exists; the fork's dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows are unrelated to MDM policy delivery. It is already recorded as a known open gap at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:694 ('File-channel shape we do not have: drop-in managed-settings.d/ … plus macOS com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences and Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode … and a lower-priority HKCU tier') — recorded, but as a gap, not as a decision, and the drop-in half of that same list has since been implemented (managed-policy-loader.ts:62 managedPiPolicyDropInDirForPlatform), which leaves the plist/registry half genuinely outstanding. Two framing corrections that do NOT rescue the finding but must not be repeated downstream: the composition module does not hold an unexamined 'two-source assumption' — :27-29 recites the full documented tier (policyHelper > remote > MDM > file-based > HKCU) and :44 says in so many words 'excludes the user-writable HKCU tier, which we do not have'; and the '/status can never say (plist)/(HKLM)/(HKCU)' clause is vacuous restatement, since a label for a channel nothing reads carries no information (config-doctor.ts:16-18 deliberately quotes only the (remote)/(file) half of settings.md:706).
verdict.correctedState: Two of the four documented sources exist, not 'only two sources' as an arbitrary shortfall, and the arbitration RULE the quoted sentence states is implemented faithfully for the two we have. Present: the server-managed source (the gateway-delivered payload, packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts) at highest priority, and the file-based managed source (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-67, rebranded to /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/managed-policy.json, %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json, plus the managed-policy.d/ drop-in directory). composeManagedPolicySources implements priority-order-first-non-empty-wins exactly (managed-composition.ts:191-198: delivered wins wholesale iff carriesManagedSettings(delivered)), including the cross-source lock-key carve-out from the same doc line. Absent: the High-priority OS policy channel (macOS managed-preferences plist, Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies) and the Lowest-priority Windows HKCU tier — the docs themselves call HKCU 'a convenience default rather than an enforcement channel', so the material gap is the tamper-resistant plist/HKLM tier, which for a bank fork sits ABOVE the file channel we do have. policyHelper, the fifth preempting source on the same page (line 54), is also absent; it is out of scope for the server channel by a recorded reason (2026-07-29-delivered-policy-enforcement.md:245-246, server-managed-settings.md:129 says the server channel does not honour it) but not for the file/MDM channels, which is where the docs say it is read from. Channel labels follow the sources rather than the other way round: ManagedPolicyWinnerV1 = 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none' is a faithful two-source label set, and widening it is a consequence of adding readers, not an independent defect.

results.claim: A configured policyHelper executable preempts every other managed source and becomes the only managed configuration for the run.
results.quote: A configured [`policyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#compute-managed-settings-with-a-policy-helper) preempts all four sources: its output becomes the only managed configuration for the run.
results.ourState: `policyHelper` appears only inside a doc comment describing Claude's precedence chain; it is not a key in MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS and nothing executes a policy helper.

verdict.why: All three checks pass in the finding's favour. (1) VERBATIM: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup.md` -> the claimed sentence is an exact substring at line 54. Reading the WHOLE line adds only a pointer, not a reversal: 'A configured [`policyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#compute-managed-settings-with-a-policy-helper) preempts all four sources: its output becomes the only managed configuration for the run. See [Settings precedence](/docs/en/settings#settings-precedence).' The same page reinforces it at :45 ('when a `policyHelper` is configured, its output is the only source these checks read'), so even the cross-source lock-key carve-out at :45 collapses to the helper. The four sources it preempts are the :47-52 table (server-managed / plist-registry / file-based / HKCU). admin-setup is row 23 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page. (2) OUR STATE, as cited: packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:29 reads ' * rather than merged", `policyHelper` > remote > MDM > file-based > HKCU.' - a docblock quoting Claude's precedence chain, nothing more. packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534 is MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS, 34 keys, no policyHelper. Binary-safe `grep -ran --binary-files=text policyHelper packages apps scripts` returns 6 hits in 6 files: exactly one in tracked source (managed-composition.ts:29); the other five are gitignored build artifacts (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js, apps/electron/resources/{pi-agent-server,session-mcp-server}/index.js - confirmed by `git check-ignore -v`), and in each the hit is a bundled Claude-Code zod schema DESCRIPTION string ('Executable that computes managed settings at startup'), not an execution path. (3) LAYERS. Up: resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-138) composes exactly two seams, `file` (loadManagedPiPolicyWithDiagnostics) and `delivered` (getDeliveredManagedPolicy) - no helper seam; composeManagedPolicySources (managed-composition.ts:192-212) labels the winner only 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'. Down: refuseUnknownKeys (managed-policy.ts:727-733) strips any key outside MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS with `invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper` - a reported drop, not a silent implementation. So the CONSEQUENCE is verified independently of the identifier: an admin cannot compute Nessy managed policy from device posture/identity/a remote service; the only inputs are a static system file and the delivered payload. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK: no helper-executable mechanism exists elsewhere to misname. apiKeyHelper / credentialHelper / awsAuthRefresh: zero hits in packages/shared/src/config and packages/server-core/src. headersHelper exists only in the plugin MCP adapter (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1055) and is explicitly NOT implemented for any transport - a different subsystem and also unimplemented, so it cannot absorb this. The only real policyHelper implementation on disk is inside the vendored Claude binary (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude and sdk.mjs), which honours Claude's OWN managed-settings tier, not Nessy's managed-policy.json - and that provider is build-flag-off by default. NOT an owner decision: I read all nine dated entries in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) - policyHelper is in none of them. NOT a fork product difference: this is not a subscription flow, not a gateway concern, not a rename; the fork ships the very configuration scope the doc names, managedPiPolicyPathForPlatform resolving /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json (verified against packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.test.ts:99), so the eligible admin surface exists and simply lacks the helper.
verdict.correctedState:
Three refinements, none of which touches the substance.

1. Scope the 'appears only in a doc comment' claim to SHIPPED SOURCE. Precise: `policyHelper` appears exactly once in tracked source - packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:29, a docblock quoting Claude's managed-tier precedence order - plus five occurrences in gitignored build bundles where it is a vendored Claude-Code zod schema description, and one real implementation inside the vendored Claude Agent SDK binary that serves Claude's own managed tier, not Nessy's.

2. State the consequence rather than the identifier. Nessy's managed configuration has exactly two sources, `delivered` and `file` (resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy, managed-policy-resolution.ts:127; winner label in managed-composition.ts:198 is 'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'). An admin who writes `policyHelper` into /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json (or /etc/nessy/, or %ProgramData%\Nessy\) gets it stripped by refuseUnknownKeys with the diagnostic 'invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper' - visibly dropped, not silently ignored. There is no spawn, no `managedSettings` envelope parse, and no refresh timer.

3. This is a DUPLICATE of an already-recorded gap and should be filed against the existing row, not opened as new. It is the admin-setup.md restatement of the settings.md finding already adjudicated as f027 (docs/superpowers/specs/data/phase2-verdicts/f027.json, also refuted=false). The owning row is R25b in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:193 - '`policyHelper`, `wslInheritsWindowsSettings`, `managed-mcp.json` delivery out of scope | Record as C | ~ record' - which sits in section 2, 'Unjustified divergences', i.e. a tracked OPEN item of category C ('documented, not implemented'), not a closed decision. The recorded rationale in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-server-managed-delivery.md:213 ('OS-policy sources only') is HALF-COVERING: it correctly excludes policyHelper from the server-delivered channel, but does not justify its absence from the system-FILE loader, which admin-setup.md:54 and the settings.md helper section both name as a valid configuration scope and which this fork does ship.

results.claim: strictPluginOnlyCustomization is a managed key that forces skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers to come only from plugins or managed settings.
results.quote: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings
results.ourState: Absent from the managed policy schema. We ship the neighbouring locks (`allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers`) but nothing blocks user/project-sourced skills and agents wholesale. `grep -a` over all of packages/ and apps/ hits only two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources.

verdict.why:
The divergence survives all three challenges. One evidence detail is wrong and is corrected below; the conclusion is unaffected.

LEG 1 - QUOTE: CONFIRMED VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/admin-setup.md` (159 lines) -> line 91 is the 'Customization lockdown' row of the '## Managed settings' control table, and the middle cell reads character-for-character: 'Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can only come from plugins or managed settings'. Read the WHOLE line: it is a three-column markdown row whose remaining cells are the link `[Customization lockdown](/docs/en/settings#strictpluginonlycustomization)` and the key name `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`, plus column padding. There is no second sentence and nothing reverses the conclusion. Cross-checked against the canonical spec: settings.md line 328 repeats the sentence with '(Managed settings only)' and adds '`true` locks all four surfaces; an array locks only the named ones'; settings.md:1162 '#### strictPluginOnlyCustomization' carries the per-surface table (skills -> blocks `~/.claude/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`, still loads plugin/bundled/managed-policy-dir skills; agents -> blocks `~/.claude/agents/` and `.claude/agents/`; hooks -> blocks user/project/local settings.json hooks; mcp -> blocks `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json`). So the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR is an accurate restatement of the contract.

LEG 2 - CITED FILE:LINE: CONFIRMED. `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534` is `export const MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS`, exactly 34 entries: schemaVersion, disabledPermissionModes, permissionDsl, allowedPluginKeys, deniedPluginKeys, enabledPlugins, allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, allowPluginHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly, disableAllHooks, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, defaultMode, channelsEnabled, allowedChannelServers, sandbox, workflow, allowedHttpHookUrls, httpHookAllowedEnvVars, claudeRules, autoMode, cleanupPeriodDays, autoCompactEnabled, connectSourcesOnStartup, env, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, requiredMinimumVersion, requiredMaximumVersion, availableModels, enforceAvailableModels, strictKnownMarketplaces, extraKnownMarketplaces. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is not among them, and none of the 34 locks skill or agent ORIGIN. The claim's neighbouring-lock list is accurate as written: `allowManagedHooksOnly` (:177, :511), `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` (:203, :513), `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` (:129 ff., :508-509) all exist. (Note this is the one place f110 is MORE accurate than the sibling finding f017, which wrongly claimed we ship `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` - that name occurs only in six comments.)

LEG 2b - THE GREP CLAIM IS WRONG, THOUGH NOT FATALLY. `grep -rlaF strictPluginOnlyCustomization packages apps` returns FIVE files, not 'two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources': packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js, apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js, apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js. Each contains the string exactly ONCE, and every one is gitignored build output (`git check-ignore -v` -> .gitignore:7:dist for three, .gitignore:11 and :12 for the two under apps/electron/resources). The single occurrence is a vendored Claude zod schema field - `preprocess(...) union([boolean, array(enum(["skills","agents","hooks","mcp"]))]).optional().catch(undefined)` - declared and never read by name, so nothing enforces it there either. First-party source is genuinely 0: `grep -ran strictPluginOnlyCustomization --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.json packages/*/src apps/*/src` returns nothing.

LEG 3 - ONE LAYER UP: NO UPSTREAM HANDLER. There is no second managed surface that could absorb the key. `refuseUnknownKeys` (managed-policy.ts:727-733) drops any key outside MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS with disposition 'stripped', so an admin document carrying `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is silently degraded (surfaced only by `nessy-general-agent doctor`). `managed-composition.ts` records no counterpart for it. The plugin-scope keys (`allowedPluginKeys`, `deniedPluginKeys`, `enabledPlugins`) narrow WHICH PLUGINS load; they never touch user- or project-sourced skills and agents.

LEG 3 - ONE LAYER DOWN: THE CONSEQUENCE IS INDEPENDENTLY TRUE, AND THE SUBSYSTEM IS NAMED CORRECTLY. The surfaces the doc names really do exist here and really are unlocked. Skills: `packages/shared/src/skills/storage.ts` merges three native tiers - global `GLOBAL_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` (:473), workspace `loadWorkspaceSkills` (:478), project `.agents/skills` via `PROJECT_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` (:37, :485, :523) - then folds plugin skills in via `mergePluginSkills` (:494). The ONLY gate on the project tier is `if (projectRoot && projectTrusted)` (:484), i.e. the per-user project-trust consent flow - a user decision, which is precisely the decision this admin key exists to take away. Agents: `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:215` detects project subagents from `.claude/agents` (alongside `.nessy-agent/skills` at :212, `.claude/commands` :218, `.claude/hooks` :221, `.claude/settings.json` :224), again gated only by project trust. So there is no 'the identifier is unwired but the consequence is already handled upstream' escape, and no sibling-subsystem mix-up: the finding names skills and agents, and skills and agents are exactly what is unlocked.

OWNER-DECISION CHECK - NOT ONE OF THE NINE. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 lists SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` appears in none of them.

PRODUCT-DIFFERENCE CHECK - DOES NOT APPLY. Not a dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not gateway retargeting, not a rename. results.claim: minimumVersion is a managed version floor that stops auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum, and is weaker than requiredMinimumVersion.
results.quote: Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum
results.ourState: We implement `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (refuse to start outside the range) but not `minimumVersion`. Our own gate comment names the difference and stops there, so a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install.

verdict.why: Doc quote and identifier both check out; the CONSEQUENCE is false, which is this repo's documented recurring false positive (inert-worklist section 4, shape 3: 'enforcement one layer up'). (1) VERBATIM: admin-setup.md:97 is the table row '| [Version floor](/docs/en/settings) | Prevent auto-update from installing below an org-wide minimum | `minimumVersion` |'. Whole line read, nothing reverses it; :98 confirms requiredMinimumVersion is the stronger sibling. (2) IDENTIFIER: managed-version-gate.ts:12 does say 'Differs from `minimumVersion`, which prevents downgrades but never blocks startup', and MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-534) carries requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion and no `minimumVersion`. `grep -rna minimumVersion` over the repo finds no reader anywhere except that one comment. Both required* keys ARE enforced, on both surfaces: apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1102 and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645 both call assertManagedVersionAllowed (headless-start.ts:117). (3) CONSEQUENCE 'a managed fleet with an auto-update feed has no floor on what the updater may install' is FALSE. The updater is electron-updater 6.8.9 (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts). `allowDowngrade` is left at its default false (node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:138) and `autoUpdater.channel` is never assigned anywhere in apps/electron/src -- the channel setter (AppUpdater.js:44) is the only thing that would silently flip allowDowngrade to true. AppUpdater.js:362 returns `this.allowDowngrade && isLatestVersionOlder`, so a feed entry below the running version is rejected outright, logged at :405 as 'downgrade is disallowed'. There IS a floor on what the updater may install, it is hard, and it cannot be lowered by a user: the currently-running version. (4) The scenario the setting exists for cannot arise here. settings.md:294 defines minimumVersion as the pin created when a user switches from the `latest` channel to `stable` via /config and elects to stay put ('Choosing to stay sets this value'), with managed use as a secondary note. Our update channel is baked into app-update.yml at build time from NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL (apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80); there is no runtime channel switcher and no `claude update <version>` equivalent, so no in-product path can request an older version in the first place. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions (checked; they cover the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, classifyAllShell, delivery drops, hooks-runtime, SdkMcpServerConfig.required and three session-mirror rows). Note also that the plans' earlier answer at 2026-07-28-managed-policy-tolerance.md:302 ('We carry none') is stale for the two required* keys, which shipped after it.
verdict.correctedState: We implement `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (startup refusal, fail-open, enforced in both the desktop shell at apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1102 and the headless server at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645) and carry no managed `minimumVersion` key. The gap is cosmetic rather than a real exposure: the updater already has an unconditional, non-overridable floor at the running version, because electron-updater's `allowDowngrade` stays at its default `false` (we never set it and never set `autoUpdater.channel`, the setter that would flip it), so AppUpdater.isUpdateAvailable rejects any feed version older than the installed one. The downgrade path `minimumVersion` guards in Claude -- a /config switch from the `latest` channel to `stable` -- has no analogue here: the update channel is fixed in app-update.yml at build time. A managed `minimumVersion` would only add value if we ever ship a runtime channel switcher or pin-to-version install; until then it would be an admin key that can never change an outcome.

verdict.why: Step 1 passes: the sentence is verbatim at admin-setup.md line 64, third of three sentences on that line, and nothing in the first two reverses it. Step 2 and step 3 fail. (a) The cited lines drift: fallbackModel sits at packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:194 (not :189) and PiAgent.getFallbackModel at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6256-6258 (not :6234). Only the absence claim is exact -- MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534 does carry availableModels and enforceAvailableModels and does not carry fallbackModel. (b) The load-bearing half of the claimed our-state is false. fallbackModel does NOT live in 'user-editable workspace defaults'. ~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json is overwritten from the app bundle's apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json on EVERY launch -- syncConfigDefaults, storage.ts:198-226, comment at :160 'Always writes on launch to ensure defaults are up-to-date with the running version' -- and writeFileSync(CONFIG_DEFAULTS_FILE, ...) at :209/:218/:225 is the only writer in the repo. A grep -a over apps/ and packages/ for fallbackModel returns no setter, no RPC handler, no renderer control, no i18n label and no per-workspace override; the only production reader is getFallbackModel. So a user cannot set it at all, and a hand-edit of the JSON is clobbered at next start. (c) Verifying the consequence separately from the identifier, per the repo's own recurring-false-positive shape: 'an admin cannot pin the fallback' does not hold in the sense the sentence guards. The doc exception exists because fallbackModel is an ARRAY that would otherwise merge -- settings.md:277, 'Unlike most array settings, this key does not merge across settings files: the highest-precedence file that defines it supplies the entire chain.' Our value is a scalar with exactly one source and no lower layer, so 'the managed value replaces lower layers rather than merging' is already trivially the effective behaviour, and the value is in fact pinned harder than Claude's model allows -- fixed by the shipped bundle and re-asserted every launch, unoverridable by any user. And that residue rides on a shape mismatch already recorded three times -- f106, f226, f242 all file our scalar single-retry knob against Claude's ordered three-model chain. f113 restates that same underlying divergence against a precedence sentence that cannot bite a single-source scalar. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions: item 2 there covers availableModels/enforceAvailableModels enforcement placement, not fallbackModel. Refuted on the evidence, not as a recorded decision.
verdict.correctedState: fallbackModel is absent from MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (managed-policy.ts:501-534), so an administrator cannot set it through the managed-policy channel (managed-policy.json or the delivered payload) without rebuilding the app. But it is equally unreachable from below: it is read only by PiAgent.getFallbackModel (pi-agent.ts:6256-6258) from ~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json, a file syncConfigDefaults overwrites from the bundled apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json on every launch (storage.ts:198-226), with no setter, no RPC, no UI and no per-workspace override anywhere in the repo. There is therefore no lower layer for a managed value to replace and no user override to defeat -- the doc's merge carve-out, which settings.md:277 ties to fallbackModel being an array, is vacuous against our scalar. results.claim: The theme setting includes colorblind-friendly dark-daltonized and light-daltonized themes.
results.quote: The `theme` [setting](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) selects the interface colors, including the colorblind-friendly `dark-daltonized` and `light-daltonized` themes.
results.ourState: Our theme model is light/dark colour overrides plus a `solid`/`scenic` mode; there is no daltonized or otherwise colour-vision-adjusted palette (0 hits for daltonized/colorblind/deuteranopia/protanopia across packages and apps).

verdict.why:
Checks 1 and 2 pass; check 3 fails on two independent grounds, so the row is refuted as a divergence.

(1) QUOTE VERBATIM: confirmed. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/accessibility.md line 115 is exactly `* The \`theme\` [setting](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) selects the interface colors, including the colorblind-friendly \`dark-daltonized\` and \`light-daltonized\` themes.` It is a single-sentence bullet in the '## Accessibility settings beyond screen reader mode' list; no second clause reverses it.

(2) CITED FILE:LINE: confirmed exactly. packages/shared/src/config/theme.ts:49 is `export type ThemeMode = 'solid' | 'scenic';` and :55 is `export interface ThemeOverrides extends ThemeColors, SurfaceColors {` with `dark?: ThemeColors & SurfaceColors;` at :57. `grep -rani` (case-insensitive, -a so NUL-byte files are not skipped) for daltonized/colorblind/color-blind/deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia over packages+apps returns 0 product hits -- the only hits are the doc-sweep's own JSON/markdown rows.

(3a) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE, RECORDED IN SHIPPED CODE. Claude's `theme` is a TERMINAL palette for a TUI: settings.md:333 lists the enum as auto/dark/light/dark-daltonized/light-daltonized/dark-ansi/light-ansi and links to terminal-config#create-a-custom-theme -- the daltonized variants sit in the same enum as the `-ansi` ones. Nessy Desktop is an Electron GUI, and the fork has an explicit, reasoned refusal of that whole vocabulary at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2219-2251: 'REFUSED, deliberately, rather than loaded... Nessy's theming is a web token set (config/theme.ts ...) and `base` has no counterpart at all... Nothing in the format defines a mapping between the two vocabularies, so loading one would mean inventing it', with an author-facing diagnostic `plugin.format.claude_theme_unsupported`. The `base` presets that decision refuses are precisely dark/light/dark-daltonized/light-daltonized/dark-ansi/light-ansi. So the absence of a `dark-daltonized` theme is the documented consequence of a recorded decision about a TUI-vs-GUI vocabulary mismatch, not an unnoticed gap. (It is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 -- the decision lives in the adapter source instead.)

(3b) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE MISCHARACTERISES THE FORK'S THEME MODEL, and the cited evidence does not support it. theme.ts:49/:55 are the *override* type, not the theme-selection surface. The fork does have a named-theme selection surface -- the actual counterpart to Claude's `theme` setting: six bundled presets (Codex, GitHub, Haze, Nord, One Dark Pro, Vitesse) at apps/electron/resources/themes/*.json, seeded into ~/.nessy-agent/themes/ by ensurePresetThemes (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1909-1955), hot-reloaded by the config watcher (packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts:1125-1144), and selected over RPC via theme:getPresets / theme:loadPreset (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:131-132). Each theme file carries the six semantic colours plus five surface colours as arbitrary CSS colours (themeToCSS, theme.ts:178-225), so a colour-vision-adjusted palette is authorable today as a JSON drop-in. 'Our theme model is light/dark colour overrides plus a solid/scenic mode' describes one struct in that system and omits the selection surface entirely.

Residual truth, much narrower than filed: no daltonized palette ships among the six bundled presets. That is a product content wish (add one JSON file), not a divergence from a Claude Code contract our GUI is bound to.
verdict.correctedState: Claude's `theme` setting is a terminal palette enum for a TUI (settings.md:333 puts dark-daltonized/light-daltonized in the same list as dark-ansi/light-ansi and links to terminal-config). Nessy Desktop is an Electron GUI with its own web-token theme system, and the fork refuses Claude's theme vocabulary deliberately and with a reason in shipped code (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2219-2251, diagnostic `plugin.format.claude_theme_unsupported`): Claude's `base` presets -- dark, light, dark-daltonized, light-daltonized, dark-ansi, light-ansi -- have no counterpart, and no mapping between the two vocabularies is defined anywhere, so loading one would mean inventing it. Nessy does have a named-theme selection surface: six bundled presets (Codex, GitHub, Haze, Nord, One Dark Pro, Vitesse) at apps/electron/resources/themes/*.json, seeded to ~/.nessy-agent/themes/ by ensurePresetThemes (config/storage.ts:1909-1955), watched for live reload (config/watcher.ts:1125-1144) and selected via the theme:getPresets / theme:loadPreset RPC channels. Every preset expresses six semantic colours plus five surface colours as arbitrary CSS colours, so a colour-vision-adjusted palette is authorable as a drop-in JSON file today. The only accurate residual is that no daltonized preset is shipped among the six -- a product content gap, not a contract divergence.

results.claim: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE (with ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH) routes Claude Code requests to an Amazon Bedrock endpoint, in addition to the older CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK path.
results.quote: Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API.
results.ourState: buildClaudeSubprocessEnv inherits the whole ambient `process.env` and then deletes exactly three Bedrock vars — CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL — under the stated invariant 'Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path'. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH are absent from our entire source tree, so they survive into the subprocess and defeat that invariant.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239 (env spread from process.env), :257-262 (three-var strip list)

verdict.why:
All three checks confirm the finding.

(1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock.md, line 433 (of 551), under '## Use the Mantle endpoint': "Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API. It uses the same AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and `awsAuthRefresh` configuration described earlier on this page." The claimed sentence is the first of two on that line, word for word; the second sentence reinforces rather than reverses it (Mantle rides the same AWS credential path). The page's own env table (:495-497) lists CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH, and :460 says setting CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE together makes Claude Code call both endpoints from one session.

(2) CITED FILE. packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-265. :239-245 builds the subprocess env as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides, NESSY_DEBUG}`; :257-259 carries the comment 'Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path. Strip only Claude-specific Bedrock routing vars here...'; :260-262 are exactly three deletes — CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL. Cited line numbers are accurate.

(3) ABSENCE, with -a. `rg -a -i mantle` over the whole tree (excluding .git and .references) returns hits ONLY inside the doc-sweep's own artifacts under docs/superpowers/specs/ — zero hits in packages/, apps/, scripts/. No NUL-byte skip: -a was passed.

(4) CONSEQUENCE, measured separately from the identifier, with a positive control. A probe imported the real buildClaudeSubprocessEnv with all five vars set in process.env. Result: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK -> null, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL -> null (the control fires — the strip list works), CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE -> '1', ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL -> 'https://mantle.example', CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH -> '1'. The three Mantle vars reach the subprocess.

(5) IS THE RECEIVING BINARY EVEN LISTENING? Yes. We pin @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.183 (root, core, shared package.json). The bundled native binary node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude contains CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE (17 occurrences), ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL (12) and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH (12), and its provider-flag tables list CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE alongside USE_BEDROCK/USE_VERTEX/USE_FOUNDRY/USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS/USE_GATEWAY. So this is NOT the 'identifier unwired but consequence already handled upstream' shape — the routing lives in the binary we ship. (The SDK's sdk.mjs/bridge.mjs mention it only to suppress error reporting under a cloud provider, which is itself evidence the flag is a live provider selector.)

(6) ONE LAYER UP. The strip is duplicated, and the duplicate is equally incomplete: packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:931-935 defines CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS (the same three), consumed by clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars() at claude-agent.ts:917 in postInit ('Claude subprocesses must never inherit Bedrock-routing toggles from a previous connection or parent process environment') and folded into MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS. Nothing upstream sanitizes Mantle. So a fix has three sites, not one: options.ts:260-262, the llm-connections constant, and its tests.

(7) NOT AN OWNER DECISION, NOT A PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none is this. Nor is it the fork's deliberate scope: the finding does not ask us to SUPPORT Mantle (we ship no Bedrock provider, and that part of the page is correctly inapplicable); it observes that our own stated Bedrock-isolation invariant is under-enforced by exactly the vars the page adds. packages/shared/AGENTS.md:37 documents the sanitization as an active invariant, so the gap is inside a live contract, not outside the product boundary.

Severity note, not a refutation: exposure requires the host shell to already export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE (plus AWS credentials or a gateway) — the same precondition as CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, which we do strip. The asymmetry is the defect.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED as stated, with two additions. buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239-245) spreads the whole ambient process.env and deletes exactly three vars (:260-262) under the invariant 'Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path'; a measured probe shows those three are removed while CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH survive into the subprocess, and the native binary we bundle (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.183, darwin-arm64) honours all three. Addition 1: the strip list is duplicated at packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:931-935 (CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS, used by clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars at claude-agent.ts:917) and is missing the same vars, so any fix touches both sites plus llm-connections-auth-env.test.ts / managed-env.test.ts. Addition 2: Mantle is not the only omission — the same bundled binary carries CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS (with ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_AWS_API_KEY / CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_ANTHROPIC_AWS_AUTH) and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY as provider selectors, none of which we strip either (overlaps f118). The correct fix is a single shared allowlist of Claude provider-routing env keys, derived from the binary's provider-flag set, rather than three more hardcoded deletes.

results.claim: apiKeyHelper is a settings key naming a shell script that returns an API key, refreshed after 5 minutes or on HTTP 401, with the interval tunable via CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS.
results.quote: * **Custom credential scripts**: configure the [`apiKeyHelper`](/docs/en/settings#available-settings) setting to run a shell script that returns an API key.
results.ourState: No apiKeyHelper, no equivalent credential-script hook, and no CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS (`grep -a` over packages/ and apps/ hits only two vendored bundles under apps/electron/resources). Rotating/short-lived credentials from a vault have no supported path: the closest thing is the gateway-specific dp flow plus the NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN env bypass, which is scoped to the Nessy Gateway and not to generic API-key or custom-endpoint connections.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:943-1065 (env-var credential assembly, no helper path); packages/shared/src/auth/dp/dp-binary.ts (gateway-only alternative)

verdict.why: Checks 1 and 2 pass; check 3 kills it. (1) The quote is VERBATIM at authentication.md:143, and the whole two-line neighbourhood supports the claimed behaviour: :144 is 'by default, `apiKeyHelper` is called after 5 minutes or on HTTP 401 response. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` environment variable for custom refresh intervals.' Nothing in the second half reverses it. (2) The cited file says what was claimed: resolveAuthEnvVars (packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:1021-1076) assembles ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and has no helper path. (3) The CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is the archetypal shape this repo keeps hitting -- the identifier is genuinely absent from first-party TypeScript while the mechanism is live one layer down, because the claimed grep was scoped to packages/ and apps/ and therefore excluded the dependency that IMPLEMENTS it. The native Claude Agent SDK binary contains apiKeyHelper's full runtime -- `grep -c -a CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` returns 7 (the JS core returns 0), and the binary carries the doc's own strings 'apiKeyHelper is taking a while', 'apiKeyHelper failed', 'apiKeyHelper is configured'. That binary is staged into the shipped app (scripts/build/common.ts:324-371 aliases claude-agent-sdk-darwin-<arch> to @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-binary; apps/electron/scripts/build-dmg.sh:169-189 and build-linux.sh:147 do the same). And our own code opens every seam the helper needs, deliberately: buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions passes settingSources: ['user','project','local'] explicitly (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305, with the comment 'Omitting this loads all three sources (CLI defaults). Spelling out the same three keeps today's behavior'), so an apiKeyHelper entry in a project .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, or the per-Workspace user scope under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:222-255) is read by the CLI; buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (options.ts:236-263) spreads the entire host process.env and deletes only three Bedrock keys, so CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS propagates unmodified -- 'no CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS' is true of our source and false of our runtime; and addClaudePermissionRules (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts:118-164) merge-preserves unknown keys, so nothing we write strips the entry. The one real difference is precedence, and it is the SAME page's documented precedence working as specified, not a gap: for an anthropic connection with authType 'api_key' we inject ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (llm-connections.ts:1042-1045), which authentication.md:170 ranks 3rd, above apiKeyHelper at 4th, so the helper is shadowed there; on authType 'oauth' we inject CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (llm-connections.ts:1057), rank 5, which apiKeyHelper OUTRANKS, so a vault-backed helper does supply the credential. isValidProviderAuthCombination limits anthropic to ['api_key','oauth'] (llm-connections.ts:801). The sibling-subsystem trap also applies to the closing sentence: authentication.md governs the Claude CLI's credential resolution, so measuring it against the Nessy Gateway dp flow and NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN names the wrong subsystem -- the Pi / Codex / Nestor paths are the fork's deliberate corporate-gateway product difference, not this page's contract. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (read all nine at :89-97; none concerns apiKeyHelper).
verdict.correctedState: apiKeyHelper is present and functional on the surface this page governs. The shipped native Claude Agent SDK binary implements the helper, its 10-second slow notice and CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS (7 occurrences in the binary, 0 in the JS core), and it is staged into the packaged app by scripts/build/common.ts:324-371. Our first-party code opens the seam rather than closing it: claude-agent.ts:305 passes settingSources: ['user','project','local'] explicitly so a settings-file apiKeyHelper is loaded (user scope resolving under the per-Workspace CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set at options.ts:255), options.ts:236-263 forwards the whole host env minus three Bedrock keys so the TTL override reaches the consumer, and claude-settings-store.ts:118-164 merge-preserves unknown settings keys. What is true is narrower and is Claude's own documented precedence, not a missing mechanism: an anthropic connection with authType 'api_key' has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY injected by resolveAuthEnvVars (llm-connections.ts:1042-1045), which outranks apiKeyHelper (rank 3 vs 4 at authentication.md:170), so the helper is shadowed on that authType; on authType 'oauth' the injected CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is rank 5 and apiKeyHelper wins, so rotating vault credentials do have a supported path. The Pi, Codex and Nestor-gateway backends are outside this page's scope; citing the dp flow and NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN as 'the closest thing' compares against the wrong subsystem.

results.claim: Cloud provider credentials outrank every other credential whenever CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX or CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY is set.
results.quote: 1. Cloud provider credentials, when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set. See [third-party integrations](/docs/en/third-party-integrations) for setup.
results.ourState: The Claude SDK subprocess env is built by spreading the host's whole process.env and deleting only the Bedrock trio. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY are not stripped and appear nowhere in our source, so an ambient value in the user's shell silently outranks the credential the session's LlmConnection configured, on the highest precedence tier the doc defines.

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md returns the sentence character-for-character on line 168 under '### Authentication precedence' ('When multiple credentials are present, Claude Code chooses one in this order:'). The whole line is that one sentence plus the 'See third-party integrations' pointer — no reversing second half. The only qualifier on the page is line 175, which says a signed-in Claude apps gateway session outranks the cloud-provider tier; we ship no Claude apps gateway session, so it does not soften the claim for us. (2) CITED LINES CORRECT: packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239-245 builds the subprocess env as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides, NESSY_DEBUG}`, and :260-262 deletes exactly CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL under the comment 'Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path.' `grep -rna` (NUL-safe) over the whole tree finds CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY in no source file at all, and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX only in config/managed-env.ts:126 — a different subsystem (the server-managed-settings withheld-env classifier for a cached policy `env` block), not the SDK subprocess env, so it does not strip anything here. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, THREE LAYERS: (a) one layer up, apps/electron/src/main/shell-env.ts:28-77 spawns the user's login shell (`$SHELL -l -i -c env`) in the packaged macOS app and copies EVERY variable into process.env, filtering only keys starting with `VITE_` — so an ambient CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX/FOUNDRY in .zshrc really does reach process.env before any agent is created; (b) the second strip list has the same hole — claude-agent.ts:911-917 does the 'clean state' delete of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL plus clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars() (llm-connections.ts:931-935, the same three Bedrock keys), and omits Vertex/Foundry too, so nothing upstream already handled it; (c) one layer down, a positive control on the binary we actually ship: `strings -a node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` (SDK 0.3.183) hits CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX 20x and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY 17x, and sdk.mjs contains the literal branch `Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS)||Ee(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE)` — the runtime we spawn does read them. NOT a recorded owner decision: the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 are the seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches an env strip list. NOT a deliberate product difference either: dropping the Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows and shipping no Vertex/Foundry provider is exactly why an ambient Vertex/Foundry toggle is unwanted, and the repo already asserts the invariant for Bedrock — it is applied inconsistently, not waived.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with three corrections of scope. (i) The hole exists in TWO strip lists, not one: options.ts:260-262 (subprocess env) and llm-connections.ts:931-935 CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS, cleared from process.env by claude-agent.ts:917 in ClaudeAgent.postInit. A fix must widen both. (ii) The gap is wider than the doc's three names: the shipped SDK 0.3.183 branches on five cloud-provider toggles — BEDROCK, VERTEX, FOUNDRY, ANTHROPIC_AWS and MANTLE. CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS is undocumented on this page and absent from our source too; CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE is finding f116, the same root cause at the same two sites, so f116 and f118 are one edit. Additionally ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN — precedence tier 2, ABOVE the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that postInit does set — appears nowhere in the Claude subprocess path (only in managed-env.ts:141), so an ambient bearer token in the user's shell outranks the connection's key by the same mechanism. (iii) Reachability: the Claude SDK subprocess only spawns in a build with NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE enabled (default off; factory.ts:182, :430, :470, :580, :748, :897 throw/return 'Claude support is not included in this build.'), so the hazard is confined to Claude-enabled builds — real, since that flag is what the Bedrock strip already exists to protect. 'Silently' is accurate only when the ambient shell carries a complete Vertex/Foundry configuration (project id, region, credentials); a half-configured shell produces a routing error instead of a silent provider swap.

results.claim: Pushes to any branch of the repository you are working in, including the default branch, are allowed by default; the protected-branch default was removed.
results.quote: Auto mode allows pushes to any branch of the repository you're working in, including the default branch, and pull request creation by default.
results.ourState: Our classifier prompt still carries the removed boundary: it instructs the judge to keep git actions 'high or critical if they touch a protected/default branch', and a high-risk verdict denies unless user authorization is at least medium. A routine push to main/master is therefore escalated where the documented default allows it. The `protectedBranch` fact the rule keys off has no producer either, so the rule fires on the model's own inference of what 'default branch' means.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:171 (rule text), :186 (high-risk verdict rule), :226 (protectedBranch fact, declared and rendered, never set)

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at auto-mode-config.md:31, but it is the first of four sentences on that line and the rest reverses the reading: deploy/publication-target branch names are still judged on their own terms, and force pushes plus secret-bearing pushes stay blocked. Line 33 adds that even BEFORE v2.1.211 the classifier already allowed 'routine pushes to the default branch'. What v2.1.211 actually removed (line 101) is a CONTEXT SLOT named 'Default / protected branches' in the autoMode config, not a risk rule. Refuted on four grounds. (1) We never had that slot: AUTO_MODE_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:469 is exactly ['environment','hard_deny','soft_deny','allow'] and no protected-branch config surface has ever existed here, so there is no removed default 'still carried'. (2) Wrong subsystem. packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts is NOT a port of Claude's auto-mode rule lists; its header (lines 1-30) and docs/architecture/guardian-command-judge.md:1-7 record that the risk taxonomy, authorization scoring, base risk levels and outcome thresholds are 'adapted VERBATIM where they fit from the openai/codex guardian policy (codex-rs/core/src/guardian/policy.md + policy_template.md, Apache-2.0)'. Lines 171 and 186 are that Codex text, adopted under the AGENTS.md rule permitting verbatim adaptation of permissively licensed upstream prompt text. Claude's own four rule lists reach the same prompt through a separate channel, GuardianOrgPolicy rendered by describeOrgPolicy (guardian.ts:332+) with exactly the four-tier precedence the page states at doc lines 172-178. (3) The consequence is false for the case it names. In auto mode the guardian is consulted ONLY when the deterministic gate already returned 'prompt' (pi-agent.ts:4048-4051; guardian-command-judge.md:28-34), and 'git push' is in DANGEROUS_COMMANDS (permission-manager.ts:49), so pre-guardian Nessy asks for EVERY push, main or feature. The guardian can only convert a would-ask into allow or block; it cannot escalate anything already allowed. For a routine push the user asked for it, so authorization scoring (guardian.ts:135) is 'high'; rule :186 reads 'risk high -> no_objection only when user authorization is at least medium and the action is narrowly scoped with no deny rule', and the Destructive deny rule at :173 requires 'no proof of user authorization'. Verdict: no_objection -> allow. The routine push is not escalated; the guardian is what lets it through WITHOUT a prompt. A deny needs low/unknown authorization, i.e. agent drift, which doc line 178 also treats as unauthorized. (4) protectedBranch:226 does have no production producer - both GuardianJudgeInput.facts sites (pi-agent.ts:3417-3421 and :3523-3527) set only mode and workspaceRoot - but that WEAKENS the finding: describeFacts (:322-328) gates the '(PROTECTED/default branch)' note on facts.gitBranch, which is also never set, so the note is never rendered in production and the judge's prompt never asserts a protected branch at all. Only the tests set either field.
verdict.correctedState: No divergence as stated. Nessy never implemented the 'Default / protected branches' context slot that v2.1.211 removed; the autoMode keys we parse are environment/hard_deny/soft_deny/allow only (managed-policy.ts:469). The sentence at guardian.ts:171 that keeps a default-branch git action 'high or critical' is Codex-derived policy text (openai/codex guardian policy.md, Apache-2.0), adopted deliberately and recorded in the file header and docs/architecture/guardian-command-judge.md, not a stale copy of a Claude default. Its effect on the case the finding names is the opposite of what was claimed: a routine user-requested push to main scores authorization 'high', clears rule :186 and the :173 deny rule, and returns no_objection, which turns a prompt Nessy would otherwise show into an allow. Only an unauthorized push (agent drift, authorization low/unknown) is denied. The protectedBranch fact is inert in both directions - never set, and therefore never rendered, since describeFacts gates the note on gitBranch, which is also never set. The residual and genuine observation - that our built-in rule text is Codex prose inside the guardian system prompt rather than Claude's four addressable default lists - is already recorded as f121.

results.claim: The classifier reads autoMode from the developer's own ~/.claude/settings.json in addition to managed settings, and a developer may extend the four lists with personal entries.
results.quote: A developer can extend `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, and `hard_deny` with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide.
results.ourState: resolveAutoMode accepts a `user` scope and composes it correctly, but the single production call site passes only `managed`, and so do both classifyAllShell call sites. There is no reader that puts a user-settings autoMode block into that parameter, so a developer's personal trusted-infrastructure entries can never reach the classifier.

verdict.why: All three factual legs of the finding hold, but it is a RECORDED DECISION with a written reason plus a deliberate corporate-fork posture, and it names the wrong subsystem's file. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at auto-mode-config.md:74. The whole line is two sentences and the second does NOT reverse the conclusion - it weakens it in our favour: 'Because allow rules act as exceptions to soft block rules inside the classifier, a developer-added `allow` entry can override an organization `soft_deny` entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary.' The doc itself says wiring the user scope makes the org policy a soft boundary. (2) CODE: accurate. resolveAutoMode (managed-policy.ts:1082-1101) composes managed-then-user; the single production call site SessionManager.ts:4109 passes `{ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode }` only, and both resolveAutoModeClassifyAllShell sites (:4119, :16269) do the same. The source comments state the restriction outright ('MANAGED scope only'). managed-policy.test.ts:1033-1041 pins that the user scope composes correctly when supplied. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately: true at the Pi guardian - no user-scope autoMode reaches buildGuardianJudgeTask, whose GuardianJudgeInput.orgPolicy is documented as 'resolved from the HOST-OWNED managed policy file'. REFUTATION GROUNDS: (a) RECORDED DECISION, dated and categorized. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-managed-policy-honesty.md:207, category 'ours, stated': 'classifyAllShell is read from the MANAGED scope only, because no user autoMode scope is wired in this product and a checked-in repo must not steer the classifier band. The composer accepts a user scope and nothing supplies one.' That last clause is verbatim the fact this finding reports. The two classifyAllShell call sites it cites are additionally covered by inert-worklist §3 item 3 ('autoMode.classifyAllShell / resolveAutoModeClassifyAllShell'). (b) WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the AGENTS.md trap-4 shape. The finding says the classifier should read '~/.claude/settings.json'. In this fork that file is a CLAUDE AGENT SDK BACKEND surface (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts, destination 'userSettings'), consumed by the real Claude Code subprocess via settingSources - a different subsystem from the Pi-harness guardian judge, which the autoMode wiring is gated to (`snapshot.context.provider === 'pi'` at SessionManager.ts:4108/:4119). And on THAT backend the user scope is also excluded by a separate recorded decision: options.ts:202-210 redirects CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per-Workspace so 'a hand-written ~/.claude/settings.json stops reaching the subprocess. It is the change the isolation is FOR - a user-scope Claude settings file is a cross-Workspace policy channel'. The Claude provider is also off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE). (c) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED, with the direction of harm narrowed.
