The finding's state is accurate; three refinements, all of which widen it rather than narrow it.

1. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` produces submission `{message:"/skill-b do XYZ", customSlashCommandId:"custom:skill:skill-a"}` (custom-slash-command-submission.ts:20-34), which the RPC expands via skillSlashCommandBody into the model message `[skill:skill-a] /skill-b do XYZ` (rpc/sessions.ts:335, custom-commands.ts:302-304). parseSkillMentionReferences on that string returns exactly ["skill-a"]; on `[skill:skill-a] [skill:skill-b] do XYZ` it returns ["skill-a","skill-b"]. Claude's contract is "passes the trailing text to each as arguments" - the same text to every stacked skill. 3. NO CAP EXISTS TO ADJUST. (1) The cited line is a DIFFERENT SUBSYSTEM. packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts:238 sits inside `runDependencyInstallerWithQuota`, and `invocation` there comes from `buildPluginRuntimeDependencyInstallInvocation(bunPath, directory, hostEnvironment, frozenLockfile)` (:44-89, command = bunPath, args = bun install flags with a sandboxed HOME/TMPDIR/cache). results.claim: A `--debug <category>` flag turns on live per-subsystem evaluation logging, naming `hooks` and `mcp` as categories.
results.quote: Start a session with `claude --debug hooks` and trigger the tool call.
results.ourState: The CLI has no `--debug` flag at all, categorised or otherwise. `apps/cli/src/index.ts` `printHelp()` lists Connection flags (`--url`, `--token`, `--workspace`, `--timeout`, `--tls-ca`, `--json`, `--safe-mode`) and LLM flags; `grep -a "'--debug'"` in `apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns nothing. We ship the hook/automation subsystem the flag exists to debug.

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at debug-your-config.md:72 ('If /hooks shows the hook but it still does not fire, the next step is to watch hook evaluation live. Start a session with `claude --debug hooks` and trigger the tool call. The debug log records each event, which matchers were checked, and the hook's exit code and output.'); the rest of the line does not reverse it, and :56 ('claude --debug mcp') and :122 corroborate the category form. The cited file:line is also correct as far as it goes: printHelp() begins at apps/cli/src/index.ts:2019 and lists exactly the Connection + LLM flags named, and `grep -a -- "--debug" apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns 0 hits (0 for NESSY_DEBUG too). But the finding is refuted one layer up on subsystem scope, and again on consequence. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. This fork DOES ship a `--debug` flag; it lives on the process that actually runs sessions, hooks and MCP — the Electron desktop host — not on the thin websocket client the finding cited. apps/electron/src/main/logger.ts:16 `if (process.argv.includes('--debug')) return true` feeds `isDebugMode` (:31), and apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:93-97 turns it into `NESSY_DEBUG=1` + `enableDebug()` + `setPerfEnabled(true)`. The same argv check is honoured in shared code at packages/shared/src/interceptor-common.ts:27, packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:244 and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1476, which propagate NESSY_DEBUG into the Pi/SDK subprocess env. The headless server takes the env half: packages/server/src/index.ts:70-72 calls enableDebug(), and packages/server-core/src/runtime/platform-headless.ts:27,:46 do the same. So 'no --debug flag at all' is true only of apps/cli, and false of the product — exactly the sibling-subsystem shape AGENTS.md warns about. (2) CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE SEPARATELY. The live hook-evaluation logging the flag exists to enable is present: packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts logs the lifecycle-hook sources loaded (:237), disableAllHooks (:229), the action count (:257), the events emitted per session (:560) and webhook failures (:795), all gated behind isDebugEnabled(); and packages/shared/src/automations/event-logger.ts keeps an append-only events.jsonl recording every automation event with its ActionExecutionResult[] and duration, independent of any flag. apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:75 exists precisely to surface these — 'Pipe server stderr to our stderr so --debug logs are visible (unless quiet)' — exposed through the CLI's own `--verbose`/`-v` (index.ts:120-122, :881, help at :2082). `NESSY_DEBUG=1 nessy-general-agent run … --verbose` is the CLI's route to the same log. Not an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision and not a branding/subscription/gateway product difference; refuted on scope and consequence, not on category.
verdict.correctedState: The fork ships a `--debug` flag, but as a global boolean on the desktop host rather than a categorised flag on the CLI client. apps/electron/src/main/logger.ts:16 (`process.argv.includes('--debug')`) sets isDebugMode, which apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:93-97 converts to NESSY_DEBUG=1 + enableDebug() + setPerfEnabled(true); the same argv check is honoured at packages/shared/src/interceptor-common.ts:27, packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:244 and packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1476, and the headless server honours the env half at packages/server/src/index.ts:70-72. It gates real hook-evaluation logging (packages/shared/src/automations/automation-system.ts:229,:237,:257,:560,:795) alongside an always-on events.jsonl audit trail (automations/event-logger.ts). The residual, narrower divergence is twofold: (a) our switch has NO subsystem categories — there is no `hooks` or `mcp` selector, so `--debug hooks` on the desktop binary enables everything globally and the bare word is ignored by the argv `includes` check; and (b) apps/cli/src/index.ts never parses `--debug` at all, so it falls through parseArgs' default branch into `args.rest`, where for `run` it would be appended to the prompt rather than rejected — the CLI's supported route is `NESSY_DEBUG=1 … --verbose`, which pipes the server's debug stderr through apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:75.

results.claim: The handler accepts exactly one path (`open`), and a deep link can only choose a directory and pre-fill the prompt box — nothing is sent or executed until the user presses Enter.
results.quote: A deep link never executes anything on its own. The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box.
results.ourState: `nessy://action/new-session?input=…&send=true` sends the prompt straight to the model with no user confirmation — `const shouldSend = parsed.params.send === 'true'` then `window.electronAPI.sendMessage(session.id, parsed.params.input!, …)`. The scheme is registered OS-wide via `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(DEEPLINK_SCHEME)` (`apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:197`), and the same handler also routes `delete-session/{id}`, `flag-session/{id}`, `rename-session` and `oauth` (`apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:22-24`), so a link on any web page reaches them. There is no external-origin gate and no `Prompt from an external link` warning line.

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) The quoted sentence is verbatim at deep-links.md:39, and the WHOLE line reinforces rather than reverses it: 'A deep link never executes anything on its own. The link only chooses a directory and fills the prompt box. If you click a link from a page you do not trust, the prompt is still inert: nothing reaches the model until you read what was filled in and press Enter.' Line 45 independently confirms the one-path claim ('Every deep link starts with claude-cli://open, which is the only path the handler accepts') and line 41 confirms the 'Prompt from an external link' warning line. (2) The cited file:line is exact: apps/electron/src/renderer/contexts/NavigationContext.tsx:754 is `const shouldSend = parsed.params.send === 'true'`, inside `case 'new-session':` opened at :677, and :755-763 calls window.electronAPI.sendMessage(session.id, parsed.params.input!, ...) behind a 100 ms setTimeout. apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:197 is app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(DEEPLINK_SCHEME) as claimed. (3) The CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier, and the external path is real and ungated end-to-end: app.on('open-url') at index.ts:~240 calls handleDeepLink unconditionally with no origin classification (the classifyExternalUrl/'dangerous' gate in main/handlers/system.ts:206-215 sits only on the renderer->main shell:openUrl IPC, not on the OS path); deep-link.ts:185-190 copies every query param except `window` and `sidebar`, so `send` survives; handleDeepLink:334-338 pushes DeepLinkNavigation to the renderer; the listener at NavigationContext.tsx:1096-1123 re-serialises actionParams back into an `action/...` route and calls navigate(); navigate() at :841 dispatches parsed.type === 'action' to handleActionNavigation at :861. No trust prompt, no origin check and no 'external link' warning string exists anywhere in apps/electron/src or the i18n bundles (grep -ani, no hits). The sibling-subsystem trap does not apply: `send=true` exists because the app uses this scheme as its own in-app command bus (new-session-deep-link.ts:25-26 'auto-sends the seeded prompt', called only from EditPopover.tsx:1089), but the same handler is registered OS-wide with no distinction between the internal caller and a web page, so the internal design intent does not bound the external surface. Not an owner decision: all nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 were read (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) and none concerns deep links. Not a deliberate product difference either: only the scheme name (craft:// -> nessy://) is rebrand; auto-send and the destructive action routes are substantive behaviour. The existing records treat the page as OPEN, not decided: coverage-map row 97 marks deep-links yellow with 'Контракт не снят', and the parity audit at :1719 files deep links under 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness' — a title-level triage the audit itself says was 'not enough to audit field by field'.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with three citation corrections and one mitigation the finding missed. CORRECT AS CLAIMED: nessy://action/new-session?input=…&send=true reaches window.electronAPI.sendMessage with no confirmation (NavigationContext.tsx:754-763), the scheme is registered OS-wide (main/index.ts:193/197) and dispatched unconditionally from app.on('open-url'), and there is no external-origin gate and no 'Prompt from an external link' warning anywhere. CORRECTION 1: the action is `new-session`, and deep-link.ts:22-24 is a STALE DOC COMMENT (it still says `new-chat` and lists resume-sdk-session/delete-session/flag-session) — it is not the routing table and it does not mention rename-session or oauth. The real routing table is the switch in NavigationContext.tsx starting at :672, where delete-session (-> deleteSession), flag-session/unflag-session, rename-session, oauth (-> performOAuth), delete-source and set-mode are all reachable from the same ungated OS path; cite that switch, not the comment. CORRECTION 2: the doc's `cwd` half is ALREADY hardened here — NavigationContext.tsx:686-690 rejects any workdir other than 'user_default'/'none' with 'Project folders must be selected through a validated project handle', and `mode` is validated through parsePermissionMode. The gap is specifically the prompt-execution half (send=true) and the destructive action routes, not directory selection. CORRECTION 3: `send=true` is not a stray parameter — it is the mechanism EditPopover.tsx:1089 uses for its own in-app 'Edit resource' flow via buildNewSessionDeepLink (new-session-deep-link.ts:51, whose unit test asserts the URL must carry send=true). Any fix must keep the internal caller working, so the correct shape is an origin/trust distinction between an in-process dispatch and an OS-delivered URL, not deleting the parameter.

results.claim: Registration of the URL-scheme handler can be prevented entirely by a settings key, and enforced fleet-wide from managed settings.
results.quote: To prevent registration entirely, set [`disableDeepLinkRegistration`](/docs/en/settings) to `"disable"` in `settings.json`.
results.ourState: Registration is unconditional at app start with no setting consulted. `grep -a` for `disableDeepLinkRegistration` across the repo returns zero hits, and `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` carries no equivalent. Given the auto-send finding above, this is the missing off-switch for it.

verdict.why: Doc half checks out; the consequence does not. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: deep-links.md:163 reads exactly 'To prevent registration entirely, set [`disableDeepLinkRegistration`](/docs/en/settings) to `"disable"` in `settings.json`.' The rest of that two-sentence line only adds managed-settings enforcement, so it does not reverse the claim. (2) CITED LINE ACCURATE: apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:190-198 calls app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient(DEEPLINK_SCHEME) unconditionally (:193 dev branch, :197 production) with no setting consulted; `grep -ran disableDeepLinkRegistration` over the repo hits only the doc-sweep JSON/markdown artifacts, never code; MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534) carries no equivalent. (3) CONSEQUENCE FALSE ON THREE COUNTS. (a) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. Claude's key gates the CLI, which lazily writes a user-level handler (~/Applications/Claude Code URL Handler.app, a .desktop file, HKCU\Software\Classes\claude-cli) when you send your first interactive prompt (deep-links.md:153-159). Nessy has no CLI-side handler at all: setAsDefaultProtocolClient appears only in the Electron main process (one src hit, plus its build output in apps/electron/dist/main.cjs); apps/cli registers nothing. The GUI's scheme is declared STATICALLY in the bundle -- apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:82-84 `protocols: - name: Nessy Desktop / schemes: [nessy]` -- which electron-builder turns into CFBundleURLTypes in Info.plist, NSIS registry entries on Windows, and MimeType=x-scheme-handler/nessy on Linux. (b) THE IMPLIED REMEDY WOULD NOT WORK. Gating index.ts:193/197 on a setting cannot 'prevent registration entirely': LaunchServices and the installer have already registered the scheme from the installed bundle, and setAsDefaultProtocolClient only selects the DEFAULT handler among claimants. So this is not the missing off-switch for the auto-send finding -- flipping it off would leave nessy:// still routed to the app. (c) THE SCHEME IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, UNLIKE CLAUDE'S. nessy://auth-callback / nessy://auth-complete is the OAuth redirect target (packages/shared/src/auth/callback-server.ts:41; carved out at apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:111-114 and packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:83), and nessy:// doubles as the app's INTERNAL navigation transport (system.ts:283-312 routes internal nessy:// links over RPC without ever touching the OS). Claude's claude-cli:// carries only the optional launch-a-terminal convenience, so switching it off costs nothing there; a key with Claude's exact semantics would break sign-in in this fork. Also a deliberate product-shape difference: Nessy Desktop is an Electron GUI, not a terminal CLI, so the feature the setting exists to disable -- click a link, a terminal emulator opens with a pre-filled prompt -- does not exist to be disabled. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3.
verdict.correctedState: The identifier is genuinely absent (no disableDeepLinkRegistration anywhere; no equivalent in MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS), and apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:190-198 does register the scheme unconditionally -- but the finding names the wrong subsystem and the wrong layer. Claude's key gates a CLI that lazily writes a user-level handler on first prompt; Nessy's CLI registers nothing, and the Electron app's nessy:// scheme is registered by the installed bundle itself (electron-builder.yml:82-84 -> CFBundleURLTypes / NSIS registry / .desktop MimeType), so no runtime settings key could 'prevent registration entirely'. The scheme is also load-bearing here in a way claude-cli:// is not: it carries the OAuth callback (nessy://auth-callback, packages/shared/src/auth/callback-server.ts:41) and the app's own internal navigation routing (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:283-312). If the sibling auto-send concern is real, the only achievable control in this fork sits at the HANDLING boundary -- handleDeepLink (apps/electron/src/main/deep-link.ts:235) or the `send` action param -- and must keep auth-callback working. That is a different finding at a different layer, not this Claude settings key.

results.claim: Preview servers are configured from `.claude/launch.json` at the session folder root, with a fixed field set (`name`, `runtimeExecutable`, `runtimeArgs`, `port` defaulting to 3000, `cwd`, `env`, `autoPort`, `program`, `args`, `url`), a top-level `autoVerify` flag that is on by default, `autoPort` tri-state port-conflict handling, a `PORT` env var handed to the server, and a rule that a localhost `url` must be origin-only with a matching port.
results.quote: Claude automatically detects your dev server setup and stores the configuration in `.claude/launch.json` at the root of the folder you selected when starting the session.
results.ourState: No reader, no writer, no equivalent. `grep -rna -a "launch\.json\|autoVerify\|autoPort" --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' packages apps` returns 0 lines; `runtimeExecutable` appears only in this repo's own `.claude/launch.json`, which is consumed by the Claude Code harness, not by our product. Our Browser pane ships a single `browser_tool` whose `navigate` subcommand takes a bare URL and starts nothing — there is no dev-server start/stop, no auto-verify-after-edit, and no port-conflict policy.

verdict.why: All three factual checks pass, but the finding is refuted as a divergence because it is an already-recorded product/scope decision in the parity audit itself. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: desktop.md line 428 contains the claimed sentence exactly (python substring check True). The whole line has two more sentences ('Preview uses this folder as its working directory, so if you selected a parent folder, subfolders with their own dev servers won't be detected automatically. To work with a subfolder's server, either start a session in that folder directly or add a configuration manually.') — they narrow scope to the session folder, they do not reverse the conclusion. The doc's field table (475-486), autoVerify default (450-452), autoPort tri-state (539-543), PORT hand-off (545) and the localhost origin-only/matching-port rule (517) all check out, so the CLAIMED BEHAVIOUR is a faithful reading of the page. (2) CITED LINE: packages/shared/src/agent/browser-tool-runtime.ts:741 is `if (cmd === 'navigate') {`, whose body takes `parts.slice(1).join(' ').trim()` as a bare URL and calls `fns.navigate(url)` — it starts nothing. Correct as cited. (3) ABSENCE, NUL-SAFE: `grep -rna -a` for launch\.json|autoVerify|autoPort|runtimeExecutable over packages, apps, scripts, docs-site returns zero. The browser tool exposes 32 subcommands (open, navigate, snapshot, find, click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, upload, set-clipboard, get-clipboard, paste, screenshot, screenshot-region, console, window-resize, network, wait, key, downloads, scroll, back, forward, evaluate, focus, windows, release, close, hide) — none starts, stops, port-checks or auto-verifies a server. ONE LAYER UP/DOWN: the only `.claude/launch.json` in the tree is the repo's own at the root, consumed by the Claude Code harness (my own preview_start tool), not by our product — the claim already says this and it is right. The only 'dev server' hits in product source are apps/electron/src/main/window-manager.ts:114/287/340/380 and apps/viewer/vite.config.ts:30, which are the app shell's OWN Vite dev server for hot reload — an identically-worded sibling subsystem, not a user-project preview server. No upstream layer supplies the consequence. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions. REFUTATION: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md — the named source of truth — already rules on this at section 5e-2, lines 1719-1726: 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness: ... and the desktop product surfaces (preview servers, PR status, diff view, integrated terminal) that are product decisions rather than loop parity.' Preview servers are named explicitly and were deliberately assigned NO ROW. So the absence is real but it is a recorded product decision, not an unrecorded parity defect.
verdict.correctedState: Accurate as a statement of fact, wrong as a classification. There is genuinely no reader, writer or equivalent of `.claude/launch.json`, `autoVerify`, `autoPort` or the preview-server lifecycle anywhere in packages/, apps/, scripts/ or docs-site/ (NUL-safe grep: 0 hits), and browser-tool-runtime.ts:741's `navigate` takes a bare URL and starts nothing. But this is already a recorded scope decision, not an open gap: parity audit section 5e-2 (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1719-1726) lists 'the desktop product surfaces (preview servers, PR status, diff view, integrated terminal)' under 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness ... product decisions rather than loop parity'. Two precisions to the doc reading if the row is ever revived: `PORT` is handed to the server only when Claude picks a port different from the requested one (desktop.md:545), not unconditionally; and a `configurations` entry carrying `url` with no command attaches the preview to a server the user already runs rather than starting one (desktop.md:521-532).

results.claim: Two managed settings keys govern the Browser pane: `browserExternalPageTools` set to `"disabled"` removes Claude's tools on external pages, and `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` set to the JSON boolean `true` blocks external navigation entirely while leaving localhost previews working.
results.quote: | `disableBrowserExternalNavigation`         | set to `true` to turn off external browsing in the [Browser pane](#browse-external-sites) entirely. Neither users nor Claude can navigate to external sites, and localhost dev server previews are unaffected. The value must be the JSON boolean `true`; the string `"true"` is ignored.
results.ourState: Neither key is read. `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` lists 34 keys and contains neither; `grep -a` for both names across all `*.ts` in the repo hits only the docs spec file. We ship the surface they govern: `browser_tool navigate` accepts any URL with no allowlist, no domain check and no managed off-switch — `grep -a "domain\|allowlist"` over `browser-tool-runtime.ts` and `browser-tools.ts` returns nothing.

verdict.why: Quote is verbatim (desktop.md:719, whole line read; the second sentence only tightens the type rule to JSON boolean true, it does not reverse anything). The identifier half of the finding is also true: managed-policy.ts:501 is `export const MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS = [` and neither `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` nor `browserExternalPageTools` appears in it, and `grep -ran` for both names over the repo hits only docs/spec/JSON sweep files. What refutes the finding as filed is its CONSEQUENCE, which is the exact recurring shape this repo warns about (identifier unwired, consequence false because a layer above already handles it): (1) 'no managed off-switch' is wrong. A managed `permissionDsl` deny rule is the documented real boundary and it reaches `browser_tool`. managed-policy.ts:298-301 states it in so many words ('An admin who needs a real boundary uses a managed `permissionDsl` deny rule, which our deterministic gate applies BEFORE the judge is consulted at all'); mode-manager.ts:2103-2117 runs `deniedToolPatterns`/`disallowedTools` and 2129 runs `toolRules` deny BEFORE the ALWAYS_ALLOWED_TOOLS set that contains 'browser_tool' (mode-manager.ts:2001), and the comment at 2010-2013 names the deny check as 'the lever'; pi-agent.ts:1729-1760 applies `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny`, which removes a whole-tool-denied binding from the exposed tool set, and `browser_tool` is a static binding (harness-tool-descriptor.ts:160, :293). (2) A second off-switch exists one layer down: `getBrowserToolEnabled()` (config/storage.ts:1053) gates `mcp__session__browser_tool` out of the session tool defs at pi-agent.ts:1610-1612, defaulting from the bundled `apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json` (`browserToolEnabled`, storage.ts:91/179), so a corporate build can ship it off. (3) The evidence's own count is wrong: MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS holds 32 keys, not 34 (counted programmatically). (4) Scope: the `desktop` page already carries a recorded verdict in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md row 98 -- U+2B1C 'vne produkta, verdikt zapisan', note 'chuzhoy desktop-produkt'. Not one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (none of those concerns the browser). A residual, much narrower gap does survive and is stated in correctedState.
verdict.correctedState: Neither managed key is read -- `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (managed-policy.ts:501) holds 32 keys and contains neither `browserExternalPageTools` nor `disableBrowserExternalNavigation`, and there is no URL allowlist, domain or origin check anywhere in `browser-tool-runtime.ts` / `browser-tools.ts` (grep -ranEi for allowlist|blocklist|domain|origin returns nothing). But 'no managed off-switch' is false: an admin CAN remove the agent's browser access through managed policy, via a `permissionDsl` deny rule on `browser_tool` -- deny is evaluated before the ALWAYS_ALLOWED_TOOLS membership at mode-manager.ts:2103/2129 vs :2001, and `filterCapabilityIdentitiesByWholeToolDeny` (pi-agent.ts:1729ff) strips the binding outright -- and a build can ship `browserToolEnabled: false` in `config-defaults.json`, which filters `mcp__session__browser_tool` at pi-agent.ts:1610. What we genuinely lack is finer-grained than the finding says: our levers are all-or-nothing and agent-only. There is no external-page-vs-localhost distinction (Claude's `browserExternalPageTools` keeps Claude's tools on localhost previews while removing them on external pages; our deny removes the tool everywhere), tool rules match on tool NAME only via glob (`matchesToolPermissionRule`, mode-manager.ts:238-257) so no URL-scoped rule is expressible, and nothing can block the USER's own navigation in the Electron Browser pane the way `disableBrowserExternalNavigation` does -- `browser-pane-manager.ts` and `browser-cdp.ts` carry no allowlist/domain logic at all.

results.claim: `managedMcpServers` pushes MCP server configurations to all users, each entry naming a transport of `"http"`, `"sse"` or `"stdio"` plus an optional per-server `toolPolicy` map, and is the documented delivery path for third-party deployments that receive no admin-console settings.
results.quote: | `managedMcpServers`                        | push MCP server configurations to all users in a third-party deployment. Each entry specifies a transport of `"http"`, `"sse"`, or `"stdio"`, connection details, and optionally a `toolPolicy` map that restricts which tools in that server users can invoke.
results.ourState: Our managed policy can only restrict — `allowedMcpServers` / `deniedMcpServers` (`managed-policy.ts:129-130`) — never push a server definition, and carries no per-server tool restriction. `grep -a managedMcpServers` across the repo hits only the docs spec. verdict.why: Legs 1 and 2 hold; leg 3 fails, and the finding's own OUR STATE carries a false half. (1) QUOTE - VERBATIM but TRUNCATED at the load-bearing clause. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md` (960 lines), line 722, in the `### Managed settings` table, contains the claimed text as an exact substring. Reading the WHOLE line, two sentences were cut: 'Available in third-party (3P) Desktop deployments only. Deliver this key through the managed settings file or MDM, since third-party deployments do not receive admin-console settings.' The second cut sentence is the one the finding paraphrases into its claim; the FIRST is the one it drops, and it is the scope limit - the key exists only in third-party deployments of Claude Desktop, i.e. Anthropic's own app shipped into a fleet whose deployer is not Anthropic. Nessy is not a Claude Desktop deployment: it is a separate application whose vendor and deployer are the same organization, so the vendor/administrator separation the MDM push channel bridges does not exist here. 'Our fork is precisely the third-party deployment shape the key exists for' is the finding's own inference, not the page's. (2) CITATIONS - ACCURATE. `managed-policy.ts:129-130` are exactly `readonly allowedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]` / `readonly deniedMcpServers?: readonly ManagedMcpEntryV1[]`; `:501` is `export const MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS = [`, whose 30-key list contains no MCP-server-definition key. The absence is real: `grep -ran managedMcpServers` over the whole tree (with -a) hits only doc/spec files - `2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:698`, the sweep TSV/JSON, and this row. `toolPolicy` appears once in product code, as the type of an unused `RuntimeMcpServer.toolPolicy` field (`capabilities/resolver.ts:316`, interface at `:133`), with no producer or consumer. (3) CONSEQUENCE - HALF FALSE. OUR STATE asserts the managed policy 'carries no per-server tool restriction'. It does. The same admin-only file the MCP lists arrive in - `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json`, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` (`server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:48-50`), plus a `managed-policy.d/` drop-in dir - carries `permissionDsl` (`managed-policy.ts:82`, key at `:504`) and `claudeRules`, and that DSL has a first-class `mcp` matcher: `permission-dsl.ts:946-950` splits a tool's `permissionName` on `__` and wildcard-matches SERVER and TOOL independently, so `mcp__jira__delete_*` is exactly 'restrict which tools in that server users can invoke'. `claude-permission-rules.ts:171` parses the `mcp__server__tool` spelling from managed `claudeRules` too. It is enforced, not parsed-and-dropped: `SessionManager.ts:4095-4096` passes `managedPermissionDsl` into the turn, `:14267`/`:16245` read it again, the shipped docblock at `managed-policy.ts:299-301` names it as THE admin boundary ('a managed `permissionDsl` deny rule, which our deterministic gate applies BEFORE the judge is consulted at all'), and `isWholeToolDenyForIdentity` additionally REMOVES a wholly-denied MCP tool from the model's context. So the per-server tool-restriction half of the divergence is simply not a gap. (4) The remaining half - no managed key that PUSHES a server definition - is true, but it is (a) already recorded, not undiscovered, and (b) met differently by this fork's deployment shape. Recorded: `docs/architecture/managed-mcp-access.md:91` files the `managed-mcp.json` fixed deployment as 'documented, not implemented - a separate deployment channel', and the sibling finding f039, on that same absence, was already refuted 2026-08-02. Met differently: the fork ships the corporate server set IN THE PRODUCT - `BUILTIN_DP_MCP_SERVERS` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/builtin-dp-servers.ts:111`) is 29 frozen `dp ai mcp` server definitions (dpGitlab, dpJira, dpSage, SpiritK8s, ...) delivered to every user of the deployment, each with a `defaultEnabled` and a per-server user toggle (`config/builtin-dp-mcp-settings.ts`, `builtin-dp-mcp-preferences.ts`). 'Every user in this deployment gets these servers' is answered at build time because there is one organization, one gateway and one builder - which is the same de-brand/corporate-target difference that removes the admin console, the claude.ai connectors and the MDM fleet from this product. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 - I read all nine; none concerns MCP deployment.

The same admin-only `managed-policy.json` (system paths at `managed-policy-loader.ts:48-50`, plus `managed-policy.d/`) carries `permissionDsl`/`claudeRules`, whose `mcp` matcher wildcard-matches server and tool separately (`permission-dsl.ts:946-950`, `claude-permission-rules.ts:171`), is applied by the deterministic gate before any judge (`managed-policy.ts:299-301`, `SessionManager.ts:4095`), and strips a wholly-denied MCP tool from context - i.e. an administrator can already restrict which tools of a named server users may invoke. results.claim: Gitignored files are copied into a new worktree by declaring them in a `.worktreeinclude` file at the project root.
results.quote: To include gitignored files like `.env` in new worktrees, create a [`.worktreeinclude` file](/docs/en/worktrees#copy-gitignored-files-into-worktrees) in your project root.
results.ourState: We ship per-session worktree isolation (`WorktreeLeaseService`, namespace resolved by `resolveWorktreeNamespace`) but no include mechanism: `grep -a worktreeinclude` across the whole repo hits only `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md`. A session's worktree therefore never receives `.env` or any other gitignored file. (Our worktree root is a deliberate documented divergence — `<parent>/.nessy-worktrees/<slug>/` rather than `.claude/worktrees/` — and is not reported here.)

verdict.why: All three checks pass and no exemption applies. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop.md (960 lines), line 329, the WHOLE line, single sentence, nothing after it: "To include gitignored files like `.env` in new worktrees, create a [`.worktreeinclude` file](/docs/en/worktrees#copy-gitignored-files-into-worktrees) in your project root." Exact match to the claimed sentence. The surrounding lines reinforce rather than reverse it: :325 "For Git repositories, each session gets its own isolated copy of your project using [Git worktrees](/docs/en/worktrees)"; :328 the worktree-location/branch-prefix/archive paragraph; :331 a Note that only says session isolation requires Git. No carve-out anywhere on the page. (2) CITED CODE MATCHES EXACTLY: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/worktree-layout.ts:47 is `export function resolveWorktreeNamespace(repoRoot: string): WorktreeNamespace`, and :54 builds `join(containmentRoot, '.nessy-worktrees', safeWorktreeSegment(basename(root)))` — precisely the `WorktreeLeaseService` namespace the ourState describes, and the file header (:12-16) names the lease service as the caller. (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN, CONSEQUENCE TESTED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER: the single worktree creation site is the `git.create` closure at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10163-10197. It runs `show-ref`, then every command from `worktreeCreateCommands` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:74-96 — only `worktree add` [+ `--no-checkout` when sparse], `sparse-checkout set --cone`, `checkout`), then the links from `worktreeSymlinkPlan` (:112-124 — `symlinkDirectories` only, directories, repository-relative, skipped when the target is missing). No file copy of any kind: grep for copyFile/cpSync/copySync/readFile over worktree-lease-service.ts and worktree-git-plan.ts returns zero. One layer further up, packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts admits exactly four keys (baseRef, symlinkDirectories, sparsePaths, bgIsolation) and THROWS on anything else, so a user cannot express an include list through settings either. NUL-SAFE ABSENCE WITH POSITIVE CONTROL: `grep -rani -l worktreeinclude packages apps scripts` hits only apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/darwin-arm64/codex-app-server and its dist copy — a bundled third-party binary matching the unrelated case-insensitive substring `WorktreeIncludesRelative` (git worktree-config includes, not Claude's dotfile), not a reader. Positive control on the same rig: `symlinkDirectories` hits eleven files including worktree-settings.ts, worktree-git-plan.ts and SessionManager.ts. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK: we DO ship `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hook events (packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:360, path capture at :1247), but Claude's linked worktrees page presents a WorktreeCreate hook as the REPLACEMENT for `.worktreeinclude` ("copy the files inside the hook script instead"), not an implementation of it, so it does not close the gap. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — not one touches worktrees. NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md:131-151 records exactly six deviations with reasons (bgIsolation default `none`, the `<dirname(repo)>/.nessy-worktrees/<slug>/` root, Task 0 scope growth, the wrong alias anchor, the widened R15 seam, worktree settings not admitted to managed policy) and `.worktreeinclude` is not among them; docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:122 required it ("Add `.worktreeinclude` at the project root, `.gitignore` syntax, copying only files that both match a pattern and are gitignored") and it was simply never built. The de-brand is orthogonal: `.worktreeinclude` lives at the PROJECT root, unprefixed, not under `.claude/` — the `.nessy-worktrees` rename does not touch it. Subscription-flow drops and the corporate-gateway target are unrelated to worktrees.
verdict.correctedState: Stands as filed, with two precisions and a duplicate note. Precision 1 — the ourState's grep line is now stale: `grep -a worktreeinclude` repo-wide no longer hits only docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md. It also hits this sweep's own generated data files (2026-08-02-doc-sweep-divergences.tsv, 2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json, 2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase2.json, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-claude-doc-sweep-divergences.md, phase2-verdicts/f096.json and f147.json) and, as an unrelated case-insensitive substring `WorktreeIncludesRelative`, the bundled third-party binary apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/darwin-arm64/codex-app-server plus its dist copy. None is an implementation, so the conclusion is unchanged. Precision 2 — the gap is stronger than 'no include mechanism': the creation path performs no file copy at all (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10163-10197 runs only worktreeCreateCommands' git subcommands and worktreeSymlinkPlan's directory symlinks), and packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts hard-throws on any key outside baseRef/symlinkDirectories/sparsePaths/bgIsolation, so there is no settings-level workaround; `symlinkDirectories` is not equivalent (directories only, repository-relative, default empty, and it links rather than copies). results.claim: Cross-session messaging is gated on whether a human is watching: an unattended run can neither send nor receive one.
results.quote: Claude can't send cross-session messages from a session nobody is watching, such as a scheduled-task run, and can't deliver messages into one.
results.ourState: `handleSendAgentMessage` validates only that the target id is non-empty and is not the caller's own session; there is no attended/unattended check on either the sender or the recipient. `grep -a "unattended\|isWatched\|attended"` over `packages/session-tools-core/src` returns nothing. Our `SchedulerTick` automations create exactly the unwatched sessions the rule exists for, and they carry the tool. The sender-envelope and 20-session-default halves of the same section do match (`tool-defs.ts:839`, `send-agent-message.ts:35-41`).

verdict.why: Doc sentence verified verbatim: desktop.md line 362, third bullet of the 'Claude Code applies three safety behaviors across sessions' list, single sentence, no reversing second half. Cited file:line verified: packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/send-agent-message.ts:16 is the `!ctx.sendAgentMessage` guard, and the handler really does validate only non-empty sessionId/message plus self-send. The finding fails on the third check -- the consequence. Its own load-bearing evidence is 'Our SchedulerTick automations create exactly the unwatched sessions the rule exists for, and they carry the tool', and that is false for the shipped default. Automation prompt actions create their session at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:18585 with `permissionMode: permissionMode || 'explore'`. `send_agent_message` is declared `safeMode: 'block'` (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1038), and packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2407-2422 denies every `mcp__session__*` tool absent from `getSessionSafeAllowedToolNames` (tool-defs.ts:1286-1293, which keeps only `safeMode === 'allow'`) for any mode that is not default/acceptEdits/auto/bypassPermissions (mode-types.ts:98-100 gate at mode-manager.ts:2160-2170). So an unattended SchedulerTick run in its default mode is already refused the tool -- enforcement one layer up from the handler, which is exactly false-positive shape #3 recorded in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md:108. The same gate blocks it in `dontAsk`, the mode this repo labels 'Unattended' (mode-manager.ts:2543). Two further scope points: our R27b scheduling primitive is session-scoped and delivers a scheduled prompt into the SAME session between turns (packages/session-tools-core/src/context.ts:428-446), so 'a scheduled-task run' has no unwatched-session counterpart on that path at all; and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md row 98 already carries the verdict WHITE / 'chuzhoy desktop-produkt' for this page. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3.
verdict.correctedState: The handler has no attendedness check, and Nessy has no attended/unattended concept at all -- but the sender half of the rule is already enforced by a different mechanism for the case the finding names. SchedulerTick prompt automations create their session in `explore` (SessionManager.ts:18585), and `send_agent_message` (`safeMode: 'block'`, tool-defs.ts:1038) is denied there and in `dontAsk` by mode-manager.ts:2407-2422. What actually remains open, and is narrower than claimed: (1) the sender block is a default, not a rule -- an automation matcher that sets `permissionMode: 'auto'` or `'bypassPermissions'` (automations/types.ts:609) produces an unwatched session that can send; (2) the recipient half is genuinely unguarded in every mode -- nothing stops a watched session from delivering into an automation session, and `listSessionsFn` (SessionManager.ts:12851-12885) filters only by status/label/search, so automation sessions are targetable.

results.claim: On app start or wake, each task is checked for runs missed in the last seven days, and exactly one catch-up run fires for the most recently missed time.
results.quote: If it did, Desktop starts exactly one catch-up run for the most recently missed time and discards anything older.
results.ourState: No catch-up of any kind. `SchedulerService.start()` aligns to the next minute boundary and then fires `setInterval(… , 60_000)`; a tick that did not happen because the app was closed is simply never emitted, and `grep -ai "catch-up\|catchup\|missedRun\|lastRun"` over `packages/shared/src/automations` and `packages/shared/src/scheduler` returns zero non-test hits. A daily 9am task on a machine that was off at 9am never runs that day.

verdict.why: All three legs survive the challenge. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks.md (HTTP 200, 11740 bytes) puts the sentence on line 74, character-for-character, in the '## Missed runs' section. The whole line was read: the surrounding sentences reinforce rather than reverse it -- 'Desktop checks whether each task missed any runs in the last seven days', 'A daily task that missed six days runs once on wake', 'Desktop shows a notification when a catch-up run starts'. Line 70 of the same page ('If your computer sleeps through a scheduled time, the run is skipped') is about the in-session tick, not about the wake sweep, and the Missed-runs section is what governs. The page is row 97 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a real Claude Code contract page, not a Codex/MCP page conflated in. (2) CITED LINE: packages/shared/src/scheduler/scheduler-service.ts start() spans :33-45. :34 is the re-entrancy guard `if (this.timer || this.alignmentTimer) return;` and the described mechanism is at :37-44 -- `msUntilNextMinute` alignment, then `setInterval(() => this.tick(), 60_000)`. Off by a line or two on the anchor, dead accurate on the substance: there is no immediate tick, no replay, no persisted cursor; the first tick lands at the next minute boundary. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier: the durable Nessy analogue of Desktop scheduled tasks is the Automations subsystem (this repo says so itself at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:258 -- 'the DURABLE half of Claude's Desktop scheduled tasks mostly exists' in packages/shared/src/automations, with 'one catch-up run for the most recently missed time within seven days' named as part of the remaining gap, proposed as R31). Its scheduled trigger is packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:289 in matchesBasePredicate -- `return !!matcher.cron && matchesCron(matcher.cron, matcher.timezone)` -- and cron-matcher.ts:25-52 matches only whether the cron's nextRun falls inside the CURRENT minute window. No last-fired cursor is read anywhere on that path. Nothing upstream compensates: automation-system.ts:162 starts the scheduler and :396 only re-emits the tick onto the event bus; the history store (appendAutomationHistoryEntry, automations:getLastExecuted) is write-and-display only -- useAutomations.ts:62 hydrates lastExecutedAt purely for the 'last ran' label and no scheduling code reads it; retry-scheduler.ts is a webhook retry queue, unrelated; and grep -ain for powerMonitor over apps/electron/src/main and packages/server-core/src finds no OS wake/resume hook at all. So a daily 9am automation on a machine that was off at 9am does not run that day. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) -- and not a branding, subscription-flow or gateway product difference either. It is a recorded-but-OPEN product-surface gap, which is still a gap. TWO CORRECTIONS the finding needs, neither of which overturns it. First, the sibling-subsystem check does bite the wording: 'No catch-up of any kind' is overstated repo-wide, because packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts + cron-store.ts + packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts DO carry a lastFiredAt cursor, a cursorFor() helper and explicit catch-up prose (cron-scheduler.ts:121-131, cron-store.ts:198, sessions/index.ts:207). That tier delivers exactly one fire for an occurrence missed while the turn was busy and discards older ones because the cursor moves at delivery, not at enqueue (session-cron-service.ts:144-184). But that is the session-scoped Cron*//loop tier implementing scheduled-tasks.md:215, a DIFFERENT contract that forbids per-interval catch-up -- and session-cron-service.ts:9-16 explicitly documents why it is not SchedulerService. It is not the Desktop-Routines durable scheduler and does not survive an app restart in that sense, so it does not supply the behaviour this page specifies. Second, the finding's grep is scoped to only packages/shared/src/automations and packages/shared/src/scheduler; 'zero non-test hits' is true for those two directories but is not a repo-wide absence claim, and stating it as one is exactly how the sibling-subsystem trap fires. With the wording narrowed to the Automations subsystem, the divergence stands.
verdict.correctedState: Nessy's durable analogue of Desktop scheduled tasks is the Automations subsystem, and it performs no catch-up for occurrences missed while the app was closed or the machine asleep. SchedulerService.start() (packages/shared/src/scheduler/scheduler-service.ts:33-45) aligns to the next minute boundary and then ticks every 60_000 ms with no immediate tick and no replay; the scheduled-trigger predicate (packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:289 -> cron-matcher.ts:25) asks only whether the cron matches the CURRENT minute and reads no last-fired cursor; automation history (appendAutomationHistoryEntry / automations:getLastExecuted) is display-only and never consulted for scheduling; and there is no powerMonitor wake hook anywhere in apps/electron/src/main or packages/server-core/src. A daily 9am automation on a machine that was off at 9am does not run that day, and no notification is shown. This is a recorded-but-open gap, not a decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:258 already names 'one catch-up run for the most recently missed time within seven days' as part of the Automations product-surface gap versus desktop-scheduled-tasks.md, proposed as R31. Separately -- and this is the part the original finding's grep scope hid -- a DIFFERENT subsystem does implement a single-fire catch-up: the session-scoped Cron tier (packages/shared/src/sessions/cron-scheduler.ts, cron-store.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts) keeps a lastFiredAt cursor, delivers exactly one fire for a missed occurrence and discards older ones by moving the cursor at delivery rather than at enqueue. That tier implements scheduled-tasks.md:215 (the /loop contract, which forbids per-interval catch-up) and is deliberately not SchedulerService, per the rationale at session-cron-service.ts:9-16. So the accurate statement is 'the Automations scheduler has no catch-up', not 'no catch-up of any kind'.

results.claim: A per-task toggle gives each scheduled run its own isolated Git worktree, rather than running against the working directory's current state including uncommitted changes.
results.quote: Enable the worktree toggle when creating the task to give each run its own isolated Git worktree, the same way [parallel sessions](/docs/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions) work.
results.ourState: The automation schema carries `permissionMode` but no isolation field: `grep -a "permissionMode\|worktree\|isolat"` over `packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts` matches `permissionMode` only. `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` exist as observable hook events (`automations/types.ts:74-75`) but nothing lets a scheduled automation request a worktree, so every scheduled run mutates the live checkout, uncommitted changes included.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) DOC: the quoted sentence exists verbatim at desktop-scheduled-tasks.md:34, inside a two-sentence <Note>. The whole line was read; the first sentence corroborates rather than reverses it — 'By default, scheduled tasks run against whatever state your working directory is in, including uncommitted changes. Enable the worktree toggle when creating the task to give each run its own isolated Git worktree, the same way [parallel sessions](/docs/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions) work.' Line :45 repeats it as a create-form field: 'below it you select the working folder and whether to run in an isolated worktree.' The page is row 99 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page. (2) CITED LINE: packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts:178 is 'permissionMode: z.preprocess(' inside AutomationMatcherSchema; grep -a for 'permissionMode|worktree|isolat' over that file returns line 178 and nothing else. automations/types.ts:74-75 are indeed the WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove observational rows owned by 'worktree-lease-service', exactly as claimed. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and at both layers: one layer UP, the two write surfaces that create a scheduled automation carry no isolation key either — shared/src/automations/management.ts and session-tools-core/src/handlers/automation-management.ts (fields: event/cron/timezone/matcher/permissionMode/labels/actions), and the Electron editor model apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/types.ts has no worktree field (grep -a -i 'worktree|isolat' over the whole automations UI directory: zero hits). One layer DOWN, the run path was traced end to end: SchedulerTick -> PromptHandler.handleEvent -> onPromptsReady (SessionManager.ts:7087) -> executePromptAutomation -> this.createSession(workspaceId, {name, labels, permissionMode, enabledSourceSlugs, llmConnection, model, thinkingLevel, ephemeral}) at SessionManager.ts:18582 — no isolation argument exists to pass, so the session is created at the workspace root and edits land in the live checkout with uncommitted changes present. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM CHECK (the mirror trap): the fork does have worktree machinery, and it is named correctly here. WorktreeLeaseService (server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:80) is real, subagent child sessions DO get worktreePolicy 'isolated-worktree' (SessionManager.ts:4900-4902), EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree ship as Pi-only session tools (session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1015), and a global settings key worktree.bgIsolation exists (config/worktree-settings.ts) — none of which is a per-scheduled-task toggle. Also checked: the session cron store (shared/src/sessions/cron-store.ts) is the fork's implementation of the OTHER page, scheduled-tasks.md (/loop, CronCreate), whose four-field record the docs never give a worktree toggle, so it is not the analogue and citing automations is the right subsystem. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) — none touches worktrees or scheduling. Not a rebrand, gateway or dropped-subscription difference either. The coverage map already flags the page 🟨 row 99: 'код есть (32 файлов, 11 с тестами), строки нет' — code exists, no plan row.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with one qualification the finding should carry. There is no per-task isolation control anywhere on the scheduled-automation path: not in AutomationMatcherSchema (packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts:168-186, which carries permissionMode at :178 and nothing else), not in either create/update surface (shared/src/automations/management.ts, session-tools-core/src/handlers/automation-management.ts), not in the Electron editor model (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/types.ts), and not in the launch call (SessionManager.executePromptAutomation -> createSession at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:18582). Under defaults a scheduled run therefore executes in the workspace working directory against uncommitted changes, matching only the FIRST half of the doc's Note. The qualification: the fork owns the machinery, it is just not reachable per task. worktree.bgIsolation exists as a GLOBAL settings key (packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts) and, when set to "worktree", blocks Edit/Write in the main checkout for every session including scheduled ones (pre-tool-use.ts:934,:948) — but it creates no worktree; the agent must then call the Pi-only EnterWorktree tool. That key's default is "none" in this fork against Claude's documented "worktree", by a reason recorded in the module note (worktree-settings.ts:9-16): the release valve is Pi-only, so a Claude- or Codex-backed session would meet an unliftable write block. So 'nothing lets a scheduled automation request a worktree' is exact for a per-task toggle, and slightly overstated as an absolute — a Pi-backed run whose prompt instructs EnterWorktree, or a user who opts the whole install into bgIsolation, can approximate it. Closing the gap is an additive matcher field (e.g. worktree?: boolean) plumbed from the schema through management.ts, the editor and createSession into a WorktreeLeaseService lease; the per-child precedent already exists at SessionManager.ts:4900-4902.

results.claim: Environment variables can be set from a settings file under an `env` key at user, project, local and managed scope; values there are re-applied to a running session when the file changes and override the inherited shell value.
results.quote: Add variables under the `env` key in a `settings.json` file, creating the file if it doesn't exist.
results.ourState: An `env` block exists only on the MANAGED policy tier (`readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string,string>>`, applied by `applyManagedEnv`). There is no user-scope settings `env` block: the only other `env` record in the config schema is the per-MCP-stdio-server `env`. At project scope `env` is a deliberately FORBIDDEN section (project-config.ts:138), which is a recorded security decision — the user-scope gap is not.

verdict.why: All three refutation grounds were tested and none holds. (1) QUOTE — verbatim. curl -sL of env-vars.md puts the sentence at line 78, word for word. Read whole: line 78 is four sentences, and the remaining three only add caveats (a startup-only reader such as OpenTelemetry keeps its startup values; removing a variable does not unset it in a running session) — they do not reverse the conclusion. (2) CITED LINES — two of three exact. managed-policy.ts:359 is literally 'readonly env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>'; project-config.ts:138 is literally the FORBIDDEN_SECTIONS line carrying 'env', 'environment'. validators.ts:521 is off by five lines (it is authType); the MCP stdio env record the finding means is at validators.ts:526. verdict.correctedState: Narrow the finding to USER and LOCAL scope; two of the four scopes it implies are wrong. MANAGED scope is implemented, including the live re-apply the claim treats as missing: managed-policy.ts:359 declares the block, config/managed-env.ts:330 applyManagedEnv applies it under a four-category withhold rule, and config/managed-delivery.ts startManagedDeliveryEnvApplication re-applies on every later state change without a restart (the host-owned policy FILE applies with source 'managed-file' and is never withheld). What is genuinely absent is user and local scope: no env key in ~/.nessy-agent/config.json (config/storage.ts:152) or config-defaults.json, no dotenv loader, no CLI --env flag, and no reader of the env block in .claude/settings.json — agent/claude-settings-store.ts touches those files only as a write destination for permission rules. results.claim: The subagent nesting-depth default is 3 as of v2.1.219 — a subagent can spawn its own subagents by default, and 1 is the value that turns nesting off.
results.quote: Number of [subagent layers](/docs/en/sub-agents#let-subagents-spawn-their-own-subagents) allowed below the main conversation {/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}(default: 3).
results.ourState: Default depth is 1 in both places that carry it, i.e. Claude's "nesting off" value is our default, so a subagent cannot spawn a subagent unless the host explicitly raises `orchestrator.depth`. There is also no `NESSY_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` env override. The repo's own parity note (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:559) records this row as CLOSED against the old default of 1.

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding stands. Read WHOLE: the row is '{/* min-version: 2.1.217 */}Number of [subagent layers](...) allowed below the main conversation {/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}(default: 3). At the default, subagents can spawn their own subagents, and a subagent at the third layer can't spawn further; set `1` to turn nesting off. In v2.1.217 through v2.1.218, the default was 1, so a subagent couldn't spawn its own unless you raised the limit; v2.1.219 raised the default to 3. Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the limit can be adjusted but not removed. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later'. Nothing in the later sentences reverses the conclusion - they corroborate the claimed behaviour word for word, including that 1 is the nesting-off value. `env-vars` is a real Claude Code contract page in scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, not a Codex or platform page. (2) CODE - packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:110 is exactly `export const DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1`, docblock :105-109 'Default child-session nesting depth: ONE level of delegation. Must stay in lockstep with `DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth`'. Enforcement is spawner.ts:513-520: `const depth = (args.depth ?? 0) + 1` then `if (depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)) return failure(..., `Subagent depth limit exceeded (${cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH})`)`. Semantics match Claude's counting: main conversation spawns at depth 1 (allowed), a child spawning a grandchild computes depth 2 > 1 and is refused - i.e. exactly one subagent layer below the main conversation, which is Claude's `1` = nesting off. The mirror default is packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:107 `depth: 1` inside DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (the claim cites :106, which is the last comment line - a one-line citation drift, not a substantive error). Env override absent, checked NUL-safe with `grep -arn SPAWN_DEPTH .` over the whole repo (no --include filter, binary-safe): five files, ALL under docs/ (this sweep's own JSON/TSV/markdown plus 2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md). verdict.correctedState: Confirmed gap, with one correction to the wording. Our 32 KiB cut at packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-178 is hardcoded (`OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES` at :24), is applied only to the inline model-facing text at :236, and its marker carries no file path; there is no disk spill and no env override (`TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` and any `NESSY_*` analogue have 0 non-doc hits repo-wide). But the overflow is NOT simply discarded: the same result block's header prints `agent_id: <id>` (:227, populated for spawned children via spawner.ts:625), and `get_subagent_result(agent_id)` (:690-712) returns the child's result text WITHOUT `truncateOutput`, so the parent has a retrieval handle for the untruncated text — a tool call keyed by agent id rather than the documented file path. That untruncated text is itself host-bounded at `MAX_RESULT_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:41, applied at :603-605), so output beyond 64 KiB is genuinely lost before it ever reaches the 32 KiB cut. Two further mismatches worth recording: Claude's cap counts characters (32000 default, 160000 maximum) while ours counts UTF-8 bytes (32768), and Claude's is user-tunable to 5x the default while ours is not tunable at all.

results.claim: A write that leaves the auto-memory index MEMORY.md over 200 lines or 25KB returns an error to the model naming the overflow, because everything past the limit is silently dropped on every subsequent load.
results.quote: Claude wrote to the [auto memory](/docs/en/memory#auto-memory) index `MEMORY.md` and left it over one of its read limits: 200 lines or 25KB.
results.ourState: We have the read limit (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`) and we DO silently truncate at load (`readFileSync(...).split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`), but the write path (`appendMemory`) performs no post-write size check and returns no error or reminder — exactly the pre-v2.1.210 behaviour the page describes as the defect. There is also no 25KB byte limit and no frontmatter/HTML-comment exclusion.

verdict.why: Tried all three refutation axes and none holds. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors.md (1679 lines) carries the quoted sentence word-for-word at :1437, opening the section '### Memory index is over its read limit'. Read the WHOLE line — it is three sentences and the other two REINFORCE rather than reverse: 'The write succeeded, but only the first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, load at the start of a session, so everything past the limit is dropped each time the index is read. Before v2.1.210, an over-limit index was silently truncated on the next load with no write-time signal.' The surrounding block adds the literal error text (:1440, naming line count and the 'Rewrite it to under 140 lines' remedy), a {/* min-version: 2.1.211 */} refinement that frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before measurement, 'Claude Code delivers the error to Claude after the write rather than printing it as a banner', and 'When Claude's write brings the file near a limit without crossing it, Claude Code returns a milder reminder to compact the index instead of this error.' :101 lists the error in the top-level index table. The page is row 102 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv ('errors	Error reference'), so it is a valid Claude contract citation, not a Codex or MCP page. (2) CITED CODE says what was claimed. memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-33 is readMemoryFile doing `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — a silent slice, no signal. remember.ts:39-49 is appendMemory: read existing, formatMemoryFile, write temp, rename, chmod — and :90-91 is `appendMemory(filePath, memory); return successResponse(`Saved memory to ${filePath}`);`. No measurement, no error, no reminder. (3) CONSEQUENCE verified separately from the identifier, one layer up and one layer down, including the sibling-subsystem trap. UP: `remember` is live and model-reachable (tool-defs.ts:981, safeMode 'block'). DOWN/SIBLING: there is a SECOND writer on a different subsystem — appendMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:122-132), reached by the renderer RPC path ChatDisplay.tsx:1557 -> dto.ts:519 `{type:'appendMemory'}` -> sessions.ts:564 -> :80 — and it has no post-write check either, so naming only the tool path understates it. Absence positively controlled with `rg -na` (NUL-byte-safe) for 'over its|read limit|left the memory|rewrite it to under|near a limit' across packages/ and apps/: zero memory-related hits, so neither the hard error nor the documented milder near-limit reminder exists. No byte cap exists anywhere on the memory path: the only *_MAX_BYTES in the subsystem is AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 (memory-cleanup.ts:33), a skip-guard in the scheduled dream pass (:125 leaves oversized files unchanged), not a 25KB load or write limit. No frontmatter or block-level HTML-comment exclusion: only the auto-marker `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` is stripped (stripAutoMemoryMarkers, memory-store.ts:159-163), and in the legacy path that strip happens in mergeMemoryContents AFTER the 200-line slice. NOT an owner decision: 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touches memory limits. NOT a deliberate product difference either: this fork has a real auto-memory subsystem (remember tool + marker + scheduled cleanup), so the de-brand, the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows and the corporate gateway are all irrelevant here. Note for the collector: this substantially duplicates f103 (same defect cited from memory.md:386) and is adjacent to f092/f098/f104 (the missing 25KB load cap) — one fix closes all of them.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with one clause of the submitted wording corrected and two scope additions. CORRECTION: 'we DO silently truncate at load' is true only on the LEGACY composer. prompts/system.ts:453-455 calls loadMemoryPromptBlock — the sole route to readMemoryFile's 200-line slice — only when `capabilityContextPinned` is false. On the live capability-runtime path, composePinnedCapabilityContext (base-agent.ts:975-1015) reads each memory layer with `await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)`, which returns the whole file; the only content ever removed there is `@import` lines (:1003-1007) and `paths:`-rule bodies. results.claim: When every entry in a subagent's `tools` frontmatter list fails to match a usable tool, the spawn is refused with a diagnostic grouping the entries by cause, rather than launching a toolless subagent.
results.quote: Every entry in the subagent's [`tools` list](/docs/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields) failed to match a usable tool, so Claude Code refused to launch the subagent: with no tools, it couldn't act.
results.ourState: `allowedTools()` filters the declared list against `disallowedTools` only and hands the result straight to the child restrictions. Unrecognised names, names not available to subagents, and names matching nothing in the session are all passed through unvalidated, and an empty result is not detected — the child launches with no usable tools and no error.

verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at errors.md:1400 (whole line read; no reversing second sentence). But the finding cites the WRONG LAYER, and its three-part description of our state is false at the layer that actually does the work. (1) The cited code, spawner.ts:296-298 `allowedTools()`, filters the declared list against `disallowedTools` only -- exactly as claimed -- yet errors.md:1406 explicitly carves that case OUT of the refusal: 'Omitting the `tools` field never triggers this refusal. If you leave the `tools` list empty, or `disallowedTools` removes every entry in it, Claude Code also skips the refusal and launches the subagent without tools.' So the one line cited as evidence is conformant, not divergent. (2) The layer that handles the doc's three groups is upstream: `resolveExplicitTools` / `buildPiRuntimeAgentDefinitions` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:92-126 and :129-179), called in production at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1313 with the session's real tool set (`manifest.tools.map(t => t.binding.piName)` plus `manifest.deferredMcp.candidatePiNames`). It resolves each declared name exactly, case-insensitively, then via PI_RUNTIME_AGENT_TOOL_ALIASES. 'Unrecognized' -> pushed onto `unresolved` and `throw new Error('Unavailable runtime agent tool(s): ...')` at :122-124 (fail-closed, and STRICTER than Claude, which refuses only when ALL entries fail). 'Not available to subagents' -> SUBAGENT_UNAVAILABLE_TOOLS (:50) stripped at :125, and ORCHESTRATION_TOOLS (:33-40) withheld from a tool-less descriptor's ceiling. 'Matched no tools in this session' -> a recognized alias with no counterpart in this manifest is 'denied by omission' at :116-120. The host re-validates the arriving list against the pinned definition (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10859, `runtime-agent-tool-unavailable:<tool>`) and re-filters it against `parentTools` at :10994. So 'unrecognised names, names not available to subagents, and names matching nothing in the session are all passed through unvalidated' is wrong on all three counts -- the textbook 'identifier unwired but consequence false because something upstream already handled it'. (3) Only a narrow residual survives: there is no 'Agent would be spawned with zero tools - refusing' refusal with entries grouped by cause (`grep -a` for 'zero tools'/'resolved to nothing' over all TS sources returns only an unrelated MCP test). A list whose entries all resolve to dropped entries yields `effectiveTools` = union with SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS (runtime-agent-definitions.ts:83, :149) -- usually five task/report tools, occasionally empty -- and the spawn proceeds. That is Claude's own pre-v2.1.208 behaviour (errors.md:1408), and it is a missing diagnostic, not the unvalidated pass-through the finding describes. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3, and not a branding/product difference.
verdict.correctedState: Declared subagent `tools` entries ARE validated, one layer above the cited line. `resolveExplicitTools` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:92-126), reached in production from index.ts:1313 with the session's actual Pi manifest tool names, throws `Unavailable runtime agent tool(s): <name>` on an unrecognised entry (:122-124), strips SUBAGENT_UNAVAILABLE_TOOLS (:50, :125), and denies a recognised alias with no counterpart in this session by omission (:116-120); SessionManager.ts:10859 and :10994 re-validate and re-filter host-side. `allowedTools()` at spawner.ts:296-298 applies only the `disallowedTools` subtraction, which errors.md:1406 explicitly exempts from the refusal. The genuine, much smaller gap is that we have no equivalent of the v2.1.208 'Agent would be spawned with zero tools - refusing' guard: when every entry drops out, the child launches with only SUBAGENT_ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_TOOLS (possibly none) and no grouped diagnostic naming which entries failed and why.

results.claim: A `pkill` whose pattern matches the agent's own process is refused before it runs; the pattern is probed with `pgrep` and the refusal is returned in the Bash tool result.
results.quote: Claude Code tests the pattern with `pgrep` before running `pkill` and refuses when its own process ID is in the result.
results.ourState: `pkill` is only classified as a dangerous command that requires a permission decision — there is no self-PID probe. `pgrep` appears nowhere in the tool/permission path (only in build scripts and a shellguard corpus fixture), so in a mode that does not prompt, a matching pattern can terminate the agent process mid-turn.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1751; packages/shared/src/agent/core/permission-manager.ts:46; grep -ra --include="*.ts" -ln "pgrep" . → no hit under packages/*/src runtime paths

Sentence 4 adds 'Before v2.1.214, the command ran, and a matching pattern killed the Claude Code session mid-turn', i.e. the claimed consequence is Claude Code's OWN shipped macOS behaviour today. results.claim: When a skill of the same name exists at more than one level, the USER-scope definition wins over the project-scope one (managed > user > project).
results.quote: **Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents).
results.ourState: Skill collisions are resolved by `scopeSpecificity`, which ranks project(3) > workspace(2) > global(1) > builtin(0) for every non-MCP capability kind including skills — the inverse of the documented skill order for the user-vs-project pair. A repo checking in `.nessy-agent/skills/deploy` silently shadows the user's own `deploy` skill; on Claude it would not. The surrounding comment cites mcp.md for the MCP arm only, so the skill arm appears unexamined.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) Quote is verbatim: features-overview.md line 193 reads '* **Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents).' The rest of that line ('Plugin skills are namespaced to avoid conflicts. See skill discovery and subagent scope.') does not reverse it, and skills.md:122 corroborates independently: 'When skills share the same name across levels, enterprise overrides personal, and personal overrides project. A skill at any of these levels also overrides a bundled skill with the same name.' (2) The cited code says what was claimed: packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869 scopeSpecificity returns project 3 / workspace 2 / global 1 / builtin 0, and applyCollisionPolicy (:2011, preference tuple :2038-2042, sort :2045-2051) sorts every non-MCP bucket -- skills included, bucket key is `${kind}\u0000${logicalName}` at :2017 -- by scopeSpecificity DESCENDING, so the project record wins the unqualified alias. The docblock at :1993-2010 cites mcp.md for the MCP arm only; no skills.md citation exists for the non-MCP arm, and no test covers the user-vs-project pair (resolver.test.ts:255-263 covers workspace-vs-plugin, :266-283 covers same-scope nessy-vs-portable). (3) The consequence is real, verified empirically and one layer down, not inferred. A throwaway probe test through createCapabilityResolver with two same-named skill records -- scope global and scope project -- returned: global key alias=false, project key alias=true. The alias is load-bearing downstream: base-agent.ts:2124-2126 builds skillsByAlias from `runtime.view.skills.filter(skill => skill.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias)`, and :2345-2350 gates bare-name skill mention resolution on the same flag, so a bare `deploy` reference resolves to the project skill and the user's own is reachable only by its qualified key. Scope mapping is unambiguous: native-sources.ts:899-904 puts BOTH `~/.agents/skills` (portable, the direct analogue of `~/.claude/skills`) and `${CONFIG_DIR}/skills` (CONFIG_DIR = `~/.nessy-agent`, paths.ts:18-21) at scope 'global', while :996-1010 puts `<project>/.nessy-agent/skills` at scope 'project'. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns scope precedence (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, and three SessionMirrorStore rows), and grepping the plans and the parity audit for a skill-precedence ruling returns nothing. The one refinement to the claim's wording: the losing record is not removed -- it stays enabled and addressable by qualified key, and an info-severity diagnostic capability.collision.unqualified-alias is emitted (:2055-2061) -- but the bare name, which is what a user or the model types, does go to the project definition, which is the inversion the doc forbids.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed with one wording refinement. verdict.why: All three checks confirm the divergence. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/features-overview.md line 227 contains the quoted sentence exactly. The whole line is a two-sentence-plus footnote whose earlier half describes `disable-model-invocation: true` in frontmatter; the second half is the quoted sentence and does not reverse it. Plugin skills are explicitly EXEMPT (`Manage those through /plugin instead`). (2) CITED STATE: the file-authored half is confirmed present -- `packages/shared/src/capabilities/types.ts:129` documents and declares `skillDisableModelInvocation`, parsed at `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:296-298`, carried through `resolver.ts:1007-1009,1659-1661` and `views.ts:190-192`, and ENFORCED twice: `agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:405` filters the skill out of `<available_skills>` and `agent/base-agent.ts:2141` refuses a model-origin invocation of the same skill.
