UP -- every settings-side skill control we do have was checked and none reproduces the behaviour: `disableBundledSkills` (`config/bundled-skills-settings.ts`, `config/storage.ts:1337-1353`) is a bulk on/off for bundled skills, not per-skill and not a visibility ladder; the native-source `enabled` flag (`native-sources.ts:551,594` -> `resolver.ts:1595` `record.sourceEnabled !== false`) is set only on `kind === 'source'` records (MCP/api/local), never on `kind === 'skill'` records built by `skillRecords()` at `native-sources.ts:266-290`, so it cannot disable a skill; session selection (`resolver.ts:737-739`, fed at `server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:859`) supplies `enabledSourceKeys` for `kind === 'source'` only and no production producer supplies `transientlyDisabledKeys`. DOWN -- `disableModelInvocation` reaches the runtime exclusively from SKILL.md frontmatter or a plugin skill declaration; nothing merges a settings layer into it. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) -- none touches skill visibility. verdict.correctedState: Confirmed gap, with the scope narrowed and the evidence line corrected. results.claim: The MEMORY.md index load is capped by BOTH a line count and a byte size; we cap only lines, so a 200-line file with long lines loads unbounded into every session's context.
results.quote: The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the `MEMORY.md` index loads at the start of every session.
results.ourState: `readMemoryFile` slices to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` lines and applies no byte limit; no 25 KB (or any) size constant exists in the memory subsystem.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`), :29-32 (`readMemoryFile` — `split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)`, no byte check); `grep -ran "25_000\|25600\|25 \* 1024" packages/shared/src/agent/memory` returns nothing

verdict.why: All three checks pass. (1) Quote is VERBATIM. curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary.md line 45 (section '### Auto memory') reads in full: 'Notes Claude writes for itself based on your corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under `~/.claude/projects/`. All worktrees of the same repository share one auto memory directory. The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the `MEMORY.md` index loads at the start of every session. Auto memory is the Claude-written counterpart to [CLAUDE.md](#claude-md), which you write.' Nothing later in the line reverses it. memory.md:384 states the same rule with more force ('Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start') and memory.md:390 scopes it ('This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length'), so the byte cap is a MEMORY.md-specific rule, not a general instruction-file rule. (2) Cited file:line is accurate. packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8 is `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and :29-32 is `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` doing `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` with no byte check. `grep -rna` (with -a, so NUL-byte files are not skipped) over packages/shared/src/agent/memory finds only AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256*1024 in memory-cleanup.ts (the scheduled rewrite pass's input guard, not a load cap) and RULE_PATTERN_EXPANSION_BYTE_LIMIT = 4MB in rule-matching.ts (glob expansion). No 25 KB constant exists anywhere in the memory subsystem. (3) Consequence verified separately, one layer up and one layer down, and it is WORSE than claimed rather than refuted. Layer down: readMemoryFile's two call sites are prompts/system.ts:455 (via loadMemoryPromptBlock) and capabilities/native-sources.ts:427 (an @import-discovery line scan, not a content load). Layer up: system.ts:453-455 reads `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, so the 200-line route is the LEGACY fallback only — AGENTS.md already records that the capability runtime is active on every normal send. The live route is: buildNativeCapabilityInventory registers `join(configDir,'MEMORY.md')` (and the session MEMORY.md) as `kind:'memory'` records via memoryFileRecords (native-sources.ts:909-916, :980-989); views.ts:218-219 puts them in `view.memory` with no size filter; base-agent.ts composePinnedCapabilityContext iterates `runtime.view.memory` and calls `runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)`; materializer.ts:169-185 does `readFileSync(contentPath)` and returns `content.toString('utf-8')` whole. The content is pushed verbatim into the pinned block that rides every session. So on the shipped path neither the 25 KB byte cap nor even the 200-line cap applies. Not a recorded owner decision: inert-worklist section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none touch memory loading. Not a deliberate fork difference either: this is not a Claude/ChatGPT subscription flow, not gateway-specific, and not a rename. The parity audit at :1672-1675 independently names 'a documented load limit (first 200 lines or 25 KB of `MEMORY.md`, whichever comes first, with frontmatter and HTML comments stripped before measurement)' as part of the auto-memory subsystem it found we had understated. The only inaccuracy in the finding is its mechanism sentence 'we cap only lines' — true of the legacy composer, false of the live one, which caps nothing.
verdict.correctedState: There is no 25 KB byte cap on the MEMORY.md load anywhere in the repo (memory-store.ts:8 declares only MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200; the only byte constants in packages/shared/src/agent/memory are AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256 KB for the cleanup rewrite pass and RULE_PATTERN_EXPANSION_BYTE_LIMIT = 4 MB for glob expansion). The gap is broader than the finding states: the 200-line cap in readMemoryFile (memory-store.ts:29-32) governs only the LEGACY composer, which prompts/system.ts:453-455 skips whenever the capability runtime is pinned — i.e. on every normal send — plus an @import-discovery line scan at native-sources.ts:427. On the live route the global ~/.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md and the session MEMORY.md are registered as kind:'memory' capability records (native-sources.ts:909-916, :980-989), carried unfiltered into view.memory (views.ts:218-219), and read by materializer.readText (materializer.ts:169-185), which readFileSync's the whole file and returns it; base-agent.ts composePinnedCapabilityContext pushes that verbatim into the pinned block. So MEMORY.md enters every session's context with NEITHER a byte cap NOR a line cap. Also missing, per memory.md:384-386: the pre-measurement stripping of frontmatter and HTML comments, and the post-write over-limit error (tracked separately as f166). memory.md:390 confirms the cap is MEMORY.md-specific and must not be applied to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction layers, which are correctly loaded in full.

results.claim: Trusting your home directory must be session-scoped and re-prompt on every launch; in our fork a home-directory grant persists to disk like any other project.
results.quote: Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch.
results.ourState: `ProjectTrustStore.record`/`resolve` persist any grant whose identity `persistence` is `'stable'`; `persistence` is decided purely by whether the platform can stat the root, with no home-directory carve-out anywhere in `projects/` or `capabilities/`.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-trust-store.ts:114-125 (`resolve` returns a persisted `'stable'` decision), :135-157 (`record`); packages/shared/src/projects/project-identity.ts:112-132 (`process-only` only on stat failure); `grep -rain "homedir\|process.env.HOME" packages/shared/src/projects packages/shared/src/capabilities` returns nothing

verdict.why: All three legs check out, and the consequence was measured, not inferred. (1) DOC: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary.md line 231 (the whole '### Project trust' paragraph) carries the quoted sentence VERBATIM: 'Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch.' The rest of the line does not reverse it — it adds 'Trust gates auto-installation of marketplace plugins and execution of project-defined hooks' and that config files take effect, which reinforces what a persisted home grant would unlock. (2) CODE: the cited lines say what was claimed. project-trust-store.ts:114-128 resolve() returns the persisted record for any identity whose persistence is 'stable'; :135-158 record() writes it to CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json for 'stable' and keeps only 'process-only' in memory; project-identity.ts:116-133 sets persistence='process-only' ONLY when statIdentity() fails or reports inode 0. grep -rain 'homedir|process.env.HOME' over packages/shared/src/projects and packages/shared/src/capabilities returns nothing, and the same grep over the layers above (packages/server-core/src, apps/electron/src/main) finds home only in credential-deny-roots, path expansion and getHomeDir — never in the trust path. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and with a positive control. Probe against the real home directory: resolveProjectIdentity(homedir()) -> persistence 'stable', key p_d70d9d9d…; ProjectTrustStore.record(home,'trusted') writes the record to disk; a FRESH store instance (restart simulation) resolves it back as {state:'trusted', persistence:'stable'}. Positive control on the same rig: a process-only identity recorded 'trusted' resolves to {state:'none'} from a fresh instance — the session-only machinery exists and works, home simply never reaches it. One layer up: ProjectHandleService.validateProjectDirectory (the sole raw-path ingress, project-handle-service.ts:140-156, 250-278) ACCEPTS $HOME — isManagedPath rejects only CONFIG_DIR (~/.nessy-agent) and managed workspace roots, and I ran it: validateProjectDirectory('ws-1', homedir()) issued a handle with trustState 'unknown'. One layer down: the grant is material — capabilities/resolver.ts:1623-1636 and :1709-1727 withhold project-scope instructions, hooks, MCP and LSP unless trustState==='trusted', so a persisted home grant permanently unlocks execution of anything under the home tree. Caveat recorded rather than used as a refutation: this fork has no CLI 'launch in cwd' — a project root is an explicit folder pick bound to a workspace/session — so 'the prompt reappears on each launch' maps here to 'the grant must not survive a restart', which is exactly what fails.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED. The fork treats the user's home directory as an ordinary project root and persists trust for it. ProjectHandleService.validateProjectDirectory accepts $HOME (isManagedPath rejects only CONFIG_DIR and managed workspace roots — project-handle-service.ts:250-278); resolveProjectIdentity($HOME) returns persistence 'stable' because the platform can stat it (project-identity.ts:116-133); ProjectTrustStore.record then writes the grant to CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json and a fresh store instance resolves it as 'trusted' after restart (project-trust-store.ts:135-158, :114-128) — measured directly on this host. Claude Code holds home trust for the current session only and re-prompts each launch. The session-only path exists in our store but is reachable only through a stat failure or a zero inode ('process-only'), never through a home-directory carve-out. Consequence is real, not cosmetic: capabilities/resolver.ts:1623-1636 / :1709-1727 gate project-scope instructions, hooks, MCP and LSP on trustState==='trusted', so one accidental 'Trust' on $HOME permanently enables project-defined hook execution across the whole home tree with no re-prompt. verdict.correctedState: Nessy implements the goal loop (condition, per-turn settlement evaluation through the mini model, automatic continuation dispatch, plus turn/token/cost/elapsed budgets and evidence-backed complete/blocked states that Claude's /goal does not have; condition cap 8192 chars vs Claude's 4000). results.claim: A SIGTERM'd non-interactive run must exit 143; ours exits 130 for both SIGINT and SIGTERM, so a supervisor cannot tell an operator interrupt from a shutdown signal.

The page is row 114 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude Code contract page, not a Codex/MCP page. (2) CODE: apps/cli/src/index.ts:795-804 says exactly what was claimed — `const onSignal = async () => { ... await cleanup(); process.exit(130) }` at :796-802, registered for BOTH signals at :803 (`process.on('SIGINT', onSignal)`) and :804 (`process.on('SIGTERM', onSignal)`), torn down at :861-862. This is inside `cmdRun`, which is our non-interactive/print surface (`spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })` at :782) — the correct analogue of `claude -p`, so this is not the sibling-subsystem trap. SIGINT is unaffected (130 is correct there, 128+2). NOT an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/foldSessionSummary) touches signals or exit codes. results.claim: Piped stdin is read unbounded into memory; the documented 10 MB cap and its clear-error/non-zero-exit behavior are absent.
results.quote: As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status.
results.ourState: `readPrompt` loops `Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` to `done`, pushing every decoded chunk into an array, with no running byte count and no cap.

verdict.why: All three challenge steps confirm the finding. (1) The quote exists VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md` line 86, inside a <Note> block in the "Pipe data through Claude" section, reads in full: "As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status. To work with larger inputs, write the content to a file and reference the file path in your prompt instead of piping it." The claimed quote is the first two sentences character-for-character; the unquoted third sentence is a workaround suggestion and does not reverse the conclusion. (2) The cited code says what was claimed. apps/cli/src/index.ts:423-442 `readPrompt` — it enters the stdin branch when `--stdin` is present or (no positional message and `process.stdin.isTTY` is false), then does `const chunks: string[] = []; const reader = Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` and loops `while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; chunks.push(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })) }` before `chunks.join('')`. There is no running byte counter, no length comparison, no throw, no `process.exit`. (3) Nothing one layer up or down supplies the cap. Layer up: the only two callers are `cmdSend` (:576) and `cmdRun` (:766) — `cmdRun` is this fork's `claude -p` analogue, spawning a local headless server in printMode — and both validate only `!message.trim()`; a binary-safe `grep -ran` over apps/cli/src finds `Bun.stdin`/`process.stdin` at exactly two lines (:427, :430), so there is no second stdin reader (no stream-json input path) that might cap. Layer down: the message travels the WsRpcServer (packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts), which constructs `new WebSocketServer({ server })` (:294, :310) with no `maxPayload` option — a repo-wide `grep -ran maxPayload` over packages/server-core/src, packages/server/src and apps/cli/src returns zero hits — so the `ws` default is 100 MiB, well above 10 MB, and even that would surface as a connection close, not a clear error. No RPC handler enforces a text-message size limit (the only "too large" errors in packages/server-core/src/handlers are image-attachment resizes in files.ts:324-336). The nearest same-named constants are in a SIBLING subsystem and do NOT apply: `ProcessSupervisor.MAX_STDIN_DATA_BYTES = 1 MiB` and `MAX_STDIN_WRITE_BYTES = 64 KiB` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:25-27) bound what the host writes to a CHILD process's stdin, not what the CLI reads from its own. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) — none concerns stdin or the CLI. Not a de-brand, gateway or dropped-subscription product difference either: docs/cli.md:118-125 and :195-199 actively document piping stdin into both `nessy-general-agent send` and `nessy-general-agent run`, so the fork ships the surface the doc caps and simply never caps it.

Both entry points are affected — `cmdSend` (:576) and `cmdRun` (:766), the latter being this fork's headless `claude -p` analogue — and each validates only that the result is non-empty (`!message.trim()`). verdict.why: Doc quote is verbatim and the whole line is that one sentence (curl https://code.claude.com/docs/en/interactive-mode.md, line 287, bullet under '### How backgrounding works'; neighbours at :286 cleanup-on-exit and :288 memory-pressure reaping do not reverse it). But the finding's OUR STATE is factually wrong and it names the wrong subsystem. (1) The two cited constants are real and say what was claimed - deferred-mcp-tools.ts:92 breaks the capability-search listing at MAX_DEFERRED_CAPABILITY_SEARCH_OUTPUT, sandbox.ts:276/:329-332 throws WorkflowEvaluationLimitError past DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES - but both belong to the deferred-tool search and the workflow sandbox, neither of which is the background shell. (2) 'the background-shell path has none' is false. The background shell is bash_background (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1402-1412, createBackgroundBashTool) -> requestSupervisedProcess({background:true}) -> ProcessSupervisor -> ProcessStore, and ProcessStore.append IS an output-byte ceiling: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-store.ts:7 'const MAX_LOG_BYTES = 64 * 1024' and :126-131 compute 'drop = max(0, combined.byteLength - limit)', rewrite the log to combined.subarray(drop) and advance baseCursor by the dropped byte count. Production uses the default with no override (SessionManager.ts:3573 'new ProcessStore({ root: join(SESSIONS_DIR, ".pi-processes") })'); the only maxLogBytes argument in the tree is a test at process-supervisor.test.ts:698. Two more ceilings on the same path the finding also missed: ProcessSupervisor.MAX_FOREGROUND_STREAM_BYTES = 64*1024 (process-supervisor.ts:28, applied by appendBoundedStream at :750-754) and OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES in orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-177. So 'the only output-byte ceilings in the tree are X and Y' is wrong on its own terms. (3) The CONSEQUENCE is handled one layer up, which is this repo's recurring false-positive shape. Claude needs a 5GB kill switch because it accumulates the full background-task output; here accumulation is structurally impossible - the on-disk log is a fixed 64 KiB rolling window, so a task that floods output writes 64 KiB forever and the cursor accounting (baseCursor/nextCursor, readLog at :142-148, surfaced to the model as next_offset via handlers/bash-output.ts and pi-agent.ts:6141 requestBashOutput) keeps the gap visible rather than silently lying. Termination is not absent either: BACKGROUND_PROCESS_MAX_LIFETIME_MS = 24h caps every background shell (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:952, applied at :1411 and :1590), and ProcessSupervisor.trackAppend (:675-681) SIGKILLs the whole process tree and marks the record 'lost' if the store write ever fails, which is the disk-exhaustion case the 5GB rule guards. The literal-number grep is a search for the wrong constant: verified binary-safe with grep -rain that no 5GB literal exists, which is true and irrelevant. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions), and not a rebrand/subscription-flow product difference. verdict.correctedState: The background-shell path DOES have an output-byte ceiling, and it is the ceiling the finding says is missing: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-store.ts:7 MAX_LOG_BYTES = 64 KiB, enforced in ProcessStore.append (:118-138) as a rolling window that drops the oldest bytes and advances baseCursor, used with the default by production (SessionManager.ts:3573). Two further caps sit on the same path: ProcessSupervisor.MAX_FOREGROUND_STREAM_BYTES = 64 KiB (process-supervisor.ts:28, :750-754) and OUTPUT_CAP_BYTES for subagent output (orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:171-177). Background tasks are also terminated on two axes: a 24h BACKGROUND_PROCESS_MAX_LIFETIME_MS (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:952, :1411, :1590) and an immediate SIGKILL of the process tree with status 'lost' if a log append fails (process-supervisor.ts:675-681). Because output never accumulates past 64 KiB, the resource-exhaustion harm Claude's 5GB rule prevents cannot occur here. The only true residual is a behavioural difference, not a missing ceiling: a runaway background task that floods output keeps running (up to 24h) with its excess output discarded, where Claude Code would kill it at 5GB and leave a stderr note; and the drop is signalled to the model only implicitly, through a next_offset that outruns the bytes returned, rather than by an explicit note. If that residual is worth filing, it should be filed as 'no explicit dropped-output note on BashOutput / no volume-triggered termination', citing process-store.ts:126-131, not as 'the background-shell path has no output-byte ceiling'.

verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED with three corrections to the wording. (a) 'no `namespace:action` vocabulary' is misleading: a namespaced action vocabulary does exist, it uses a dot instead of a colon — apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/definitions.ts declares 27 ids of the form `app.newChat`, `nav.focusChat`, `view.toggleSidebar`, `navigator.selectAll`, `panel.focusNext`, `chat.stopProcessing`. (b) 'no `null`-to-unbind' is imprecise: the registry's data model already treats null as unbound — types.ts:7 `defaultHotkey: string | null  // null = no default hotkey`, registry.tsx:31 `Map<ActionId, string | null>`, :61-62 `?? null`, and the keydown loop at :84 does `if (!hotkey || !matchesHotkey(...)) continue`. results.claim: We enable git's `extensions.worktreeConfig` by running `sparse-checkout set` in a linked worktree but never unset it when the last worktree is removed, leaving the main checkout in the state the doc says causes go-git tools to fail.
results.quote: Claude Code removes that entry after the last worktree is removed, but only if Claude Code added it.
results.ourState: The lease `remove` handler runs exactly one command, `git -C <root> worktree remove <path>`; there is no `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig`, no ownership marker recording that we added it, and no last-worktree bookkeeping. `worktree-settings.ts` documents the side effect but nothing acts on it.
results.evidence: packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10210-10213 (the whole `remove` handler); packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:85-95 (`sparse-checkout set --cone` is what enables it); packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:38-44 (the side effect, noted only); `grep -ran "worktreeConfig" packages apps` matches that comment alone

verdict.why: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) VERBATIM: large-codebases.md line 242 reads, whole line: "Sparse checkout requires git to enable `extensions.worktreeConfig` in the repository's shared `.git/config` while a sparse worktree exists. Claude Code removes that entry after the last worktree is removed, but only if Claude Code added it. It never removes a value you set yourself. Before v2.1.207, the entry remained after the last worktree was removed, and go-git-based tools such as `tea` failed to open the repository until you ran `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig`." The second/third/fourth sentences reinforce rather than reverse the claim, and settings.md:372 carries the enabling half and links back to this section. (2) CITED STATE CONFIRMED: SessionManager.ts:10210-10213 `remove: async lease => { const root = await projectRoot(); await runGit(root, ['-C', root, 'worktree', 'remove', lease.path], 'remove') }` is the entire handler; worktree-git-plan.ts:85-89 pushes `['-C', worktreePath, 'sparse-checkout', 'set', '--cone', ...sparse]`; worktree-settings.ts:38-44 documents the shared-.git/config side effect and nothing acts on it. `grep -ran "worktreeConfig"` over source (with -a, binaries excluded) matches only that comment; `git config --unset` appears nowhere in the repo (the one `--unset` hit is `claude-bash-rule.ts:269`, an `env -u` flag table, a different subsystem). No `git config` invocation exists anywhere in worktree-git-plan.ts or worktree-lease-service.ts. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY, not assumed: on git 2.43.0 I built a scratch repo, added a linked worktree with `--no-checkout`, ran exactly our argv `git -C <wt> sparse-checkout set --cone pkg/a` -- the shared `.git/config` gained `[extensions] worktreeConfig = true` (absent before both `worktree add` and the sparse-set) -- then ran `git worktree remove <wt>`, removing the LAST worktree: the entry is still `true`. So the layer below really does enable it and the layer above really does leave it. Nothing upstream handles it either: the only other removal path, `WorktreeLeaseService.sweepOrphans`/`release` (worktree-lease-service.ts:146-192, :331), routes through the same `git.remove` closure. NOT a recorded decision: inert-worklist section 3's nine dated owner decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions -- none touches worktrees. The deviation register has zero `worktreeConfig` hits, and the R2 plan (2026-07-27-session-worktrees.md:85) lists sparsePaths with no cleanup step. NOT a product difference either: this is neither a subscription-flow drop, a gateway change, nor a rename (the rename here is the worktree location, `.nessy-worktrees/<repo>/<leaseId>` instead of `.claude/worktrees/`, which is unrelated to the config entry). Root cause is the repo's own named failure mode -- an upstream contract change we did not catch up with: the doc dates the cleanup to Claude Code v2.1.207, and our own R2 doc-verification snapshot from 2026-07-26 (2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:126) quotes only the older 'git enables extensions.worktreeConfig' half, with no removal sentence.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as claimed, with three refinements. (a) The divergence is gated on an opt-in setting: `worktree.sparsePaths` defaults to `[]` (WORKTREE_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, worktree-settings.ts:71-76), and worktreeCreateCommands returns early with no sparse-set when the list is empty (worktree-git-plan.ts:84), so an unconfigured user never triggers it. It reproduces for any user who sets `worktree.sparsePaths` in config.json (read live per operation via getUserWorktreeSettings, SessionManager.ts:10116; parsed at storage.ts:1313). (b) The consequence is measured, not inferred: on git 2.43.0 our exact argv writes `[extensions] worktreeConfig = true` into the shared `.git/config`, and removing the last worktree leaves it -- git does not clean it up, so the doc's go-git failure state persists in the user's main checkout after Nessy is done. (c) Closing it needs three parts our code has none of, matching the doc's 'only if Claude Code added it' carve-out: read `extensions.worktreeConfig` before the first sparse-set and record whether we enabled it, count remaining worktrees at remove time, and `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig` only when we own it and the count reaches zero -- with the added wrinkle that Nessy leases are per-session under one shared namespace root, so 'last worktree' must be computed across sessions (via `git worktree list`), not per WorktreeLeaseService instance.

And the managed-settings channel the finding says cannot work is exactly the one the CLI keeps open unconditionally: its allowed-source resolver is `function $D(){let e=Qgt();...let t=new Set(e);t.add('flagSettings'),t.add('policySettings');...}` -- policySettings is added on top of whatever settingSources we pass, and `kbe('policySettings')` resolves to `join(RR(),'managed-settings.json')` where RR() is '/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode' (plus a managed-settings.d drop-in dir), a system path untouched by our per-Workspace CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR redirect (options.ts:195-255, which only moves the 'user' scope). (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE ON THE SUBSYSTEM THIS PAGE GOVERNS. llm-gateway-connect.md is a Claude Code page, so in this fork it governs the Claude Agent SDK backend, and every seam the helper needs is open there, deliberately: the native binary is staged into the packaged app (scripts/build/common.ts:337-376 `copySDK`, apps/electron/scripts/build-dmg.sh:165-193, build-linux.sh:127-148, build-win.ps1:182-210), gated on NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE - the same flag that turns the Claude provider on at all, so whenever the page's subject exists the helper runtime ships with it; buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions passes `settingSources: ['user','project','local']` explicitly (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305), so an `apiKeyHelper` entry in .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json or the per-Workspace user scope under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:220-255) is read; buildClaudeSubprocessEnv (options.ts:236-263) spreads the entire host process.env and deletes only three Bedrock keys, so CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS propagates unmodified - 'no helper-TTL setting' is true of our source and false of our runtime; and addClaudePermissionRules (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts:118-164, `const next = { ...document, permissions }`) merge-preserves unknown keys, so nothing we write strips the entry. WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the mirror trap: the finding's 'our state' measures the dp/Nestor corporate-gateway path (the `dp` binary, ~/.nessy/dp_auth_creds.json, and 'a custom endpoint' - which in this fork means providerType `pi_compat`/`codex-runtime` with authType `api_key_with_endpoint`, per isValidProviderAuthCombination at packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:796-810). verdict.correctedState:
apiKeyHelper is shipped and reachable on the surface this page governs; what is actually true is a much narrower precedence point, and it is Claude's own documented precedence rather than a missing mechanism.

SHIPPED: the native Claude Agent SDK binary implements apiKeyHelper and CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS (46 and 7 occurrences respectively in node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude; 1 and 0 in the JS core), and it is staged into the packaged app by scripts/build/common.ts:337-376 and the three platform build scripts, under the NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE flag that also gates the Claude provider itself. Also correct the framing: the dp/Nestor path and 'custom endpoint' (pi_compat / codex-runtime, api_key_with_endpoint) are the Pi and Codex backends, the fork's deliberate corporate-gateway product difference, and are outside this page's scope. Context :361-:386 confirms the framing (nonessential traffic 'to Anthropic and to third-party services such as GitHub: version checks, telemetry, error reports, release notes'). So the finding is not refuted on the quote. (2) CITED LINES: apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts:127 is 'autoUpdater.autoDownload = true' and :130 is 'autoUpdater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = true', both module-level and unconditional, and 'grep -ain' over that file finds no env/config gate (its only process.env read is LOCALAPPDATA at :47). Literally correct. BUT :127 is a dead default and cannot be the mechanism: checkForUpdates() saves previousAutoDownload (:333), overwrites autoUpdater.autoDownload with the option (:334) and restores it in finally (:369), and all four production call sites pass an explicit {autoDownload: true} (auto-update.ts:448, menu.ts:75, menu.ts:200, handlers/system.ts:274). Also a sibling-subsystem mismatch: the doc governs the Claude Code CLI's self-update via npm/native installer, ours is electron-updater swapping an app bundle. (4) ALREADY REGISTERED, twice. The page-contract half is admitted by the finding itself: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:319 records that CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC has no reader anywhere ('grep -rain DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC' over the repo, excluding node_modules/.git/dist, returns only doc files - zero source readers, confirmed). Managed policy carries requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion (managed-policy.ts:386-398) but no update kill switch, so the gap is real - it is just already booked elsewhere and mis-attributed here.

results.claim: When a gateway enforces an output limit below the model's, the remediation is a client-side output cap via `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`.

results.ourState: No equivalent under any spelling. `grep -rain "MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS|maxOutputTokens" packages apps` returns only error-code strings and two comments that explicitly say the field is dropped as "capacity, not consumption". There is no way to cap requested output tokens below a gateway model's limit.
results.evidence: packages/core/src/types/message.ts:464 and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:94 — the only hits, both dropping the field

verdict.why: 1) QUOTE: exists verbatim, but only inside one troubleshooting-table cell (llm-gateway-connect.md line 500), and the whole line reframes it. The row's trigger is a gateway enforcing a smaller CONTEXT WINDOW ('400 errors stating a context or token limit ... ContextWindowExceededError or prompt token count of N exceeds the limit of M'); the remediation is '/compact' plus CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, and 'Also set CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS below the gateway model's output limit' is the trailing clause of that same cell. The claimed BEHAVIOUR ('when a gateway enforces an output limit below the model's, the remediation is a client-side output cap') detaches the tail clause from the row it belongs to. 2) EVIDENCE: wrong subsystem, and one wrong line. packages/core/src/types/message.ts:464 is 'export type CostReporting = ...'; the comment is at :477, and both it and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/claude/event-adapter.ts:94 are the PERSISTED USAGE TELEMETRY projection (ModelUsage -> PersistedModelUsage), explaining why the SDK's REPORTED maxOutputTokens capacity figure is not summed across turns. That is accounting, not a request parameter; the two hits neither support nor bear on an output cap. Sibling-subsystem confusion of exactly the shape AGENTS.md warns about. 3) CONSEQUENCE ('there is no way to cap requested output tokens'): false one layer up, on the very backend the doc page governs. packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-264 buildClaudeSubprocessEnv builds the Claude runtime's env as {...process.env, ...proxy, ...overrides} and deletes exactly three vars (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL); pi-agent.ts:1465 likewise spreads ...process.env. CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS therefore reaches the bundled Claude runtime unstripped, and that runtime implements it: positive control, `strings node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` contains 'output token maximum. To configure this behavior, set the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable.' (5 further occurrences of the bare name). The documented remediation works today on the Claude backend with no fork-side code at all. 4) 'No equivalent under any spelling' is a sweep artifact: only MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS/maxOutputTokens were grepped. This repo's spelling for a requested output cap is maxTokens - claude-agent.ts:3150 forwards request.maxTokens into the SDK query, codex-agent.ts:580 sends `max_tokens: request.maxTokens ?? 4096`, llm-tool.ts:587 exposes maxTokens (1..64000) to the model, and packages/pi-agent-server/src/custom-endpoint-models.ts:67 hard-caps `maxTokens: 8_192` on every custom/gateway endpoint model definition (buildCustomEndpointModelDef, called from pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1181). So a client-side output cap below the gateway model's limit demonstrably exists on the gateway path; it is fixed at 8k rather than absent. 5) The sibling half of the SAME doc cell is implemented under the fork's rename convention: packages/shared/src/config/auto-compaction-settings.ts:34-45 resolves NESSY_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, NESSY_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE and DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT (mirror mandated by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-compaction-parity.md:82). Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none concerns token budgets).
verdict.correctedState: Narrow, tunability-only gap - not the absence claimed. results.claim: The gateway model-list request must not follow redirects; a redirect is a failure specifically so the credential is not forwarded to the redirect target.
results.quote: The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target.
results.ourState: Both model-list fetches use bare `fetch(url, { headers })` with no `redirect` option, so the WHATWG default `"follow"` applies. The Nessy Gateway fetch carries the user's JWT in the custom header `Nestor-Token`, and the fetch spec strips only `Authorization`/`Cookie`/`Proxy-Authorization` across an origin change — a custom header rides the redirect intact. The Anthropic-format fetch has the same shape with `x-api-key`. A gateway (or a captive proxy in front of one) that answers `/v1/models` with a 30x hands the credential to whatever host it names.

verdict.why: Tried to refute on all four available grounds and none held for the live half. (1) QUOTE: verbatim. llm-gateway-protocol.md line 157 begins exactly 'The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential can't leak to a redirect target.' The whole line was read: the second sentence ('A gateway that responds slowly or redirects /v1/models, even http to https, fails discovery silently; serve the endpoint directly at the configured base URL') reinforces the conclusion rather than reversing it. (2) CODE: both cited lines say what was claimed. packages/server-core/src/model-fetchers/nestor.ts:41-42 is `await fetch(NESTOR_MODELS_URL, { headers: { 'Nestor-Token': credentials.apiKey ?? '' } })` and packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts:50 is `await fetch(`${baseUrl}/v1/models?${params}`, { headers })` — no `redirect` option on either, so the WHATWG default 'follow' applies. (3) LAYER UP: nothing mitigates. The only global fetch wrapper is packages/shared/src/config/network-runtime.ts:236-265, which fills in `proxy` and `tls` only and never touches `redirect`; apps/electron/src/main/network-proxy.ts installs an undici dispatcher with no maxRedirections (and fetch-layer redirects are handled above the dispatcher anyway); packages/shared/src/config/network-address-guard.ts is the sibling subsystem (Monitor ws targets and mcp-pool.ts:488), never reached by a model fetch; `Response.redirected` is read nowhere in the repo (grep -a, three hits, all unrelated test doubles named `redirected`). (4) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier with a positive control: two local HTTP servers on different ports, the first answering 302 to the second. Node v24.4.1/undici and Bun 1.3.14 behave identically — the redirect target receives `nestor-token` and `x-api-key` while `authorization` and `cookie` are stripped, and `redirect: 'error'` prevents the second request from being made at all. So the credential-forwarding mechanism is real in both runtimes this code runs on. LIVE PATH: the Nestor fetch is the default-on Nessy Gateway provider and runs at startup and on the 60-minute refresh (model-fetchers/index.ts:86-101, registry.ts:26 reuses it for codex-runtime). Checked the escape hatches and they do not apply: inert-worklist §3's nine dated owner decisions (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) contain nothing about redirects or model fetches; and this is not a rebrand/subscription product difference — the endpoint shape is Nessy-specific but the no-redirect hardening is orthogonal to branding. The finding survives, but its scope is materially overstated on the Anthropic half and its attacker model is overstated on the Nestor half; see correctedState.
verdict.correctedState: CONFIRMED for the Nestor path, OVERSTATED elsewhere. Corrections: (a) 'Both model-list fetches' undercounts and mislabels the population — the repo has four /v1/models-shaped call sites, and only the two cited carry a redirect-surviving credential. agent/diagnostics.ts:162 sends no credential at all (HEAD, unauthenticated reachability probe) and drivers/pi.ts:264 (testOpenAiCompatible) sends `Authorization: Bearer`, which the measured probe shows IS stripped on a cross-origin redirect. (b) The Anthropic half is not reachable in a shipped default build. fetchBackendModels (agent/backend/factory.ts:430) throws CLAUDE_DISABLED_ERROR when provider === 'anthropic' && !isProviderEnabled('claude'), and PROVIDER_FLAG_DEFAULTS.claude is false (feature-flags.ts:129). Even under NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1, providerType 'anthropic' is the direct-API path: resolveSetupTestConnectionHint (factory.ts:415) returns 'pi_compat' whenever a baseUrl is present, so anthropic.ts:50 normally targets https://api.anthropic.com and there is no gateway in front of it to emit the 30x. (c) On the Nestor path NESTOR_MODELS_URL is a hardcoded constant (nestor.ts:10, https://code-completion-nestor.tcsbank.ru/api/v1/cli/models), never connection.baseUrl, so the 30x can only come from the corporate gateway itself or from a TLS-terminating proxy the operator already trusted via certStore/tlsCaPath — both of which already hold the JWT in the request they answered. 'A gateway (or a captive proxy in front of one) ... hands the credential to whatever host it names' overstates the attacker model: the exposure the doc actually closes is a trusted-but-compromised or misconfigured gateway forwarding the JWT to a THIRD host, which is real and currently open. Also note the Nestor request matches none of the documented request shape (path is /api/v1/cli/models not /v1/models, no limit=1000, and no timeout at all — the Anthropic-format fetch has a 30s outer budget, the Nestor one has none), because it is Nessy's own corporate-gateway REST endpoint returning a bare NestorModel[] rather than Claude Code's Anthropic-Messages discovery returning {data:[...]}; only the no-redirect hardening transfers. Fix is one line at each site: `redirect: 'error'` on nestor.ts:41 and anthropic.ts:50.

results.claim: Discovery keeps every entry whose `id` begins with `claude` **or** `anthropic`.
results.quote: Claude Code reads `id` and the optional `display_name` from each entry in the response's `data` array, and ignores entries whose `id` doesn't begin with `claude` or `anthropic`:
results.ourState: Our Anthropic-format discovery filter is `m.id.startsWith('claude-')` only — no `anthropic` branch, and it additionally requires the hyphen. The two dominant LLM-gateway products namespace Anthropic models as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (LiteLLM, OpenRouter) or `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6-v1:0` (Bedrock-proxying gateways); every such id is dropped, so the picker comes back empty against a gateway whose model list Claude Code would populate. Path ships only in `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1` builds.

verdict.why: Doc sentence verbatim: YES, line 166 of llm-gateway-protocol.md; the rest of the line does not reverse it. Cited line accurate: YES, packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/drivers/anthropic.ts:76 is `.filter(m => m.id.startsWith('claude-') && !m.id.startsWith('claude-2') && !m.id.startsWith('claude-instant') && !m.id.startsWith('claude-1'))`. The CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is the inert-worklist section 4 shape #3/#4 (enforcement one layer up + wrong sibling subsystem named). (1) Wrong subsystem. The doc's section is Claude Code CLI's opt-in gateway model discovery: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`, off by default, `GET /v1/models?limit=1000`, 3s timeout, redirects treated as failure, cached to `~/.claude/cache/gateway-models.json`, feeding the CLI's `/model` picker. That feature does not exist in the fork at all -- `grep -ran GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY` over the repo returns one docs line and zero code. `anthropicDriver.fetchModels` is a different mechanism: Nessy's own catalog refresh for the app's model list, always on, paginated `limit=100` + `after_id`, no 3s timeout, no redirect ban, no gateway-models.json cache. (2) The claimed failure path is unreachable. A `providerType: 'anthropic'` connection never carries a gateway baseUrl by construction: `createBuiltInConnection('anthropic-api', baseUrl)` returns `pi_compat` (server-core/src/domain/connection-setup-logic.ts:142), pinned by two tests (apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/connection-setup-logic.test.ts:83-88 and server-core/src/domain/connection-setup-logic.test.ts:165); the SETUP handler flips an existing anthropic api_key connection to `pi_compat` + `customEndpoint: {api:'anthropic-messages'}` the moment a baseUrl is set and back to `anthropic` when it is cleared (server-core/src/handlers/rpc/llm-connections.ts:78-89); and `resolveSetupTestConnectionHint` returns `pi_compat` whenever a baseUrl is present (shared/src/agent/backend/factory.ts:415). So every gateway connection routes to `piDriver.fetchModels` (drivers/pi.ts:311-333), which never calls `/v1/models` and applies no `claude-` prefix filter. (3) The picker does not come back empty: the setup UI REQUIRES a declared model list for a custom endpoint -- 'Default model is required for custom endpoints.' (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/apisetup/ApiKeyInput.tsx:441-445) -- and the pi_compat picker is populated from those user-declared models. (4) The fork is not blind to the namespaced ids the claim cites: `isClaudeModel` (shared/src/config/models.ts:345-347) matches `anthropic/claude-...` (OpenRouter/LiteLLM) and `anthropic.claude-...` (Bedrock) explicitly, and `isBareBedrockClaudeModel` (shared/src/config/models-pi.ts:98) handles the Bedrock form on the Pi path. Both namespaces are handled -- just in the sibling subsystem the finding named wrongly. verdict.why: Quote verified verbatim at prompt-caching.md:237, second sentence of a two-sentence line ('Disabling caching is occasionally useful when debugging caching behavior with a specific model or provider. To turn it off, set one of these environment variables to `1`:'), table at :241-245, plus :247 on the managed-settings `env` block. The identifier half of the finding is true — no file we own reads DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING or its four family variants, and the only Nessy-side knob is `extendedPromptCache` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:134), which the interceptor uses to upgrade or strip a TTL (packages/shared/src/unified-network-interceptor.ts:368 stripPromptCacheTtl, :437 upgradePromptCacheTtl) and never to remove a breakpoint. But the CONSEQUENCE — 'there is no way to disable caching for a model or provider while debugging' — is false, and it is the classic 'unwired identifier, handled one layer up' shape. These are the upstream Claude runtime's own env vars, and we ship that runtime: `strings -a node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` contains 19 occurrences of DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING — six bare, six each of _HAIKU/_SONNET/_OPUS/_FABLE, plus three of an undocumented _MYTHOS (positive control on the same dump: ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, 4 hits; an earlier zero-hit run was a false negative from macOS lacking `timeout`). results.ourState: Our counterpart is a single boolean, `extendedPromptCache` (default `false`), reachable only through the desktop Settings → AI toggle and its RPC pair. Neither env spelling is read, so there is no local override of a policy-delivered value and no way to set the TTL on the headless server or in CI. The auto-selection half of this section is already registered (deviation-register.md:406); the two override variables are not.

verdict.why: The quote is verbatim (prompt-caching.md:204, whole line: 'Set `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` to force the five-minute TTL regardless of authentication. This is useful when you're debugging cache behavior, comparing the two TTLs, or overriding an `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` set in managed settings.'). The identifier half of the finding also holds: a NUL-safe `grep -ra 'FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M|ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H' packages apps scripts` returns zero hits. But BOTH stated consequences are false, which is the classic 'identifier unwired, consequence already handled one layer up' shape. (1) 'No local override of a policy-delivered value' is wrong: `extendedPromptCache: false` is not a passive default, it is an ACTIVE force-5m. `upgradePromptCacheTtl` (unified-network-interceptor.ts:437) opens with `if (!isExtendedPromptCacheEnabled()) return stripPromptCacheTtl(body)`, and `stripPromptCacheTtl` (:367-414) deletes `ttl` from every ephemeral `cache_control` block in tools, system, message content and top-level. Its own comment names the exact scenario the doc names: 'When extendedPromptCache is disabled, the SDK may still send ttl: "1h" natively (via prompt-caching-scope beta). This function removes the ttl field so blocks fall back to the API default (5 min).' It is called unconditionally from the Anthropic provider's `modifyRequest` (:978), i.e. on the wire, DOWNSTREAM of the SDK -- so it overrides whatever the SDK chose from authentication or from an inherited env var, which is strictly more authoritative than `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M`, and it is the default. The doc's stated purpose (overriding a managed-settings `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`) is therefore already satisfied: an unclassified key in a managed `env` block lands in `process.env` as category `immediate` (config/managed-env.ts) and is inherited by the SDK subprocess, and our strip removes the resulting 1h TTL anyway. `extendedPromptCache` itself is a per-user config.json key that no managed-policy path writes, so there is nothing policy-delivered to be trapped by. (2) 'Reachable only through the desktop Settings -> AI toggle and its RPC pair ... no way to set the TTL on the headless server or in CI' is wrong twice over. It is a documented user-editable config.json key -- docs-site/content/reference/config/config-file.md:169 and the ru mirror :172 -- living at `CONFIG_DIR/config.json`, where `CONFIG_DIR` honours `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` (config/paths.ts:19-21). The consumer that applies the TTL is the interceptor inside the SDK subprocess, which reads that file straight off disk with a 100 ms cache (interceptor-common.ts:104-114) and never touches the renderer or the RPC layer; the repo's own suite drives both branches by writing the key into config.json (unified-network-interceptor.schema.test.ts:156,163), which is the CI recipe the finding says does not exist. And the RPC pair is registered in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/settings.ts:401,407 -- the HEADLESS server's own handler table, allow-listed for remote at protocol/routing.ts:166-167; apps/electron/src/transport/channel-map.ts:358-359 is a client of it, not its owner. So the RPC pair is a headless-server surface, not a desktop-only one. Context that makes this naming rather than behaviour: this fork replaces CLAUDE_*/ANTHROPIC_* env knobs with config.json keys under `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` repo-wide, and the same sweep already reached that conclusion for this exact knob on another page -- 2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3361: '`1h` prompt-cache TTL exists under our own `extendedPromptCache` config key rather than `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` ... env-var naming, not a behaviour gap.' f197 contradicts it. The finding is nevertheless refuted on subsystem and product-scope grounds. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM - the sibling-symbol trap. The quoted line sits under '## Mobile push notifications' on the Remote Control page and governs pushes delivered to your PHONE via the Claude mobile app while a Remote Control session runs on your machine. CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE exists precisely BECAUSE the delivery target is a second device: the CLI cannot otherwise tell whether you are at your desk in another window. Our `deliverModelNotification` (the claim names it `showAgentNotification`, which has 0 hits repo-wide) is the desktop-shell backend of the `PushNotification` TOOL, cited to `tools-reference.md:41` and described in packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:628 as 'Raise an OS notification on the user's desktop'. It is an Electron Notification on the SAME machine, reached via packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/push-notification.ts -> deliverDesktopNotification. Read the whole line: the doc's own recommended wiring is 'create the file when your screen unlocks and delete it when your screen locks'. Importing the gate would be a defect, not parity. (3) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. Remote Control requires 'Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. verdict.correctedState: Our PushNotification path is a LOCAL desktop notification on the machine hosting the session, not a cross-device mobile push. `deliverModelNotification` (apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:100; the finding's `showAgentNotification` does not exist) gates on window focus, the notifications setting, and platform support, and reads no presence-marker file - correctly, because CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE answers 'is the human at the host machine', a question that only matters when the notification travels to a second device. results.claim: A settings key `autoUpdatesChannel` selects the release channel for auto-updates, defaulting to `latest`, with `stable` as the other value.

The finding still fails on all three of the remaining checks. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM / deliberate product difference. `autoUpdatesChannel` governs the Claude Code CLI's own self-updater: the native installer's `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` tree, `claude update`, npm-global installs, Homebrew cask names (`claude-code` vs `claude-code@latest`), `minimumVersion`, `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` -- the whole surrounding section of setup.md is about that mechanism.
