results.quote: The `minimumVersion` setting establishes a floor.
results.ourState: Not implemented. Our managed-settings version gate implements only the start-up range check (`requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion`); nothing constrains what the updater is allowed to install.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/config/managed-version-gate.ts:92-93 (only the two required* keys); `grep -rain minimumVersion` finds no `minimumVersion` reader distinct from those

verdict.why: Quote is real and the cited line is accurate, but the CONSEQUENCE is false. (1) setup.md:246 reads verbatim 'The `minimumVersion` setting establishes a floor.' and the rest of that two-sentence line plus :260 support the claimed behaviour, so the finding is not refuted on the quote. (2) packages/shared/src/config/managed-version-gate.ts:89-94 does declare only requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion, and `grep -an minimumVersion` over packages/*/src apps/*/src scripts returns exactly one hit -- a doc-quote comment at managed-version-gate.ts:12 that itself names the distinction ('Differs from `minimumVersion`, which prevents downgrades but never blocks startup'). So the identifier really is unwired. (3) But 'nothing constrains what the updater is allowed to install' is wrong. Our updater is electron-updater (apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts). Its allowDowngrade defaults to false (node_modules/electron-updater/out/AppUpdater.js:138) and isUpdateAvailable returns true only when gt(latest,current), otherwise `allowDowngrade && lt(...)` -> false (AppUpdater.js:356-362). Nothing in our source sets allowDowngrade, allowPrerelease, or autoUpdater.channel -- the channel setter is the one thing that would flip allowDowngrade to true (AppUpdater.js:33-45) -- verified with grep -an over apps/electron/src, packages/*/src, apps/cli/src (zero hits). Both the background check and the manual 'Check Now' go through the same gate (checkForUpdates at auto-update.ts:327-370 calls autoUpdater.checkForUpdates), and installUpdate() (:381) only ever installs what that gate accepted. The floor therefore exists: it is the running version, enforced by construction instead of by a settings key. Layer up: the mechanism Claude's minimumVersion exists to guard -- a runtime 'latest' -> 'stable' switch that would downgrade you (setup.md:246, :248) -- has no analogue here. The channel is baked into the artifact at build time (apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:80 `channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"`, set at .gitlab-ci.yml:235); there is no autoUpdatesChannel setting, no /config channel switch, and no `claude update`-equivalent manual installer (apps/cli has no self-update path). Layer down: the residual capability -- an admin-pinned floor ABOVE the running version -- is what the IMPLEMENTED requiredMinimumVersion startup gate already delivers, by refusing to start below the org minimum; the doc itself (setup.md:261) points admins at exactly those two keys for enforcement. Product difference: setup.md is CLI-installation surface (npm/native installer, Homebrew, WinGet, apt/dnf/apk, `claude update`, ~/.claude/settings.json autoUpdatesChannel); this fork ships a signed Electron .dmg/NSIS/AppImage from a corporate S3/R2 feed (scripts/prepare-release-assets.mjs, scripts/verify-update-feed.mjs), and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:268 already records row 152 `setup` as out of product. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 -- none of those nine touches update/version gating -- but the coverage-map verdict is a recorded scope decision for this page.
verdict.correctedState: Partially implemented by a different mechanism, and the stated consequence does not hold. Our managed-settings version gate (packages/shared/src/config/managed-version-gate.ts) implements only the start-up range check (requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion), and no key named minimumVersion is read anywhere. However, the updater is NOT unconstrained: apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts drives electron-updater with allowDowngrade left at its false default and autoUpdater.channel never set at runtime, so isUpdateAvailable only accepts a feed version strictly greater than the running one -- both the background check and the manual check refuse to install anything below the current build. The release channel is a build-time property of the artifact (electron-builder.yml:80 / .gitlab-ci.yml:235), so the runtime channel switch that Claude's minimumVersion exists to protect against does not exist here. The only genuinely absent capability is an admin-configurable floor ABOVE the running version, and the implemented requiredMinimumVersion startup gate already covers the org-enforcement half of it.

results.claim: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER stops the background update check, and DISABLE_UPDATES blocks every update path — the documented control for organizations distributing the app through their own channel.
results.quote: `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` only stops the background check; `claude update` and `claude install` still work. To block all update paths, including manual updates, set [`DISABLE_UPDATES`](/docs/en/env-vars) instead.
results.ourState: Neither flag, nor a Nessy-prefixed equivalent, is read. Auto-download and install-on-quit are hardcoded on; the only `process.env` read in the updater is `LOCALAPPDATA` for a cache path. A corporate deployment cannot pin users to a distributed version.
results.evidence: apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts:127 and :130 (unconditional), :47 (sole env read); `grep -rain -e DISABLE_UPDATE -e DISABLE_AUTOUPDAT --include='*.ts' packages apps scripts` returns 0 hits

verdict.why: (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: CONFIRMED. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.md puts the sentence at line 275, byte-identical. Read the WHOLE line: it is three sentences, not two, and the uncited third reinforces rather than reverses -- 'Use this when you distribute Claude Code through your own channels and need users to stay on the version you provide.' Section context (:263 '### Disable auto-updates', :265-273 the settings.json env block) confirms the reading. But that third sentence is also what breaks the finding, because it names the exact deployment posture this fork already occupies. (2) CITED LINES: partially confirmed, with one dead line. auto-update.ts:130 `autoUpdater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = true` is genuinely an unconditional module-level assignment. auto-update.ts:47 is indeed the sole `process.env` read (`process.env.LOCALAPPDATA` in getUpdateCacheDir). But auto-update.ts:127 `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` is a DEAD default: checkForUpdates() overwrites it at :334 from its own parameter and restores the previous value at :369 on every single check, and all four call sites pass an explicit `{autoDownload: true}` (auto-update.ts:448, menu.ts:75, menu.ts:200, handlers/system.ts:274). Deleting :127 changes nothing. The grep is accurate -- `grep -rain -e DISABLE_UPDATE -e DISABLE_AUTOUPDAT --include='*.ts' packages apps scripts` returns 0, and a repo-wide `grep -ain` across ts/tsx/json/md/mjs/js/yml finds the strings only inside this sweep's own artefacts. So the IDENTIFIER half of the claim is true. (3) LAYER UP AND DOWN -- the CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier, is FALSE, on two independent grounds. LAYER UP: there is no vendor-run update feed to opt out of. apps/electron/electron-builder.yml:77-80 sets `publish: {provider: generic, url: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL}", channel: "${env.NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL}"}`, injected at build time from the deploying organisation's own CI secret (.gitlab-ci.yml:234-235, `export NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL="$NESSY_DESKTOP_DEV_UPDATE_URL"`; apps/electron/README.md:79 shows the same knob for local rehearsal). In Claude Code, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER/DISABLE_UPDATES exist because Anthropic runs the feed and the redistributing org does not -- the flags are how the org takes the vendor's updater out of the loop. Here the premise is inverted: the organisation that deploys Nessy Desktop is the organisation that builds it (AGENTS.md: internal desktop-agent fork rebranded for T-Bank), and it already decides which version every user can reach by controlling what it publishes to its own feed. A build with no URL has no working provider at all (GenericProvider.js:12 passes configuration.url straight to newBaseUrl). So the claimed harm -- 'A corporate deployment cannot pin users to a distributed version' -- is false; pinning is the fork's structural default, achieved by the mechanism the quoted third sentence prescribes rather than by an env flag. Also relevant one layer up: the launch probe is gated on `app.isPackaged` (index.ts:1259-1265, else-branch logs '[auto-update] Skipping auto-update in dev mode'), so even 'hardcoded on' is not literally unconditional. LAYER DOWN / SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: DISABLE_UPDATES is distinguished from DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER by exactly one thing -- blocking the MANUAL paths `claude update` and `claude install`, i.e. the native installer that manages ~/.local/bin/claude as a symlink into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ (setup.md:205, :277-293). Nessy Desktop has no native installer, no versions/ directory and no self-update subcommand: apps/cli/src/index.ts parses only flags (--url, --token, --model, --version, ...) with no `update` or `install` verb, and `grep -rain -e self-update -e selfUpdate apps/cli/src` returns nothing. The entire reason the second flag exists as a separate flag has no counterpart to diverge from. Measuring a CLI-installer two-flag contract against an Electron electron-updater subsystem is the sibling-subsystem error this series warns about. (4) NOT an inert-worklist section 3 owner decision -- the nine are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions; none is this. (5) It IS partly a deliberate product difference: desktop Electron app with a build-time-injected generic feed vs a self-updating CLI binary. Refuted on the consequence, not on the identifier.
verdict.correctedState: Neither `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` nor `DISABLE_UPDATES` nor a NESSY_-prefixed runtime equivalent is read -- that part is accurate (0 hits repo-wide with `grep -a`). Three corrections to the rest. (a) The evidence line is wrong: auto-update.ts:127 `autoUpdater.autoDownload = true` is a dead default, overwritten at :334 and restored at :369 on every check while all four call sites pass an explicit `{autoDownload: true}` (auto-update.ts:448, menu.ts:75, menu.ts:200, handlers/system.ts:274); the only operative unconditional assignment is :130 (`autoInstallOnAppQuit`), and the launch probe itself is gated on `app.isPackaged` at index.ts:1259. (b) The claimed harm is false. Update behaviour IS organisation-controlled here, just at build time rather than runtime: electron-builder.yml:77-80 bakes `publish.provider: generic` with `url`/`channel` from `NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_URL` / `NESSY_DESKTOP_UPDATE_CHANNEL`, supplied by the deploying org's own CI (.gitlab-ci.yml:234-235). There is no Anthropic-equivalent vendor feed to opt out of -- the org that ships the build owns the feed and pins users by controlling what it publishes to it, which is exactly the 'distribute through your own channels' posture the quoted sentence's third clause prescribes. (c) `DISABLE_UPDATES`'s distinguishing purpose -- blocking `claude update` / `claude install` and the native installer under ~/.local/share/claude/versions/ -- has no analogue: apps/cli/src/index.ts exposes no `update` or `install` subcommand and nothing in this fork self-updates a CLI binary. The genuine residual, narrower than the finding as filed, is that a PACKAGED build has no runtime off switch: an admin cannot suppress the per-launch probe or the user-facing 'Check for Updates' menu item (menu.ts:75) and Settings 'Check Now' (AppSettingsPage.tsx:149) without a rebuild, and there is no settings toggle (the only `disabled` in that page is the in-flight spinner guard at :457). That residual overlaps f189 and f202, which cite the same two lines.

results.claim: A `statusLine` settings object with `type: "command"`, `command`, and optional `padding` (default 0), `refreshInterval` (minimum 1) and `hideVimModeIndicator` runs a shell command and pipes it a documented JSON session payload on stdin.
results.quote: Add a `statusLine` field to your user settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`, where `~` is your home directory) or [project settings](/docs/en/settings#settings-files).
results.ourState: No reader for the key at any scope. The only repo hits for the identifier are an unrelated markdown-parsing local in the session store. A Claude plugin that ships `settings.json` is recorded as a deferred retained surface rather than having its keys interpreted, so a plugin-shipped statusLine is also inert.
results.evidence: `grep -rain -e '"statusLine"' -e "'statusLine'" -e 'statusLine:' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.json' packages apps` → 0; nearest hit packages/shared/src/sessions/storage.ts:901 is an unrelated local; plugin settings deferral at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding; it survives, with one sub-clause corrected. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md` puts the sentence at line 44, character for character. The whole line is three sentences and neither of the other two reverses anything: 'Set `type` to "command" and point `command` to a script path or an inline shell command. For a full walkthrough of creating a script, see [Build a status line step by step](#build-a-status-line-step-by-step).' The claimed behaviour is also fully supported by the page: :51 shows `padding`, :67 'The optional `padding` field ... Defaults to `0`', :69 'The optional `refreshInterval` field re-runs your command every N seconds ... The minimum is `1`', :71 `hideVimModeIndicator`, :137 'Claude Code runs your script and pipes JSON session data to it via stdin', and :169-198 enumerate the stdin payload. (2) CITED STATE ACCURATE. `grep -rain -e '"statusLine"' -e "'statusLine'" -e 'statusLine:' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.json' packages apps` returns 0 (re-run with -a, node_modules filtered). A wider case-insensitive `grep -rain statusline` over all source outside node_modules/.git/.references/docs returns exactly two lines, both the claimed unrelated local: packages/shared/src/sessions/storage.ts:901 `const statusLine = lines.find(l => l.startsWith('**Status:**'));` and :902, a plan-markdown parser. packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275 reads exactly `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }`, the last row of CLAUDE_RETAINED_SURFACE_FIELDS, consumed by addClaudeRetainedSurfaceDeferrals, which pushes a deferral row and interprets no keys. (3) ONE LAYER UP AND ONE DOWN BOTH HOLD. Nothing upstream honours it by another route: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:2994 states in shipped source 'we have no reader for `~/.claude/settings.json`', and the Claude backend actively moves that scope out of reach - packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:204-206 redirects CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per Workspace so 'a hand-written `~/.claude/settings.json` stops reaching the subprocess', called a deliberate isolation decision. The Claude Agent SDK subprocess we do spawn has no TUI, so it renders no status line either. Sibling-subsystem check: the only status-shaped surface in the fork is apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/ToolbarStatusSlot.tsx, a fixed priority overlay for the escape-to-interrupt hint and browser-session state - no user command, no stdin JSON, not configurable; apps/cli is a 'Terminal client for Nessy Desktop server' with no TUI footer (no ink, no footer renderer). So the consequence is true independently of the identifier. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries) - I read all nine. Not a rebrand, gateway or dropped-subscription product difference either. ONE CORRECTION, which does not overturn the row: the third sentence of the claimed our-state ('so a plugin-shipped statusLine is also inert') is not a divergence. plugins.md:298 says verbatim 'Plugins can include a `settings.json` file at the plugin root to apply default configuration when the plugin is enabled. Currently, only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys are supported.' - a top-level `statusLine` in a plugin's settings.json is ignored by Claude Code too, so our deferral of that file costs us `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` (f053, f206), not `statusLine`. ALSO NOTE FOR RANKING, NOT REFUTATION: this gap is already recorded twice. The parity audit, the source of truth, lists it at 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1720 under 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness ... keybindings, statusline, deep links', and the deviation register at :448 carries a 'not implemented' row noting Nessy has no third-party loader for the status line because it is not a capability kind. The coverage map already verdicts the page red, 'no surface'. Accurate and confirmed, but a known triaged no-row gap rather than a new defect.
verdict.correctedState: No reader for `statusLine` at any scope, and no status-line surface to read it into. `grep -rain` over packages/apps returns 0 hits for the settings key; the only source hits for the identifier are packages/shared/src/sessions/storage.ts:901-902, a plan-markdown parsing local. Nothing handles it one layer up: pi-agent.ts:2994 records that we have no reader for `~/.claude/settings.json` at all, and options.ts:204-206 deliberately redirects CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per Workspace so that scope does not even reach the Claude SDK subprocess (which, having no TUI, would render no status line regardless). The nearest sibling, ToolbarStatusSlot.tsx, is a fixed escape-hint/browser-state overlay, not a configurable command-driven line. Drop the finding's last clause: a plugin-shipped top-level `statusLine` is inert in Claude Code as well, since plugins.md:298 supports only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` in a plugin-root settings.json - our blanket settings deferral at format-adapters/claude.ts:2275 is a gap for those two keys, not for this one. Already triaged: parity audit :1720 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness', deviation register :448, coverage map verdict red/'no surface'.

results.claim: A `subagentStatusLine` settings object renders a custom row body per subagent, receives one JSON object with `columns` and a `tasks` array (id, name, type, status, description, label, startTime, model, effort, contextWindowSize, tokenCount, tokenSamples, cwd), and emits one `{"id":…,"content":…}` line per overridden row — and plugins may ship it as a default.
results.quote: The `subagentStatusLine` setting renders a custom row body for each [subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) shown in the agent panel below the prompt.
results.ourState: Identifier does not exist anywhere in the repo, including in the plugin adapter that imports Claude plugin bundles. We do ship subagents and an agent panel, so the row this would customize exists; the customization point does not.

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md gives a 1113-line page; the sentence is character-for-character line 1017 under '## Subagent status lines'. Reading the WHOLE line, its second sentence reinforces rather than reverses: 'Use it to replace the default `name - description - token count` row with your own formatting.' The rest of the section corroborates every element of the claim - :1029 'receives all visible subagent rows as a single JSON object on stdin ... a `columns` field with the usable row width, and a `tasks` array. Each task has `id`, `name`, `type`, `status`, `description`, `label`, `startTime`, `model`, `effort`, `contextWindowSize`, `tokenCount`, `tokenSamples`, and `cwd`.'; :1034 'Write one JSON line to stdout per row you want to override, in the form {"id": "<task id>", "content": "<row body>"}'; :1036 'Plugins can ship a default `subagentStatusLine` in their settings.json.' The only nuance the claim omits is harmless version gating (`model`/`contextWindowSize` need v2.1.205, `effort` needs v2.1.214). (2) OUR STATE. Absence re-verified with -a as required: `grep -rain subagentStatusLine .` excluding node_modules/.git/.references returns hits ONLY inside the sweep's own docs (docs/superpowers/specs/data/*.json and the divergence tables) - zero source hits in any .ts/.tsx/.js/.json under packages/, apps/ or scripts/. The plugin-shipped-default half is independently dead too: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275 carries { externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' } in CLAUDE_RETAINED_SURFACE_FIELDS, and addClaudeRetainedSurfaceDeferrals (:2278-2317) only existsSync-checks the file and pushes `plugin.deferred.claude_settings`; that row has no `refusal`, so a Claude plugin shipping a subagentStatusLine default installs with a plain success toast and does nothing (same mechanism as f053). (3) ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN. Sibling-subsystem check: the ONLY `statusLine` identifier in fork source is an unrelated local in packages/shared/src/sessions/storage.ts:901-902 parsing a markdown '**Status:**' line - the finding does not confuse the two, and no sibling subsystem implements the surface under another name. Consequence check, run separately from the identifier: the row this would customize genuinely exists - apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/AgentPanel.tsx (309 lines) renders SubagentCard.tsx, whose AgentRow (:88-122) draws exactly the documented row shape (agent.label, agent.agentType, status, elapsed, phase, formatTokens(totalTokens) with an in/out breakdown), and nothing anywhere lets a user or a plugin replace that body. Nothing upstream honours the setting by another route. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries). Not a deliberate product difference of the documented kind either: it has nothing to do with the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway or the rebrand, and importing Claude plugin bundles is a first-class supported surface here. What DOES need recording is that the gap is already known and deliberately un-rowed rather than newly discovered - see correctedState.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with two additions and no reversal. (a) NOT A NEW FINDING - it is already triaged in the source of truth: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1720 lists 'keybindings, statusline, deep links (claude-cli://)' under '**Minor, no row, listed for completeness**', and 2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md row 46 already verdicts the whole page RED ('1 sovpadenie, poverhnosti net'). results.claim: CLAUDE.md is deployable at an organization-wide tier from system directories, above the repository tier.
results.quote: **Organization-wide**: Deploy to system directories such as `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` (macOS), `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` (Linux and WSL), or `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` (Windows) for company-wide standards
results.ourState: Our context-file tiers are project-directory files (agents.md / claude.md / claude.local.md, scopes ent/project/local) plus one read-only user-global claude.md in the config directory. There is no system-directory tier, so an org cannot ship company-wide standards the way it already ships `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json` — the system tier exists for policy but not for memory.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:32-41 (CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS, CONTEXT_FILE_SCOPE_BY_PATTERN, CONTEXT_FILE_SCOPE_ORDER) and :36 (user-global tier); repo-wide grep for the three system paths or any `/etc/nessy/CLAUDE*` equivalent → 0 hits

verdict.why: All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: third-party-integrations.md:327 carries the sentence character-for-character, under '## Best practices for organizations' -> '### Invest in documentation and memory'. The whole line was read; it is a single-clause bullet with no reversing second half, and the sibling bullet ('Repository-level') plus the trailing 'Learn more in Memory and CLAUDE.md files' confirm this is a real tier list, not prose. Corroborated on a second page: memory.md:58 gives the tier its own row in the precedence table -- '| **Managed policy** | macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md; Linux and WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md; Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md | Organization-wide instructions managed by IT/DevOps | ... | All users in organization |' -- and repeats the three paths at :279-281. So it is a specified, highest-precedence memory tier, not a deployment suggestion. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:32 CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERNS = ['agents.md','claude.md','claude.local.md']; :37-41 CONTEXT_FILE_SCOPE_BY_PATTERN maps them to ent/project/local; :42-47 CONTEXT_FILE_SCOPE_ORDER = ent 0, project 1, user 2, local 3; :36 USER_GLOBAL_CONTEXT_FILE_PATTERN = 'claude.md', read from getUserGlobalContextDirectory() = join(homeDir, '.nessy-agent') (:136-138). Reads exactly as claimed. (3) ONE LAYER UP -- and this is where the finding could have died, but does not. The cited path is the LEGACY route: packages/shared/AGENTS.md records that buildVolatileContextParts skips the project-context-file block whenever the capability runtime is active, 'which is every normal send', and that instruction/memory layers ride BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext() instead. I therefore re-checked the LIVE route. capabilities/native-sources.ts:buildNativeCapabilityInventory has exactly three roots -- global (CONFIG_DIR = ~/.nessy-agent: skills, agents, mcp.json, hooks.json, MEMORY.md, rules/), workspace (context.workspaceRootPath), and project (trusted cwd, .nessy-agent/ + portable .claude/.agents tiers, PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES = ['AGENTS.md','CLAUDE.md','CLAUDE.local.md'] at :82). capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869 scopeSpecificity enumerates the entire scope vocabulary: project 3, workspace 2, global 1, builtin 0. There is no system/enterprise scope on either path, so the consequence survives on the live path as well as the legacy one. ONE LAYER DOWN: could an admin ship standards some other way? No. Managed policy is 34 keys (managed-policy.ts:501-533 MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS) and not one carries instruction, memory, systemPrompt or context content -- grep for those terms in managed-policy.ts returns zero. Force-enabling a plugin does not substitute either: 'instruction' and 'memory' are NATIVE_BINDING_KINDS only (resolver.ts:897-900); grep for 'instruction'/'memory' across packages/shared/src/plugins/ and format-adapters/ returns zero, so a plugin cannot contribute either kind. SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: the finding names the right one. The system-directory tier genuinely does exist in this fork, and only for policy -- managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52 returns '/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json' (darwin), '/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json' (linux), %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json (win32), pinned by managed-policy-loader.test.ts:99-101, plus a managed-policy.d/ drop-in dir at :62-67. A NUL-safe grep -a for Nessy/CLAUDE, nessy/CLAUDE, Nessy/AGENTS, Nessy/MEMORY across packages/ and apps/ returns 0 hits: those three system directories are read for one JSON policy file and nothing else. OWNER DECISION? results.claim: CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH accepts four filenames — bash.exe, sh.exe, bash, or sh — and ignores any other name.
results.quote: Claude Code accepts only a file named `bash.exe`, `sh.exe`, `bash`, or `sh`; with any other name, such as Git for Windows' `git-bash.exe` launcher, it ignores the variable and auto-detects Git Bash as if it were unset, logging a warning visible with `--debug`.
results.ourState: Our validator accepts only `bash.exe` — the regex is anchored to that single name — and returns the hard error "Path must point to bash.exe" for anything else. A user who points at Git for Windows' `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe`, which the SDK we spawn would accept, is refused by our onboarding and by the persisted-path revalidation, which then clears the stored path. Strictly narrower than the documented enum on a value we write into the SDK's own env var.
results.evidence: packages/server-core/src/services/git-bash.ts:8 (`/(?:^|[\\/])bash\.exe$/i`) and :17-19 (refusal); consumed at packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:216, :224, :238, :272 where the value is assigned to process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH

verdict.why: Could not refute on any of the three axes. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install.md line 654 carries the quoted sentence character-for-character, prefixed by the MDX marker {/* min-version: 2.1.219 */}. Read whole: the remainder of the line is 'A path that doesn't exist gets the same fallback and warning. Before v2.1.219, Claude Code used any existing file as the shell without checking its name, and exited at startup with `Claude Code was unable to find CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH path` when the path didn't exist.' Nothing there reverses the conclusion; it only version-gates the four-name enum to >= 2.1.219. (2) CITED CODE: packages/server-core/src/services/git-bash.ts:8 is exactly /(?:^|[\\/])bash\.exe$/i and :18-19 returns {valid:false, error:'Path must point to bash.exe'}. Cited consumer line numbers are exact: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/system.ts:216, :224, :238 (auto-detect assignments) and :272 (SET_PATH assignment), with :219 clearGitBashPath() on a persisted path that fails revalidation. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN, and the CONSEQUENCE tested separately from the identifier. Layer down gave a positive control for the claim's load-bearing half ('which the SDK we spawn would accept'): the bundled consumer, node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.183, bridge.mjs, resolves the variable as `if(process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH){if(existsSync(...))return process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH; console.error(`Claude Code was unable to find CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH path "..."`),process.exit(1)}` — no filename test whatsoever, so it would accept C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe (and bash, and sh). Our gate is therefore narrower than the documented enum AND narrower than the consumer we actually ship. Layer up: the narrowing is reached on three independent paths, not one — the onboarding SET_PATH handler (system.ts:266), the RPC auto-detect (system.ts:213-219), and the startup revalidation at apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:596-604, which on failure calls clearGitBashPath() and deletes the env var; the same code is duplicated at apps/electron/src/main/handlers/system.ts:137-196. The Browse dialog (system.ts:250-263) filters to extensions:['exe'], so the extension-less `bash`/`sh` names cannot even be selected, and the auto-probe list is four hardcoded bash.exe paths. Sibling-subsystem check: rg over the repo finds no second, broader Git Bash validator; isGitBashExecutablePath/validateGitBashPath/isUsableGitBashPath have exactly these consumers plus one test. The narrowing is locked in by apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/git-bash.test.ts:21, which asserts isGitBashExecutablePath('/tmp/git/bin/sh.exe') === false. Not an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions — none is this, and grep for bash.exe/GIT_BASH across the parity audit and the deviation register returns no recorded ruling. Not a rebrand or dropped-subscription product difference either: CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH is written verbatim under Claude's own name for Claude's own subprocess, and the Git Bash onboarding step is not provider-gated. Only bound on the finding: practical exposure is limited to Windows hosts whose Git install is being pointed at by hand, and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE is off by default (though the SDK JS core always ships).
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed as filed, with one correction to the framing of the consumer. git-bash.ts:8 anchors on bash.exe alone and :19 hard-errors 'Path must point to bash.exe'; a Git for Windows sh.exe is refused by onboarding (system.ts:266-272), by auto-detect (system.ts:213-239) and by the startup revalidation (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:596-604), which additionally clears the persisted path. Split the fix accordingly: the existence half of validateGitBashPath is protective — it prevents the shipped SDK's hard exit and should stay — while the name half should widen to the documented enum (basename in {bash.exe, sh.exe, bash, sh}, case-insensitive), together with the auto-probe list, the Browse dialog's exe-only filter (which blocks the extension-less names outright), the error string, and the assertion at apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/git-bash.test.ts:21. results.claim: A user whose bundled ripgrep will not run can force Claude Code onto a system ripgrep with the `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` environment variable.
results.quote: Then set `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0` in your [environment](/docs/en/env-vars).
results.ourState: `resolveRipgrepPath` hard-resolves `node_modules/@vscode/ripgrep/bin/rg` through three fixed candidates (packaged app root, upward walk, cwd) and consults no environment variable. When none exists, `getRipgrepPath`/`searchSessions` throw `SearchUnavailableError` and session search is dead with no user-reachable recovery. `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP` has 0 hits repo-wide (checked with `grep -ra`, per the NUL-byte trap).

verdict.why: Quote is verbatim (troubleshooting.md:113), but the finding names the wrong subsystem and its consequence is false one layer up. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. The doc scopes the knob in its own section opener at :77 -- 'If the Search tool, `@file` mentions, custom agents, or custom skills aren't finding files' -- and the second half of the very line quoted confirms it: 'run `claude doctor` ... and check that the Search line'. All of those are the AGENT's file-discovery surfaces inside the Claude Code process. The cited `resolveRipgrepPath` (runtime-resolver.ts:442) feeds only `packages/server-core/src/services/search.ts` -> `searchSessions`, which is the desktop shell's session-HISTORY full-text search: it greps `-g '**/session.jsonl'` under the sessions dir for transcript text. Claude Code has no session-history search feature at all, so USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP was never its knob. This is exactly the disallowed-tools-for-subagents-vs-skills trap. (2) CONSEQUENCE FALSE UPSTREAM. For the surface the doc IS about, the fork already honours the variable, by inheritance rather than by code of ours. The Claude backend runs the real Claude Agent SDK subprocess, and `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-243) builds its env as `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides}` -- an open passthrough that deletes only three Bedrock vars (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL). A user who exports USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 before launching gets it into the SDK subprocess, which implements the documented switch. The repo states this design explicitly for a sibling SDK knob at claude-agent.ts:310-318: MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES 'reaches the subprocess by env inheritance -- deliberately NOT renamed on the Claude side (the Nessy Pi loop has its own NESSY_-prefixed knob)'. So 0 repo hits for USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP is the CORRECT state, not a gap: the variable belongs to the SDK we embed, and re-implementing it here would be the defect. (3) THE CITED CODE IS MISREAD. The claim of 'three fixed candidates ... and consults no environment variable' undercounts: lines 457-466 add a FOURTH, resolving system `rg` from PATH via which/where whenever `!hostRuntime.isPackaged` (headless server, dev mode) -- i.e. the non-packaged host already does what the doc asks, without a flag. The packaged exclusion is a stated deliberate decision in the same comment: 'Packaged apps must use vendored binary only -- never resolve from PATH to avoid picking up an incompatible system install.' (4) 'DEAD WITH NO USER-REACHABLE RECOVERY' IS OVERSTATED. SearchUnavailableError is caught in apps/electron/src/renderer/hooks/useSessionSearch.ts:352-357, which sets isSearchUnavailable; SessionList.tsx:723 forwards it and SessionSearchHeader.tsx:99 renders the localized `session.searchUnavailable` notice. Only CONTENT search degrades -- title/name filtering is a separate non-ripgrep path and keeps working -- and the failure is surfaced, not silent. Also checked: this is not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) -- it is refuted on subsystem and consequence, not on a recorded decision.
verdict.correctedState: No divergence. The documented recovery applies to the Claude Code agent's own file discovery (Search tool, @file, agents, skills), and the fork preserves it unchanged: `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:236-243) spreads `...process.env` into the Claude Agent SDK subprocess, stripping only three Bedrock routing vars, so an exported USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 reaches the SDK and takes effect. Zero repo hits is correct by design -- the same env-inheritance rule the repo records for MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES at claude-agent.ts:310-318. The cited `resolveRipgrepPath` (runtime-resolver.ts:442) serves a DIFFERENT, Nessy-only subsystem with no Claude Code counterpart: session-history full-text search over session.jsonl (server-core/src/services/search.ts). Even there the claim is inaccurate -- a fourth candidate at :457-466 resolves system `rg` from PATH for non-packaged hosts, packaged builds exclude PATH by a stated in-code decision, and failure surfaces to the user as `session.searchUnavailable` (SessionSearchHeader.tsx:99) while title search continues.

results.claim: `/heapdump` writes a heap snapshot plus a `-diagnostics.json` memory breakdown to `~/Desktop` (home directory on Linux without one).
results.quote: If memory usage stays high after these steps, run `/heapdump` to write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`.
results.ourState: No heapdump surface of any kind. The fork runs a long-lived Electron main process plus a Pi subprocess and offers no memory-diagnostic command, so a leaking session has no artifact to report with.
results.evidence: grep -ra heapdump packages apps scripts docs | grep -v node_modules  → no output

verdict.why: All three checks pass, so the finding survives. (1) Doc quote is VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshooting.md, line 39 reads in full: "If memory usage stays high after these steps, run `/heapdump` to write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`. On Linux without a Desktop folder, the files are written to your home directory." The second sentence of that two-sentence line does not reverse the claim - it is exactly the Linux fallback the claimed behaviour states. The following line (:41) supplies the rest of the claimed behaviour: "The breakdown shows resident set size, JS heap, array buffers, and unaccounted native memory ... the breakdown is the file ending in `-diagnostics.json`", plus a Warning block telling users to attach only the `-diagnostics.json` when reporting a memory issue. So `-diagnostics.json` is documented, not invented by the finding. (2) Absence confirmed with `grep -rai` (NUL-safe) across the whole repo excluding node_modules/.git/.references/.codegraph: the only hits for heapdump|heapsnapshot are this sweep's own artifacts (docs/superpowers/specs/data/*.json, the divergences .md/.tsv) and four vendored third-party Codex binaries under apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/. Zero hits in packages/, apps/*/src, scripts/. A wider search for the mechanism rather than the name - heapSnapshot, writeHeapSnapshot, node:v8, v8.getHeapStatistics, inspector - returns nothing in production source either, so the absence is of the capability, not just of the command name. (3) One layer up and one layer down, and the sibling-subsystem check: the near-miss surface is `process.memoryUsage()` in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/server.ts:58 (server:getStatus returns memory {heapUsed, heapTotal, rss}) and :124 (getHealthCheck's 1.5 GB heap check, reused by the RPC handler, the headless HTTP health endpoint at webui/http-server.ts:212 and packages/server/src/index.ts:292). The sibling diagnostic surface that DOES exist, apps/cli/src/doctor.ts, is deliberately scoped read-only to configuration (its docblock cites debug-your-config.md:46 and settings.md:208) and reports nothing about memory. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/foldSessionSummary) touches memory diagnostics. Not a deliberate product difference either: heapdump is not a subscription flow, not a gateway concern and not a rebrand, and unlike the same page's 200-row table cap and /terminal-setup it is not a terminal-renderer concern - a heap snapshot applies to any Node/Electron process, and this fork runs a long-lived Electron main plus a Pi subprocess, which is if anything a stronger case for it. The coverage map already scores the page consistently: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:175 marks `troubleshooting` red, traces but no implementation.
verdict.correctedState: No heapdump surface and no heap-snapshot capability anywhere in the fork: `grep -rai heapdump|heapsnapshot` over the repo hits only this sweep's own artifacts and vendored Codex binaries, and no production file imports node:v8/inspector or calls writeHeapSnapshot. The nearest thing that exists is process-level counters, not a dump: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/server.ts:58 returns memory {heapUsed, heapTotal, rss} on the server:getStatus RPC, and :124 adds a pass/fail heap check at 1.5 GB reused by server:getHealth and the headless HTTP health endpoint. results.claim: A `bin/` directory at the plugin root is added to the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled, making its executables invokable as bare commands.
results.quote: Place an executable in a bin/ directory at your plugin root and Claude Code adds that directory to the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled.
results.ourState: We detect `bin/` files and reason about which ones a manifest command already reaches, but we never extend the Bash tool's PATH from a bundle. An executable that no capability references by path is classified unrunnable and left deferred, so a plugin whose command/agent/hook invokes its helper as a bare name fails. The code states the deviation in its own comment.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2364 — "Nessy does not extend the Bash tool's PATH from a bundle, so an executable nothing else reaches really is unrunnable and stays deferred."

verdict.why: The doc sentence is verbatim (w14.md:107, first of a three-sentence lede) and the cited line exists verbatim (claude.ts:2364) -- but the claim quoted the PREMISE of a doc-comment whose later paragraph reverses it, the exact 'second half of the line reverses the conclusion' trap. claude.ts:2379-2385 continues: '**The PATH half IS built** (`appendPluginBinPath`, wired at `claude-agent.ts` and `pi-agent.ts`), so on both shipping backends a `bin/` executable of an ENABLED plugin does resolve as a bare command. This function therefore no longer records the surface as deferred'. Both halves of the claimed state are false at HEAD (working tree clean for all four files). (1) PATH IS extended: `appendPluginBinPath` (data-paths.ts:247) appends `<bundleRoot>/bin` for every root of the turn's runnable capability view (`enabledPluginBundleRoots`, data-paths.ts:200), wired on the Claude backend at claude-agent.ts:691 and :736 (node shim stays first, plugin bins last) and on the Pi backend at pi-agent.ts:5187, composed for EVERY supervised child start because 'any Bash tool call' is the documented scope. Appended never prepended, so a plugin cannot shadow a system binary. (2) NOT deferred: `addClaudeBinSurfaceDeferral` (claude.ts:2392-2435) pushes no `deferred` row at all -- it returns early when every bin file is already reached (:2415) and again whenever the bundle declares any capability (:2422); the only remaining output is a `warning` diagnostic for the single residual case of a bundle declaring zero capabilities, hence carrying no runtime root. Consequence verified separately from the identifier by positive control: `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/plugin-bin-path.test.ts` (6 tests, all pass) asserts a bundle executable resolves as a bare command on both backends, appends rather than shadows, grants nothing while the plugin is disabled, and reaches every Pi supervised child start; `format-adapters.test.ts:2817` ('defers every file-backed Claude surface it cannot run') passes with deferred kinds `['settings','theme']` -- no `bin` row. results.claim: Hook output above 50K is written to disk and replaced with a path plus a preview, rather than being injected into context or dropped.
results.quote: Hook output over 50K saved to disk with a path + preview instead of injected into context
results.ourState: We buffer hook stdout+stderr to a hard 8,192-byte ceiling and silently discard the remainder (a `truncated: true` flag is set on the result but no content is preserved and nothing is written to disk). ` in the `Other wins` grid; the whole line is that one sentence and nothing in it reverses the conclusion. Output that exceeds this limit is saved to a file and replaced with a preview and file path, the same way large tool results are handled.` and hooks.md:845 repeats it for additionalContext (`writes the full text to a file in the session directory and passes Claude the file path with a short preview`). 2) EVIDENCE: the identifier is real. packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:26 is `const OUTPUT_LIMIT = 8_192;` and appendCapped at :215-221 truncates to it and returns `truncated`. 3) CONSEQUENCE: false on the path that actually executes the hooks this page governs - the classic wrong-subsystem shape. `runHookCommand` is the FALLBACK execution authority and the shipped host never selects it. packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-automation.ts:1103 reads `const runner = options.runner ?? results.claim: A `PreCompact` hook can stop a compaction, either by exiting 2 or by returning a top-level `decision: "block"`.

results.ourState: PreCompact cannot block anything, and the two halves of our own contract disagree. `hook-decision-contract.ts` lists PreCompact in `TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS`, so its parsed output is allowed to carry `block`/`deny` + `reason` — but the frozen event table declares it `kind: 'observational'`, and its single emission site awaits `options.emit('PreCompact', …)` whose signature returns `Promise<void> | void`, so any decision the parser produced is discarded before compaction proceeds. A hook author writing the documented blocker sees it accepted and parsed, and the context is compacted anyway.
results.evidence: packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:83 (`kind: 'observational'`) vs packages/shared/src/automations/hook-decision-contract.ts:49 (PreCompact in TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS); emission at packages/pi-agent-server/src/extensions/lifecycle-bridge.ts:151 with the void-returning `emit` declared at :28

verdict.why: The finding survives all three checks, but two of its sub-claims are wrong and must not travel with it. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at whats-new/2026-w16.md:125, a single-clause <div> in the 'Other wins' grid with nothing after it that reverses the conclusion. It is not an isolated release note either: hooks.md:730 carries the row '| `PreCompact` | Yes | Blocks compaction |' in the exit-code-2 table; hooks.md:865 and :890 list PreCompact among the nine top-level-`decision` events ('The only value is "block"'); and hooks.md:2613 states 'Exit with code 2 to block compaction. For a manual `/compact`, the stderr message is shown to the user. You can also block by returning JSON with "decision": "block".' hooks.md:2615 even specifies what a blocked auto-compact does. whats-new/2026-w16 is row 178 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a Claude contract page. (2) CITED LINES: all accurate. types.ts:83 is `{ version: 1, event: 'PreCompact', owner: 'lifecycle-bridge', kind: 'observational', ... }`; hook-decision-contract.ts:49 has 'PreCompact' as the ninth entry of TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS; lifecycle-bridge.ts:150-153 is the sole emitter (`pi.on('session_before_compact', ...)` -> `await options.emit('PreCompact', ...)`) and :28 declares `emit(event, input): Promise<void> | void`. There is no compaction consumer anywhere: the projected `block`/`reason` from projectHookDecisionForEvent is produced and dropped, and the emit is fire-and-forget through createPiLifecycleSinkGate (lifecycle-bridge.ts:37-48), so compaction proceeds. CORRECTION A — the claim's 'the two halves of our own contract disagree' is a misreading and should be struck. `kind` in AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1 is a permission-receipt axis, defined at lifecycle-bridge.ts:19-21: '`kind`: `decision` for the frozen decision-bearing hooks (PreToolUse receipt/epoch and PermissionRequest); every other hook is `observational` and can never block or bypass a permission receipt.' PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop and ConfigChange are ALL `kind: 'observational'` and ALL in TOP_LEVEL_BLOCK_EVENTS, and TaskCreated/TaskCompleted are `kind: 'decision'` yet deliberately NOT in it (they are exit-code-only). The two tables are orthogonal axes, so there is no internal contradiction — only one missing consumer. CORRECTION B — the finding missed the internal staleness that IS real: hook-decision-contract.ts:236 asserts '`ConfigChange`/`PreCompact` are advisory', which hooks.md now contradicts for BOTH events (:719 'ConfigChange | Yes | Blocks the configuration change from taking effect (except `policy_settings`)' and :730 for PreCompact). So the veto primitive exists in-process; the missing piece is an awaited host round trip that maps a block to `{ cancel: true }`, not a new Pi capability. verdict.why: The quote is real but the CLAIMED OUR STATE is false for three of the four subprocess classes the doc names, and for the majority of the fourth. (1) QUOTE: `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w19.md` carries it in the `digest-wins-grid`, as `Subprocesses such as Bash, hooks, MCP, and LSP no longer inherit OTEL\_\* environment variables, so OTEL-instrumented apps run via the Bash tool no longer pick up the CLI's own OTLP endpoint`. One sentence, whole div read, nothing reverses it. (2) THE ABSENCE CLAIM IS TRUE BUT IRRELEVANT: `grep -ran -a -i OTEL packages apps scripts` (non-dist, non-test) really does find no scrub site -- because this fork does not scrub OTEL_* by DENYLIST, it ALLOWLISTS host env per subprocess, which is strictly stronger. (3) BASH: `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1577` runs shell commands through `requestSupervisedProcess`, which round-trips to the host `handleProcessStartRequest` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:5138`). No OTEL_*. (5) THE CITED HOOK EVIDENCE IS A SIBLING SUBSYSTEM: `packages/shared/src/automations/utils.ts:380` is `cleanEnv()`, the AUTOMATIONS env builder, not the hook runner. Its only two consumers never become a subprocess environment -- `buildEnvFromSdkInput` feeds webhook URL/header/body template substitution (`automation-system.ts:751`, comment: 'Webhook-safe env'), and `buildEnvFromPayload` feeds `${VAR}` expansion in prompt text (`handlers/prompt-handler.ts:86`). verdict.correctedState: Not a wholesale gap. Bash, hooks and LSP already inherit NO OTEL_* variable, and by a stronger mechanism than Claude's: the process supervisor's default `restricted` profile allowlists ~26 host keys plus `LC_*` (process-supervisor.ts:703-732), plugin hooks and plugin MCP servers use `explicit` (empty host env), and the direct hook runner allowlists six keys (hook-command.ts:34). results.claim: The Agent tool's `subagent_type` resolves case-insensitively AND separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" reaches the agent named code-reviewer.
results.quote: Agent tool subagent_type now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" resolves to code-reviewer
results.ourState: `resolveAgentDefinition` normalises with `normalizeName` = `name.trim().toLowerCase()` only. No separator folding: spaces and underscores are not collapsed to hyphens, so "Code Reviewer" normalises to "code reviewer", misses both the name match and the author-declared alias list, and throws `Unknown agent "Code Reviewer"`. This is the same class as the Task→Agent rename that broke every turn.

verdict.why:
All three legs check out, and the consequence was MEASURED with a positive control. 1. DOC — VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w20.md` -> 6878 bytes, 95 lines. The claim is line 91, the last cell of the `digest-wins-grid`, in full: `
Agent tool subagent\_type now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so "Code Reviewer" resolves to code-reviewer
`. Modulo Mintlify's `` wrappers and the `\_` escape, the quoted sentence is exact. It is a one-sentence line — there is no second clause reversing it, and no version gate or research-preview pill on this row (the pills sit on the three feature blocks above, not on `Other wins`). The page is row 182 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a Claude Code contract source, not a Codex/MCP page. 2. FILE — AS CITED. `packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283` is exactly `function normalizeName(name: string): string { return name.trim().toLowerCase(); }` — trim and lowercase, no separator folding. `:718-731` is `resolveAgentDefinition`: `const normalized = normalizeName(name)`, fork short-circuit, then `defs.find(def => def.name === normalized) ?? defs.find(def => def.aliases?.includes(normalized))`, then `throw new Error(`Unknown agent "${name}". Available agents: …`)` at :728. `normalizeName` is the ONLY normalizer in the file (all 6 call sites: :235, :441, :688, :690, :699, :719), and the stored `name` is itself only trim+lowercased at load (:441), so nothing slugifies either side of the comparison. Author-declared aliases (:698-701) are passed through the same `normalizeName`, so they do not fold separators either. 3. CONSEQUENCE — MEASURED TRUE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Ran `resolveAgentDefinition` against a runtime definition named `code-reviewer` (bun, real module, no mocks): "code-reviewer" => OK code-reviewer "CODE-REVIEWER" => OK code-reviewer <- CONTROL: case-insensitivity really is live on this rig " Code-Reviewer " => OK code-reviewer <- CONTROL: trim really is live "Code Reviewer" => THROW Unknown agent "Code Reviewer". Available agents: scout, planner, worker, reviewer, code-re… "code_reviewer" => THROW Unknown agent "code_reviewer". … The doc's own example is the failing case. Because the two controls pass on the same rig, the absence is a real absence and not a broken harness. LAYER UP — nothing upstream folds separators. `packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts` takes the model's string raw: `asTask` (:101-110) only type-checks `typeof value.agent !== 'string'`, `normalizeSubagentRequest` (:122) never touches the value, and :512 passes `taskInput.agent` straight into `resolveAgentDefinition`. The JSON schema at :382/:419/:432 is a bare `agent: { type: 'string' }` — no `enum` of live agent names that would keep the model on canonical spellings. `orchestrator/agent-defs.ts` is a 10-line re-export, not a second resolver. `prerequisite-manager.ts:450` (the skill agent ceiling) reads both `agent` and `subagent_type` and applies `.trim().toLowerCase()` — the same case-only fold, so the sibling path has the identical gap rather than compensating for it. LAYER DOWN — the separator-insensitive normalizer this repo already owns is in a SIBLING subsystem and is not shared: `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:242`, `parsePermissionMode`, does `mode.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[-_ ]/g, '')` and its doc comment at :238 literally says "case- and separator-insensitively". So the pattern, the regex and the vocabulary exist here for permission modes and were simply never applied to agent names. Naming the subsystem: this is `packages/shared/src/agents` (agent-name resolution), not `agent/mode-types` (permission modes). NOT A RECORDED DECISION. Read all nine dated owner decisions in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) — none touches agent-name matching. `grep -a` over `docs/superpowers/plans` and `specs` for `normalizeName`/slugify finds only the sibling verdict f220's own sweep rows and f088, whose measured verdict independently confirms `normalizeName` is trim+lowercase only. Not a rebrand either: the tool being spelled `subagent`/`agent` here instead of `Agent`/`subagent_type` is a rename, but the behaviour under test (tolerant matching of a requested agent type) is orthogonal to the spelling, and the fork already implements the case half of the same rule. SEVERITY CORRECTION, which is why the finding's own framing overshoots: this is NOT "the same class as the Task->Agent rename that broke every turn". The throw is not fatal — it surfaces as a failed tool result whose message enumerates the available agents (`Available agents: scout, planner, worker, reviewer, …`), so the model can retry with a canonical spelling on the next tool call. It is a one-round-trip robustness gap on a free-form string field, not a turn-killer.
verdict.correctedState: The divergence is real but narrower than filed. `normalizeName` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283) trims and lowercases only, so `resolveAgentDefinition` (:718-731) matches the requested agent type case-insensitively — MEASURED: "CODE-REVIEWER" and " Code-Reviewer " both resolve to `code-reviewer` — but NOT separator-insensitively: "Code Reviewer" and "code_reviewer" both throw `Unknown agent`, which is exactly the example Claude's w20 page says now works. The skill agent ceiling in prerequisite-manager.ts:450 has the same case-only fold, so it shares the gap rather than covering it. The fix is one line reusing the pattern this repo already ships for permission modes (`agent/mode-types.ts:242`, `.replace(/[-_ ]/g, '')`, whose comment already reads "case- and separator-insensitively"), applied to `normalizeName` so it folds both stored names and requested ones; note that collapsing separators would also make `code-reviewer` and `codereviewer` collide, so the loader's duplicate-name behaviour should be checked in the same change.

results.claim: MCP stdio servers receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in their spawn environment, the same as hooks, and configs may reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} inside commands.
results.quote: MCP stdio servers now receive CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in their environment, matching hooks, and plugin configs can reference ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} in commands
results.ourState: Only half. Plugin-supplied MCP servers get the project dir via `claudeCompatPluginEnv` (`NESSY_PROJECT_DIR` + `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`). Native and project `.mcp.json` stdio servers take the non-plugin branch, whose env is `{...processEnv, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...config.env}` — no project-dir variable is injected, so `${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR}`/`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a project `.mcp.json` command expands from `process.env` and resolves to nothing.

verdict.why: 1) SENTENCE EXISTS. whats-new/2026-w20.md line 87 (Other wins grid, single-sentence div): "MCP stdio servers now receive CLAUDE\_PROJECT\_DIR in their environment, matching hooks, and plugin configs can reference \${"{"}CLAUDE\_PROJECT\_DIR{"}"} in commands". De-escaping the MDX (\_ escapes and the {"{"} brace-literal trick) yields the claimed quote exactly; the whole line was read and there is no second clause reversing it. 2) CITED CODE SAYS SO. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:373-401 -- the stdio branch splits on config.pluginRuntime: plugin servers go to SupervisedStdioClientTransport, everything else builds env: { ...processEnv, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...config.env } where processEnv is process.env minus BLOCKED_ENV_VARS. No project-dir variable is added. packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:127-134 confirms the plugin-only injection (exact line is :132, not :131 -- :131 is CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). 3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY, ONE LAYER UP AND DOWN. Up: native/project .mcp.json entries take the resource branch in mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:~452-465 -> parseMcpServersDocument, and mcp/project-config.ts:106 expands command/args/env/url/headers against `const environment = process.env` only; nothing in packages/ or apps/ assigns process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or process.env.NESSY_PROJECT_DIR (grep -a, whole repo, excluding node_modules/dist/bundled resources -- the only CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR literal outside plugin code is capabilities/native-sources.ts:726, an unrelated '.claude' directory constant, i.e. the sibling-symbol trap, and it is not this). Down: mcp-pool.ts:1112-1145 connect() -> sdkConfigToClientConfig (mcp-pool.ts:429-482, passes config.env straight through) -> new NessyMcpClient; there is no other spawn seam. The Claude SDK backend does NOT spawn stdio MCP itself -- claude-agent.ts:1136-1148 hands the SDK only in-process session tools plus createSourceProxyServers backed by the same McpClientPool, so client.ts is the single spawn authority and nothing upstream supplies the variable. NOT an owner decision: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3's nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions -- none touch the project-dir env. NOT a rename or product difference either: the Nessy spelling NESSY_PROJECT_DIR is not injected for these servers any more than the Claude one is, and the host demonstrably knows the project root (capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:137 resolves projectDirectory: ['NESSY_PROJECT_DIR','CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR'] for skills). Two corrections to the claim's wording are in correctedState.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with two corrections to the claimed state. (a) claudeCompatPluginEnv (packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:127-134) emits CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR ONLY -- not 'NESSY_PROJECT_DIR + CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR'. Nothing in the repo emits NESSY_PROJECT_DIR into any process env (pluginRuntimeEnv at :98-105 emits only the four PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA spellings). The CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR entry is line :132; :131 is CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. This makes the gap slightly WIDER than claimed, and exposes a second defect the finding did not name: format-adapters/claude.ts:2708-2711 rewrites a Claude plugin manifest's ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} to ${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR} at import, but no layer supplies NESSY_PROJECT_DIR, so a Claude-plugin MCP command referencing the project dir resolves to NEITHER spelling -- contradicting the data-paths.ts:123-125 comment which asserts 'both resolve to the same validated path'. The spawned plugin process does still carry CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in its environment, so the doc's first clause holds for plugin servers; only the in-command ${...} reference is broken. (b) An unresolved reference in a project .mcp.json does not 'resolve to nothing': expandConfigVariables (mcp/server-config-values.ts:51-65) defaults to unset: 'literal', so the command keeps the literal ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} text and project-config.ts:202 warns 'references unset environment variables with no default'. The server therefore starts with a bogus literal path rather than a blank one. Net state: native and project .mcp.json stdio MCP servers receive no project-dir variable under either spelling; only Claude-profile plugin MCP servers do, and for them only as spawn env, not as an expandable ${...} token. The doc's 'matching hooks' comparison is also unmet on the hooks side in this fork -- buildHookCommandEnv (automations/hook-command.ts:46-80) inherits only HOME/PATH/SHELL/TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP plus NESSY_* event fields and the plugin actionEnv, so a native hook gets no project dir either; the fork is internally symmetric (project dir is a plugin-runtime-only concept) but diverges from Claude for both hooks and MCP.

results.claim: Fast mode's default model moved to Opus 4.8; Opus 4.7 and 4.6 keep the old price and Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
results.quote: Fast mode now defaults to Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per MTok: 2x the standard rate for about 2.5x the speed. Opus 4.7 and 4.6 stay at $30/$150. Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
results.ourState: `shouldEnableFastMode` returns true for exactly one literal — `model === 'claude-opus-4-7'`. A session on `claude-opus-4-8` (which IS in our model table and IS the current default upstream) never gets the fast-mode beta header, so the fast toggle is silently inert on the model fast mode now defaults to. Stale pin, not a policy decision — the comment still reads "Only activates for Opus 4.7".

verdict.why: Sentence verified verbatim at whats-new/2026-w22.md:89 (the raw MDX escapes the dollars as \$10/\$50 and \$30/\$150; wording is otherwise identical, and the line is a self-contained three-sentence lede that does not reverse itself). The identifier half of the finding is also correct: unified-network-interceptor.ts:496-499 is exactly `if (!FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode) return false; return typeof model === 'string' && model === 'claude-opus-4-7';`, and the doc comment at :493-494 still says 'Only activates for Opus 4.7'. The CONSEQUENCE is false, which is inert-worklist shape 3 (enforcement one layer up) plus shape 4 (wrong subsystem named). (1) Line :497 short-circuits on FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode, which is a hardcoded `fastMode: false` literal in feature-flags.ts:182 — the ONLY non-getter in that object; every sibling flag (developerFeedback, embeddedServer, codexRuntime) is a getter reading a NESSY_FEATURE_* env override, and fastMode has none. `grep -rna FAST_MODE|FASTMODE` over packages/apps/scripts/docs returns only FAST_MODE_BETA, the beta string itself. So shouldEnableFastMode returns false for EVERY model, Opus 4.7 included; the model literal at :498 is unreachable, not a live discriminator that works on 4.7 and misses 4.8. (2) There is no 'fast toggle' to be silently inert: no /fast command, no setting, no IPC, no i18n key (the only 'fast' hits in en.json are the Guardian fast-model rows). /fast is a Claude Code CLI slash command; this fork drives the Claude Agent SDK, and NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE defaults off. (3) Even with the flag flipped, the Anthropic adapter's fast-mode branch (:991-999) can never fire for a Claude session: the interceptor's only consumer is agent/backend/internal/drivers/pi.ts:290 via resolveInterceptorBundlePath, i.e. it Bun --preloads into the Pi subprocess (and the headless server's own process) only. packages/shared/AGENTS.md records this as a decision with a reason: 'The Claude SDK no longer runs under Bun (since 0.2.113 it spawns a per-platform native `claude` binary), so --preload is not available there. Features that used to live in the interceptor for Claude (rich tool intent, fast-mode override, MalformedBodyError validation, etc.) are Phase-2 work.' (4) 'Stale pin, not a policy decision' is therefore wrong on the record: both the hardcoded-off flag and the 4-7 literal date from the same baseline commit 845cf0a4 (2026-07-05), and no fast-mode UI has ever existed. Not one of the nine §3 owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md (no 'fast' hit in that file), but the Phase-2 deferral in packages/shared/AGENTS.md is an equivalent recorded decision. Incidental confirmation: claude-opus-4-8 IS a real MODEL_REGISTRY entry (config/models.ts:133) and claude-opus-4-6 remaps forward to it (:62), so the model-table half of the claim holds — it is only the fast-mode consequence that does not.
verdict.correctedState: Fast mode is not implemented as a user-facing feature in this fork at all. FEATURE_FLAGS.fastMode (feature-flags.ts:182) is a hardcoded `false` const with no env override — alone among that object's flags — so shouldEnableFastMode (unified-network-interceptor.ts:496-499) returns false for every model, and the `model === 'claude-opus-4-7'` literal at :498 is unreachable rather than a stale live pin. There is no /fast command, setting or i18n string. Independently, the interceptor that houses the fast-mode branch preloads only into the Pi subprocess (drivers/pi.ts:290) and the headless server process, never into the Claude Agent SDK's native binary; packages/shared/AGENTS.md records the Claude-side fast-mode override as Phase-2 work pending SDK hooks or a local proxy. The only real residue is documentation staleness: the comment at :493-494 and feature-flags.ts:181 still say 'Opus 4.7' and '6x pricing' where upstream now defaults fast mode to Opus 4.8 at 2x, and Opus 4.6 fast mode is deprecated.
