results.claim: A SessionStart hook can return `reloadSkills: true` to make skills it installed available in the same session, and `/reload-skills` re-scans skill directories without a restart.
results.quote: New /reload-skills command re-scans skill directories without restarting, and SessionStart hooks can return reloadSkills: true to make skills they install available in the same session
results.ourState: `reloadSkills` has zero occurrences in any .ts/.tsx in the repo (grep -ran -a, node_modules excluded) — the only hit anywhere is a docs file listing it as an open R9 item. The hook output parser reads `additionalContext`, `updatedInput`, `updatedToolOutput`, `worktreePath`, `retry`, elicitation `action`/`content` and the universal five, and ignores anything else, so a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session.

verdict.why:
The quote is verbatim and the identifier absence is real, but the stated CONSEQUENCE is false, and the consequence is what the finding asserts. This is the exact recurring shape AGENTS.md warns about: the identifier is genuinely unwired while something upstream already produces the documented effect. (1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w22.md, line 106, inside the 'Other wins' digest grid: '
New /reload-skills command re-scans skill directories without restarting, and SessionStart hooks can return reloadSkills: true to make skills they install available in the same session
'. Read the whole line and both neighbours (`plugin init` scaffolding above, skill/command `disallowed-tools` below) — nothing reverses it. (2) IDENTIFIER — CONFIRMED. `grep -ran 'reloadSkills' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` (with -a, node_modules excluded) → 0. `grep -ran 'reload-skills'` over packages/ apps/ → 0. The only repo hits are this sweep's own docs/JSON. packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:313-407 (`parseHookCommandOutput`) extracts exactly permissionDecision/permissionDecisionReason, the PermissionRequest `decision` band (behavior/interrupt/updatedPermissions/updatedInput/message), reason, additionalContext, updatedInput, retry, worktreePath, updatedToolOutput and elicitation action/content; `parseUniversalHookOutput` (:443-454) adds continue/stopReason/suppressOutput/systemMessage/terminalSequence. No `reloadSkills`, and `parseHookOutputForEvent` (:464) has no unknown-field passthrough. The cited file:line says what was claimed. (3) CONSEQUENCE — REFUTED BY EXECUTION. The claim 'a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session' is wrong, because Nessy never caches the agent's skill list for the session the way Claude Code does — so there is nothing for `reloadSkills` to reload. - The skill inventory that feeds the agent is rebuilt FROM DISK ON EVERY TURN. `SessionManager.withCapabilityRuntime` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:5881) calls `createCapabilityTurn` (:3983) per turn, which calls `resolver.resolve(context)` (:4045); that runs `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:624, inventory built at :635) → `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:880) → `skillRecords` (:266), which does a bare `existsSync`/`readdirSync` over every skill root (~/.agents/skills :903, /skills :904, workspace skills/ :949, project .nessy-agent/skills :1016 and .agents/skills :1065). No memo, no TTL on that path. - POSITIVE CONTROL (the finding is an absence claim, so it needs one). Ran `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` twice in one process against a temp workspace, writing skills/hook-installed/SKILL.md between the calls — i.e. simulating a hook installing a skill after the turn's snapshot was taken. Result: BEFORE ['find-skills','officecli'], AFTER ['find-skills','officecli','hook-installed']. 1 pass, 2 expect() calls. The control half (absent before) fired, so the observation is not a vacuous pass. - Nessy ALSO has the disk watcher Claude's /reload-skills exists to replace. packages/shared/src/config/watcher.ts watches `/workspaces/{id}/skills/{slug}/SKILL.md` recursively (header :15, routing :504-520); `handleSkillsDirChange` (:772) calls `emitWorkspaceInvalidation('skill')` (:775 → `emitNativeSourceInvalidation` :263) and `invalidateSkillsCache()` + `loadAllSkills()` (:824-826). storage-runtime.ts:347 turns that bus event into `capabilityResolver.invalidate(..., 'refresh-before-next-turn')`. So a skill dropped on disk mid-session is picked up automatically, with no restart and no command. SUBSYSTEM CHECK. The finding cites the right subsystem — packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts is the LIVE parser, not the unreachable `plugins/hooks-runtime.ts` executor that is owner-decision §3 item 5. No mis-naming there. NOT AN OWNER DECISION, NOT A BRAND DIFFERENCE. None of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 covers reloadSkills (they are SEATBELT wildcard, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). It is also unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rename. The finding is refuted on its consequence alone.
verdict.correctedState:
Refuted as written — the consequence is false. What survives is a much narrower, one-turn timing gap.

TRUE: `reloadSkills` has 0 occurrences in any .ts/.tsx (grep -ran -a, node_modules excluded), there is no `/reload-skills` command, and `parseHookCommandOutput` (packages/shared/src/automations/hook-command.ts:313-407) plus `parseUniversalHookOutput` (:443-454) read neither field and have no unknown-field passthrough.

FALSE: 'a SessionStart hook that installs a skill cannot surface it this session.' Nessy has no per-session skill cache for `reloadSkills` to invalidate. The agent's skill list is rebuilt from disk on EVERY capability turn — `withCapabilityRuntime` (SessionManager.ts:5881) → `createCapabilityTurn` (:3983) → `resolver.resolve` (:4045) → `buildCapabilityResolutionInputsV2` (storage-runtime.ts:635) → `buildNativeCapabilityInventory` (native-sources.ts:880) → `skillRecords` (:266), which `readdirSync`s all five skill roots uncached. Measured: two inventory builds in one process with skills/hook-installed/SKILL.md written between them returned ['find-skills','officecli'] then ['find-skills','officecli','hook-installed']. Independently, ConfigWatcher watches skills/{slug}/SKILL.md and emits a 'skill' native-source invalidation (watcher.ts:772-775, 824-826) that storage-runtime.ts:347 converts to `refresh-before-next-turn` — Nessy's structural equivalent of /reload-skills, fired automatically by the file event.

THE RESIDUAL GAP (worth at most a low-severity row): ORDERING, not capability. SessionStart is emitted from inside the turn at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6538, after `createCapabilityTurn` already resolved that turn's snapshot. So a skill the hook installs is missing from the FIRST prompt's snapshot and present from the second turn onward. Claude's page promises it 'starting with the first prompt'. Nessy's divergence is therefore a one-turn delay, not a session-long absence — and closing it means re-resolving the capability snapshot after SessionStart hooks settle, not adding a `reloadSkills` field to the parser. Adding the field alone would be a no-op, since the re-scan it requests already happens unconditionally.

results.claim: A `MessageDisplay` hook event fires per assistant message and lets a hook transform or hide the displayed text.
results.quote: New MessageDisplay hook event lets hooks transform or hide assistant message text as it is displayed
results.ourState: Not emitted. `PluginHookEventName` carries 28 of the documented events plus two of our own and deliberately excludes `MessageDisplay`; a plugin declaring it imports as a recorded deferral (`plugin.deferred.event_message_display_unsupported`) rather than registering a hook that can never fire. Reason on record: no per-message display interception channel exists.

verdict.why:
All three refutation routes fail; the finding stands as written. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w22.md line 108 reads '
New MessageDisplay hook event lets hooks transform or hide assistant message text as it is displayed
'. That div is the entire line (an 'Other wins' grid cell) — there is no second sentence and nothing reverses the conclusion. (2) CITATIONS ACCURATE: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:100 is exactly `MessageDisplay: 'plugin.deferred.event_message_display_unsupported',` inside DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS (:99), whose doc comment (:88-97) states MessageDisplay 'needs a per-message display interception channel we do not have -> R30' and records the 10s (not 600s) timeout. packages/shared/src/plugins/hooks-runtime.ts:12-23 is the doc comment on PluginHookEventName: 'hooks.md enumerates 30 events; we emit 28 of them, and this union carries exactly those 28 plus our own McpServerStart and McpToolCall'. I counted the union members (:25-53): 30 literals, minus McpServerStart/McpToolCall = 28 documented, MessageDisplay and TeammateIdle absent. The claimed count is exact. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both directions. One layer up: mapExternalHookEventName (format-adapters.ts:625-645) misses all three dialect tables for 'MessageDisplay', falls to the DEFERRED_EXTERNAL_HOOK_EVENT_REASONS lookup and returns `{diagnostics: [], deferredReasonCode}` with NO `event` — so claude.ts:1310-1319 and codex.ts:1347-1355 push a deferral entry and `return`, registering no hook. Confirmed by test at __tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:3648. One layer down: nothing upstream already provides the behaviour. `grep -ran displayContent` over packages/ and apps/ finds only unrelated sibling-subsystem locals (ui/src/components/chat/TurnCard.tsx:916, UserMessageBubble.tsx:403 — plain render-time string variables) plus pi-agent-server bundle internals; there is no hookSpecificOutput.displayContent channel. AGENT_EVENT_CONTRACTS_V1 (packages/shared/src/automations/types.ts:37) contains no MessageDisplay entry. NOT AN OWNER DECISION: checked docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 — the nine dated decisions are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts's PluginHookRuntime/runHooks/parseHookOutput/createHookRegistryFromProjection, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. MessageDisplay is not among them (row 5 touches the same FILE but is about the dead hook executor, not this type's membership — naming that as the decision would be the sibling-subsystem trap). NOT A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE either: it is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rebrand. It is an acknowledged, reason-carrying OPEN gap routed to a work item, which is what the finding says. Minor bookkeeping note that does not change the verdict: the '-> R30' pointer in the deferral comment and in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-hook-decision-patterns.md:22 looks stale — R30 in the parity audit was split into a (skill frontmatter + substitution), b (/doctor) and c (subagent frontmatter), none of which is a display-interception channel, so the routed work item may no longer exist under that number.

verdict.why:
All three checks were run and the finding's FACTS survive all three; it is refuted on the fourth ground the brief names -- it is an already-recorded, reasoned deviation, not a new defect. (1) Quote: verbatim at whats-new/2026-w23.md:96, inside the 'Other wins' grid, modulo Mintlify's markdown escaping and tags: 'OTEL\_RESOURCE\_ATTRIBUTES values are now attached as labels on metric datapoints, so you can slice usage metrics by custom dimensions like team or repo'. WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED: this exact variable is named in a recorded deviation with a reason, so it is a decision, not a gap. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-observability-and-cost.md:182 carries the category string 'documented, not implemented -- monitoring-usage.md:446 to :455 define the standard attribute set every metric shares: session.id, app.version, app.entrypoint, organization.id, user.account_uuid, user.account_id, user.id, user.email, terminal.type, and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES passthrough, each with its own OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_* toggle. Any widening toward :442's table is a privacy decision to be made on purpose, not an omission to be patched.' results.claim: `fallbackModel` holds an ordered list of up to three models, each tried in turn when the primary is overloaded or unavailable.
results.quote: fallbackModel configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and --fallback-model now applies to interactive sessions too
results.ourState: `fallbackModel` is a single string in both the schema (`z.string()`) and the default (`''`), and the runtime does exactly one hop: `getRetryFallbackModel` returns that one id, `setModel`s to it, and retries once with `fallbackModelRetry: true` — a second failure has nowhere to go. There is no `fallbackModels` array anywhere in the repo.

verdict.why:
All three checks pass, so the finding survives. STEP 1 (verbatim): curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w24.md puts the sentence on line 69, the whole line being one
in the 'Other wins' grid: 'fallbackModel configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and `--fallback-model` now applies to interactive sessions too'. The linked section corroborates rather than softens it -- model-config.md:365 'Configure one or more fallback models and Claude Code tries them in order ... Chains are capped at three models after duplicate removal, and extra entries are ignored', :373 'set `fallbackModel` in settings as an array', :381 'The `--fallback-model` flag takes precedence ... `"default"` expands to the default model.' STEP 2 (cited lines): validators.ts:135 is exactly `fallbackModel: z.string()`. storage.ts:189 has drifted -- the default `fallbackModel: ''` is at :194 (FALLBACK_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.workspaceDefaults), with the load-time coercion at :273-276; the shipped apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:28 is `"fallbackModel": ""` too, and config-defaults-schema.ts types it `fallbackModel: string` with the docstring 'Pi model ID to retry once after model/network drain errors. STEP 3 (consequence, tested separately from the identifier): the one-hop cap is real, not merely an unwired identifier. `getRetryFallbackModel` bails at :6314 on `options?.fallbackModelRetry`, and `retryWithFallbackModel` re-enters `chatImpl` with `fallbackModelRetry: true` (:6342) after `setModel(fallbackModel)` (:6335) -- so the second failure returns null and falls through to `emitStopFailureHookOnce` + `typed_error` at both call sites (:6755-6761 in the event loop, :6795-6801 in the catch). Even a fresh outer retry cannot get a second hop, because :6319 also returns null once `fallbackModel === this.getModel()`. The repo's own test is literally named 'retries once with the configured fallback model for a typed drain error' (pi-agent-fallback-model.test.ts:85). No upstream or downstream layer supplies the missing hops: `normalizePiFallbackModelId` (models-pi.ts:20-22) is `typeof x === 'string' ? x.trim() : ''` with no comma split, `grep -a` for `fallbackModels` returns zero source hits (only the sweep's own JSON), and greps for modelChain/failover/tryNextModel/fallbackChain across shared, server-core and pi-agent-server return nothing. Sibling-subsystem check: this is the only fallbackModel in the repo -- packages/server, packages/server-core, packages/ui, apps/electron/src and packages/pi-agent-server have no reference at all, and apps/cli has no `--fallback-model` flag, so the sentence's second clause diverges as well. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3 (none concerns fallback), and not a de-brand or subscription-drop difference -- a model chain on overload is orthogonal to dropping Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows. It IS already a recorded deviation (deviation-register.md:110, 'not implemented -- model-config.md:361 configures an ordered chain ... Neither exists'), whose tail 'read by nothing' is now stale: pi-agent.ts:6257 reads it. NOTE on f106: the same underlying gap on the model-config page was refuted, but on grounds specific to that claim's wording -- it asserted an array 'fails validation' (false: ConfigDefaultsSchema is test-only) and framed the key as Claude's settings.json. f226 asserts neither, and f106's own correctedState calls the arity gap 'Real'.
verdict.correctedState: Confirmed, with three additions that make the gap wider than stated. (1) Line drift in the evidence: the default is storage.ts:194 (not :189), the load-time trim storage.ts:273-276, the runtime pi-agent.ts:6313-6344 (not :6291-:6320). (2) The single hop fires only for the six codes in FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES (pi-agent.ts:337-343: invalid_model, model_no_tool_support, network_error, service_error, service_unavailable, provider_error) and is Pi-only -- claude-agent.ts never passes a fallback model to the Claude Agent SDK, so a Claude-backed session has no fallback at all. There is no dedup, no three-entry cap, no ordered chain, no "default" expansion, no availableModels filtering and no compaction context-window rule. (3) In a packaged build the one hop is itself inert: the shipped apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:28 has `"fallbackModel": ""`, syncConfigDefaults (storage.ts:200-227) overwrites ~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json from that bundled asset on every launch, and no UI, IPC or CLI surface writes the key -- so a user edit does not survive a restart. The sentence's second clause diverges too: apps/cli has no `--fallback-model` flag, interactive or otherwise.

results.claim: A `sandbox.allowAppleEvents` opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS.
results.quote: New sandbox.allowAppleEvents opt-in setting lets sandboxed commands send Apple Events on macOS
results.ourState: No occurrence of `allowAppleEvents` (or `AppleEvent` at all) anywhere in the repo. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` is a closed seven-entry list — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem — and unknown keys are rejected/stripped, so an admin or user who writes the documented key gets a validation drop rather than the opt-in. We do ship the macOS sandbox this governs.

verdict.why:
The quote is verbatim (w25.md:79, a one-sentence <div>, nothing after it reverses it) and the identifier half is correct, but the finding fails on its own evidence and on its consequence, and its true residue is already adjudicated.

1. THE STATED EVIDENCE IS FALSE. 'grep -ran -a "AppleEvent" . -> 0' does not reproduce. `allowAppleEvents` occurs four times on disk, in bundles the app ships: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:350289, apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:350289, apps/electron/dist/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:350289 and apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js:176630. It is the vendored Pi SDK's own sandbox zod schema, carrying the full describe(): 'macOS only: Allow sandboxed commands to send Apple Events (and look up the appleeventsd Mach service) ... Removes code-execution isolation ... Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings ... Default: false'. They are untracked build artifacts, so 'absent from first-party tracked source' survives; 'no occurrence anywhere in the repo' does not.

2. THE CONSEQUENCE NAMES THE WRONG SANDBOX. Claude's setting governs sandboxed *commands*, i.e. Bash. Nessy has two macOS profiles and the finding conflates them.
   - The Bash-tool seatbelt (packages/shared/src/agent/core/bash-seatbelt.ts) is what the doc line is about. It is OFF BY DEFAULT (`getMacosSeatbeltBashSandboxEnabled`, storage.ts:1124, `?? false`), and when a user turns it on `buildMacosBashSeatbeltProfile` returns `(version 1) (allow default)` because `SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD = true` (bash-seatbelt.ts:88, owner decision 2026-07-21, REAFFIRMED 2026-07-29 — inert-worklist section 3 item 1). So a sandboxed Bash command in Nessy can already send Apple Events today; the documented opt-in would be a no-op on that path, and the -600 symptom it exists to relieve does not arise.
   - The profile that does deny them is `buildDarwinSandboxProfile` (session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:128) — `(deny default)` plus a filtered `machLookupRule`, governing supervised processes and `script_sandbox`, not the model's Bash tool.

3. THE NON-GRANT IS DELIBERATE, PROBE-BACKED AND RECORDED. mach-services.ts:27-35 withholds the LaunchServices names (`com.apple.CoreServices.coreservicesd`, `com.apple.lsd.mapdb`, `com.apple.lsd.modifydb`) and `com.apple.pasteboard.1` because `sandbox-exec -p '<profile>' /usr/bin/pbpaste` returned 0 — a sandboxed command read the pasteboard and could `open` an app outside the sandbox. That is precisely the hazard the Pi describe() names ('sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt'). Recorded in plan 2026-07-30-sandbox-mach-and-protected-paths.md and deviation-register.md:430-435.

4. THE DOC'S OWN ALTERNATIVE IS IMPLEMENTED. `excludedCommands` is the first accepted key and is enforced end to end (SessionManager.ts:3579 -> process-supervisor.ts:476 -> downgrade receipt :211 + risky-band prompt), so `open`/`osascript` can be run outside the sandbox.

5. DUPLICATE OF AN ADJUDICATED ROW. f035 covers the same key and its verdict (docs/superpowers/specs/data/phase2-verdicts/f035.json) already dropped it from `gap` to 'at most a narrow documented, not implemented note on allowAppleEvents ... with the security rationale attached'.

Minor: the cited range is off — SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS is sandbox-settings.ts:172-180; :182-183 are SANDBOX_NETWORK_KEYS and SANDBOX_FILESYSTEM_KEYS. The rejection mechanism is right: `assertKnownKeys` (:216-221) throws on any other key, and the tolerant managed sink drops it as 'tightened'.
verdict.correctedState:
Not a `gap`. Downgrade to a narrow `documented, not implemented` note, already covered by f035.

True: `allowAppleEvents` is not a first-party settable key. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180) is a closed seven-entry list — excludedCommands, deniedReadRoots, deniedWriteRoots, additionalWritableRoots, allowUnsandboxedCommands, network, filesystem — and `assertKnownKeys` (:216-221) throws on anything else, so a settings file carrying the documented key is rejected (or dropped 'tightened' by the tolerant managed sink) rather than honoured. Precedent that this class is fixable exists: `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` was added for exactly this reason (plans/2026-07-30-switches-and-sandbox-key.md, Task 5).

Wrong as written, on three counts:

- **'No occurrence of allowAppleEvents (or AppleEvent at all) anywhere in the repo' / 'grep -> 0'.** Four occurrences exist on disk in shipped bundles (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:350289, apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:350289, apps/electron/dist/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:350289, apps/electron/resources/session-mcp-server/index.js:176630) — the vendored Pi SDK's sandbox schema, complete with the setting's describe() text. They are untracked generated files and are not wired to Nessy's key list, so the key is still unreachable, but the absence claim must be scoped to first-party tracked source.
- **'We do ship the macOS sandbox this governs.'** Not for the surface the doc line addresses. The Bash-tool seatbelt is disabled by default (storage.ts:1124 `?? false`) and emits `(version 1) (allow default)` when enabled, because `SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD = true` (bash-seatbelt.ts:88; owner decision 2026-07-21, reaffirmed 2026-07-29). Apple Events from a sandboxed Bash command are therefore already permitted; the opt-in would change nothing there today. The `(deny default)` profile that does deny them, `buildDarwinSandboxProfile` (session-tools-core/src/runtime/filesystem-isolation.ts:128), governs supervised processes and `script_sandbox` instead.
- **The absence is unmotivated.** It is the opposite: mach-services.ts:27-35 deliberately withholds `com.apple.pasteboard.1` and the three LaunchServices names on the strength of a probe (`sandbox-exec -p '<profile>' /usr/bin/pbpaste` returned 0), which is the same hazard Claude's own setting warns removes code-execution isolation. Recorded in plans/2026-07-30-sandbox-mach-and-protected-paths.md and deviation-register.md:430-435. The doc's named alternative, `excludedCommands`, is the first accepted key and is enforced end to end.

Any future implementation should follow Claude's own scoping — honoured from user, managed/policy and CLI settings only, never from project settings — and must be paired with the pre-GA `SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD` flip, since until that flip the Bash profile allows everything and the key is decorative.

results.claim: Output from a `!`-prefixed command now gets a model response by default; `respondToBashCommands: false` in settings.json restores the old context-only behavior.
results.quote: To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json.
results.ourState: We ship `!` shell mode in the composer, and it is stuck on the pre-change behavior: `runShellCommand` spawns the command, records the result and returns — it never queues a turn — and `respondToBashCommands` has zero occurrences in the repo, so there is neither the new default nor the escape hatch.

verdict.why:
All three checks positively confirm the finding. (1) DOC — curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w26.md returns a 4471-byte page; the quoted sentence exists verbatim on line 37 (inside the

of the feature block titled 'Shell mode responds to command output', v2.1.186). With the inline markup stripped the sentence is character-for-character the claimed quote: 'To keep the earlier behavior, where the output is added to context without a response, set respondToBashCommands to false in settings.json.' Reading the WHOLE line: it is a three-sentence lede and neither of the other two reverses the conclusion — 'Commands you run with the ! prefix now get a response from Claude once the output lands in the transcript, so you can run ! npm test and get an explanation of the failures without a second prompt.' establishes the new default, and 'The response costs the same as sending a normal prompt.' is a cost note. The feature links to /docs/en/interactive-mode#shell-mode-with-prefix. (2) CITED FILES — apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/FreeFormInput.tsx:1399-1416 says exactly what was claimed: inside submitMessage, `if (trimmedInput.startsWith('!')) { const command = trimmedInput.slice(1).trim(); if (!command || !sessionId || !runShellCommand) return false; setIsShellCommandRunning(true); void runShellCommand(sessionId, command).then(...clearSubmittedDraft...).catch(...).finally(...); return true }` — it returns before ever reaching the onSubmit(...) calls that queue a turn (the customSlashCommand branch at :1419 and the normal path below it). packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16372 is `async runShellCommand(sessionId, rawCommand, workspaceId?): Promise`, and its body (16372-16495) does exactly what was claimed: permission/mode gates, executeDirectShellCommand, then push a role:'user' message whose content is formatDirectShellTranscript(...) with a '!' command badge, persistSession + flushSession, sendEvent({type:'user_message', status:'accepted'}), and return the result. No turn is started, managed.isProcessing is never set, and no agent invocation follows. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier. One layer up: the renderer's only owner of this path, ChatDisplay.tsx:1242-1255 handleRunShellCommand, just RPCs `{type:'runShellCommand'}` and toasts on !executed — it does not follow with a prompt. One layer down: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:566-567 is a straight pass-through, and the contract test packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.shell-command.test.ts:148-180 ('appends executed shell output as a command-badged user message') PINS the pre-change behaviour — it asserts exactly one message, role user, persisted, flushed, one user_message event, and nothing else. So the output genuinely IS added to context without a response: our state is precisely the 'earlier behavior' the doc sentence describes. Absence check with -a: `grep -rna -a respondToBashCommands . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=docs` and `git grep -In -a respondToBashCommands -- . ':!docs'` both return zero; the only hits anywhere are the sweep's own docs/specs rows. Searched for the false-positive shapes and found neither: no differently-named equivalent (respondToShell|bashModeRespond|shellModeRespond|respondToCommand|autoRespond → 0 across apps, packages, docs-site) and no sibling subsystem owning it (no shell-respond key in packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts; the only shell-related config key there is useAutoModeDuringPlan). NOT one of the nine owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 — those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions. §3 item 3 is autoMode.classifyAllShell, a DIFFERENT key that happens to appear in this same page's 'Other wins' list; do not conflate them. Nor is it in §4's false positives. No plan or doc in docs/ mentions runShellCommand or the composer '!' mode at all, so no decision to keep the old behaviour is recorded anywhere. NOT a deliberate product difference either — it is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, to the corporate-gateway targeting, and to the NESSY_/@nessy-agent/ renaming. Note the repo's coverage map grades this page 🟩 at 2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:292 on the strength of the 2026-07-29 weekly-changelog pass, but that pass filtered only for renames/new component types and its findings file (2026-07-29-weekly-changelog-findings.md) contains no w26 shell-mode row — this changed default slipped through that filter, so the green verdict is not evidence against the finding.
verdict.correctedState: The finding stands as written; three refinements. (a) Our '!' mode is not merely 'stuck on the pre-change behavior' by omission — the pre-change behavior is PINNED BY A TEST. sessions.shell-command.test.ts:148-180 asserts the executed command produces exactly one appended user message and one user_message event and nothing further, so implementing the new default means changing a green contract test, not just adding a branch. (b) The escape hatch would not literally be `respondToBashCommands` in `settings.json` in this fork. Nessy's own preference surface is packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts (schema + validators + config-defaults.json), and settings.json here is the Claude-compatibility store (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts) used for permissions/managed policy, not for composer UI behaviour. The correct parity target is a Nessy config key with the documented default (respond = true) plus an opt-out, matching the fork's config-naming convention — the behaviour is the contract, the key location is not. (c) One adjacent divergence the row does not mention, worth carrying with it: our '!' mode also refuses to run at all in explore and plan permission modes (SessionManager.ts:16393-16402) and prompts for permission in default mode (:16416-16421), neither of which Claude's shell mode does. That is a separate, deliberate-looking hardening, not part of this gap, but anyone implementing the respond-by-default change will touch the same function and should not silently drop it.

results.claim: A `sandbox.credentials` setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables, with `files` and `envVars` sub-keys.
results.quote: New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
results.ourState: `credentials` is not a member of `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS`, so the key is stripped as unknown. The name appears in this repo only as a shape ANALOGY in two comments ("an individual invalid entry in `files` or `envVars` is stripped… a wholly invalid `credentials` value is dropped") borrowed to describe tolerant parsing of `sandbox.network` and of the permission DSL — the setting itself has no reader and no enforcement.

verdict.why:
REFUTED on four independent grounds. The quote is real and the two cited lines say what was claimed, but the row is a duplicate of an already-adjudicated finding, it is a dated parked owner decision, its stated mechanism is factually wrong, and BOTH halves of the claimed exposure are already delivered one layer up. 1) QUOTE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM, and the whole line carries no reversing second half. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w26.md` line 53 is a single-item grid cell in the 'Other wins' section: `
New sandbox.credentials setting blocks sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables
`. Stripping the `` markup gives the claimed sentence character-for-character. One sentence, no qualifier. The `files`/`envVars` sub-key claim is independently supported by settings.md:421-:424 (`credentials.files`, `credentials.envVars`, `credentials.envVars[].injectHosts`, `credentials.allowPlaintextInject`). No refutation here. 2) CITED FILE:LINE — accurate on the letter, wrong on the reading. packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:172-180 is exactly `['excludedCommands','deniedReadRoots','deniedWriteRoots','additionalWritableRoots','allowUnsandboxedCommands','network','filesystem']` — no `credentials`. `grep -ran credentials` on that file (NUL-safe) returns only :321 and :324. But the claim that the name appears 'only as a shape ANALOGY … borrowed' framed as a defect inverts what the comments do: :318-327 says '`settings.md:200`\'s `sandbox.credentials` row applied to the sub-block we actually have', a deliberate, argued borrow of the doc's ONLY published nested-block tolerance rule, quoted in full with its reason ('Returning `undefined` for a wholly invalid `network` is what makes the rest of `sandbox` still apply'). managed-policy.ts:1164 states it outright: 'Shaped like `settings.md:200`\'s `sandbox.credentials` row, which is the doc's only nested-document case'. And settings.md:200 really is that row, verbatim. Citing the one published precedent for a tolerance shape is not evidence of a gap. 2b) THE CLAIMED MECHANISM IS WRONG. 'the key is stripped as unknown' is false on the strict path. Ran the real parser: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({credentials:{files:[…],envVars:[…]}})` → `THREW: invalid sandbox setting: credentials` (assertKnownKeys, :216-221). Positive control on the same rig: `parseManagedSandboxSettingsV1({deniedReadRoots:['/Users/x/.aws']})` → parses clean, so the throw is about the key name, not a broken probe. Stripping happens only on the tolerant managed-delivery path. A row whose mechanism is wrong cannot be dispatched as written. 3) OWNER DECISION — this is parity row R19, PARKED. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:690: row R19, status ⏸, scope 'Egress proxy and domain policy: … `mask` mode for named env vars', marked 'PARKED by owner decision 2026-07-28 — «нужно всё разрешить, ограничения будут потом»', with the plan deliberately retained at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-egress-proxy.md (:15 'there is no mask/deny path for `credentials.envVars` today — Task 4 adds `deny` there'; :31 lands the documented `mask`-without-`tlsTerminate` failure). docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:218 carries 'R19 — `credentials.envVars` `mask` … Half-shipped, then parked by owner decision — so nothing is live'. Audit :478 records an earlier finder hitting this same row and being told it belonged to R19. Not one of inert-worklist §3's nine (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions), but an equivalent dated owner decision recorded in three places. 4) CONSEQUENCE REFUTED UPSTREAM ON BOTH HALVES (trap shape #3 — the identifier is unwired, the consequence is false). The doc sentence names two protections; this fork ships both unconditionally, by other names, and is STRICTER than a default Claude install on each. (a) CREDENTIAL FILES. `credentialDenyRoots` (packages/session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) is a host-seeded, unremovable floor covering the doc's own two examples (~/.ssh, ~/.aws) plus ~/.nessy, ~/.netrc, ~/._netrc, ~/.docker, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.config/git/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.kube, ~/.gnupg, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.azure, ~/Library/Keychains, the per-vendor browser cookie/login stores and the Windows DPAPI trio. It is seeded into `deniedReadRoots` at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/host-sandbox-settings.ts:61 and independently at packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/script-sandbox.ts:83, composed into the isolation funnel as `unconditionalDeniedReadRoots` (filesystem-isolation.ts:136-184), and passed as `credentialFloor` at bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:225 so /doctor and the funnel agree. sandbox-settings.ts:708-716 makes a user `filesystem.allowRead` unable to re-open a floor path, and :798-815 RETAINS the floor even when `filesystem.disabled` turns the layer off, with the reason written in-line ('so releasing it here would let one boolean in a user file hand over ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and the gateway token under ~/.nessy'). Claude documents the opposite default at sandboxing.md:271 — 'There is no built-in credential deny list, so only the files and variables you list are restricted' — which credential-deny-roots.ts:20-22 quotes as its rationale. (b) SECRET ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES. This half was NOT covered by the earlier sibling verdict and I verified it directly. Supervised processes get their host env through `hostEnvironment(profile)` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:726-732), and the DEFAULT profile is `restricted` (`resolveEnvironmentProfile` :716-724 — `restricted` unless a caller explicitly asks otherwise). `restricted` is an ALLOWLIST, not a deny list: `RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT` (:703-711) admits 25 names plus an `LC_*` pattern — HOME/PATH/SHELL/USER/LOGNAME, locale and terminal vars, toolchain roots, the Windows quartet, and four NESSY_* doc-path vars. Nothing else from process.env crosses. So AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and NESSY_DP_AUTH_TOKEN are absent from a sandboxed command's environment by construction. `grep -ran "'trusted-host'"` over production source returns only the type declaration, the two enum validators and the supervisor's own comparison — no production caller requests it, and no bash path sets `inheritHostEnv: true` (local-tools/runtime.ts:398-404 is `processBinding`, a result-REPORTING projection back onto the observability record, not a start request). The protection the doc sentence describes is not absent; it is on by default and not removable. 5) NOT a brand/gateway/subscription product difference — this is a settings-schema question, not renaming. 6) PROVENANCE. This row is the whats-new restatement of docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:3573-3574, and its `sandboxing.md` twin (phase1 :388-390) was already challenged and REFUTED in docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase2-partial.json on grounds 3 and 4(a). Our Claude provider path does not stream over its own HTTP client: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1 imports query() from @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk and :1636 reads options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, which packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:271-296 points at the NATIVE upstream binary ('This is the native `claude` binary, not a JS file'). results.claim: A transient server rate-limit error that is not the account usage limit must be retried automatically with backoff rather than ending the turn.
results.quote: Transient server rate-limit errors unrelated to your usage limit are now retried automatically with backoff for subscribers instead of failing the turn
results.ourState: Both backends classify a rate limit and surface it to the user instead of retrying. claude-agent.ts carries the explicit comment 'Rate limit errors - don't retry immediately, surface to user' and then yields typed_error + complete; pi-agent.ts returns a `rate_limited` diagnostic with a manual 'Retry' action and retryDelayMs 5000. No backoff loop, and no distinction between a transient server 429 and the account usage limit. (Backoff retry does exist elsewhere — MCP connect, webhooks, session mirror — so the absence is specific to the model turn.)

verdict.why: Doc sentence is verbatim (w27.md line 98, a single-clause <div> in 'Other wins'; no second sentence reverses it). Both cited code sites exist roughly as described, with line drift: the claude-agent.ts comment is at :2045 not :2023, and pi-agent.ts's rate_limited block is at :7644-7662 — the cited :7621-7636 is the invalid_api_key block, not the rate-limit one. But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is exactly the 'enforcement one layer down' false-positive shape that inert-worklist §4.3 warns about: both handlers are POST-EXHAUSTION terminal paths, not the first response to a transient 429. (1) PI BACKEND (the fork's default): the shipped Pi runtime auto-retries with exponential backoff, on by default. apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:590052 _prepareRetry computes `delayMs = settings.baseDelayMs * 2 ** (this._retryAttempt - 1)`; defaults are enabled:true (:599429 `return this.settings.retry?.enabled ?? true`), maxRetries:3, baseDelayMs:2000 (:599442-599443). _handlePostAgentRun (:589014) returns true after a successful _prepareRetry and the caller runs `await this.agent.continue()` (:589001) — the turn continues rather than failing. The transient-vs-usage-limit distinction the claim says does not exist is explicit and in the source: NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN (:538149) = GoUsageLimitError, FreeUsageLimitError, 'Monthly usage limit reached', 'available balance', insufficient_quota, 'out of budget', 'quota exceeded', billing; RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN (:538159) = overloaded, rate.?limit, 'too many requests', 429, 500/502/503/504, and more; isRetryableAssistantError (:538194) retries only when the error matches the retryable set and NOT the usage-limit set. The HTTP layer enforces the same split independently: isRetryableError (:106449) returns false for `status===429 && isTerminalRateLimitError(errorText)` and true for other 429/5xx, and the loop at :107424 applies `BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** attempt` or the honored retry-after / retry-after-ms header. Nessy's own host is wired to surface this: packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:900-915 maps auto_retry_start to a 'Retrying (attempt N/M)...' status and auto_retry_end to an error only when !success. packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js carries the identical code at shifted offsets. So parsePiError's rate_limited + manual Retry is what the user sees only after 3 backed-off retries have already failed. (2) CLAUDE BACKEND: the bundled Claude Agent SDK's HTTP client already retries 429 with backoff before any error reaches claude-agent.ts. node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs shouldRetry: `if(e.status===408)return!0;if(e.status===409)return!0;if(e.status===429)return!0;if(e.status>=500)return!0;return!1`, with `maxRetries = n.maxRetries ?? 2` and a retryRequest that reads retry-after-ms then retry-after. The comment 'don't retry immediately, surface to user' is therefore correct in context — a host-level retry there would be a second, uncoordinated loop on top of the SDK's. (3) The fork's own error taxonomy contradicts the claim in plain text: packages/shared/src/agent/errors.ts:105-112 defines rate_limited with the message 'Rate limit reached. Will auto-retry shortly.' (4) Secondary: the doc sentence is scoped 'for subscribers' — a Claude Pro/Max subscription behaviour — and this fork ships NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE off by default and targets the Nestor corporate gateway, so the subscriber-scoped surface is largely outside the fork's default build anyway. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist §3. Positive control for the absence claim was established and it failed: the claim asserted backoff exists only in MCP connect / webhooks / session mirror and is absent from the model turn; grepping the model-turn path found it present in both backends.
verdict.correctedState: Both backends already retry transient server rate-limit errors automatically with exponential backoff, and both distinguish a transient 429 from an account usage limit — the retry lives one layer below the cited handlers, so the cited code is the post-exhaustion terminal path rather than the first response. Pi (default backend): the shipped runtime's agent loop retries with `baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt-1)`, enabled by default at maxRetries 3 / baseDelayMs 2000 (apps/electron/resources/pi-agent-server/index.js:590052, :599429-599443), continuing the turn via `agent.continue()` (:589001, :589014) and gating on RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN vs NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN (:538149-538194); its HTTP layer separately skips retry for `429 && isTerminalRateLimitError` and otherwise backs off honoring retry-after (:106449, :107424). Nessy surfaces the retries as status via packages/shared/src/agent/backend/pi/event-adapter.ts:900-915. Claude backend: the bundled SDK's HTTP client retries 429/408/409/5xx with maxRetries 2 honoring retry-after-ms/retry-after (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs, shouldRetry/retryRequest), which is why claude-agent.ts:2045 deliberately does not add a second loop. The residual, much smaller, gap is cosmetic and Claude-side only: pi-agent.ts:7644-7662 offers a manual Retry after the budget is exhausted, whereas Claude's post-exhaustion path at claude-agent.ts:2045-2056 yields typed_error + complete.

results.ourState: No rule anywhere names session transcript files as a protected target. SESSIONS_DIR … is <configDir>/sessions' — listed under 'NOT here, deliberately'); packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts (no transcript rule; lines 128-130 mention the transcript only as untrusted evidence)

verdict.why:
The doc sentence exists verbatim (2026-w28.md:50, a single-sentence <div> in 'Other wins'; the whole line was read and its second clause is the unrelated rm -rf item). The claimed OUR STATE is wrong on both of its load-bearing consequences.

(1) FILE TOOLS -- the decisive error. The claim says the protected-path floor fires on the .nessy-agent segment 'but in auto mode its outcome is routed to the classifier'. That is the CLAUDE DOC's table row (permission-modes.md:435-441), not our code. Our fork deliberately deviates and is STRICTER, and says so at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/protected-paths.ts:181-186: 'auto prompts, and the prompt reaches the HUMAN: the protected-path floor is nonNegotiable, and pi-agent.ts's autoBorderlineEligible refuses non-negotiable prompts, so the guardian classifier is never consulted for it. This is a deliberate deviation from the doc table's Routed to the classifier row -- a judge no_objection must not convert a floor into an allow.' Verified end to end, not from the comment: pre-tool-use.ts:1580-1590 emits the prompt with nonNegotiable:'protectedPath'; promptIsNonNegotiable (pre-tool-use.ts:681-687) returns true for it; pi-agent.ts:4051-4054 gates autoBorderlineEligible on !promptIsNonNegotiable(checkResult), so the guardian consult at :4094 is unreachable for this class. A committed test pins it: pre-tool-use-checks.isolated.ts:2180-2186 loops ['ask','acceptEdits','auto'] and asserts prompt + nonNegotiable==='protectedPath' EVEN WITH an allow rule naming the path. So auto mode does not auto-approve a file-tool write to the transcript; it stops for a human, and dontAsk denies outright. That satisfies -- and exceeds -- the documented behaviour.

(2) BASH -- the claim's inference from self-config-deny.ts:31-34 is a misreading of what that deny list is for. The quoted comment is accurate on disk, but deniedWriteRoots is the belt for paths INSIDE a writable grant; it is not the only guard. The darwin/linux/win32 profiles are deny-by-default for writes: filesystem-isolation.ts:167-176 emits '(deny file-write*)' and then opens ONLY /dev/null, the writableRoot and additionalWritableRoots, and darwin.ts:34-48 sets writableRoot = workspaceRoot (networked/workspace profiles; credential-deny-roots.ts:15 names 'networked' as 'the shipped default for the foreground shell') plus scratchRoot. A measured positive control for exactly this already exists in-repo, in the sibling subsystem's note (bash-seatbelt.ts:74-80, the phase-4 sandbox probe under the real shipped profile): 'writes are still contained (a write to ~ returns Operation not permitted)'. ~/.nessy-agent/sessions/... is such a path.

Sibling-subsystem trap checked: the SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD owner decision (inert-worklist §3 item 1) belongs to packages/shared/src/agent/core/bash-seatbelt.ts, a DIFFERENT wrapper; its own comment states that buildDarwinSandboxProfile -- the profile the supervised-process isolation actually composes -- 'has no wildcard branch', so the wildcard does not open the transcript path.

The one literally-true fragment ('no rule names session transcript files as a protected target', and guardian.ts has no transcript-tampering rule -- confirmed, its only transcript mentions are :128 and :130 treating it as untrusted evidence) carries no consequence: coverage comes from the .nessy-agent segment one layer up, and the guardian is never consulted for this class anyway.

But the CONSEQUENCE is false, and it is false exactly in the recurring shape this repo's trap list names: the enforcement lives one layer up, in the host, not in the spawner. (1) A per-session spawn COUNT budget DOES exist. spawner.ts:600-608 forwards `budgets: { fanout: cfg.maxFanout ?? 100, concurrency: cfg.concurrency ?? DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY, ... }` to the host, and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/child-session-service.ts:148 enforces it inside the persisted-state commit: `if (children.length >= input.budgets.fanout) throw new Error('child-session-fanout-limit')`. `children` is the parent session's FULL child-record list; records are removed only on the cancelled-start rollback (:154), never on completion, so `children.length` is a CUMULATIVE per-session spawn count, not an active count. child-session-service.test.ts:178-184 proves the cumulative semantics: child-1 is stopped first, and a subsequent start with `fanout: 1` still throws `child-session-fanout-limit`. The value comes from `orchestrator.maxAgents` (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1280 `maxFanout: config.orchestrator?.maxAgents`), default 1000 in DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/harness-manifest.ts:109); the spawner's own fallback when the host supplies nothing is 100. (2) A concurrency limit DOES exist, in BOTH layers. spawner.ts:144-208 defines a `Semaphore` sized by `computeEffectiveConcurrency(cfg.concurrency ?? 16)` = `max(1, min(ceiling, cpuCores - 2))`, rebuilt on every `configureSpawner` (:208), and every spawn goes through `semaphore.run(...)`. The host re-checks independently at child-session-service.ts:149: `if (active.length >= input.budgets.concurrency) throw new Error('child-session-concurrency-limit')`. Both are covered by tests (spawner.test.ts imports `computeEffectiveConcurrency`/`Semaphore`; child-session-service.test.ts:172 and :370 assert `child-session-concurrency-limit`). (3) 'A depth-1 loop can spawn unboundedly' is therefore false on two counts: the Nth spawn of a session is refused once N reaches the fanout budget, and at most min(16, cores-2) run at once meanwhile. Budgets are additionally clamped monotonically down the tree (SessionManager.ts:11142-11143 `Math.min(input.budgets.fanout, inherited.fanout)` / same for concurrency, and :4933-4934 pins a child's fanout/concurrency to 1), and the workflow tool carries its own per-run cap (workflow-tool.ts:562-563, `workflow maxAgents exceeded`). verdict.correctedState: Refuted — the consequence is inverted.
